**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Turning what the court record already says (eCourts next date, last date, stage, new order) into a short, factual, plain-language update in the client's language, sent on WhatsApp only to a client who has opted in from that number, after a lawyer approves it (or automatically for date-only updates if the firm has turned that on), and flagging client messages that nobody has answered. Most 'what happened today?' messages are about facts the system already syncs. It can also spot silence, meaning a matter with no update for N days.

### What it can't fix

Software can't make a lawyer explain strategy, return calls or care. Orders uploaded days late, or cases missing from the eCourtsIndia provider, can't be fixed by us; the update then says 'order not yet uploaded'. We can't read courtroom events that never reach eCourts (what the judge said orally, the opponent's tactics). Those need the lawyer's one-line outcome pick. WhatsApp template approval by Meta and Meta's policy changes are outside our control.

### What the user sees

Lawyer: a new 'Client updates' tab in /inbox (and a badge on /cases) after the evening sync. Each card reads, for example: 'Sharma v. Gupta, CC 212/2025, listed 24 Oct. Next date 14 Nov. Stage: Misc. Arguments, shown to the client as "the court will hear short arguments on a side application". Client: Ramesh (Hindi, verified +91…).' The lawyer picks an outcome line from a pre-translated picklist ('adjourned at the other side's request', 'time given to file reply', 'arguments heard, order reserved', 'you need not attend', 'you must attend') and can add a note. One tap sends all, and edits are allowed. A second panel, 'Waiting for a reply', lists client WhatsApp messages unanswered for more than X business hours (firm-set, default 8), oldest first. Each has a suggested reply built from the matter's current state, shown as a draft. A third list, 'Silent matters', shows matters where the client has heard nothing in 30 days. Client: a WhatsApp message in Hindi or English, with no app and no login: 'आपके केस शर्मा बनाम गुप्ता (CC 212/2025) की सुनवाई 24 अक्टूबर को हुई। अगली तारीख 14 नवंबर है। अदालत ने दूसरे पक्ष को जवाब देने का समय दिया है। इस तारीख पर आपको आने की ज़रूरत नहीं है। — Adv. X'. Replying STOP ends updates. Replying with a question puts it in the lawyer's inbox.

### What the system does

1) Migration 014_client_experience.sql adds `client_contacts` (court_case_id, org_id, phone E.164, name, relation, language, verified_at, consent_at, consent_method, opted_out_at; RLS like court_cases) and `client_updates` (court_case_id, kind date_change|new_order|status_change|manual|silence, facts jsonb, body text, language, status draft|approved|sent|failed|discarded, approved_by/at stamped by trigger like stamp_draft_approval, sent_message_id). 2) A contact is verified only when the client's WhatsApp wa_id has messaged the firm number and matches (whatsapp_conversations.wa_id = to_wa_id(phone)), or a lawyer records written consent with method and date. Consent to case updates is a separate YES from the intake consent; the prompt is a fixed template. STOP/रोकें sets opted_out_at in code. 3) ecourts_service.sync returns a diff (old vs new next_hearing_date, last_hearing_date, case_status, orders list). A new pure function `client_updates.from_diff(old, new) -> list[UpdateFacts]` produces facts only, with no prose. 4) `client_updates.render(facts, language, outcome_key, attendance)` fills fixed templates from `app/data/client_templates/{en,hi,mr,ta,bn,te,kn,gu}.json`. Stage text comes from `app/data/stage_glossary.json`, which maps normalized eCourts stage labels ('appearance', 'misc. arguments', 'evidence', 'framing of charge'…) to lawyer-reviewed plain text per language. An unknown stage renders as 'stage recorded by the court: <label>' and logs the label so it can be added to the glossary. There is no machine translation at run time. 5) The cron gains a second run at 19:30 IST (`task_case_updates`), using the existing service-role server job scoped per org. It syncs today's listed cases, creates drafts, and posts the lawyer an n8n/WhatsApp alert: 'N updates waiting'. 6) Sending: inside the 24-hour window via send_text; outside it via the Meta-approved utility template `case_update` with parameters {title, listed date, next date, plain stage, attendance line}. Status changes and send results go to audit_logs (new AuditAction SEND_CLIENT_UPDATE, APPROVE_CLIENT_UPDATE). 7) Date-only updates (date_change with no order and no lawyer note) can be sent without approval only if the org enabled `auto_send_date_updates` through approval_requests (new action 'enable_auto_updates', maker-checker like enable_intake). Anything with an order summary or free text always waits for a lawyer. 8) An optional order summary: when an order PDF exists, the lawyer can click 'Summarise order for client'. OCR, then mask_pii, then Haiku with a fixed prompt (informational, no advice), then citation_service.verify_text, verify_output_safety and intake_guard-style checks. The result is shown as a draft and is never sent unapproved. 9) Unanswered tracker: a pure function `sla.overdue(messages, business_hours, holidays, now)` computes business-hour lag from the last inbound client message to the next outbound lawyer/system message. The firm's working hours and the court holiday list live in `org_settings`. A suggested reply uses only matter facts (next date, stage, last update) and is stored as a pending whatsapp_message (existing status='pending' path, settle_held_reply). 10) Silence: matters with no sent update and no outbound message in N days appear in the 'Silent matters' list. 11) Every sent update is also written to matter_events (see P48).

### Where it is built

Extend app/services/ecourts_service.py (sync returns diff; from_provider keeps stage text and order list), app/worker.py (task_case_updates cron; reuse send_hearing_reminders' per-org number lookup), app/services/whatsapp_service.py (send_template with the case_update template), app/services/whatsapp_intake.py (STOP / update-consent keywords, links the conversation to client_contacts), app/services/safety_service.py and migration 013's approval_requests (new action enable_auto_updates), app/services/audit_service.py (new actions). New: supabase/migrations/014_client_experience.sql, app/services/client_updates.py, app/services/sla_service.py, app/data/stage_glossary.json, app/data/client_templates/*.json, app/routers/client_updates.py (GET /api/v1/client-updates, POST /{id}/approve, POST /{id}/discard, POST /court-cases/{id}/contacts), frontend/src/app/inbox/page.tsx (Updates, Waiting and Silent tabs), frontend/src/app/cases/page.tsx (contacts and language per case).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI only face the lawyer and have no client channel. Clio, MyCase and Case Status need a human to write every update (the step that lapses), make clients install an app and log in, work only in English, and read no eCourts data. The eCourts app and Indian trackers (KanoonKit and others) push raw dates and English stage labels with no 'what this means / do I need to come'. Ours starts from the synced court record, so a draft exists without anyone writing it. The approve step is one tap over facts already filled in, and the output is in the client's language on WhatsApp, which clients already use. Because the templates are fixed and pre-translated, the factual part can't hallucinate, and only lawyer-approved text carries anything beyond the record.

### Safeguards

BCI Rule 36: messages go only to people who are already clients and opted in from that number; no promotional content. Templates are categorised 'utility'. UPL: the deterministic templates state court-record facts and the lawyer-chosen attendance line; any AI order summary passes citation_service, verify_output_safety and the lawyer's approval. DPDP: separate, recorded, revocable consent for updates (consent_at, method, opted_out_at); purpose-limited; contacts erased through trash_item like other client records. Privilege and confidentiality: no strategy or internal notes in updates; updates go only to verified numbers; family contacts need a lawyer to authorise each number. PII masking: order text is masked before Haiku; templates need no AI. Invariant 2: the cron is a server-side job scoped per org (an existing listed exception); the lawyer-facing endpoints use get_supabase_for_user. Maker-checker for turning on auto-send. Everything is audited.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_client_updates.py::test_from_diff_date_change: old next_hearing_date=2026-10-24, new=2026-11-14, last_hearing_date=2026-10-24 -> exactly one UpdateFacts(kind='date_change', listed='2026-10-24', next='2026-11-14').
- test_from_diff_no_change: identical rows -> no facts; a sync that only changes last_synced_at creates no update.
- test_render_hindi_golden: facts plus outcome 'reply_time_given' plus attendance 'not_required' in 'hi' -> byte-for-byte match with the golden string in tests/golden/update_hi.txt; the same for 'en'.
- test_unknown_stage_fallback: stage 'XYZ Stage 9' -> body contains the raw label in the fallback sentence and the label is logged; no exception.
- test_glossary_complete: every key in stage_glossary.json has non-empty text for every supported language (catches untranslated stages in CI).
- test_no_send_without_approval: a draft update with an order summary is never passed to whatsapp_service (mocked) by task_case_updates, even with auto_send_date_updates=true.
- test_auto_send_date_only_requires_org_flag: a date-only update is sent when the flag is on and stays a draft when it is off.
- test_unverified_contact_blocked: a contact with verified_at null and no written consent -> approve endpoint returns 409 and nothing is sent.
- test_stop_opt_out: inbound 'STOP' from a verified number sets opted_out_at; later updates for that contact are skipped and audited as skipped.
- test_sla_business_hours: a client message at Fri 21:00 IST with firm hours Mon-Sat 10-19 and an 8h SLA -> overdue at Sat 18:00, not before; a court holiday from org_settings is skipped.
- test_order_summary_guarded: a model mock returning 'You will definitely win, file under Section 999 IPC' -> the summary is held, with reasons [citation invalid/repealed, guarantee pattern], and status stays draft.
- Local Postgres RLS test: a user in org B can't select client_contacts or client_updates of org A; an associate sees only updates for court_cases they own.
- test_approval_stamp_trigger: editing body after approval clears approved_by/approved_at (same pattern as drafts).

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Auto-sent date-only updates rely on eCourtsIndia provider data that can be wrong. Auto-send only when two syncs agree, or when the date matches an ingested cause list, and never for an accused whose personal attendance is required.
- The 'you need not attend' picklist entry should be blocked or warned on for criminal trial stages without an exemption order recorded on the matter.
- Family or relative contacts need the client's own recorded authorisation for each number (or the authorisation of the person who instructed the firm, for a client in custody). A lawyer's authorisation alone is not enough for confidentiality.
- Auto-sent date-only updates must not carry an attendance line. Say 'your lawyer will tell you if you need to attend', since an automatic 'need not attend' could cost an accused their bail.
- The updates consent prompt should carry the s.5 DPDP notice items (purpose, how to withdraw, grievance contact, right to complain to the Board), with the notice available in the client's language.
- eCourts already sends litigants SMS/email next-date alerts when their mobile is registered. Make the differentiator the plain-language stage, the attendance line and the lawyer's outcome, not 'the client gets the date'.
- court_cases.client_phone already exists. Migrate it into client_contacts (unverified) rather than keeping two sources.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Stop unchecked authority from leaving the firm in a filing. A 'filing copy' export stays blocked until every citation is either verified by code or attested by a named lawyer, and each export carries a per-citation verification record. The check also runs on text we didn't write: an associate's Word draft, pasted ChatGPT output, a senior's brief. Sanctions follow the signer whatever tool produced the citation.

New this round:
- The judgment side is cleaned deterministically before any word matching. Line-end hyphens are joined, running headers and footers, page numbers and footnote markers are stripped, and offsets back to the original PDF page are kept. A correctly copied quote that crosses a page break or a hyphenated line therefore verifies.
- A difference that falls in a layout zone downgrades to amber, never hard red.
- An official court translation is never green. It is an amber 'restricted use' reading aid, bound to the English paragraph it mirrors, and the record prints the Court's own disclaimer word for word next to the English paragraph.

### What it can't fix

Limits of the gate:
- We can't stop a lawyer copying text out of the app, or filing something that never went through it. The gate covers our export path and is evidence of diligence.
- An external_source row records what the lawyer says they read. We can't confirm that reading.
- We can't prove an uploaded copy is a certified copy.

Limits of quote checking:
- We check that each fragment is the court's exact words, in order and close together. Negations and qualifiers next to omissions are flagged. Whether an elision distorts the meaning stays the signing advocate's duty of candour.
- Layout cleaning is rule-based. A PDF with an odd layout (two columns, a header the rules don't recognise, scanned pages) can leave artefacts. When an unexplained difference sits in a layout zone, we say 'layout unclear, check page 7' (amber) rather than guess. We never call it fabricated.

Limits on translations:
- We can't check counsel's own translation against the English by code, so the lawyer attests it.
- The Supreme Court's SUVAS/vernacular translations are published for the litigant's restricted use, with the English version authentic. We therefore never treat them as a verification source or as quotable authority.
- Whether even storing them as a reading aid is within the Court's terms is a legal question. scripts/ingest_sc_translations.py ships disabled (INGEST_SC_TRANSLATIONS=false) until the firm's or our counsel's review of the terms clears it. Until then, only translations a lawyer uploads for their own matter are used, labelled lawyer-supplied.

Other limits:
- We don't index US/UK judgments, so those rows read 'unverified: jurisdiction not indexed'.
- Whether a court excuses an error is for the court.

### What the user sees

Unchanged from earlier rounds:
- In /studio the export menu has 'Working copy' (never blocked, watermarked until approved) and 'Filing copy'.
- 'Filing copy' opens the Verification Ledger and stays disabled while a counter such as '3 citations need you' shows.
- The three ways to attest, rebind, carry-forward, the record PDF and /verify work as before.
- The round-5 statuses are unchanged: green 'Verified word for word' (also 'elided, n parts'), red 'Not the court's exact words' with a word diff and negations highlighted, amber 'Omission next to a qualifier', amber 'Translation by counsel', amber 'Corrected to the court's words, now confirm', and 'Make it a paraphrase'.

New this round:
- A quote that crosses a page break, a hyphenated line end or a footnote marker in the S.C.R./INSC PDF shows plain green 'Verified word for word'. A small 'layout' note lists what the cleaner joined or skipped, for example 'joined discre-|tion (p. 6-7); skipped running header "SUPREME COURT REPORTS [2019] 5 S.C.R." and page no. 412; skipped footnote marker 12'. Clicking it opens the original page image with those spots outlined.
- Amber 'Layout unclear on p. 7: check the page'. This appears when the only differences between quote and judgment sit at a page edge or line end the cleaner couldn't explain. The judgment pane shows the cleaned text above the original page image, and the lawyer clears the row in_app after looking. It is never red.
- The 'Use the court's words' candidates show cleaned text only. A candidate that spans an unexplained layout artefact is greyed out with 'Layout unclear on p. 7; open the page image'. It can't be inserted, so a header or 'discre tion' can never reach the pleading.
- Amber 'Matches the Court's translation (restricted use)' replaces last round's green official-translation status. The panel shows three things side by side: the Hindi quote, the Court's translated para 14 and the English para 14. The English para is pre-selected because the translations mirror its numbering, and the lawyer must confirm it. The Court's disclaimer is shown verbatim above the translation. Two exits:
  - 'Add the English original to the draft' inserts English para 14 as a block quote or footnote in a new version. The English quote is then checked like any other quote and must come out green.
  - 'I adopt this as my translation of para 14' records translation_by_counsel.
  The row is filing-ready only after one of these, plus the lawyer's confirmation of the English para binding.

### What the system does

Unchanged: steps 1-3 (audit endpoint, binding_method, disambiguation, text_quality), 4a parse_quote, 4a' normalize_words, 4b' script_of, 4d elision_polarity, 4f/4g correction and paraphrase flows, and steps 5-11 except as noted below. The checksummed quote_conventions.yaml gains a judgment_layout section and a translation_disclaimer_markers list.

NEW 0. Judgment text cleaning: app/services/judgment_text.py, shared with P12. Pure and deterministic, versioned as CLEANER_VERSION.

(i) Extraction keeps pages. ingest_sc_judgments.pdf_text currently joins pages with '\n'. It is replaced by pdf_pages() -> list[str], one string per page with line breaks kept. The RAG chunker receives the cleaned text, which also improves retrieval.

(ii) Running headers and footers. For each page take the first 3 and last 3 lines. Mask digits to '#' and collapse whitespace. A masked line that recurs at the same edge on at least 30% of pages (and at least 2 pages) is a running header/footer. Examples: 'SUPREME COURT REPORTS [####] # S.C.R.', '###'. So are lines matching the fixed judgment_layout patterns: a bare page number, '[YYYY] n S.C.R. nnn', 'YYYY INSC nnn' alone on a line, 'Digital Supreme Court Reports', 'REPORTABLE', 'NON-REPORTABLE', a 'Signature Not Verified' stamp block. These lines are removed and recorded as artefacts {page, kind, original_offset, text}.

(iii) Footnotes. On a page whose bottom block, after an optional rule line, has lines starting with a number n, that block is moved to a separate footnotes stream tagged (page, n). A quote taken from a footnote is still matchable there, but running text never crosses it. A glued marker is stripped from running text when a footnote n exists on the same page: 'liberty12' becomes 'liberty', recorded. Superscript digits ('liberty¹²') are always stripped. A glued digit with no matching footnote is left alone and marked as an unresolved artefact.

(iv) Line-end hyphens. 'X-\nY', where X ends in a letter and Y starts with a lowercase letter, is joined. The joined form drops the hyphen if it occurs elsewhere in the same judgment, or in the bundled legal lexicon app/data/lexicon_en.txt. It keeps the hyphen ('self-incrimination') if only the hyphenated form occurs. Otherwise it is joined both ways and marked hyphen_ambiguous; the matcher accepts either form.

(v) Ordinary line breaks inside a paragraph become spaces. Paragraph numbers at line start become para indices, via the P12 parser.

(vi) Offsets. Output is CleanText {text, offset_map: list of (clean_start, clean_end, page, orig_start), artefacts, cleaner_version, layout_zones}. layout_zones are clean-text character ranges within 2 tokens of a page join, a removed line, a hyphen join or an unresolved artefact.

(vii) text_quality also becomes 'layout_uncertain' when unresolved artefacts exceed 1 per 2 pages, or when more than 2 edge lines per page fit neither the header rules nor body text. Under rule 2, that alone removes every hard status for this judgment.

The result is stored in judgment_text_cache: raw_sha256, clean_text, offset_map, artefacts, cleaner_version. A cleaner_version bump re-cleans lazily. The carry-forward key now includes cleaner_version.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI generate citations but don't stop an unchecked draft being exported. The Lacey sanctions involved CoCounsel/Westlaw output, and Gauthier shows an AI checker missing fabricated cases. SCC Online, Manupatra and Indian Kanoon find judgments but don't check a draft, and are English-only.

Quote checkers fail in one of four ways:
- Whole-string comparison flags every elided quote.
- Fuzzy matching passes a quote whose last clause turned 'shall' into 'may'.
- Exact matching on raw PDF text flags every correct quote that crosses a page break. Lawyers learn to ignore red, and the gate becomes busywork.
- Treating a court's vernacular translation as quotable authority contradicts the Court's own disclaimer.

Ours works differently:
- Layout artefacts are removed by recorded, reversible rules before exact word matching.
- Token splits and merges are equal only when the letters are identical.
- Anything the cleaner can't explain goes to amber with the page image, never red and never into the pleading.
- Translations are reading aids tied to the English paragraph, which is the text the bench is shown.
- Green still means only one thing: the court's exact words in its authoritative English text, checked by code.

### Safeguards

A lawyer is always the last step:
- Green comes only from an exact word match by code against the cleaned authoritative English text, and every cleaning step is listed in the record and traceable to the original page.
- An unexplained layout difference is amber, with the original page image shown, never red and never inserted into a pleading.
- Every automatic correction or form change needs the signing lawyer to read the inserted words, and junior drafts then also need partner approval.

Translations:
- Court translations are used only as restricted-use reading aids, never labelled verified, and always printed below the English paragraph with the Court's disclaimer verbatim.
- Ingesting them stays off until a terms review.
- Counsel's own translation is attested and printed beside the English text.

Rules and records:
- All rules (layout patterns, the lexicon, polarity words, spelling equivalents, editorial markers, disclaimer markers) are checksummed, lawyer-signed data, never an LLM.
- The record never says 'guaranteed accurate'.
- Every attestation, correction, paraphrase, English insertion and filing export is audit-logged.

Data handling:
- The working copy is never blocked.
- Only citation strings go to Indian Kanoon.
- Any LLM hint uses masked text (invariant 1).
- Uploaded copies and translations stay org-scoped, with no service-role use in user paths (invariant 2).

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection 1 (exact matching on uncleaned corpus text gives false hard blocks):

(a) Clean the judgment side, deterministically, with offsets kept. I confirmed the gap: scripts/ingest_sc_judgments.py's pdf_text() just joins pypdf page text with '\n', with no cleaning. The new app/services/judgment_text.py, shared with P12:
- keeps pages;
- removes running headers and footers, detected by digit-masked recurrence at page edges on at least 30% of pages, plus fixed checksummed patterns for S.C.R./INSC/page-number/REPORTABLE lines;
- moves footnote bodies to a separate stream;
- strips glued footnote markers only when footnote n exists on that page (superscripts always);
- joins line-end hyphens, resolved against the same judgment and a bundled lexicon, with ambiguous joins accepted both ways.
Every removal is an artefact with page and original offset. The offset_map maps clean text back to the PDF page, and the record lists what was joined or skipped.

(b) Token splits and merges, and downgrade instead of block:
- match_fragment treats 1-3 token runs as equal when their letter concatenations are identical ('discre tion' = 'discretion'), recorded as join_equivalence.
- A match that spans an unresolved artefact is 'exact_layout'.
- A diff whose every change sits in a layout zone, with no polarity change, becomes quote_layout_soft (amber, in_app with the page image), never quote_differs.
- Hard red now needs a change outside layout zones or any polarity change.
- A judgment whose layout is too noisy gets text_quality layout_uncertain, which removes hard statuses entirely.

(c) Insertion uses clean text only:
- closest_passages and use_court_words render from clean_text with resolved hyphen joins.
- A candidate spanning an unresolved artefact is not insertable.
- A post-insert assertion refuses any insertion that would contain an artefact string.

Fixtures: a page break with a running header and page number, a hyphenated line end (both resolution cases), a glued footnote marker and a superscript marker each give verified. An unrecognised header gives layout soft, not hard. A removed 'not' at a page break is still hard.

Objection 2 (the official-translation match was green although the Court restricts its use): the green status is gone.
- A word-for-word match with a held translation is now official_translation_restricted (amber), 'Matches the Court's translation (restricted use)'.
- It is filing-ready only after the lawyer confirms the paragraph-aligned English original. The para is proposed by mirrored numbering and confirmed only when para counts agree, otherwise picked.
- Then either 'Add the English original to the draft' is used (the English para is inserted and must check exact by code, so the bench has the authentic text), or translation_by_counsel is recorded naming that para.
- The record prints the English para in full first, then the translation labelled 'Court's translation, restricted use', then the Court's disclaimer byte-for-byte. The disclaimer is taken from the translation document itself (NOT NULL; a translation without a captured disclaimer is unusable).

I also accept the reading that ingestion 'where its terms allow' could ingest nothing. ingest_sc_translations.py now ships disabled pending a terms review, and until then only lawyer-uploaded translations, labelled lawyer-supplied, are used.

Test: a Hindi quote matching the fixture official translation is not filing-ready after only the binding confirmation. It is filing-ready after add_english_original or translation_by_counsel. The record contains the English para, the disclaimer verbatim and no 'Verified' label on that row.

### Acceptance tests

- Page break with a running header: a 30-word quote from fixture 2019 INSC 512 that runs from the foot of p. 6 to the top of p. 7, where pypdf output has 'SUPREME COURT REPORTS [2019] 5 S.C.R.' and '412' between, gives verified. layout_notes lists the skipped header and page number, and offset_map points to pages 6 and 7
- Hyphenated line end: a quote containing 'discretion', where the fixture text has 'discre-\ntion', gives verified with a join_equivalence note. A quote containing 'self-incrimination', where the fixture has 'self-\nincrimination' and the hyphenated form occurs elsewhere, also gives verified
- Footnote marker: a quote '... the right to personal liberty is ...' against fixture text 'personal liberty12 is' with footnote 12 on the same page gives verified. A quote copied from footnote 12 itself verifies against the footnotes stream, and running text never crosses into the footnote body
- Superscript marker: 'liberty¹²' in the judgment and 'liberty' in the quote gives verified
- Unrecognised layout: a fixture with a one-off header line, not recurring and matching no pattern, inside the quoted span gives quote_layout_soft (amber), never quote_differs. in_app clears it, and the page-image endpoint returns the rendered p. 7
- A polarity change still bites at a page break: the same cross-page quote with 'not' removed at the page join gives quote_differs (hard) with the polarity flag, not layout soft
- A body change is still hard: changing 'shall' to 'may' in mid-page text, outside any layout zone, of a cleaned fixture gives quote_differs (hard). The round-5 tail-change and added-'not' tests are unchanged
- Join equivalence can't change a word: 'discre tion' against 'discretion' passes, while 'discrete ion' against 'discretion' (different letters) gives differs
- Clean insertion: use_court_words on a cross-page candidate inserts text that contains no artefact string ('SUPREME COURT REPORTS', '412', '12' as a marker) and contains 'discretion', not 'discre tion'. A candidate spanning an unresolved artefact has insertable=false, and the route returns 409
- Cleaner determinism: the same PDF bytes give a byte-identical CleanText 100 times. A CLEANER_VERSION bump invalidates carry-forward for rows bound to that judgment and nothing else. Mapping every clean span back through offset_map reproduces the original substrings
- layout_uncertain: a fixture with dense unclassified edge lines sets text_quality to 'layout_uncertain', and no row bound to it can be hard
- Official translation is restricted: a Hindi quote matching the fixture judgment_translations row word for word gives official_translation_restricted (amber), and filing_ready is false. After english_binding_confirmed for para 14 alone it is still false. After add_english_original (the English para 14 inserted and checked exact by code) or translation_by_counsel naming para 14, it becomes true. external_source returns 422
- The record prints the disclaimer and the English text: for that row the record PDF contains English para 14 in full, the label 'Court's translation, restricted use', and disclaimer_text byte-equal to the fixture's disclaimer block. It never contains the word 'Verified' on that row
- No disclaimer, no use: a fixture translation without a disclaimer block is stored with usable=false, and a matching Hindi quote falls back to quote_translation_soft
- Translation ingestion is off: ingest_sc_translations.py without INGEST_SC_TRANSLATIONS=true exits non-zero and writes nothing
- Para mismatch: when the translation and the English judgment have different para counts, no English binding is proposed automatically, and the lawyer must pick the para
- Round-5 tests still pass: the Hindi translation_by_counsel test, romanised Hindi, mixed quote, bracket_hides_polarity, elision_polarity, negation-flip correction with partner approval, make_paraphrase, and normalize_words keeping Devanagari vowel signs. The evidence_service._normalize output is byte-identical on the contradiction fixtures
- Round-3 and round-4 tests still pass: the elided, '* * *', bracket and emphasis-marker tests, the checksum tamper test, the 500-quote property test, the same-name trap, ambiguous_match, rebind, upload identity 422, s. 124B IPC invalid, 40-citation carry-forward, byte-identical record PDFs and RLS isolation

### Still blocking

- The 'I adopt this as my translation of para 14' exit for official_translation_restricted lets the Supreme Court's restricted-use vernacular translation reach a court inside a pleading, attested as counsel's own translation. The status only arises when the Hindi quote matches the Court's translation word for word, so the attestation is false on its face. It is also exactly the 'other purpose' that the Court's disclaimer prohibits. The internal record prints the disclaimer, but the filed pleading carries only the Hindi text, which is attributed to counsel. Fix I would accept: for official_translation_restricted, make add_english_original (the authentic English para inserted and checked exact by code) the only exit that makes the row filing-ready. Offer translation_by_counsel only after the lawyer has replaced the Hindi with their own rendering, which then no longer matches the Court's translation verbatim and falls to quote_translation_soft, or in addition to the English insertion and never instead of it. Add a test: a verbatim match plus translation_by_counsel alone gives filing_ready false.
- Join equivalence is not 'can't change a word', so green no longer means 'the court's exact words'. As specified, any run of 1-3 tokens anywhere in the span counts as equal when the letters concatenate to the same string. The proposal's own 'cannot' / 'can not' example is one case, and others are 'may be' / 'maybe', 'any one' / 'anyone', 'every one' / 'everyone', 'a part' / 'apart', 'in to' / 'into' and 'some times' / 'sometimes'. These are different words with different meanings in legal text ('any one of the accused' vs 'anyone of the accused'). Yet a mid-page quote that swaps them, nowhere near a line break, would be 'Verified word for word'. Fix I would accept: allow join equivalence only where the judgment-side token boundary falls in a layout zone (a line end, a page join, or a recorded hyphen or soft-hyphen join). Anywhere else, a split or merge is a non-equal opcode outside the layout zones. It is hard red, or amber at most if the pair is listed in a checksummed, lawyer-signed compound list such as 'cannot' / 'can not'. Also add tests: 'may be' against mid-page 'maybe' is not green, while 'discre tion' against 'discre-\ntion' is green.

proposal.out_of_scope:
Limits of the gate:
- We can't stop a lawyer copying text out of the app, or filing something that never went through it. The gate covers our export path and is evidence of diligence.
- An external_source row records what the lawyer says they read. We can't confirm that reading.
- We can't prove an uploaded copy is a certified copy.

Limits of quote checking:
- We check that each fragment is the court's exact words, in order and close together. Negations and qualifiers next to omissions are flagged. Whether an elision distorts the meaning stays the signing advocate's duty of candour.
- Layout cleaning is rule-based. A PDF with an odd layout (two columns, a header the rules don't recognise, scanned pages) can leave artefacts. When an unexplained difference sits in a layout zone, we say 'layout unclear, check page 7' (amber) rather than guess. We never call it fabricated.

Limits on translations:
- We can't check counsel's own translation against the English by code, so the lawyer attests it.
- The Supreme Court's SUVAS/vernacular translations are published for the litigant's restricted use, with the English version authentic. We therefore never treat them as a verification source or as quotable authority.
- Whether even storing them as a reading aid is within the Court's terms is a legal question. scripts/ingest_sc_translations.py ships disabled (INGEST_SC_TRANSLATIONS=false) until the firm's or our counsel's review of the terms clears it. Until then, only translations a lawyer uploads for their own matter are used, labelled lawyer-supplied.

Other limits:
- We don't index US/UK judgments, so those rows read 'unverified: jurisdiction not indexed'.
- Whether a court excuses an error is for the court.

  - 'exact': an exact contiguous match modulo join equivalence and spelling_equivalents, with no unresolved artefact inside the matched span.
  - 'exact_layout': the same, but an unresolved artefact or hyphen_ambiguous join lies inside the span.
  - 'differs': the existing opcode diff, with each non-equal opcode tagged in_layout_zone = (its judgment-side range intersects layout_zones).

CHANGED 4e quote_status. New step (3a) is inserted before the hard steps. If a fragment is 'exact_layout', or 'differs' where every non-equal opcode has in_layout_zone and none changes a polarity word, the result is quote_layout_soft (amber, in_app). The lawyer clears it after viewing the original page image, rendered from the stored PDF at offset_map's page. quote_differs (hard) now requires at least one non-equal opcode outside every layout zone, or a polarity change anywhere. A real one-word change in body text stays hard, and so does a 'not' hidden at a page break.

CHANGED 4f closest_passages and use_court_words. Candidates come from clean_text, and are rendered from clean spans with hyphen joins in their resolved form. A candidate whose span contains an unresolved artefact or hyphen_ambiguous join has insertable=false. A post-condition assertion runs on every insertion: the inserted string contains none of the judgment's artefact texts, no bare page-number token at a page join, and no footnote marker. If the assertion fails, the insertion is refused (500 and an audit event), never applied.

CHANGED translation path, 4e(1).
- A translated-script fragment is matched with match_fragment against a held judgment_translations row for the same authority_id and language.
- A match gives official_translation_restricted (amber), never verified.
- The system proposes the English binding: English para p for translated para p. Translations mirror the para numbering, and this is confirmed when both texts have the same para count; otherwise the lawyer picks the para.
- No match gives quote_translation_soft, as before.
- Neither status is ever hard.

NEW attestation and exit rules for official_translation_restricted. The row is filing-ready only when (a) the lawyer has confirmed the English para binding (an in_app attestation naming the para indices, fetched in the pane) AND (b) one of the following holds:
- add_english_original has inserted that para into the draft as a new version, and the English quote then checks exact by code; or
- translation_by_counsel is recorded naming the same para.
external_source returns 422 for this status. Audit events: TRANSLATION_ENGLISH_BOUND and ENGLISH_ORIGINAL_ADDED.

CHANGED 12. judgment_translations gains disclaimer_text (NOT NULL), disclaimer_sha256 and use_terms='restricted_reading_aid'.
- The disclaimer is extracted verbatim from the translation document itself: the block found by translation_disclaimer_markers, e.g. 'Disclaimer', 'अस्वीकरण', on the first or last page.
- A translation without a captured disclaimer is stored with usable=false, and is never used for matching or display.
- The record PDF prints, with no LLM, in this order:
  1. the English para in full as the authority;
  2. the Court's translated para labelled 'Court's translation, restricted use';
  3. disclaimer_text verbatim;
  4. the binding attestation.
- scripts/ingest_sc_translations.py is disabled by default (a flag plus a refusal message pointing to the terms review). Lawyer uploads use the same disclaimer extraction and identity check as uploaded_copy.

proposal.why_incumbents_fail_and_this_wont:
Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI generate citations but don't stop an unchecked draft being exported. The Lacey sanctions involved CoCounsel/Westlaw output, and Gauthier shows an AI checker missing fabricated cases. SCC Online, Manupatra and Indian Kanoon find judgments but don't check a draft, and are English-only.

Quote checkers fail in one of four ways:
- Whole-string comparison flags every elided quote.
- Fuzzy matching passes a quote whose last clause turned 'shall' into 'may'.
- Exact matching on raw PDF text flags every correct quote that crosses a page break. Lawyers learn to ignore red, and the gate becomes busywork.
- Treating a court's vernacular translation as quotable authority contradicts the Court's own disclaimer.

Ours works differently:
- Layout artefacts are removed by recorded, reversible rules before exact word matching.
- Token splits and merges are equal only when the letters are identical.
- Anything the cleaner can't explain goes to amber with the page image, never red and never into the pleading.
- Translations are reading aids tied to the English paragraph, which is the text the bench is shown.
- Green still means only one thing: the court's exact words in its authoritative English text, checked by code.
acceptance_tests: Page break with a running header: a 30-word quote from fixture 2019 INSC 512 that runs from the foot of p. 6 to the top of p. 7, where pypdf output has 'SUPREME COURT REPORTS [2019] 5 S.C.R.' and '412' between, gives verified. layout_notes lists the skipped header and page number, and offset_map points to pages 6 and 7

Hyphenated line end: a quote containing 'discretion', where the fixture text has 'discre-\ntion', gives verified with a join_equivalence note. A quote containing 'self-incrimination', where the fixture has 'self-\nincrimination' and the hyphenated form occurs elsewhere, also gives verified

Footnote marker: a quote '... the right to personal liberty is ...' against fixture text 'personal liberty12 is' with footnote 12 on the same page gives verified. A quote copied from footnote 12 itself verifies against the footnotes stream, and running text never crosses into the footnote body
Superscript marker: 'liberty¹²' in the judgment and 'liberty' in the quote gives verified

Unrecognised layout: a fixture with a one-off header line, not recurring and matching no pattern, inside the quoted span gives quote_layout_soft (amber), never quote_differs. in_app clears it, and the page-image endpoint returns the rendered p. 7
A polarity change still bites at a page break: the same cross-page quote with 'not' removed at the page join gives quote_differs (hard) with the polarity flag, not layout soft

A body change is still hard: changing 'shall' to 'may' in mid-page text, outside any layout zone, of a cleaned fixture gives quote_differs (hard). The round-5 tail-change and added-'not' tests are unchanged
Join equivalence can't change a word: 'discre tion' against 'discretion' passes, while 'discrete ion' against 'discretion' (different letters) gives differs

Clean insertion: use_court_words on a cross-page candidate inserts text that contains no artefact string ('SUPREME COURT REPORTS', '412', '12' as a marker) and contains 'discretion', not 'discre tion'. A candidate spanning an unresolved artefact has insertable=false, and the route returns 409

Cleaner determinism: the same PDF bytes give a byte-identical CleanText 100 times. A CLEANER_VERSION bump invalidates carry-forward for rows bound to that judgment and nothing else. Mapping every clean span back through offset_map reproduces the original substrings
layout_uncertain: a fixture with dense unclassified edge lines sets text_quality to 'layout_uncertain', and no row bound to it can be hard

Official translation is restricted: a Hindi quote matching the fixture judgment_translations row word for word gives official_translation_restricted (amber), and filing_ready is false. After english_binding_confirmed for para 14 alone it is still false. After add_english_original (the English para 14 inserted and checked exact by code) or translation_by_counsel naming para 14, it becomes true. external_source returns 422

The record prints the disclaimer and the English text: for that row the record PDF contains English para 14 in full, the label 'Court's translation, restricted use', and disclaimer_text byte-equal to the fixture's disclaimer block. It never contains the word 'Verified' on that row
No disclaimer, no use: a fixture translation without a disclaimer block is stored with usable=false, and a matching Hindi quote falls back to quote_translation_soft
Translation ingestion is off: ingest_sc_translations.py without INGEST_SC_TRANSLATIONS=true exits non-zero and writes nothing
Para mismatch: when the translation and the English judgment have different para counts, no English binding is proposed automatically, and the lawyer must pick the para

Round-5 tests still pass: the Hindi translation_by_counsel test, romanised Hindi, mixed quote, bracket_hides_polarity, elision_polarity, negation-flip correction with partner approval, make_paraphrase, and normalize_words keeping Devanagari vowel signs. The evidence_service._normalize output is byte-identical on the contradiction fixtures

Round-3 and round-4 tests still pass: the elided, '* * *', bracket and emphasis-marker tests, the checksum tamper test, the 500-quote property test, the same-name trap, ambiguous_match, rebind, upload identity 422, s. 124B IPC invalid, 40-citation carry-forward, byte-identical record PDFs and RLS isolation
proposal.safeguards:
A lawyer is always the last step:
- Green comes only from an exact word match by code against the cleaned authoritative English text, and every cleaning step is listed in the record and traceable to the original page.
- An unexplained layout difference is amber, with the original page image shown, never red and never inserted into a pleading.
- Every automatic correction or form change needs the signing lawyer to read the inserted words, and junior drafts then also need partner approval.

Translations:
- Court translations are used only as restricted-use reading aids, never labelled verified, and always printed below the English paragraph with the Court's disclaimer verbatim.
- Ingesting them stays off until a terms review.
- Counsel's own translation is attested and printed beside the English text.

Rules and records:
- All rules (layout patterns, the lexicon, polarity words, spelling equivalents, editorial markers, disclaimer markers) are checksummed, lawyer-signed data, never an LLM.
- The record never says 'guaranteed accurate'.
- Every attestation, correction, paraphrase, English insertion and filing export is audit-logged.

Data handling:
- The working copy is never blocked.
- Only citation strings go to Indian Kanoon.
- Any LLM hint uses masked text (invariant 1).
- Uploaded copies and translations stay org-scoped, with no service-role use in user paths (invariant 2).
proposal.answers_to_objections:
Objection 1 (exact matching on uncleaned corpus text gives false hard blocks):

(a) Clean the judgment side, deterministically, with offsets kept. I confirmed the gap: scripts/ingest_sc_judgments.py's pdf_text() just joins pypdf page text with '\n', with no cleaning. The new app/services/judgment_text.py, shared with P12:
- keeps pages;
- removes running headers and footers, detected by digit-masked recurrence at page edges on at least 30% of pages, plus fixed checksummed patterns for S.C.R./INSC/page-number/REPORTABLE lines;
- moves footnote bodies to a separate stream;
- strips glued footnote markers only when footnote n exists on that page (superscripts always);
- joins line-end hyphens, resolved against the same judgment and a bundled lexicon, with ambiguous joins accepted both ways.
Every removal is an artefact with page and original offset. The offset_map maps clean text back to the PDF page, and the record lists what was joined or skipped.

(b) Token splits and merges, and downgrade instead of block:
- match_fragment treats 1-3 token runs as equal when their letter concatenations are identical ('discre tion' = 'discretion'), recorded as join_equivalence.
- A match that spans an unresolved artefact is 'exact_layout'.
- A diff whose every change sits in a layout zone, with no polarity change, becomes quote_layout_soft (amber, in_app with the page image), never quote_differs.
- Hard red now needs a change outside layout zones or any polarity change.
- A judgment whose layout is too noisy gets text_quality layout_uncertain, which removes hard statuses entirely.

(c) Insertion uses clean text only:
- closest_passages and use_court_words render from clean_text with resolved hyphen joins.
- A candidate spanning an unresolved artefact is not insertable.
- A post-insert assertion refuses any insertion that would contain an artefact string.

Fixtures: a page break with a running header and page number, a hyphenated line end (both resolution cases), a glued footnote marker and a superscript marker each give verified. An unrecognised header gives layout soft, not hard. A removed 'not' at a page break is still hard.

Objection 2 (the official-translation match was green although the Court restricts its use): the green status is gone.
- A word-for-word match with a held translation is now official_translation_restricted (amber), 'Matches the Court's translation (restricted use)'.
- It is filing-ready only after the lawyer confirms the paragraph-aligned English original. The para is proposed by mirrored numbering and confirmed only when para counts agree, otherwise picked.
- Then either 'Add the English original to the draft' is used (the English para is inserted and must check exact by code, so the bench has the authentic text), or translation_by_counsel is recorded naming that para.
- The record prints the English para in full first, then the translation labelled 'Court's translation, restricted use', then the Court's disclaimer byte-for-byte. The disclaimer is taken from the translation document itself (NOT NULL; a translation without a captured disclaimer is unusable).

I also accept the reading that ingestion 'where its terms allow' could ingest nothing. ingest_sc_translations.py now ships disabled pending a terms review, and until then only lawyer-uploaded translations, labelled lawyer-supplied, are used.

Test: a Hindi quote matching the fixture official translation is not filing-ready after only the binding confirmation. It is filing-ready after add_english_original or translation_by_counsel. The record contains the English para, the disclaimer verbatim and no 'Verified' label on that row.

objections: The 'I adopt this as my translation of para 14' exit for official_translation_restricted lets the Supreme Court's restricted-use vernacular translation reach a court inside a pleading, attested as counsel's own translation. The status only arises when the Hindi quote matches the Court's translation word for word, so the attestation is false on its face. It is also exactly the 'other purpose' that the Court's disclaimer prohibits. The internal record prints the disclaimer, but the filed pleading carries only the Hindi text, which is attributed to counsel. Fix I would accept: for official_translation_restricted, make add_english_original (the authentic English para inserted and checked exact by code) the only exit that makes the row filing-ready. Offer translation_by_counsel only after the lawyer has replaced the Hindi with their own rendering, which then no longer matches the Court's translation verbatim and falls to quote_translation_soft, or in addition to the English insertion and never instead of it. Add a test: a verbatim match plus translation_by_counsel alone gives filing_ready false.

Join equivalence is not 'can't change a word', so green no longer means 'the court's exact words'. As specified, any run of 1-3 tokens anywhere in the span counts as equal when the letters concatenate to the same string. The proposal's own 'cannot' / 'can not' example is one case, and others are 'may be' / 'maybe', 'any one' / 'anyone', 'every one' / 'everyone', 'a part' / 'apart', 'in to' / 'into' and 'some times' / 'sometimes'. These are different words with different meanings in legal text ('any one of the accused' vs 'anyone of the accused'). Yet a mid-page quote that swaps them, nowhere near a line break, would be 'Verified word for word'. Fix I would accept: allow join equivalence only where the judgment-side token boundary falls in a layout zone (a line end, a page join, or a recorded hyphen or soft-hyphen join). Anywhere else, a split or merge is a non-equal opcode outside the layout zones. It is hard red, or amber at most if the pair is listed in a checksummed, lawyer-signed compound list such as 'cannot' / 'can not'. Also add tests: 'may be' against mid-page 'maybe' is not green, while 'discre tion' against 'discre-\ntion' is green.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

A cheap, India-specific pre-filing check that knows Indian reporters (SCC, AIR, SCR, INSC, SCC OnLine, HC neutral citations) and checks transition-era code citations correctly. Red 'wrong code' is reserved for the matter's own charge, stated under a code that is wrong for the offence date. The cause title and prayer count as the matter's own charge even though they name the matter as 'State v. X'. Precedent discussion, dual 'IPC (now BNS)' citations and descriptions of what an FIR says never go red. The output is a per-citation due-diligence record the advocate can keep or show a bench. The target users are solos and district-court advocates without SCC or Manupatra.

### What it can't fix

We can't confirm an SCC or AIR page number, because they are proprietary with no open concordance. We say 'reporter page not checked; parties and year match <judgment>'.

Which procedural code governs a straddling matter is law to be argued (s.531 BNSS, s.170 BSA, divergent High Court views). We show it as a note; we don't decide it.

Cause-title and prayer detection uses headings and phrases. A pleading with no recognisable headings and no parties recorded on the matter falls back to phrase-only detection, and the record says 'own parties not identified; add them on the matter panel'.

Unusual drafting may be missed. It then gets an info note, never a false red.

The BCI's AI norms are still being framed, so the record is a diligence aid, not a certified compliance instrument. Judgments in no open index stay unverified until they are uploaded or attested (P02).

### What the user sees

'Check before filing' on /verify, plus the lawyer-side 'check this PDF' command on the firm's WhatsApp number. The ledger is plain English: green, amber and red as before.

The matter panel holds:
- the offence date (and an end date for continuing offences);
- the date the proceeding began, and its kind;
- charge or FIR sections;
- new: 'Parties in this matter' (for example State / Ramesh Kumar), prefilled from court_cases or detected from the document's cause title and confirmed by the lawyer.

The document view shades the parts the checker treated as the cause title and the prayer, so the lawyer can see why a section went red. A section mention in the cause title such as 'State v. Ramesh Kumar … u/s 302 IPC', in a 2024-offence matter, shows red: 'The cause title states the offence as s. 302 IPC, but the offence date is 3 Sept 2024: the offence provision is s. 103(1) BNS'.

The other labels are unchanged: precedent info, dual info or amber, FIR-description amber, procedural amber. A precedent that happens to share the client's name, but carries its own reporter citation, is labelled as a precedent. The record downloads with Hindi or English fixed labels.

### What the system does

1-3. Same engine (/citations/audits); deterministic reporters; migration 014 adds offence_date, offence_end_date, proceeding_instituted_on, proceeding_kind and charge_sections. NEW: it also adds own_parties jsonb ({side_a:[names], side_b:[names], source: court_case|manual|cause_title_confirmed}) to case_threads, with court_cases' petitioner and respondent used as the default. /verify accepts the same fields.

NEW 4a. segment_document(text) -> Structure is a pure function. Markers live in charge_phrases.yaml (checksummed). It finds:
- title_blocks: from the document start, and every later repeat (index pages, annexure covers), until the first body-start marker. The markers are 'MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH', 'RESPECTFULLY SHEWETH', 'The humble application of', 'The applicant above-named', 'SYNOPSIS', 'INDEX', 'BRIEF FACTS', 'सविनय निवेदन है' or the first numbered paragraph. A repeat is recognised by a 'versus|v.|vs.|बनाम' line whose parties match own_parties.
- prayer_blocks: from 'PRAYER', 'प्रार्थना', 'It is therefore most respectfully prayed' or 'It is, therefore, prayed' until 'PLACE', 'DATE', 'Through', 'Advocate for', 'VERIFICATION', 'सत्यापन' or the end of the document.

NEW 4b. own_case(case_name_span, matter, structure) is a pure function. The parties are own_parties, or, if none is recorded, the parties parsed from the first title block's versus line (shown for confirmation). Names are normalised with P12's party_names classification, so generic litigants such as State, Union of India or the Government are ignored for matching. A span counts as the own case when its non-generic party tokens contain the own non-generic party (a full name, or a 2-token sub-name), AND the clause attaches no reporter or neutral citation, year bracket or 'reported in' to it. 'State v. Ramesh Kumar (2019) 3 SCC 100' is therefore a precedent even when our client is also a Ramesh Kumar.

NEW 4c. citation_role(mention, sentence, structure, matter) uses a new precedence order:
1. Position first. If the mention is inside a title_block or prayer_block:
   (i) the clause contains a foreign case reference (a case citation span, or a v.-name that is not own_case) -> precedent_context;
   (ii) a dual pattern -> dual;
   (iii) an 'FIR No.', 'Crime No.', 'Case Crime No.' or 'प्राथमिकी सं.' token on the same line or clause -> fir_description;
   (iv) otherwise -> charge_assertion.
2. Elsewhere, precedent_context. Own-case names are excluded from the v.-name marker. Forum self-references are excluded from 'the Court' markers: 'this Court', 'this Hon'ble Court', 'the Hon'ble Court below', 'the learned Trial Court' in a present or future-tense request ('may be pleased', 'pray'). The verb markers ('held', 'observed', 'it was laid down', 'in that case') still apply.
3. Then dual, then fir_description.
4. charge_assertion by charging phrase, or by a section recorded in matter.charge_sections.
5. other.

5. Transition rules (app/data/transition_rules.yaml, checksummed, lawyer-signed) and code_status are unchanged:
- substantive sections are keyed on offence_date: red only for charge_assertion in the wrong code; amber for a span over 1 July 2024, for fir_code_note and for a dual mismatch; info for precedent and other;
- procedure and evidence are never red, with the s.531 and s.170 notes;
- the s.479 BNSS exception;
- a recorded charge_sections data-entry check.

6. Only red wrong_code_for_date blocks the P02 filing copy, until edited or attested with a reason (for example, the charge sheet genuinely uses that code).

7. Catch-all format_unrecognised; bare case names resolved by name.

8. Metering through P19; Indian Kanoon spend through the P29 budget.

### Where it is built

Extend:
- app/services/citation_service.py (_CASE_PATTERNS, catch-all, case-citation spans reused by citation_role and own_case, the code_status hook)
- app/services/jurisdiction_service.py (P22 correspondence)
- migrations 005 case_threads and 011 court_cases (014 adds the date fields, charge_sections and own_parties)
- app/services/whatsapp_intake.py
- app/services/ocr_service.py and document_service.py (FIR 'u/s' extraction for confirmation)
- the P12 party_names classification (generic_litigant / common_name / distinctive, shared with P36's leak check)
- the P02 record PDF

New:
- app/services/document_structure.py (segment_document; shared with P18's own-cause-title exclusion)
- app/services/citation_role.py (own_case, citation_role)
- app/data/charge_phrases.yaml (charging phrases, title and prayer markers, forum self-references, in English and Hindi)
- app/services/transition_rules.py and app/data/transition_rules.yaml
- tests/fixtures/transition/ golden pleadings (bail application, discharge application, quashing petition) in English and Hindi

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey and CoCounsel are grounded in US/UK law. SCC Online, Manupatra and CaseMine search their own databases but don't audit a draft written elsewhere or produce a per-citation record, and district advocates often don't subscribe. Free ChatGPT verifies nothing and routinely mixes IPC and BNSS.

A naive 'IPC after July 2024 = error' rule floods every criminal draft with false reds. A naive 'any v. name = precedent' rule misses the most important place a wrong code appears: the pleading's own cause title and prayer.

We read the document's structure first. We know which parties are ours, from the matter record or the confirmed cause title. So 'State v. Ramesh Kumar … u/s 302 IPC' in our own title is our charge, and 'Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab … s. 302 IPC' is a precedent. A record shown to a bench neither calls a correct precedent wrong nor misses a wrong charge. Checks run on open SC/HC data plus pay-per-call Indian Kanoon, so they cost paise per citation.

### Safeguards

Labels state exactly what was checked; an SCC or AIR page is never marked verified. Red is reserved for code-provable errors: a nonexistent section, or the matter's own charge (cause title, prayer, charging phrase or recorded charge) under the wrong code for the offence date. Precedent, dual and FIR-description mentions can't be red, by a tested precedence order. Own parties come from the matter record or are confirmed by the lawyer. The structure shading shows the lawyer what was treated as the title and prayer. Contested transitional questions are amber or info and never block. The rules and phrase files are lawyer-signed and checksummed. FIR extraction is lawyer-confirmed. Only citation strings leave the server for Indian Kanoon. Advocates keep responsibility for the filing (BCI duties of competence and candour). No scraping of SCC Online or Manupatra.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection: the cause-title rule could never fire, because any 'v.' name made a mention precedent_context first.

Fixed in three parts:
(1) A deterministic segment_document finds title blocks (including repeats) and prayer blocks from checksummed English and Hindi markers. Position is evaluated before precedent_context. Inside the title or prayer, a mention is charge_assertion unless the clause cites a different case (foreign case, giving precedent), is a dual form, or describes an FIR by number.
(2) own_case() identifies the document's own parties, from own_parties on the matter (defaulting to court_cases' parties) or from the first title block's versus line once the lawyer confirms it. It matches them with P12's party_names classification (generic litigants ignored) and excludes that case name from the v.-name precedent marker, the same exclusion P18 uses for an order's own cause title. A same-named case carrying a reporter citation is still a precedent.
(3) Forum self-references ('this Hon'ble Court may be pleased') no longer count as precedent markers.

Tests added exactly as requested: the cause title 'State v. Ramesh Kumar … u/s 302 IPC' is red; the prayer 'in State v. Ramesh Kumar, the applicant charged under s. 302 IPC' is red; 'In Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab … s. 302 IPC' stays info. Also added: the same-name precedent with a citation, an FIR number in the title, and the Hindi title.

### Acceptance tests

- Cause title: offence_date 2024-09-03, own_parties State / Ramesh Kumar, and a document starting 'IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE … State v. Ramesh Kumar … u/s 302 IPC … MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH' give red wrong_code_for_date suggesting s. 103(1) BNS
- Prayer naming the matter: 'PRAYER … in State v. Ramesh Kumar, the applicant charged under s. 302 IPC may be released on bail' gives red
- Cause title with no own_parties recorded: parties are detected from the versus line and shown for confirmation; the same cause-title mention is red
- Precedent stays info: 'In Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, the Court, considering s. 302 IPC, held…' in the body gives precedent_context info
- Precedent inside the prayer: 'following Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, s. 302 IPC' inside the prayer gives precedent_context (foreign case), not red
- Same-name precedent: own party Ramesh Kumar, body text 'In State v. Ramesh Kumar (2019) 3 SCC 100, s. 302 IPC was considered' gives precedent_context, because a reporter citation is attached
- Forum self-reference: 'this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to release the applicant charged under s. 302 IPC' in a body paragraph is charge_assertion (red), not precedent
- FIR in cause title: 'FIR No. 123/2024, u/s 420 IPC, P.S. Saket' in the title block of a 2024-offence matter gives amber fir_code_note, not red

- Repeated cause title on an index page and an annexure cover: each title-block mention is evaluated, with one red per mention and no duplicates in the counter
- Correct code: a cause title 'State v. Ramesh Kumar … u/s 103(1) BNS' in a 2024-offence matter gives no flag

- Round-3 tests still pass: precedent info; dual info or amber; charge phrase inside a precedent is info; FIR description amber; recorded charge red; zero reds for the 30-page bail application with 25 IPC precedents; reverse direction (2023 offence, s. 103 BNS) red; straddling golden cases; continuing offence amber; amber and info don't block; checksum refusal; format_unrecognised; incident strings flagged; Hindi labels not passed through an LLM; Indian Kanoon budget
- charge_phrases.yaml with altered title, prayer or forum markers fails its checksum at load

### Reviewers' minor notes

- When police or the court have registered a post-July-2024 matter under IPC, the cause title has to match the court record, so the red flag will be correct but must be attested every time. Make 'title reproduces the court's registration' a preset attestation reason so this costs one click.
- Body-start markers should also include 'LIST OF DATES' and 'MEMO OF PARTIES' used in SLPs and High Court petitions. Otherwise the title block can run on into the synopsis.
- Migration number 014 is also claimed by P02, P36 and P08.
- The shading of the parts treated as title and prayer is essential. Also show it in the downloaded record, so a bench sees why a mention went red.
- Standard Delhi and UP cause titles put the FIR details on separate lines ('FIR No. 123/2024' / 'P.S. Saket' / 'U/s 302 IPC'). Rule (iii) only looks for an FIR token on the same line or clause, so a correctly reproduced FIR section would go red. Treat a contiguous FIR/PS/U/s field group in the title block as one clause, and add that fixture. Red stays attestable, but the 'never a false red' claim should match what is built.
- Where police registered a 2024 FIR under the IPC, the red message should say the pleading reproduces the FIR, not only that the provision is wrong, so the record shown to a bench reads fairly.
- Indian cause titles usually carry the FIR number on the same line as the sections ('FIR No. 123/2024 u/s 302/34 IPC, P.S. Saket'). Rule (iii) will therefore turn most cause-title mentions amber (fir_description), and red will mainly come from the prayer or a charging phrase. That is defensible, because it accurately describes what the FIR says, but the headline example will rarely fire in practice. Say so.
- own_case needs a full name or a 2-token sub-name, so single-token party names ('State v. Ramesh') fall through to precedent and info. That is a false negative, and safe.
- Migration 014 is also claimed by P02, P36 and P08. Coordinate the numbering.

We can't confirm an SCC or AIR page number, because they are proprietary with no open concordance. We say 'reporter page not checked; parties and year match <judgment>'.

Cause-title and prayer detection uses headings and phrases. A pleading with no recognisable headings and no parties recorded on the matter falls back to phrase-only detection, and the record says 'own parties not identified; add them on the matter panel'.

The BCI's AI norms are still being framed, so the record is a diligence aid, not a certified compliance instrument. Judgments in no open index stay unverified until they are uploaded or attested (P02).
