solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Spotting clashes the evening before instead of during the morning. That means a firm-wide view of each advocate's listings across courtrooms and complexes, with reach estimates that every logged call improves, keyed to the bench actually sitting. Real overlaps are kept apart from mornings where the data is thin. The system suggests a reassignment first, gives the proxy a brief, counts adjournments per party, and offers a client message only where the record supports one, worded so it never predicts the court's decision.

### What it can't fix

Out of scope: judges' board management, courts not reaching their lists, the shortage of judges and the culture of seeking dates. Reach estimates are statistics from our own appearance logs. Courts have not endorsed them and they are never put to the court as a ground. A clash is not a ground for adjournment (Order XVII Rule 1 proviso (b) CPC), and the product cannot make a court grant a pass-over. A pace model can't foresee a long part-heard matter, a judge rising early or out-of-turn mentions, so windows are ranges, not promises. In the first weeks most courtrooms have no data and the board says so (amber) instead of guessing. We can't stop a client travelling if the firm chooses not to message them. We can't know about a bench change before the cause list or roster is published.

### What the user sees

On the board (P05), each advocate's morning is a strip showing courtroom, bench ('Justice A / Justice A & Justice B'), item number and its position in the day's list ('item 8, 14th call'), the estimated reach window and travel time between complexes. A window reads 'usually reached 11:15-12:30 before this bench (pace from 34 calls at items 2-41, this roster)'. Thin data reads 'new bench since 14 Oct: not enough data (9 of 20)'. History carried from another courtroom reads 'carried from Justice A's earlier court, low confidence'. There are two clash states. A red OVERLAP appears only when both items have estimated windows and the padded windows overlap: 'Court 12 item 8 (11:15-12:30) and Court 31 item 5 (11:40-12:10) overlap; 25 min apart'. Red items get the fix list. An amber POSSIBLE CLASH, NO DATA appears when at least one courtroom lacks a window. It is shown once per advocate-morning ('2 courtrooms without reach data today'), not as a pair-by-pair alarm, and offers no reassignment unless the advocate ticks 'treat as clash' for that day or sets it as a standing preference. Items in the same courtroom never clash. Fixes come in a fixed order: (1) reassign to an available colleague who knows the matter; (2) only if nobody is free, a 'seek pass-over / keep back' note for the appearing counsel. The system never offers 'seek adjournment because counsel is engaged elsewhere'. Proxy brief, adjournment counter and client-message button are unchanged from the last round.

### What the system does

1. Positions (deterministic): for each courtroom and date the P05 parser gives the printed cause list in order, with each item's segment label (fresh / after notice / regular / supplementary / advance, normalised per court profile). An item's position P is its rank in the full printed order for that courtroom and day. Connected matters listed 'with' an item count as one call, and deleted or 'not to be taken up' items are skipped.
2. Sitting clock: court timings are data per complex (sitting start, lunch interval, rising time, e.g. Delhi HC 10:30, lunch 13:00-14:15). The day's sitting start is the junior's 'bench assembled' tap if logged, otherwise the profile time. Elapsed time is counted in sitting minutes, which exclude the lunch interval.
3. Observations: every 'called' tap (first call only; a pass-over and recall keeps the first) stores bench_key, roster_period_id, segment label, position P and elapsed sitting minutes E. Its pace is r = E / max(P, 3); the floor of 3 stops item-1 noise from dominating. Every tap at any item number therefore informs every item in that (bench, segment).
4. Weights (as last round): current roster period 1.0; the same bench in earlier periods 0.5^(periods back), labelled 'carried'; other benches 0; history of the same judge(s) from another courtroom is a labelled low-confidence hint with weight 0 toward the threshold. An unparsed header gives bench_key null and 'bench unknown'.
5. Estimator: for (bench_key, segment) with effective weight W >= 20, compute the weighted 25th and 75th percentiles of r. The weighted quantile q is the smallest r whose cumulative normalised weight, sorted ascending, is >= q; there is no interpolation, so the result is reproducible exactly. The window for a target item at position P is [start + q25 x max(P,3), start + q75 x max(P,3)] in sitting minutes, mapped back to clock time by adding the lunch interval where crossed, and capped at rising time ('may not be reached today' if the lower bound passes rising). When a segment has W < 20 but the bench's pooled segments have W >= 20, the pooled pace is used, labelled 'pooled across list types'. Otherwise the window is 'not enough data'. A firm that logs 3 calls a day in a courtroom crosses 20 in about a week.
6. Reach frequency (display only): from 'court rose at item K' taps, the share of current-roster sittings that reached position P ('reached in 7 of 9 sittings'). It is never used for clash colouring.
7. Clash classification (deterministic): for each advocate and date, take the pairs of items in different courtrooms. A pair is OVERLAP (red) iff both windows exist and [lo-travel, hi+travel] intersect, using the firm-maintained complex-to-complex travel matrix (same complex, different courtroom: a default of 5 minutes). It is POSSIBLE_NO_DATA (amber) iff either window is missing. Amber pairs are collapsed into one advocate-morning notice. Only red items, or amber ones where the advocate opted in, enter the resolution step.
8. Resolution order, in code (unchanged): reassignment candidates first, meaning colleagues free in the padded window (a colleague with an amber item at that time counts as free only if that item is in the same complex), of adequate seniority for the stage, enrolled in the roster, ranked by prior appearance in the matter. Only when the list is empty is the fixed pass-over note offered, never an adjournment request.
9. Proxy brief, adjournment counter and client-message gate are unchanged from round 2 (quote-verified AI summary of the last order; Order XVII Rule 1 / s.346 BNSS counts; message suppressed for an accused without an exemption, a presence direction or a summoned witness; reason taken from the record; lawyer's click; audit-logged). No AI anywhere in steps 1-8.

### Where it is built

P05's cause_list_items, the parser (extended to the bench header, segment labels and connected-matter grouping) and the board. app/services/ecourts_service.agenda. New app/services/schedule_service.py (positions, sitting clock, pace estimator, classification, resolution) and app/data/court_timings/*.json. Migration 016_cause_lists.sql adds judges, bench_rosters, appearance_logs (bench_key, roster_period_id, segment, position, elapsed_sitting_min, pace, tap_kind called/assembled/rose), complex_travel_times, advocate_clash_prefs, hearing_outcomes and attendance_exemptions. Also whatsapp_service.send_template with the migration 012 consent records, evidence_service.quote_found, audit_service and frontend/src/app/board/page.tsx.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Clio and US docketing tools assume one calendar per matter and US rules. eCourts and Indian trackers (eCourts app, eCourtsIndia API, LawStar-type diaries) work per case and per court. They don't show one advocate's clashes and don't know which bench is sitting. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI have no scheduling layer. Our estimate is a defined pace model per bench and list segment, which every call at any item number feeds, so it becomes useful within about a week. A roster change resets it. Thin data shows as one amber notice instead of a red alarm. Clashes are resolved by reassignment before anything reaches the court, and the client message is gated by the record, not by a prediction.

### Safeguards

Client messages need a lawyer's click and a reason taken from the record. They are suppressed for an accused without an exemption and wherever an order requires presence. They never predict the outcome, and they go only to the firm's existing clients with recorded consent, so there is no solicitation under BCI Rule 36. Nothing produced for the court seeks an adjournment because counsel has a clash. Proxies are assigned only to enrolled advocates in the roster. Order text is masked before AI, and the brief is internal work product. Reach statistics stay internal and are labelled with their observation count and roster period. Amber notices never generate work unless the advocate opts in.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection 1 (window undefined for the actual item; months to reach 20 per item; every two-courtroom morning red): (a) the estimate is no longer per item number. Each 'called' tap gives a pace r = elapsed sitting minutes / max(position, 3) for its (bench, segment), and the window for any item is the weighted q25-q75 pace times that item's position. Every call informs every item, so 20 observations per bench accrue in about a week at normal logging rates, with a pooled-segment fallback. (b) States are split. Red OVERLAP needs both windows estimated. Amber POSSIBLE CLASH, NO DATA is one notice per advocate-morning, offers no reassignment unless the advocate opts in, and same-courtroom items never clash. (c) test_cold_start_3_weeks seeds 10 advocates x 6 matters x 3 courtrooms from zero logs and asserts zero red and zero suggestions on day 1, red precision >= 0.8 by day 15, and at least 70% of mornings with no notice; test_amber_opt_in and test_same_courtroom_no_clash cover the rest. Objection 2 (estimator undefined as written; test doesn't say which N): the model is now fully specified. Position is the rank in the day's printed list, with connected matters counted once and deleted items skipped. Segment labels are kept separate. The clock is in sitting minutes excluding lunch. The pace floor is 3. The weighted quantile is defined as the first cumulative weight >= q with no interpolation. The projection is start + q x position, capped at rising. test_mixed_item_numbers compares the service against an independent reference implementation on calls at mixed positions, test_reach_window_positions recovers known generating quantiles, and test_connected_matters_one_call, test_lunch_excluded and test_position_floor pin down the definitions.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_schedule.py::test_mixed_item_numbers: 40 synthetic calls for one bench and segment at positions {2,3,5,7,12,19,25,33,41} with known elapsed times yield, for a target at position 8, a window equal to a separate reference implementation (tests/reference/weighted_quantile.py, written independently of the service: sort, cumulative weight, first >= q) to the minute.
- test_reach_window_positions: 100 calls spread over positions 1-60 with pace drawn from a known distribution give q25/q75 pace within 2% of the generating quantiles, and the window for position 30 is start + q x 30 in sitting minutes.
- test_position_floor: a call at item 1 after 4 minutes contributes pace 4/3, not 4.
- test_connected_matters_one_call: a list where item 8 is 'with 9-12' gives item 13 position 9, not 13.
- test_lunch_excluded: a projected window crossing 13:00 is shifted by the lunch interval; elapsed for a 14:30 call excludes 75 minutes.
- test_rising_cap: a position whose lower bound passes rising time reads 'may not be reached today' and is never red.
- test_pooled_fallback: a segment with W=8 on a bench with pooled W=30 uses the pooled pace and the 'pooled' label; pooled W=12 gives 'not enough data'.
- test_cold_start_3_weeks: seeded firm of 10 advocates, each with 6 matters in 3 courtrooms per sitting day over 15 sitting days, zero logs on day 1 and about 3 synthetic calls per courtroom per day after that. Day 1: zero red pairs, at most one amber notice per advocate-morning, zero reassignment suggestions. By day 15: every red pair is a true overlap in the synthetic ground truth with precision >= 0.8, and at least 70% of advocate-mornings have no notice at all.
- test_amber_opt_in: an amber morning yields reassignment suggestions only after the advocate's 'treat as clash' flag is set.
- test_same_courtroom_no_clash: two items for one advocate in the same courtroom never produce a clash state.
- test_clash_detection: two estimated windows in complexes 25 minutes apart that overlap after padding give red; non-overlapping ones give none; one estimated and one missing give amber.
- test_roster_change_resets_window, test_older_roster_downweighted (effective weight 10 + 0.5 x 30 = 25), test_unparsed_header: as in round 2, now asserted on pace observations.

proposal.solvable_part: Spotting clashes the evening before instead of during the morning. That means a firm-wide view of each advocate's listings across courtrooms and complexes, with reach estimates that every logged call improves, keyed to the bench actually sitting. Real overlaps are kept apart from mornings where the data is thin. The system suggests a reassignment first, gives the proxy a brief, counts adjournments per party, and offers a client message only where the record supports one, worded so it never predicts the court's decision.
proposal.out_of_scope: Out of scope: judges' board management, courts not reaching their lists, the shortage of judges and the culture of seeking dates. Reach estimates are statistics from our own appearance logs. Courts have not endorsed them and they are never put to the court as a ground. A clash is not a ground for adjournment (Order XVII Rule 1 proviso (b) CPC), and the product cannot make a court grant a pass-over. A pace model can't foresee a long part-heard matter, a judge rising early or out-of-turn mentions, so windows are ranges, not promises. In the first weeks most courtrooms have no data and the board says so (amber) instead of guessing. We can't stop a client travelling if the firm chooses not to message them. We can't know about a bench change before the cause list or roster is published.
proposal.what_the_user_sees: On the board (P05), each advocate's morning is a strip showing courtroom, bench ('Justice A / Justice A & Justice B'), item number and its position in the day's list ('item 8, 14th call'), the estimated reach window and travel time between complexes. A window reads 'usually reached 11:15-12:30 before this bench (pace from 34 calls at items 2-41, this roster)'. Thin data reads 'new bench since 14 Oct: not enough data (9 of 20)'. History carried from another courtroom reads 'carried from Justice A's earlier court, low confidence'. There are two clash states. A red OVERLAP appears only when both items have estimated windows and the padded windows overlap: 'Court 12 item 8 (11:15-12:30) and Court 31 item 5 (11:40-12:10) overlap; 25 min apart'. Red items get the fix list. An amber POSSIBLE CLASH, NO DATA appears when at least one courtroom lacks a window. It is shown once per advocate-morning ('2 courtrooms without reach data today'), not as a pair-by-pair alarm, and offers no reassignment unless the advocate ticks 'treat as clash' for that day or sets it as a standing preference. Items in the same courtroom never clash. Fixes come in a fixed order: (1) reassign to an available colleague who knows the matter; (2) only if nobody is free, a 'seek pass-over / keep back' note for the appearing counsel. The system never offers 'seek adjournment because counsel is engaged elsewhere'. Proxy brief, adjournment counter and client-message button are unchanged from the last round.
proposal.what_the_system_does:
1. Positions (deterministic): for each courtroom and date the P05 parser gives the printed cause list in order, with each item's segment label (fresh / after notice / regular / supplementary / advance, normalised per court profile). An item's position P is its rank in the full printed order for that courtroom and day. Connected matters listed 'with' an item count as one call, and deleted or 'not to be taken up' items are skipped.
2. Sitting clock: court timings are data per complex (sitting start, lunch interval, rising time, e.g. Delhi HC 10:30, lunch 13:00-14:15). The day's sitting start is the junior's 'bench assembled' tap if logged, otherwise the profile time. Elapsed time is counted in sitting minutes, which exclude the lunch interval.
3. Observations: every 'called' tap (first call only; a pass-over and recall keeps the first) stores bench_key, roster_period_id, segment label, position P and elapsed sitting minutes E. Its pace is r = E / max(P, 3); the floor of 3 stops item-1 noise from dominating. Every tap at any item number therefore informs every item in that (bench, segment).
4. Weights (as last round): current roster period 1.0; the same bench in earlier periods 0.5^(periods back), labelled 'carried'; other benches 0; history of the same judge(s) from another courtroom is a labelled low-confidence hint with weight 0 toward the threshold. An unparsed header gives bench_key null and 'bench unknown'.
5. Estimator: for (bench_key, segment) with effective weight W >= 20, compute the weighted 25th and 75th percentiles of r. The weighted quantile q is the smallest r whose cumulative normalised weight, sorted ascending, is >= q; there is no interpolation, so the result is reproducible exactly. The window for a target item at position P is [start + q25 x max(P,3), start + q75 x max(P,3)] in sitting minutes, mapped back to clock time by adding the lunch interval where crossed, and capped at rising time ('may not be reached today' if the lower bound passes rising). When a segment has W < 20 but the bench's pooled segments have W >= 20, the pooled pace is used, labelled 'pooled across list types'. Otherwise the window is 'not enough data'. A firm that logs 3 calls a day in a courtroom crosses 20 in about a week.
6. Reach frequency (display only): from 'court rose at item K' taps, the share of current-roster sittings that reached position P ('reached in 7 of 9 sittings'). It is never used for clash colouring.
7. Clash classification (deterministic): for each advocate and date, take the pairs of items in different courtrooms. A pair is OVERLAP (red) iff both windows exist and [lo-travel, hi+travel] intersect, using the firm-maintained complex-to-complex travel matrix (same complex, different courtroom: a default of 5 minutes). It is POSSIBLE_NO_DATA (amber) iff either window is missing. Amber pairs are collapsed into one advocate-morning notice. Only red items, or amber ones where the advocate opted in, enter the resolution step.
8. Resolution order, in code (unchanged): reassignment candidates first, meaning colleagues free in the padded window (a colleague with an amber item at that time counts as free only if that item is in the same complex), of adequate seniority for the stage, enrolled in the roster, ranked by prior appearance in the matter. Only when the list is empty is the fixed pass-over note offered, never an adjournment request.
9. Proxy brief, adjournment counter and client-message gate are unchanged from round 2 (quote-verified AI summary of the last order; Order XVII Rule 1 / s.346 BNSS counts; message suppressed for an accused without an exemption, a presence direction or a summoned witness; reason taken from the record; lawyer's click; audit-logged). No AI anywhere in steps 1-8.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Reconciling the firm's whole matter list every evening against that night's cause lists (daily, supplementary, advance) from every court the firm appears in, resolving court number and item number, catching matters listed under the firm's advocates that we don't track or that carry a misprinted number, warning when a past order hasn't been uploaded, assigning an appearing advocate and a fallback, and escalating until someone confirms appearance.

### What it can't fix

Courts publishing late or not at all, portal downtime, the one-day notice policy of a High Court, and whether a matter is reached. We never bypass eCourts captchas: where a list sits behind a captcha, a munshi downloads and forwards it and we parse it. Coverage is per court parser; unsupported courts fall back to the provider API or manual entry.

### What the user sees

Tonight's board (/board): for tomorrow, every listed firm matter grouped by court complex and courtroom, with item number, bench, list type (daily / supplementary-3 / advance), the appearing advocate and fallback, and a Confirm button. Unconfirmed items turn amber at 20:00 and red at 21:00. A 'Possibly ours' section shows list items naming a firm advocate that match no tracked matter, or match a tracked matter on parties but not number, for someone to claim or dismiss. Matter rows carry warnings: 'last hearing 14 Oct, order not uploaded yet', 'shown disposed with no judgment online: limitation is provisional'. Forwarding a cause-list PDF to the firm's email-in address or WhatsApp number adds it.

### What the system does

1. Sources: per-court fetchers for cause lists published as open PDFs/HTML (starting with Supreme Court, Delhi HC, Bombay HC and the courts our firm uses most); the eCourtsIndia provider where it offers cause lists; and forwarded PDFs. Fetchers poll from 17:00 to 10:00 IST every 30 minutes for supplementary lists, keyed by URL + content hash so a revised list replaces the old one.
2. Parsing is deterministic: pypdfium2 text extraction (OCR fallback via ocr_service for scans, with Tesseract only; no vision fallback for lists), then a per-court grammar (regex plus table layout) producing items {court no, bench, item no, list type, case type, number, year, parties, advocates}. Every parser ships with labelled fixture PDFs.
3. Matching: case-type alias table (e.g. 'W.P.(C)', 'WP(C)', 'Writ Petition (Civil)') and normalized number/year give exact matches; then a second pass matches parties plus advocate name (token similarity above threshold) as 'probable'; any item naming a firm advocate (roster with name variants and enrolment numbers) that is unmatched goes to 'Possibly ours'. Match type and reason are shown; only exact matches update next_hearing_date automatically, probable ones need a click.
4. Assignment: the matter's default advocate and fallback are pre-filled; the advocate confirms. Escalation via deadline_service (P13): unconfirmed at 20:00 goes to the fallback, at 21:00 to the partner, again at 07:30.
5. Order lag: when last_hearing_date passes and no order appears in provider_data or uploads within 3 days, a warning is raised; a 'disposed' status with no judgment marks any P06 limitation computation provisional and uses the safe date.
6. Each list ingested is stored (`cause_lists`, `cause_list_items`) with source URL and hash for audit.

### Where it is built

app/services/ecourts_service.py (provider, sync, agenda); app/services/ocr_service.py and document_service for PDF text; new app/services/causelist_service.py with app/services/causelists/<court>.py parsers; app/worker.py cron `task_fetch_cause_lists`; whatsapp_intake.py to accept forwarded PDFs from firm members' numbers; migration 016_cause_lists.sql (cause_lists, cause_list_items, listing_matches, advocate_aliases); frontend/src/app/board/page.tsx.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

The eCourts app, eCourtsIndia API, LawStar and India Case Status re-serve portal data by CNR and inherit its lag; they miss supplementary lists, items under a different counsel or a wrong number, and High Court board formats. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI have no Indian court data; SCC Online and Manupatra are research databases. We read the actual list PDFs the court publishes tonight, match the whole firm's roster deterministically, surface near-misses for a human, and escalate until someone confirms appearance.

### Safeguards

Public cause lists contain names of parties; stored under RLS per org (shared raw list storage is read-only and holds only public court data). No AI in parsing or matching. Forwarded PDFs are accepted only from registered firm members' numbers. Court terms of use respected: polite polling intervals, no captcha bypass. The fetch job is a server-side job scoped per org and must be added to invariant 2.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_causelists.py parser fixtures: at least 20 real public cause-list PDFs per supported court (including the Delhi HC supplementary list of 03.07.2026 and the SC chamber list of 12.02.2026 cited in the vault) with hand-labelled items; case-number field recall 100% and precision at least 99%; item numbers exact.
- test_alias_matching: seeded matters 'W.P.(C) 1234/2025' match list items written 'WP(C) 1234 of 2025' and 'W.P.(C.) 1234/2025' exactly; '1243/2025' with matching parties is 'probable', not exact.
- test_possibly_ours: an item naming a firm advocate's enrolment-name variant with no tracked matter appears under 'Possibly ours'.
- test_revised_list_replaces: a second PDF at the same URL with a different hash replaces items and re-notifies only changed matters.
- test_confirmation_escalation: freezegun at 20:00 and 21:00 shows escalation to fallback then partner for an unconfirmed item.
- test_order_lag_warning: last hearing 4 days ago, no order: warning raised; order uploaded: cleared.
- Captcha test: fetchers have no code path for captcha-protected URLs (static check that the eCourts services URL isn't in any fetcher).

### Reviewers' minor notes

- An exact match in an advance list is not a listing for tomorrow. Only daily and supplementary items should set next_hearing_date; advance items should be shown as 'expected'.
- Delhi HC and other supplementary lists often appear after 21:00. The amber/red escalation clock should run from when the list is ingested, not from a fixed time.
- Handle items marked 'deleted', 'not to be listed' and 'after notice' in the grammar, or they will create false listings.
- Forwarded PDFs from members arriving on the client intake number must be routed away from the client-intake AI path entirely, and never reach consent or intake flows.
- Record each court website's terms of use and robots policy in the fetcher config, and skip any court whose terms forbid automated access instead of only avoiding captchas.
- The incumbent section omits advocate-name cause-list alerts that already exist: court-run advocate-wise lists and alerts on several HC sites, and commercial trackers such as Provakil. 'They miss items under a different counsel' is partly untrue. Restate the differentiator as reconciling the whole firm's roster against tracked matters (alias and probable matches), the order-lag warnings and the confirmation escalation.
- Confirm per court that the chosen cause-list URLs aren't behind a captcha (district lists on eCourts are, so they're forward-only). The static check should cover every captcha host you know of, not just the eCourts services URL.
- 100% recall on case numbers across 20 PDFs per court is achievable only on those fixtures. Monitor parse failures in production (an items-per-page anomaly alert).

**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Computing a matter's limitation or statutory date correctly and showing how: the Schedule article or special-statute period, s.12 exclusions (day of judgment, time from copy application to copy ready, decree copy), s.4 (court closed on the last day), s.14 (bona fide proceedings in a wrong forum), the Supreme Court's COVID exclusion (15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022), and hard non-condonable outer limits (commercial written statement 120 days, s.34 Arbitration Act 3 months + 30 days). Also chasing the certified copy and telling the lawyer the date is provisional until the copy-ready date is known.

### What it can't fix

Whether a court will condone delay under s.5, whether a given free or ordinary copy counts as a certified copy (SBI v India Power is itself litigation), how slow a copying section is, and novel questions of which article applies. We cannot pull copy-section status from court systems that have no API; the copy-ready date is entered by the clerk.

### What the user sees

A Limitation calculator on each matter and at /workflows/limitation: pick the remedy (appeal, revision, SLP, s.34, written statement, etc.) and forum; enter date of judgment/service, copy applied, copy ready (notified), copy delivered, and any s.14 period. The result is a dated worked computation: start date, period, each exclusion line with its section and days, the COVID line if relevant, the s.4 shift with the holiday from the loaded court calendar, the final date, and a red line if the limit cannot be extended. If the copy-ready date is missing it shows two dates: 'if the copy is ready today' and 'without copy exclusion (safe date)', and the docket uses the safe date. A Copy tracker lists every pending certified-copy application with days since applied and a 'check the copy section' task every 3 working days.

### What the system does

1. New deterministic module app/services/limitation_service.py with a rule registry as data (app/data/limitation_rules.json): rule_id, remedy, forum, period (days or months), start event, which exclusions apply, whether s.5 applies or the statute excludes it (s.29(2)), outer limit, statutory source, status draft/verified, verified_by (two advocates). Only `verified` rules are offered; draft rules are invisible outside an admin view.
2. Computation follows the statute: day of the start event excluded (s.12(1)); for appeals/revisions/reviews the time from the copy application to the date the copy was ready is excluded (s.12(2)), but not time before applying and not if applied after the period expired; decree copy time likewise (s.12(3)). COVID: if the period would have expired between 15.03.2020 and 28.02.2022, the date becomes 90 days from 01.03.2022 or the balance if longer; otherwise the window is excluded. s.4: if the last day of the prescribed period is a day the court is closed (from `court_calendars`), it moves to the reopening day; s.4 is not applied to a condonable extension window (e.g. the 30 days under s.34(3)).
3. Conservatism rule, in code: when an input or calendar is missing, the engine uses the assumption that gives the earlier date and says so; it never shows a later date than the safe one.
4. `court_calendars` table (court, date, closed reason, source URL, entered_by, verified_by) loaded from each court's published annual calendar; a court with no loaded calendar gets no s.4 shift and a warning.
5. Results write deadlines (P13) with rule_id, version and inputs, so a rule correction re-computes every affected deadline and notifies its owner.
6. Every statutory reference in the basis text is run through citation_service (status must be `statute`).

### Where it is built

New app/services/limitation_service.py and app/data/limitation_rules.json; reuse add_months and Result.deadline from app/services/workflow_service.py and register a `limitation` Pack there; citation_service.py for basis checking; migration 014_deadlines.sql adds court_calendars and copy_applications (applied_on, ready_on, delivered_on, court, matter); frontend/src/app/workflows/page.tsx gets the calculator, cases page a Copy tracker tab.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Manupatra, SCC Online and LegitQuest retrieve judgments on limitation but compute nothing; the eCourts app and LawStar have no limitation model; Clio-style calendaring follows US rules; Harvey and CoCounsel will produce a plausible date in prose, which is exactly what must not be trusted. Ours is a rule table signed off by two advocates, computed in code, shown line by line, conservative when inputs are missing, and re-computed when a rule changes.

### Safeguards

Results are labelled 'computation for a lawyer to check', not advice; no AI is involved in the date. Rules activate only after two advocates sign off (recorded). Calendar entries carry their source URL. No client data leaves the server. Deadlines inherit P13's escalation.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_limitation.py golden table: tests/fixtures/limitation_cases.json with at least 60 worked examples prepared by our litigation team (and cross-checked by a second advocate), covering month-end and leap-year arithmetic, s.12(2) copy exclusion, copy applied after expiry (no exclusion), s.4 with a holiday on the last day, s.4 not applied to the s.34 grace window, COVID inside and outside the window, commercial WS day 120 vs day 121, ordinary WS 90 days; every example must match exactly.
- Property tests (hypothesis): the final date is never earlier than the unexcluded date when exclusions are valid; adding copy-ready days never moves the date by more than those days; a missing copy-ready date always yields the safe (earlier) date.
- test_unverified_rule_hidden: a rule with status draft cannot be evaluated through the API (422).
- test_rule_change_recomputes: bumping a rule's version re-computes linked deadlines and creates a notification for each owner.
- test_basis_citations: every basis string in the registry passes citation_service with status statute.
- test_calendar_missing_warns: a court with no calendar rows returns the unshifted date plus a warning.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- When s.4 shifts a date because the court is closed, the shift should be shown as a separate line. Where the shift is legally uncertain (special statutes reached through s.10 General Clauses Act, hard outer limits like the commercial WS day 120), the docket should keep the unshifted date as the safe date and treat the shift as informational.
- Ad hoc closures (sudden holidays, local declarations) are frequent. Let a clerk add a closure with its source mid-year, and re-compute the affected deadlines.
- The 60 golden cases depend on advocates who are not yet on the team. Name them and record their sign-off in the repo before the rules go live.
- Say whose advocates sign off the rule registry (the vendor's or each firm's). Let each firm see the sign-off and add a firm-level confirmation, so the vendor's rule table is not presented as advice to the firm.
- Apply s.4 Limitation Act and s.10 General Clauses Act only where the special statute allows them, and record which one applies in each rule (s.29(2)).
- The COVID exclusion lines matter little by 2026. Keep them, but show the SC order reference as a statute or judgment that passes citation_service, not as free text.
- The property test 'adding copy-ready days never moves the date by more than those days' is false once s.4 runs: one extra excluded day can land the date on a court holiday and shift it by several days. Assert it on the pre-s.4 date, or restate it as 'by at most those days plus the closure run'.
- The 60 golden examples need a named advocate and a second checker who actually exist. Record their sign-off in the repo as for P22's correspondence file.
- Say whether the COVID exclusion is applied to condonable outer limits (the SC order of 10.01.2022 covers them) and test it for s.34(3).

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Making sure every enquiry that reaches the firm's WhatsApp or phone gets a correct, safe reply within a minute at any hour. The reply says when a lawyer will respond, computed from the firm's hours. The system turns the conversation into a structured brief, computes in code any statutory clock that may be running (s.138 notice/complaint windows, default-bail days) from the dates the person gave, wakes the lawyer only for real emergencies, and lets the lawyer accept, decline or refer in one tap. It also measures first-response time.

### What it can't fix

Enquiries sent to a lawyer's personal number or Instagram DMs never reach us. We won't scrape personal WhatsApp, and Instagram auto-replies risk breaching Rule 36. We can't make a lawyer actually take the matter, or take on more than they can handle. Proactive outreach to leads (ads, cold follow-ups) is out by design under Rule 36. Whether the person stays with the firm depends on the human follow-up.

### What the user sees

Prospect, 9:40 pm on WhatsApp: the existing consent prompt, then intake questions in their language (voice notes work), then a fixed acknowledgement: 'Thank you. The firm's lawyers work Mon-Sat 10am-7pm. A lawyer will reply by 11:00 am tomorrow (Sat 26 Oct).' If the person mentions an arrest or detention (detected by keywords in code, including Hindi and Hinglish: arrest, giraftar, गिरफ्तार, police station, custody), a fixed firm-approved message says a lawyer has been alerted now, and gives the NALSA helpline 15100 as a factual fallback. Lawyer: an 'Intake briefs' list in /inbox. Each brief card shows matter type, parties, key dates (each with the client's own quote as proof), urgency computed in code ('s.138: the 30-day notice window from the bank memo dated 3 Oct closes on 2 Nov, 8 days left'), a conflict-check result (from the P46 service), the language, the channel and time waiting. The buttons are Accept (opens a case thread with the brief and asks consent for AI processing), Decline (sends a fixed polite decline in the client's language with legal-aid/DLSA pointers) and Refer (to a named colleague in the org). A small 'first-response time' tile shows the median this week.

### What the system does

1) `org_settings` (migration 014): working hours, timezone IST, court holiday list, SLA hours, emergency alert numbers (lawyers' own phones, opted in). 2) `intake_hours.next_reply_by(now, settings) -> datetime` is pure code. The acknowledgement is a fixed template filled with that time, sent by the system sender. This avoids the AI entirely and passes intake_guard because it carries no legal substance. 3) Intake stays as it is in whatsapp_intake (consent first, masked, intake_guard on every AI reply). When the conversation goes quiet for 10 minutes, or the client says they're done, `intake_brief.build` runs one Haiku extraction over the masked history into a fixed JSON schema: matter_type from a closed enum matching workflow packs and practice areas, parties, events [{label, date, quote}], client_language and asks. 4) Verification in code: each event date must parse, and its quote must pass evidence_service.quote_found against the unmasked client messages; failures are dropped and counted, as in invariant 6. 5) Triage in code: if matter_type is cheque_bounce and a 'bank return memo received' date is verified, call workflow_service.evaluate('cheque_bounce', …) and put its deadlines and flags on the brief. The same goes for bail/default bail (arrest date, offence) and consumer packs. With no verified date the brief says 'date needed' and no deadline is shown. 6) Emergency: `intake_triage.is_emergency(text)` uses a regex list over the raw inbound text (the same list as the phone intake). If it matches, the lawyer gets an alert at once through the WhatsApp template `lawyer_alert` to the lawyer's own opted-in number, with no client PII beyond the first name and conversation link, regardless of hours. 7) Conflict check: party names from the brief go to the P46 conflict service. Until that exists, a fallback compares normalized names with court_cases.petitioners/respondents and case_threads in the org and shows possible matches, never auto-declining. 8) Accept/Decline/Refer are audited endpoints. Decline and refer send fixed templates. Accept creates a case_thread with ai_consent fields filled from the WhatsApp consent. 9) Metrics: a Prometheus histogram `intake_first_response_seconds{channel, by=system|lawyer}` and the /inbox tile computed from whatsapp_messages timestamps. 10) Phone: the Twilio after-hours flow reuses telephony_session. At call end the same brief builder runs on the masked transcript.

### Where it is built

Extend app/services/whatsapp_intake.py (acknowledgement after consent and on each quiet period; emergency branch; brief trigger), app/services/intake_guard.py (unchanged checks; HOLDING_MESSAGE gains the computed reply-by line), app/services/telephony_session.py (brief at call end), app/services/workflow_service.py (reused as-is for triage), app/services/evidence_service.py quote_found (reused), app/core/metrics.py (new histogram), app/routers/whatsapp.py (brief accept/decline/refer). New: app/services/intake_hours.py, app/services/intake_brief.py, app/services/intake_triage.py, migration 014 (org_settings, intake_briefs table: conversation_id, brief jsonb, verified counts, triage jsonb, decision, decided_by/at), app/data/intake_templates/{en,hi,...}.json, frontend/src/app/inbox/page.tsx (Briefs list and response-time tile).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI do no intake. Clio Grow, Lawmatics and US intake bots work through web forms and email in English, with no WhatsApp Business, no Hindi or Hinglish voice notes, no consent before AI processing, and canned replies that drift into advice. None computes Indian statutory clocks. Answering services take messages but don't triage. Our intake already exists with consent first, PII masking and intake_guard. This adds a reply-by time that is always correct (code, not model), a brief whose dates are proven by the client's own words, and deadlines from the same deterministic workflow_service the lawyer already uses. So the urgent s.138 or default-bail matter is at the top at 10 am, not lost in a phone.

### Safeguards

Rule 36: replies only to people who wrote or called first; no follow-up marketing and no outbound to leads who went silent; decline and refer texts are factual. UPL: the AI only asks questions (intake_guard). Deadlines, acknowledgement times and emergency messages are code and fixed templates; deadlines go to the lawyer, not to the prospect, unless the lawyer sends them. DPDP: the existing YES consent before anything reaches the AI; brief retention follows the conversation; a declined prospect's data goes to the 30-day trash and is then erased (tombstone). PII masking before extraction. Public intake stays off until enabled through maker-checker (migration 013). Lawyer alerts carry minimal client data. Invariant 2: the WhatsApp webhook is an existing listed server job; accept/decline endpoints use RLS.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_intake_hours.py: Fri 21:40 IST with hours Mon-Sat 10-19 -> reply_by Sat 11:00 (10:00 plus 1h SLA); Sat 18:50 -> Mon 11:00; a court holiday on Mon -> Tue 11:00.
- test_ack_passes_intake_guard: each rendered acknowledgement template in each language -> intake_guard.check_reply-style substance check finds no legal substance (dates are allowed in the system template; the test documents that the template is system, not AI).
- test_brief_dates_verified: a mocked extraction returns events [{date: 2026-10-03, quote: 'bank ne 3 October ko memo diya'}] and [{date: 2026-09-01, quote: 'invented quote'}] -> the first is kept, the second dropped, discarded_unverified=1.
- test_triage_s138: a verified memo date of 2026-10-03 with today 2026-10-25 -> the brief has the deadline 'demand notice by 2026-11-02' with its basis string, equal to workflow_service.evaluate output.
- test_triage_no_date: matter_type cheque_bounce without a verified memo date -> triage shows 'date needed' and no deadline.
- test_emergency_keywords: 'mere bhai ko police ne giraftar kar liya' and 'गिरफ्तार' -> is_emergency True; 'my arrest of payment' fixture -> documented behaviour; the alert is sent to the lawyer number (mocked) within the same handle() call at 23:00.
- test_decline_template: decline sends the fixed hi/en template and contains no section, amount or prediction (intake_guard regexes).
- test_conflict_fallback: a brief party 'Ramesh Kumar Gupta' and an existing respondent 'R. K. Gupta' -> a 'possible match' is shown and the brief is not auto-declined.
- test_brief_pii: the extraction prompt receives masked text only (assert no phone number or Aadhaar from the fixture in the mocked Anthropic call).
- test_metrics: a sequence of messages -> intake_first_response_seconds observed with by=system < 60 in the simulated clock.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- When the decline is sent after the system has computed a running statutory clock, the template should add a neutral line, 'time limits may apply to your matter; please consult a lawyer promptly'. This is standard non-engagement practice and not advice.
- The emergency keyword list needs a documented false-positive policy (e.g. 'arrest' in 'arrears'). A lawyer woken at 23:00 too often will mute it.
- Send the emergency 'a lawyer has been alerted' text only when an opted-in alert number is configured and the send succeeded. Otherwise send the NALSA 15100 fallback without that claim.
- The declined-prospect tombstone should keep the names and matter type needed for later conflict checks (a prospect who disclosed facts can create a conflict). State this retention in the consent notice.
- The extraction model sees masked text, so its quotes may contain placeholders (<PHONE_1>). Verifying them with quote_found against the unmasked messages will drop valid events. Verify against the masked history (or unmask the quote via the session's PiiMasker first) and add a test.
- Keyword emergency detection will miss many phrasings. Record misses that a lawyer marks later, so the list can be extended.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Software can do three things. (1) Help an adult see that their problem may be legal, in their own language, on channels they already use: WhatsApp, a phone call or the keypad. (2) For orgs verified as legal-aid bodies, or firms with a recorded pro bono commitment, work out in code whether the person is likely eligible for free legal aid under s.12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. (3) Point everyone to the right DLSA/TLSC and the NALSA 15100 helpline, and hand a consented, PII-masked intake packet to the accountable org. On every channel, nothing a person says is transcribed, stored in readable form or shown to staff until they have consented and confirmed they are an adult. That gate runs before every other branch, and a DB trigger backs it up. A self-declared minor at the gate gets a fixed card pointing to free help, and their data is hard-deleted, leaving only a per-day count. If an adult conversation later contains a present-tense age statement, which the patterns only match when it is anchored to an age unit or the end of a clause, the system first decides in code whether the conversation is sensitive. A conversation is sensitive if it was handed off or viewed by staff, or if any of its text matches the abuse lexicon. Sensitive held text is written to Postgres at once, encrypted, under legal_hold and readable only by supervisors, and it never expires. Only unseen, non-sensitive text is held in Redis, and every held message is re-checked against the abuse lexicon as it arrives, so a disclosure is persisted whether or not the age question is ever answered. Deletion happens only after a confirmed 'under 18 now' answer on a conversation with nothing sensitive in it.

### What it can't fix

Software can't hire or pay legal aid counsel (1 per 18,609 people, Rs 5,000 retainers, late payment). It can't fix connectivity or reach people with no phone. It can't make DLSAs answer quickly, and it can't decide eligibility: the DLSA decides and we only pre-screen. It can't stop limitation running. It can't verify anyone's age or a guardian's identity over WhatsApp or a phone call. We rely on self-declaration at the gate, then a confirmed answer to a fixed question. A minor who says they are an adult and never makes an anchored present-tense age statement won't be caught. The abuse lexicon is a fixed word list. A disclosure in words it doesn't contain, in a non-sensitive unseen conversation, in a conversation where the person never answers the age question, can still expire from Redis after 24 h. We say so plainly and do not claim to detect every disclosure. Supervisors can grow the lexicon through the approval flow. While a held message waits for a supervisor, the handling lawyer sees only a placeholder. A supervisor can release it in one audited step, but software can't guarantee that a supervisor is on duty at 2 a.m. The age question carries 1098 and 112 for that reason. It can't make the s.19 POCSO reporting decision: a named supervisor makes and records it. It can't control what Meta and Twilio keep, and it can't recall text already sent to Anthropic or audio already sent to Deepgram before a later under-18 confirmation. It will not be a lawyer marketplace or ranking (BCI Rules 36/37). Languages that Deepgram STT or Tesseract can't handle get only the keypad menu and pre-recorded cards.

### What the user sees

Caller and WhatsApp gate: unchanged from round 5. Consent notice ('Reply YES to continue', with no LAWYER offer), then 'Are you 18 or older? 1 yes, 2 no'. At the gate, any other input re-sends the gate question. Answering 2 gives the minor card (DLSA, 15100, 1098, 112). Adults get the numbered menu. Late age statement, new behaviour: 'मैं 16 साल की हूँ' or 'I am 16 years old' gets the fixed question 'आपकी उम्र अभी 18 से कम है? 1 हाँ, 2 नहीं। अगर कोई आपको नुकसान पहुँचा रहा है तो 1098 या 112 पर कॉल करें।' and the AI says nothing else. 'I am 15 minutes away from court', 'I'm 16th in the queue' and 'मेरी उम्र 17 थी जब शादी हुई' change nothing. Handling lawyer (/inbox) on a handed-off conversation that triggers the detector: the conversation stays in their list with the banner 'Age statement detected: new messages held for supervisor review (supervisor alerted 14:02)'. Each held message appears as a dated placeholder row 'Message held for supervisor review', with no text. When a supervisor releases a message, its text appears with 'Released by <supervisor> at <time>'. Lawyer (/inbox) on an AI-intake conversation in age_check: the badge 'Age check pending: AI paused', with no held text shown. Supervisor (/triage, owner, partner and legal_aid_supervisor only): a 'Held for POCSO assessment' queue with three sections. 'Abuse disclosure held' is pinned top and red. 'Age check: sensitive, awaiting answer' and 'Age check unanswered > 24 h' follow. Each item shows the decrypted held messages read-only, in order, with the lexicon term that matched highlighted, and the buttons 'Release to handling lawyer' (when the person answered 2, or after the supervisor has reviewed it) and 'Record s.19 assessment' (report made with reference, or no report required with reasons). Associates and paralegals see neither the queue nor any held text. The 'Minors redirected' tile shows counts per day, channel and language, as before.

### What the system does

1-6. Unchanged from round 5. Triage mode flags. The phone gate runs before STT (media frames discarded undecoded, pre-rendered hash-checked prompts, caller_hash only). _gate_turn() is the first branch in _handle for triage numbers, with a closed vocabulary, and LAWYER, intake_enabled and free text can't leave the gate. The whatsapp_gate_guard trigger. Pre-gate minimisation: HMAC wa_id, raw id and name only in Redis wa_gate (24 h), the RLS policy excludes 'gate', voice notes are withheld, and a 24 h gate purge runs. msg_ref() HMAC message IDs for inbound and outbound, with dedup by hash and 30-day previous-key overlap. triage_log() logs only msg_ref, status codes and exception class names, with exc_info off. Gate minor_stop hard-deletes and writes a minor_block plus an identifier-free count and audit row. 7. Late age statements, rewritten. (a) Anchored detector. data/legal_aid/minor_patterns.json holds compiled, anchored regexes, run after NFC normalisation and conversion of Devanagari, Tamil and Gujarati digits to ASCII. English: `\bI(?:'m| am)\s+(1[0-7])\s*(?:years?|yrs?|y\.?o\.?)\b(?:\s+old)?` OR `\bI(?:'m| am)\s+(1[0-7])(?:\s+(?:now|only))?\s*(?:[.!?,;।]|$)`. The number must be followed by an age unit, or by an optional 'now'/'only' and then the end of a clause. Hindi: `मैं\s+(1[0-7])\s*(?:साल|वर्ष|बरस)\s+(?:का|की|के)\s+(?:हूँ|हूं)`, `मेरी\s+उम्र\s+(?:अभी\s+)?(1[0-7])\s*(?:साल|वर्ष)?\s*(?:है|हैं)\b`, and `मैं\s+(?:कक्षा|class)\s+[5-9]\s+में\s+पढ़(?:ता|ती)\s+(?:हूँ|हूं)`. Marathi uses `वय\s+(1[0-7])\s+(?:वर्षे|वर्ष)\s+आहे` and `मी\s+(1[0-7])\s+वर्षांचा|वर्षांची\s+आहे`. Tamil uses `எனக்கு\s+(1[0-7])\s+வயது`. Hinglish uses `\bmai(?:n)?\s+(1[0-7])\s*(?:saal|sal|years?)\s+(?:ka|ki|ke)\s+(?:hu|hoon|hun)\b`. After that, the per-sentence past-marker exclusion from round 5 runs (था/थी/थे/थीं, was/were, 'when I was', 'at the age of', जब मैं, उस समय, की उम्र में, होते, वयात). The detector runs only in status 'intake' or 'lawyer' and is off in guardian sessions. (b) Classify at the moment of detection, in code, inside the conversation lock: sensitive = (status == 'lawyer') OR staff_viewed_at IS NOT NULL OR a handoff packet exists OR abuse_match(any stored message body in this conversation, or the triggering text). abuse_match uses data/legal_aid/abuse_lexicon.json after normalisation: यौन, छेड़छाड़, बलात्कार, गलत तरीके से छुआ, गंदी हरकत, 'touched me', 'sexual', 'rape', 'abuse', 'POCSO', plus Marathi and Tamil terms, as before. (c) Sensitive path: status 'age_check_sensitive'. legal_hold = true is set on the conversation and on its transcripts row at once. The triggering message, and every later inbound message while the status is held, is written immediately to the new table whatsapp_held_messages (id, conversation_id, seq, received_at, kind, body_enc, nonce, key_kid, lexicon_hits text[], released_at, released_by). body_enc is AES-256-GCM with the org's hold key (TRIAGE_HOLD_KEYS, versioned by kid, envelope-wrapped). whatsapp_messages gets a placeholder row '[held: supervisor review]' pointing at the held id, so the handling lawyer sees that a message arrived and when. There is no TTL and no Redis copy. Held rows are decrypted only in GET /api/v1/triage/held/{conversation_id}, after a role check for owner, partner or legal_aid_supervisor. RLS on whatsapp_held_messages allows select to those roles only, and the API never returns body_enc. Supervisors get an in-app alert, marked urgent when lexicon_hits is non-empty. The fixed, hash-checked age question (with 1098/112) is sent. If the status was 'lawyer', the AI stays off as before. Lawyer-initiated replies still work, so the lawyer is not muted. (d) Non-sensitive path (status 'intake', never viewed, no packet, no abuse match): status 'age_check'. The AI is paused, the triggering text and later inbound text go to Redis age_hold:{id} (TTL 24 h) and are stored as '[held: age check]', and the age question is sent. Every held message runs through abuse_match when it arrives, before it goes to Redis. On a hit, escalate() runs in the lock: it writes every Redis-held text in seq order, plus the new one, to whatsapp_held_messages, deletes the Redis key, sets status 'age_check_sensitive' and legal_hold, and alerts supervisors urgently. Nothing waits for the answer. (e) Answers. '2' on the non-sensitive path restores the previous status, writes the Redis texts to whatsapp_messages in order, deletes the key, resumes, and audits 'triage.age_check_cleared', as in round 5. '2' on the sensitive path restores the previous status. If no held row has lexicon_hits, the held rows are released into whatsapp_messages (decrypted server-side and written as normal messages), legal_hold is cleared, and 'triage.age_check_cleared' is audited. If any lexicon hit exists, the rows are released to the handling lawyer's view, but legal_hold stays and the item stays in the supervisor queue as 'Abuse disclosure: adult declared' until a supervisor closes it with a recorded review. '1' on the non-sensitive path calls purge_minor() (hard-delete the conversation, messages, transcript and Redis keys; daily count; identifier-free audit row), as before. '1' on the sensitive path calls freeze_for_pocso(): status 'frozen_pocso', the held rows kept, legal_hold kept, the minor card sent, and the item kept in the queue until a pocso_assessments row exists. 'no_report_required' then purges, including whatsapp_held_messages. 'report_made' retains everything. (f) No answer. Non-sensitive 'age_check' after 24 h: the Redis text (which by construction never matched the lexicon) expires, the conversation stays paused, and it appears in the supervisor queue as 'Age check unanswered' with counts only. 'age_check_sensitive' after 24 h: nothing expires. The worker's 'task_age_check_escalate' cron moves it to 'Age check unanswered > 24 h' in the supervisor queue and re-alerts. Every delete path refuses it: purge_minor, the gate cron, the migration 013 trash, the 30-day adult purge, and the BEFORE DELETE trigger, which refuses rows with legal_hold or a status in ('age_check_sensitive', 'frozen_pocso') on whatsapp_conversations, whatsapp_messages, whatsapp_held_messages and transcripts. (g) Release to the handling lawyer: POST /api/v1/triage/held/{id}/release (supervisor roles, audited 'triage.held_released' with supervisor id and held ids, no text). It sets released_at/by, and the lawyer's inbox then shows the text. (h) Trigger whatsapp_gate_guard is extended. Allowed transitions are intake|lawyer -> age_check|age_check_sensitive, age_check -> age_check_sensitive|intake|(delete via purge_minor), and age_check_sensitive -> frozen_pocso|previous status. Leaving age_check_sensitive needs a matching audit row id passed via a session setting (set_config('triage.audit_id')), so a raw UPDATE can't clear it. (i) Phone mirrors this. On a detector match, segments are held in memory and the fixed audio question (with 1098/112) is played. Each held segment runs abuse_match as it arrives. On a hit, the call transcript is persisted at once as a transcripts row with legal_hold and status age_check_sensitive, held segments go to whatsapp_held_messages' phone twin call_held_segments (same encryption and RLS), and supervisors are alerted. If the call ends with no answer, a lexicon hit stays persisted. Without one, the held segments are dropped and the call is not persisted. DTMF '1' or '2' follows (e). 8-15. Unchanged: the guardian path with fresh origin='guardian', the screening gate needs legal_aid_verified_at or an audited pro bono commitment, compose_card's hash-checked block order, eligibility in code from s12_categories.json and income_ceilings.json, the menu state machine, the DLSA directory, recipient-specific handoff consent with build_packet, and PiiMasker before every model call.

### Where it is built

Extend app/services/whatsapp_intake.py: the gate branch from round 5, the anchored detector call, classify_sensitivity(), the hold paths (Redis for non-sensitive, whatsapp_held_messages for sensitive), escalate() on a per-message abuse_match, and answer handling. Extend app/routers/whatsapp.py (placeholder rows for held messages; stamp staff_viewed_at; hide frozen_pocso and held text from other roles), app/services/telephony_session.py and app/services/live_session.py (in-call hold, per-segment lexicon check, immediate frozen persistence, no_persist), app/services/audit_service.py (triage.age_check_sensitive, held_released, age_check_cleared, pocso_frozen, pocso_assessed), app/worker.py (task_age_check_escalate cron; the gate purge and the 30-day purge skip legal_hold), and the migration 013 trash code. New: app/services/triage_service.py (minor detector with anchored patterns and the past-tense exclusion, abuse_match, classify_sensitivity, hold encryption helpers built on the cryptography package's AESGCM, compose_card, build_packet), app/routers/triage.py (GET held/{id}, POST held/{id}/release, pocso-assessments, guardian intake, daily counts), data/legal_aid/{minor_patterns,minor_negatives,past_markers,abuse_lexicon,s12_categories,income_ceilings,dlsa_directory}.json, and data/legal_aid/locked_notices/{hi,en,mr,ta}.json (the age question now includes 1098/112). Migration supabase/migrations/014_triage_and_legal_aid.sql additionally adds the 'age_check_sensitive' status, whatsapp_held_messages and call_held_segments (supervisor-only RLS, no body column readable in plaintext), and the extended whatsapp_gate_guard and BEFORE DELETE triggers covering held tables. Frontend: frontend/src/app/inbox/page.tsx (held placeholder rows, banner, released text) and frontend/src/app/triage/page.tsx (three queue sections, held message viewer, release button, assessment form).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel, Lexis+ AI and Clio start once the lawyer already has the client. Tele-Law and the NALSA helpline depend on scarce staff and give every caller the same menu. WhatsApp bots keep numbers and message IDs from the first word, put 'talk to a human' ahead of any consent or age check, and show every chat to every staff member. Child-safety filters either do nothing or delete on a keyword. That would destroy an adult survivor's account of being married at 16, or a lawyer's 'I am 15 minutes away' message. In ours, the gate is a state machine backed by a trigger. Age patterns are anchored and past-tense aware. A match only pauses and asks. Whether held text is preserved is decided in code before anything can expire, and it is re-checked on every message. Abuse disclosures and handed-off conversations go straight to encrypted, supervisor-only, undeletable storage, without waiting for a frightened child to answer. Deletion is reserved for a confirmed child whose conversation nobody saw and which discloses nothing.

### Safeguards

DPDP s.6/s.9: nothing is processed beyond what the gate needs until consent and self-declared adult status, with the gate first in code and enforced by a trigger. Before the gate, the number and all Meta message IDs are keyed HMACs, and logs carry only msg_refs, status codes and exception class names. POCSO s.19/s.21: whether held text is preserved is decided deterministically at detection time and again on every message. Abuse-lexicon hits, handed-off conversations and staff-viewed conversations go straight to AES-GCM-encrypted, supervisor-only storage under legal_hold, with no TTL. Every delete path refuses it, triggers included, until a named supervisor records the s.19 assessment. The software never makes the reporting decision. Text from a client to their own lawyer is never destroyed by a TTL. At worst it is held for a supervisor, who releases it in one audited step. Redis-only holding is limited to unseen, non-sensitive text, and every message is re-checked before it is held there. Patterns are anchored and past-tense aware, so ordinary adult sentences don't trigger them. The age question carries 1098 and 112. Phone audio isn't decoded before the keypad gate. PII is masked before any model call. BCI Rules 36/37: no ranking, the free DLSA route comes first, and the fee notice is locked. UPL: legal text comes only from hash-checked cards. Approval points: an owner, partner or supervisor approves cards, notices, the lexicons and the pattern files. Supervisors release held text and make the s.19 assessment. The platform admin verifies legal-aid orgs.

### How the panel's objections were answered

(1) A disclosure no longer expires while waiting for an answer. Every message held under age_check runs through abuse_match as it arrives, before it goes to Redis. On a hit, escalate() immediately writes all held texts in order to whatsapp_held_messages (encrypted, supervisor-only RLS), deletes the Redis copy, sets age_check_sensitive and legal_hold, and alerts supervisors, without waiting for '1'. The triggering text and all stored messages are also checked at the moment of detection. The test you asked for is the first acceptance test: age statement, then abuse message, then 25 h with no reply, gives a row readable by a supervisor JWT and by no associate JWT. (2) (i) The patterns are anchored. The number must be followed by an age unit (years/yrs/y.o./साल/वर्ष/बरस/वय/வயது/saal), or by optional 'now'/'only' and then the end of a clause. Negative fixtures cover 'I am 15 minutes away from court', 'I'm 16th in the queue', 'I am 17 km', 'I am 16 hours late' and 'मैं 15 मिनट में', and each must leave a lawyer-status conversation untouched. (ii) The abuse lexicon runs on each held message as it arrives, and a hit freezes and persists it whether or not '1' is answered. (iii) Conversations in status 'lawyer', or with staff_viewed_at set or a handoff packet, never use Redis or a TTL. Held messages are written at once, AES-256-GCM encrypted, to whatsapp_held_messages with supervisor-only RLS. With no answer within 24 h, task_age_check_escalate moves the conversation to the supervisor queue and nothing expires. (iv) Tests cover no-answer with abuse (preserved), the lawyer-status false positive (nothing held, nothing lost) and a lawyer-status true positive with no abuse (persisted, released by a supervisor, nothing lost). (3) Sensitivity is checked at detection time, in the lock. A conversation that was already viewed, handed off or in 'lawyer' status, or whose held text matches the lexicon, goes to 'age_check_sensitive', with immediate persistence under legal_hold, supervisor-only access and an alert, and never expires. Redis is used only for unseen, non-sensitive conversations. To avoid blinding the lawyer, they see a timestamped placeholder for every held message, a banner naming the alerted supervisor, and the text itself once a supervisor releases it in one audited action. The lawyer can still reply. Your test is the second acceptance test: a lawyer-status conversation receives a present-tense age message that matches the lexicon, there is no reply for 25 h, and the text still exists under legal_hold and is visible to the supervisor.

### Acceptance tests

- No-answer abuse disclosure is preserved (tests/test_triage_age_hold.py): an adult-gated, unseen intake conversation receives 'मैं 16 साल की हूँ' (status becomes 'age_check', Redis hold), then 'उसने मुझे गलत तरीके से छुआ'; immediately after the second message the status is 'age_check_sensitive', both texts exist in whatsapp_held_messages in order (decryptable with the org key), the Redis key age_hold:{id} no longer exists, legal_hold is true and an urgent supervisor alert exists; time is advanced 25 h (freezegun + fakeredis TTL expiry) and task_age_check_escalate runs; the rows still exist, the conversation is in the 'unanswered > 24 h' queue, a supervisor JWT's GET /triage/held/{id} returns both texts, an associate JWT gets 403 and an associate-JWT RLS select on whatsapp_held_messages returns zero rows
- Lawyer-status age statement with abuse and no reply for 25 h: a conversation in status 'lawyer' receives 'I am 16 years old and he touched me again today'; it is written at once to whatsapp_held_messages (no Redis key is created at any point, spy), the lawyer's inbox shows a placeholder row with a timestamp and no text, and the supervisor is alerted; after 25 h the text still exists under legal_hold, is visible to the supervisor, and purge_minor, the gate cron, the 013 trash, the 30-day purge and a direct SQL DELETE are all refused
