All reads go through security-definer RPCs that mask the date, candidates, inputs and computed values for the assigned checker while the check is pending, and deadline_entries are returned only to their author until then. The checker is assigned at creation, before anyone else has seen the values. Anyone with a recorded unmasked view is never eligible. Audit rows store only hashes. A reminder that must reach the checker cancels the check rather than staying hidden. test_checker_direct_select (a partner-checker's direct PostgREST selects and RPC responses contain none of the first entry's values), test_checker_audit_and_side_channels, test_viewer_never_checker and test_safety_cancels_check prove it.

minor: deadline_value_views rows are written on every unmasked list_deadlines read. A partner who opens the firm docket therefore becomes ineligible as checker for every visible deadline. That is intended, but in small firms the eligible pool will quickly run dry. Show in the UI why a check fell back to self re-entry.

The maker can still leak the date through matter notes, the case timeline, eCourts next-date fields or chat. State that blindness covers the deadline record only, and keep the eCourts next-hearing date of the same matter out of the checker's view while the check is pending, or note that it isn't covered.
The '3 days' safety cancel threshold should be per-rule data (short IBC or bail windows may need more lead).
Migration 014 is claimed by P02, P03, P29, P36 and P08 too. Renumber or merge them.

The audit rows store sha256(inputs). Inputs are a handful of dates, so the hash can be reversed by enumeration: a partner-checker could hash every plausible date combination and recover the first entry. That makes the claim 'a partner-checker reading the audit log learns nothing' untrue. Use an HMAC with a server-held per-org key, or write no hash until check_state leaves 'pending'. Then add a test that brute-forces dates over a one-year window and fails to match.

The escalation contact's phone number and undertaking are personal data of a non-member. Record a DPDP notice to the clerk and a purpose limited to deadline pings. Purge the row when the employment relationship or undertaking ends, with a partner review at least yearly.

Every unmasked list_deadlines call writes deadline_value_views rows, and partners browse the whole docket. So after creation almost nobody stays eligible for a reassigned check, and small firms will mostly fall back to self re-entry. The partner digest should say this openly ('re-check impossible: all eligible members have viewed'), not leave it as a silent fallback.
Choose the migration number together with P02, P03, P29, P36 and P08, which also claim 014.

The checker can still read court_cases hearing and order dates and the /workflows outputs. That is the 'source record' exception the proposal already states, but the DB test should list those tables explicitly as allowed exposures so a reviewer doesn't count them as leaks.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Watching every custody file and telling the right lawyer, on the exact day, that default bail has accrued (s.187(3) BNSS or s.167(2) CrPC, picked by when the investigation began) or that an undertrial has reached the s.479 BNSS threshold, which applies to every undertrial whatever the offence date. The application is drafted and the statutory basis shown, so the right is used before a late chargesheet extinguishes it.

### What it can't fix

Whether the court grants bail, surety arrangements, the prosecution filing a chargesheet on day 59, and identifying undertrials inside the jail. We only know about prisoners whose files the firm or legal-aid panel holds; we don't scrape e-Prisons. Unsettled transition questions under s.531 BNSS (e.g. differing High Court views on proceedings begun around 1 July 2024) are flagged for the lawyer, not decided by the software. The s.479 exclusions that turn on facts (other pending cases, delay caused by the accused) are confirmed by the lawyer.

### What the user sees

A Custody board (/custody) lists every client in custody with offence sections (BNS or IPC), offence date, FIR date, remand date, days in custody today, the default-bail date and provision, whether the chargesheet is filed, and the s.479 BNSS date (with 'one-third: first-time offender' or 'one-half'). Where it is more favourable, s.436A CrPC is shown alongside as an alternative citation. A transition badge reads 'Offence before 1 Jul 2024, FIR after: check s.531 BNSS' where applicable. Red 'apply today' rows sit at the top. Maximum and minimum punishment are filled from a statute table, not typed. On the accrual day the counsel, backup and partner get an alert with a prefilled application (marked AI DRAFT, UNREVIEWED until a lawyer approves). A legal-aid panel can upload a CSV of undertrials and get a list of who is eligible under s.479 and from when, including pre-July-2024 cases.

### What the system does

1. New `custody_files`: matter; accused; offence_date (used only for the substantive BNS/IPC punishment lookup); fir_date; investigation_started_on (defaults to fir_date); arrest_date; sections; first_remand_date; custody type; chargesheet_filed_on; first_time_offender (lawyer-confirmed); other_pending_cases (lawyer-confirmed); special-statute flags; extension orders.
2. Statute table app/data/offence_punishments.json: for BNS and IPC sections, maximum term, minimum term, death/life flags, and special-statute periods (UAPA, NDPS periods and extension provisions), verified by two criminal advocates. The substantive code (IPC or BNS) is picked by offence date, because punishment is fixed by the law in force when the offence was committed.
3. Procedural code for default bail, by s.531 BNSS: if the investigation began (FIR registered, or for a complaint case the complaint filed) before 1 July 2024, the provision is s.167(2) CrPC; on or after, s.187(3) BNSS. The offence date plays no part in this choice. If fir_date is missing, the system uses arrest_date and flags 'FIR date not entered: provision assumed from arrest date'. If the offence predates 1 July 2024 but the FIR doesn't, it shows 'transition: check s.531 BNSS' for the lawyer. Same rule in the custody watch and the existing pack.
4. Default-bail period, fixed in code: 90 days only where the offence is punishable with death, life imprisonment or a term of not less than ten years (keyed on minimum term/life/death from the table); otherwise 60 days. This fixes the current `_bail` pack's `max_years >= 10` test (workflow_service.py line 273), which gives 90 days for 'up to ten years' offences that attract 60 under Rakesh Kumar Paul v State of Assam (2017).
5. Day counting includes the remand date, per the Supreme Court rule (encoded only after our criminal team signs the golden cases). Special-statute extensions are applied only when an extension order date is entered.
6. Undertrial release under s.479 BNSS, computed for every undertrial whatever the offence, FIR or arrest date. The basis text cites s.479 BNSS and the Supreme Court's order of 23.08.2024 in In re Inhuman Conditions in 1382 Prisons applying it to undertrials in cases registered before 1 July 2024. The threshold is one-third of the maximum for a first-time offender, otherwise one-half. Offences punishable with death or life are excluded. The s.479(2) other-pending-cases exclusion and any delay caused by the accused are shown as a checklist the lawyer confirms. Where the case began under the CrPC, s.436A CrPC (one-half) is shown as an alternative citation only when it is more favourable. Under current arithmetic it never gives an earlier date, so in practice it appears as a supporting citation, and the deadline is always the s.479 date.
7. Fix to the existing pack: `_bail` gets new optional fields `fir_date` and `min_punishment_years`. The procedural code follows step 3, the 60/90 test follows step 4, and the undertrial computation follows step 6. The error raised without offence_date stays, because offence_date is still needed for the punishment lookup.
8. Each date becomes a P13 deadline with a hard flag ('the right is lost once a chargesheet is filed'). The ladder runs daily from T-5 and the sweep re-runs every morning at 07:00 IST.
9. On accrual, the drafting engine is called with the computed facts (PII-masked). The draft stays unreviewed until approved through the existing /drafting/{id}/approve.

### Where it is built

Extend `_bail` in app/services/workflow_service.py (procedural code by FIR/investigation date, minimum-term test, s.479 for all) and reuse it per row in a stateful custody watch; new app/data/offence_punishments.json; new app/services/custody_service.py and app/routers/custody.py; migration 014_deadlines.sql (custody_files); deadline_service from P13; drafting_engine.py and the existing draft approval flow; citation_service for the basis strings; frontend/src/app/custody/page.tsx and new fields in frontend/src/app/workflows; CSV import reuses review_service's upload handling pattern.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

No tool watches a custody file. Global tools are US-centric, and Indian research databases (SCC Online, Manupatra, Indian Kanoon) return case law, not dates. Even our own current pack is a one-off calculator that relies on a typed maximum, has the 60/90-day error, and picks the code by offence date, which wrongly denies the s.479 one-third rule to pre-July-2024 first-time offenders. The fix is a statute table, the s.531 BNSS rule keyed on the FIR date, s.479 for all undertrials per the Supreme Court's order, and a daily sweep that alerts on the accrual day and hands the lawyer a drafted application.

### Safeguards

Custody data is sensitive personal data under DPDP. It is stored under RLS and never sent to Claude except as masked facts for the draft, which passes a lawyer before filing. Legal-aid CSVs are processed for the DLSA panel's own clients only. Every date on the board carries its statutory basis and the disclaimer that dates are computations for the advocate to check. Transition cases and the s.479 exclusions are flagged for a lawyer's decision.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Both objections (s.479 denied to pre-July-2024 undertrials; procedural code chosen by offence date): (a) s.479 BNSS is now computed for every undertrial whatever the offence, FIR or arrest date, with the basis citing s.479 BNSS and the Supreme Court's order of 23.08.2024 in In re Inhuman Conditions in 1382 Prisons. The one-third first-time-offender rule applies to pre-July cases. s.436A CrPC is shown only as an alternative citation where the case began under the CrPC, never as the governing date. (b) custody_files gains fir_date and investigation_started_on. The default-bail provision (s.167(2) CrPC vs s.187(3) BNSS) is chosen by that date under s.531 BNSS; the offence date is used only for the substantive BNS/IPC punishment lookup. When the offence predates 1 July 2024 and the FIR doesn't, a 'transition: check s.531 BNSS' flag is shown; a missing FIR date falls back to the arrest date with a flag. (c) Golden cases and unit tests cover a pre-July offence with a post-July FIR (test_procedure_by_fir_date) and a pre-July first-time offender under s.479 (test_s479_pre_july_first_time_offender). (d) The existing `_bail` pack is fixed the same way (new fir_date and min_punishment_years fields, minimum-term 60/90 test, s.479 for all), with regression tests in tests/test_workflows.py::test_bail_pack_regressions.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_custody.py::test_up_to_ten_years_is_60_days: an offence with maximum 10 and no minimum yields 60 days (regression for the current bug); 'not less than 10 years' and life yield 90.
- test_procedure_by_fir_date: offence 2024-06-20, FIR 2024-07-05 gives s.187(3) BNSS plus the 'transition: check s.531 BNSS' flag; offence 2024-06-20, FIR 2024-06-25 gives s.167(2) CrPC; offence 2024-08-01, FIR 2024-08-02 gives s.187(3) BNSS with no flag.
- test_missing_fir_date_flag: no fir_date uses arrest_date and raises the 'FIR date not entered' flag.
- test_s479_pre_july_first_time_offender: offence and FIR in 2023, max 7 years, first-time offender, custody from 2023-03-01 gives the s.479 date at one-third (custody_from + 7*365.25/3 days), with basis text naming s.479 BNSS and the SC order of 23.08.2024; s.436A appears only as an alternative citation, never as the deadline.
- test_s479_pre_july_not_first_time: same facts without first-time status give one-half under s.479, with s.436A shown as an alternative citation.
- test_s479_excluded_life_death: a life-punishable offence gives no undertrial date and an explanation.
- test_s479_pending_cases_checklist: other_pending_cases unconfirmed shows the deadline with an 'exclusion check pending' badge, not an eligibility statement.
- tests/test_workflows.py::test_bail_pack_regressions: the existing pack, given offence 2023-05-01, first-time offender, max 6 years, returns the one-third s.479 date (previously one-half s.436A); given 'up to 10 years' with no minimum, returns 60 days; existing passing cases still pass.
- Golden custody cases (tests/fixtures/custody_cases.json, at least 30, signed off by two criminal advocates): pre-July offence with post-July FIR, pre-July first-time offender under s.479, BNSS vs CrPC by FIR date, remand-date counting, UAPA/NDPS extension entered vs not, chargesheet filed before vs after accrual.
- test_offence_table_complete: every section in the table has a max term or a life/death flag, and every statute reference passes citation_service.
- test_accrual_alert: freezegun at the accrual date shows the counsel, backup and partner alerted at 07:00 IST and a draft created with status unreviewed.
- test_chargesheet_stops_clock: entering chargesheet_filed_on before accrual marks the deadline done with that evidence; after accrual with no application, the history shows 'right lost'.
- test_csv_import: a 500-row legal-aid CSV with mixed pre- and post-July cases yields the s.479 eligible list in under 5 s with no AI calls (call counter asserted zero), and pre-July first-time offenders appear at one-third.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- The 60/90-day test under s.187(3) BNSS ('ten years or more') differs in wording from s.167(2) CrPC ('not less than ten years'). Whether Rakesh Kumar Paul carries over unchanged, and how to treat offences with a maximum above 10 years and no minimum, should be golden-case items signed off by the criminal team, not hard-coded from the CrPC reading alone.
- The _bail fix overlaps with P22's criminal_codes() change to the same function. Implement it once and share it, otherwise the two will diverge.
- s.479(2) (multiple pending cases) excludes release outright. Make the badge read 'not eligible if other cases are pending' rather than only 'exclusion check pending'.
- DPDP Act 2023 has no 'sensitive personal data' category (that was the SPDI Rules). Say 'personal data of an accused / custody data, treated with heightened safeguards'.
- s.187(3)(i) BNSS reads 'imprisonment for a term of ten years or more', while s.167(2)(a)(i) CrPC reads 'not less than ten years'. Whether Rakesh Kumar Paul's reading carries over to the BNSS wording (for example, maximum exactly 10, no minimum) is arguable. The 60-day alert is the safe direction, but for BNSS cases show a 'BNSS wording differs; 90 days arguable' note and keep the alert at day 60.
- s.436A CrPC excludes only death-punishable offences, not life. For CrPC-era life-but-not-death offences, the 'no undertrial date' explanation should say that s.479 BNSS does not apply and s.436A may be argued (half of an indeterminate maximum), instead of implying no remedy.
- For legal-aid CSV imports, record the DLSA as data fiduciary and the org as processor, with a written processing instruction, and set a retention limit for uploaded undertrial lists.
- For multiple offence sections, state that the gravest section (highest minimum, then life/death, then maximum) decides both the 60/90-day period and the s.479 maximum. Add a golden case for it.
- s.479 counts total detention, so interrupted custody (released, then re-arrested) needs custody periods, not a single custody_from date.
- P14 adds fir_date/investigation_started_on and P22 adds proceeding_instituted_on, and both rewrite _bail. Unify on one field and one criminal_codes() function so they don't diverge.
- Remand-date inclusion (ED v. Kapil Wadhawan, 2023) is correctly gated on sign-off. Cite the authority in the basis text once signed.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Routing routine contract requests end to end, with a checkable reason for every routing decision. Business users get an intake form. Deterministic triage puts each request in one of three lanes. Green: we generate the signature copy from our own approved template and the requester types the variable values into validated fields; the copy is hash-recorded and nobody's file but ours is ever signed. Amber: anything on counterparty paper, any returned file and any playbook deviation; the playbook redline is pre-made for a lawyer to approve. Red: unknown clauses, walk-away breaches, foreign law or seat, value over the threshold, or missing classification. Legal gets an SLA queue. After signature, a check confirms the executed copy is our generated file, the stamp and execution checklist come from P17, and the obligations go to P16. NDAs and simple agreements are self-served from approved templates only.

### What it can't fix

Headcount and budget. Negotiating with the counterparty. The Green lane is only as safe as the templates, variable types and thresholds the GC approves; we record that policy but don't make it. Most contracts arrive on counterparty paper with real deviations. They always need lawyer time: we shorten it, we don't remove it. A counterparty file is never eligible for 'sign without a lawyer'. Wet-ink executed scans can't be hash-matched, so for those we only help a person compare. E-signature itself: we hand the generated PDF to the company's e-sign tool or Leegality.

### What the user sees

Business users, in a new 'requester' role, use /requests. 'New request' asks for contract type, counterparty, value, our paper or theirs, needed-by date and business owner. For a Green-eligible template they fill typed fields: legal entity name, CIN or LLPIN (optional), registered address with PIN code and state, effective date from a date picker, term chosen from the template's allowed list, and value as a number. A field rejects input that doesn't fit its type, e.g. 'Party name may only contain a company name; words like "liability" or "notwithstanding" aren't allowed'. Status reads Green (ready to sign), Amber (with legal) or Red (with legal, high risk), with the SLA clock and the current holder. Legal's queue is sorted by lane, then SLA breach risk, then value. Each card lists the checks behind its lane, e.g. 'Counterparty paper: lawyer review required', 'Returned DOCX contains 3 unaccepted tracked changes and 1 hidden run (cl. 9)', 'PDF page 4: text layer differs from rendered page', 'Value Rs 1.2 cr > Rs 50 lakh threshold', 'Governing law England: walk-away'. Amber cards open straight into the P44 redline with suggestions filled in, and with hidden content and tracked changes shown inline. A Green request gives a signature-ready PDF/DOCX with the stamp panel, the note 'Generated from NDA v5 under standing approval v3 (GC A. Rao); SHA-256 3f9a…', and a 'Send to e-sign' export. When the signed copy comes back, the card shows 'Executed copy matches generated document (original revision hash verified)' or 'Executed copy can't be matched: paralegal comparison required'. A weekly dashboard shows volume by lane, median turnaround, and contracts that bypassed legal (uploaded later with no intake request).

### What the system does

1. Migration 017_contract_requests.sql adds three tables. contract_requests: org_id, requester_id, type, counterparty, value_inr, paper ours|theirs, document_id, needed_by, owner_id, lane, lane_reasons jsonb, status, assignee_id, sla_due_at, decided_by, generated_sha256, generated_document_id, executed_check. standing_approvals: org_id, version, templates (ids plus content hash), variable_schema per template, value_threshold, allowed_laws, approved_by, approved_at; maker-checker applies when the org has more than one senior. holiday_calendar: org_id NULL shared national holidays, plus per-org rows. 2. Green never handles a counterparty file. It is offered only when paper=ours and the template is in the current standing approval. The signature copy is rendered by drafting_engine.to_docx and the PDF exporter from the approved template, whose content hash must equal the hash recorded in the standing approval, together with the variable values typed into our form. 3. Variable validation is code in app/services/template_variables.py. Each [●…●] slot in an approved template declares a type: entity_name (max 120 chars; letters, digits, spaces and & . , ' ( ) -; must end in a recognised entity suffix such as Private Limited, Pvt Ltd, LLP, Limited or a sole-proprietor marker; no digits except within a CIN field), cin/llpin/gstin (format regex plus GSTIN check digit), indian_address (max 250 chars, a six-digit PIN code, state from the fixed list), date (ISO, from a picker, within ±2 years), enum (template-listed options only), and inr_amount (number, min/max). Every free-text type rejects a blocklist of clause words: shall, notwithstanding, liabilit*, indemn*, clause, cl., section, governing, arbitrat*, terminat*, waive*, unlimited, exclusive, plus newlines and control characters. Rejected input blocks Green, and the requester may send the request to Amber with the text attached. 4. When the file is generated, its SHA-256 is stored. The DOCX is built with no comments, revisions, hidden runs, fields, embedded objects or altChunks, and a unit test inspects every OOXML part of the output to prove it. 5. Triage order, all in code: (a) paper=theirs, or any uploaded counterparty file, goes to Amber at best. (b) The full-fidelity file inspector (app/services/file_inspector.py) runs on every uploaded file. For DOCX it unzips all parts and checks document, headers, footers, footnotes, endnotes, comments, glossary and embeddings. It flags w:ins, w:del, w:moveFrom/To, w:vanish, w:specVanish, white or 1-pt text, w:altChunk, OLE objects, external relationships and macros (vbaProject). The text of every part is extracted, so contract_diff_service compares headers, footers, footnotes and schedules too. For PDF it checks invisible text (render mode 3), text drawn in the background colour, pages without a text layer, and annotations or form fields. It also renders each page with pypdfium2, OCRs it, and compares the result with the text layer; a page below 0.9 similarity is flagged. Any flag is shown to the lawyer as a risk line, and the request can't drop below Amber. (c) governing_law.detect must return a law in the allowed list. (d) The value must be under the threshold; the value parsed from the document by code must equal the stated value, or the request goes to Amber. (e) A P17 stamp assessment must exist and be confirmed. (f) No P44 walk-away rule may fire. Green requires paper=ours plus all of (c) to (f). Any walk-away rule, unknown topic, foreign law or seat, or over-threshold value gives Red. Everything else is Amber. The model is never asked whether a document is safe to sign. 6. Signature verification: when the executed copy is uploaded, we check that it is our file. For an e-signed PDF, code locates the original revision (the bytes before the first incremental update, found from the signature /ByteRange and %%EOF offsets) and compares its SHA-256 with generated_sha256. A match sets executed_check='verified'. Any other file, such as a wet-ink scan or a re-saved PDF, gets executed_check='unverified'. For those we OCR the scan, run contract_diff against the generated text and the file inspector, and a paralegal or lawyer must tick 'compared'; a diff in any clause escalates the request to Amber after signature, and legal is alerted. 7. Amber and Red: the P44 redline runs automatically and the assigned lawyer accepts or rejects. The final DOCX is generated only after approval (drafts.approved_by), and any edit clears the approval. 8. SLA timers and reassignment are plain rules over holiday_calendar. Reminders reuse the worker cron. 9. Email-in through the P42 connector (DMARC-aligned only) creates a draft request with the attachments; those are counterparty files, so the request is Amber at best.

### Where it is built

app/services/drafting_engine.py (templates, [●…●] slots, to_docx), app/services/contract_diff_service.py (used here only to show lawyers the differences, never to grant Green), app/services/document_service.py (gains DOCX extraction, shared with P42), app/services/ocr_service.py and pypdfium2 rendering, app/services/governing_law.py, P44 playbook_rules, P17 stamp_assessments, P16 obligations, app/core/rbac.py (new 'requester' role), organization_members roles (migration 004), drafts approval and approval_requests (migration 013), app/worker.py cron. New files: supabase/migrations/017_contract_requests.sql, app/services/triage_service.py, app/services/template_variables.py, app/services/file_inspector.py, app/services/signature_verify.py, app/routers/requests.py, frontend/src/app/requests/page.tsx, tests/test_triage.py, tests/test_template_variables.py, tests/test_file_inspector.py, tests/test_signature_verify.py, tests/db/test_requester_rls.py, tests/fixtures/ooxml/ (hand-built DOCX fixtures).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI are built and priced for BigLaw research and drafting, not for the intake queue of a two-lawyer legal team. Ironclad and Icertis take months to configure. SpotDraft's AI review is generic on Indian points. CLMs that auto-approve on a text diff can be beaten by hidden runs, tracked changes or a doctored PDF text layer, because they compare extracted text, not the file that gets signed. Our Green lane has a reason a GC can defend: the file signed is the one we generated, from a hash-pinned template, with typed and validated values, under a named standing approval, and the hash is checked again on the executed copy. Every counterparty file goes to a lawyer, with hidden content surfaced and the playbook redline already made.

### Safeguards

No counterparty file is ever signed without a lawyer: Green signs only our generated file from a hash-pinned template under a named standing approval. Free-text slots can't carry clause language. The executed copy is hash-verified or compared by a person. No AI-written text is in a Green file, and AI-suggested redlines reach the counterparty only after a lawyer approves them. The requester role has least privilege under RLS. PII is masked before anything goes to Claude (the Green path makes no Claude call). Lane decisions, standing-approval changes, variable rejections and executed-copy checks are audit-logged. In a law-firm deployment (a panel firm running a client's contract desk), the firm's advocate is the approver, which keeps the BCI position clear. In-house, the company's legal team is responsible for its standing approval.

### How the panel's objections were answered

All three objections say Green can't rest on a text diff of a counterparty file. Fixed. (1) Green never uses a counterparty file. It exists only for our paper, and the signature copy is regenerated from a template whose hash is pinned in the standing approval, filled with values typed into our form. contract_diff_service is now only a review aid for lawyers. (2) Variable-slot injection: template_variables.py gives every slot a type (entity_name, cin/gstin, indian_address, date, enum, inr_amount) with length, character and format limits and a blocklist of clause words. 'Beta LLP, notwithstanding clause 9…' is rejected, and a test covers it. (3) Hidden content: the new file_inspector.py inspects every OOXML part (headers, footers, footnotes, endnotes, comments, embeddings). It rejects w:ins/w:del/move, w:vanish/specVanish, white or tiny text, altChunk, OLE objects and macros. For PDFs it flags invisible text, background-colour text, image-only pages, and pages whose rendered OCR differs from the text layer. Any flag keeps a request at Amber or higher. Fixtures for hidden runs, unaccepted tracked changes, footers, footnotes, comments, OLE objects and a doctored PDF layer must never be Green. (4) What is signed is what we generated. generated_sha256 is recorded, and after e-signature the PDF's original revision is hash-matched. Wet-ink or re-saved copies are 'unverified' and need a recorded comparison by a person; a diff escalates after signature. (5) DOCX extraction is added in document_service (shared with P42), since the current extractor rejects DOCX.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_template_variables.py: 'Beta LLP' passes entity_name; 'Beta LLP, notwithstanding clause 9 whose liability shall be unlimited' is rejected and names the blocked words; a newline in an address is rejected; an address without a six-digit PIN code is rejected; an invalid GSTIN check digit is rejected.
- tests/test_triage.py: an NDA v5 request on our paper with valid typed variables, confirmed stamp, Indian law and value under the threshold gives Green; its generated DOCX has zero w:ins/w:del/w:vanish/comments/embeddings in every part, and generated_sha256 is stored.
- A counterparty-returned DOCX whose visible text is identical to the approved NDA v5 is Amber, never Green, with reason 'counterparty file'.
- Fixture with a hidden run (w:vanish) adding 'liability unlimited' in cl. 9: Amber, and the flag names cl. 9 and quotes the hidden text.
- Fixture with an unaccepted w:ins in cl. 15, one with a changed footer, one with a footnote, one with a comment and one with an embedded OLE object: each is Amber with its own flag.
- PDF fixture whose text layer says 'Indian law' while the rendered page image says 'English law' (white overlay): the page is flagged as a rendered-vs-text mismatch and the request is not Green. PDF with a page lacking a text layer: flagged.
- Template whose content hash differs from the hash in the standing approval: Green is disabled with reason 'template changed since approval'.
- Governing law Singapore gives Red even when a mocked Claude says it's fine. Stated value Rs 20 lakh but document says Rs 2 crore gives Amber with a value mismatch reason. No confirmed stamp assessment gives Amber with reason 'stamp not computed'.
- Green is disabled when standing_approvals has no current version or when the GC toggles it off.
- tests/test_signature_verify.py: our generated PDF signed with an incremental update (fixture made with pyHanko) verifies against generated_sha256. The same PDF with one byte changed in the original revision, or re-saved without the incremental structure, gives 'unverified' and a paralegal task.
- A wet-ink scan whose cl. 9 differs from the generated text: after signature, escalates to Amber and alerts legal.
- The final DOCX endpoint returns 409 for an Amber request until the assigned lawyer approves; any edit after approval clears it.
- tests/db/test_requester_rls.py: a requester sees only their own requests and their department's contract summary fields, never legal's notes, redline explanations or other departments' contracts.
- SLA: a request created Friday 18:00 with a 2-business-day SLA is due Tuesday 18:00, with holidays in holiday_calendar excluded, checked with a frozen clock.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Green requires a confirmed P17 stamp assessment, but the requester is a business user. Pin the instrument key and state per template in the standing approval, so a non-lawyer never confirms a stamp classification.
- entity_name rejects legitimate counterparties: names with digits ('3M India Limited'), partnership firms, trusts, societies, government bodies and individuals. Add those types, or route them to Amber with a clear reason instead of a hard rejection.
- Many e-sign tools (DocuSign, some Aadhaar eSign vendors) flatten and re-save, or append certificate pages, so the original-revision hash will often fail. Expect the paralegal comparison path to be the common case, and size the workload accordingly.
- Green requires a 'confirmed' P17 stamp assessment, but P17 lets 'the user' confirm. A business requester should not decide stamp classification. Pin the instrument key and state per template in the standing approval, or require a lawyer to confirm.
- In a law-firm deployment, the standing approval should record the approving advocate's name and enrolment number, and an engagement with the client company. That evidences that the firm advised on the template and is not offering software-delivered advice to non-clients.
- Migration 017 collides with P46.
- The entity_name blocklist pattern 'liabilit*' rejects the full form 'XYZ Limited Liability Partnership'. Strip recognised entity suffixes before applying the clause-word blocklist, and add a test.
- entity_name requires a corporate or proprietor suffix. Individuals, partnership firms, trusts, societies and government bodies need their own typed slots, or they will always fall to Amber.
- Most Indian e-sign or e-stamp flows (Leegality, stamp page prepended) rewrite the PDF instead of appending an incremental update. Expect 'unverified' to be the common case and size the paralegal comparison work accordingly.
- Depends on P44 and P17 modules, which aren't in this batch. Migration 017 collides with P46.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Turning signed contract text, including scanned stamp-paper leases, side letters and amendments, into dated obligations with an owner and reminders. Every obligation is a window [open, close], and three conditions hold for each. (a) It quotes its clause, and the quote is verified against the document. (b) Both bounds are computed in code under one versioned rule table, from numbers the code reads in that quote. Where the wording allows more than one reading, every plausible reading of each bound is computed. The safe window takes the LATEST reading of the opening bound and the EARLIEST reading of the closing bound. (c) Nothing is scheduled as trusted until a lawyer confirms it. Covers auto-renewal and non-renewal notice windows, two-sided option, renewal and put/call windows ('not earlier than … and not later than …', 'within N days after <anniversary>'), termination notice, lock-in end, rent and price escalation, expiry, SLA credit claim windows, warranty periods, indemnity claim notice periods, payment milestones and deposit refunds.

### What it can't fix

Contracts nobody has given us: P42 widens coverage, but we can't find a contract that was never stored. Deciding whether to renew, exercise or exit is a business decision. Whether notice was validly served (mode, address, proof) depends on facts outside the document; we show the notice clause's service wording and leave service to the lawyer. Event-triggered clauses ('within 30 days of becoming aware of a claim') can be scheduled only once someone enters the event date. We don't decide which reading a court would adopt. We schedule the narrowest safe window and show the other readings, and the lawyer may choose a different reading with a recorded reason. Whether a premature or late exercise can be cured, waived or estopped is a legal question for the lawyer. OCR quality limits scanned vernacular annexures.

### What the user sees

An Obligations calendar at /obligations, plus a section on each contract page. Each row is one of four kinds: deadline (close bound only), window (both bounds), from-date (open bound only, e.g. 'may terminate after the lock-in') or event-pending.

Deadline example: 'Non-renewal notice: send by 30 Dec 2026 (latest safe day). Basis: cl. 14.2 "not less than ninety (90) days' written notice prior to the expiry of the Term"; Term ends 31 Mar 2027 (cl. 3.1 "three years commencing on 1st April 2024", rule TERM-INCL). Readings for the closing bound: clear days gives 30 Dec 2026, plain subtraction gives 31 Dec 2026. Earliest used.'

Window example: 'Renewal option: act between 1 Oct 2026 and 30 Dec 2026 (safe window). Do NOT send before 1 Oct 2026: a notice sent before the window opens may be invalid. Basis: cl. 15.1 "not earlier than six (6) months and not later than three (3) months prior to the expiry of the Term". Opening-bound readings: 30 Sep 2026 (plain) and 1 Oct 2026 (strict), latest used. Closing-bound readings: 31 Dec 2026 (plain) and 30 Dec 2026 (clear), earliest used.' For 'within thirty (30) days after the fifth anniversary of the Commencement Date' (1 Apr 2024), the row reads 'act between 2 Apr 2029 and 30 Apr 2029; the anniversary day itself is outside the window.' When the safe window is empty, or shorter than the org's minimum (default 3 business days), the row is red, reads 'Window conflict: needs legal', and carries no business reminders. Unconfirmed items sit in legal's 'To confirm' tray with the quote highlighted in the document viewer. There the lawyer accepts the safe window or picks another reading for either bound, with a mandatory reason. The reason and the rule are printed on the row.

Reminders: before the window opens, owners get only 'Heads-up: window opens 1 Oct 2026; do not send before then'. This message has no 'Handled' button, only 'Noted'. The first 'Act now' reminder goes out on the opening day. Further reminders count back from the close (60, 30, 14, 7 and 1 days, those that fall inside the window), and a short window gets reminders on the open day, its midpoint, close-1 and the close. Action reminders carry 'Handled', 'Decided not to exercise' and 'Escalate to legal'. If someone clicks 'Handled' before the open date, they get the warning 'The window opens 1 Oct 2026. A notice sent earlier may be invalid', and the click goes to legal for review instead of closing the item. Unacknowledged items escalate to legal at close-7. The ICS feed shows two events per window, 'Window opens' and 'Last safe day'. A row superseded by an amendment is struck through with 'superseded by Amendment No. 2, cl. 1'.

### What the system does

1. Extraction: a fixed 'obligations' preset in review_service makes one PII-masked call per document. It returns candidate obligations: type, verbatim quote, and the anchor(s) the bounds depend on (start, expiry, anniversary, rent start or an event). Quotes failing evidence_service.quote_found are discarded and counted in discarded_unverified.

2. Parsing, in services/obligation_dates.py, from the verified quote only. Code splits the quote into bound phrases. Opening markers: 'not earlier than', 'not before', 'no earlier than', 'after', 'from', 'on or after', 'at any time after'. Closing markers: 'not later than', 'not less than … before', 'at least … prior to', 'within', 'by', 'before', 'prior to', 'on or before'. A phrase like 'within N days after E' produces both bounds. Durations are read in words and digits, which must agree. Indian date formats are DD/MM. Business or calendar days are detected. If code can't assign every duration in the quote to a bound, if the model's structured values disagree with what code parsed, or if code can't parse the quote at all, the item is needs_lawyer and has no dates.

3. One rule table, data/obligation_rules/v1.json, versioned. Start rules TERM-INCL, TERM-S9 and TERM-AMBIG are unchanged from round 2.
- Closing-bound rules (unchanged): NOTICE-CLEAR (anchor - N - 1), NOTICE-PLAIN (anchor - N, always computed with NOTICE-CLEAR), WITHIN-S9 (E + N) and WITHIN-INCL (E + N - 1).
- New opening-bound rules: OPEN-PLAIN, for 'not earlier than N before A', gives A - N. OPEN-STRICT reads 'earlier than' as excluding the boundary day and gives A - N + 1; both are always computed. AFTER-S9, for 'after E' / 'within N days after E', excludes E, so the window opens E + 1. AFTER-INCL (opens on E) is computed as the alternative. ANNIV gives the Nth anniversary of the named date, with 29 Feb clamped to 28 Feb and the clamp recorded.
- Month arithmetic uses workflow_service.add_months with explicit month-end clamping. Business days use the shared holiday_calendar (P15).

4. Conservative selection, now two-sided. For an act we must do: safe_open = max over all opening-bound readings, across every expiry or anchor reading as well; safe_close = min over all closing-bound readings, across every anchor reading. A deadline-only obligation has safe_open = the document's effective date. A from-date-only obligation has safe_close = null. If safe_open > safe_close, or the window is shorter than the org's minimum, the status is needs_lawyer and no business reminder is created. For an act the other side owes us (deposit refund), we remind at the earliest close reading as a follow-up and show the latest as the day it falls overdue. Any difference between readings flags the row 'ambiguous'. A lawyer override that moves the open earlier or the close later needs a reason in override_reason, plus a second lawyer where the org has one. An override that narrows the window needs only a reason.

5. Migration 015_contract_obligations.sql. contract_obligations has: org_id, document_id, contract_id, type, window_kind (deadline|window|from_date|event_pending), quote, quote_verified, parsed jsonb, open_readings jsonb, close_readings jsonb, rule_ids, rule_table_version, window_open, window_close, chosen_open_reading, chosen_close_reading, override_reason, owner_user_id, status (candidate|confirmed|needs_lawyer|superseded|done|pending_legal_review), confirmed_by, confirmed_at, superseded_by. It has CHECK (status <> 'confirmed' OR window_open IS NULL OR window_close IS NULL OR window_open <= window_close). obligation_reminders has: obligation_id, kind (heads_up|act_now|escalation), offset_days, channel, sent_at, unique(obligation_id, kind, offset_days, channel). A trigger stamps confirmation, and confirmation lapses if the quote, parsed values, either set of readings, either bound, or the rule version changes. Each obligation also shows the P42 execution_status of its document. Business-owner reminders need execution_status = 'executed', or a lawyer's 'treat as binding' flag with a reason.

6. Worker cron task_obligation_reminders (7:00 IST, next to task_hearing_reminders), confirmed items only. A pure function plan_reminders(obligation, today) returns the messages due. It never returns an act_now message when today < window_open: before the open it returns heads_up only, at the fixed offsets open-14 and open-1. act_now starts on window_open, and the close-based offsets are filtered to dates on or after window_open. Sends go through whatsapp_service.send_template (an internal staff template) or email via n8n, and every send is recorded.

7. Acknowledgement endpoint: 'Handled' with now < window_open is refused as a completion. It sets pending_legal_review, notifies legal, and is audit-logged.

8. Amendments: when P42 links an amendment, extraction reruns. Items whose clause is expressly substituted by the amendment's verified quote are superseded only after a lawyer confirms.

9. ICS feed: a per-user signed-token URL carrying only titles and the two bound dates.

### Where it is built

app/services/review_service.py (preset, masked per-document call), app/services/evidence_service.quote_found, app/services/workflow_service.add_months and its Result.deadline pattern, app/worker.py cron and the send_hearing_reminders pattern, app/services/whatsapp_service.send_template, app/services/n8n_service.py, app/services/ocr_service.py, holiday_calendar from P15 (created here first if 015 ships earlier), and P42 execution_status. New files: data/obligation_rules/v1.json, supabase/migrations/015_contract_obligations.sql, app/services/obligation_service.py, app/services/obligation_dates.py (bound parser, readings, safe-window selection), app/services/obligation_reminders.py (pure plan_reminders), app/routers/obligations.py, frontend/src/app/obligations/page.tsx, tests/test_obligation_dates.py, tests/test_obligation_windows.py, tests/test_obligation_reminders.py, evals/obligations/ (30 labelled Indian contracts, including scanned leave and licence agreements and SHAs with put/call windows).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

CLM date fields depend on someone typing a single 'notice date' at signature. That models only the deadline and misses legacy scans, side letters and two-sided windows. A premature option notice is as fatal as a late one, and none of them warn against it. Where a CLM computes dates, it uses one unexplained convention. Harvey and CoCounsel answer questions about a document but don't keep live dated obligations with owners, and an LLM's date arithmetic is neither reproducible nor explained. Clio is organised around matters and time, not contract obligations. We model every obligation as a window and compute both bounds from the verified clause under a named, versioned rule. We shrink the window from both ends under ambiguity (latest open, earliest close), refuse to schedule an empty window, and make it impossible in code for an 'act now' reminder to fire before the window opens. A lawyer sees every reading before anything is trusted, and reminders run on the proven hearing-reminder cron and WhatsApp pipeline.

### Safeguards

Text is PII-masked before Claude (invariant 1). Both bounds are computed by code from verified quotes under a named, versioned rule; the model's dates are never used. Ambiguity shrinks the window from both ends. An empty or too-narrow window goes to a lawyer and is never scheduled. A pure, tested reminder planner guarantees no 'act now' before the window opens, and early 'Handled' clicks are routed to legal. Widening a window (earlier open or later close) needs a stated reason and, where available, a second lawyer. Reminders go to business users only after a lawyer confirms, and only for executed documents or ones a lawyer has marked binding. Reminders go to internal staff only and carry the contract title, the bounds and the clause quote. The ICS feed carries the minimum. Staff WhatsApp needs opt-in (DPDP consent and purpose); email is the default. Every confirmation, override, early acknowledgement and send is audit-logged. The service role is used only in the cron, scoped per org like hearing reminders, and is documented as an invariant-2 server-side job.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection: conservative selection handled only one side of the window, so 'act early to be safe' could cause a premature, void exercise. Fixed as the reviewer asked.
(1) Every obligation is now a window [window_open, window_close] with a window_kind of deadline, window, from_date or event_pending. Opening-bound rules are added: OPEN-PLAIN and OPEN-STRICT for 'not earlier than N before', AFTER-S9 and AFTER-INCL for 'after E' and 'within N days after E', and ANNIV for anniversaries.
(2) Selection is two-sided: the opening bound takes the LATEST reading across all rules and anchor readings, and the closing bound takes the EARIEST.
(3) If the safe window is empty (open > close) or narrower than the org minimum, the item is needs_lawyer and has no business reminders. A DB CHECK forbids confirming an inverted window.
(4) The user sees 'act between X and Y (safe window)' with 'Do NOT send before X'.
(5) Reminders come from a pure plan_reminders function that cannot emit an act_now message before window_open. Before the open it sends only a 'window opens on X, do not send before' heads-up with no 'Handled' button. A 'Handled' click before X is refused as completion and routed to legal.
(6) Lawyer overrides that widen the window at either end need a reason and a second lawyer.
Tests added: the six-months/three-months fixture (open 2026-10-01 from the latest reading, close 2026-12-30 from the earliest), the bare-'from' variant (open 2026-10-02), the 'within 30 days after the fifth anniversary' fixture (open 2029-04-02, close 2029-04-30, plus a property test that the open is always after the anniversary), the empty-window case, a day-by-day frozen-clock reminder test proving no act_now before the open, and an eval hard failure for any open earlier than the hand-computed earliest safe day.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_obligation_windows.py: cl. 'not earlier than six (6) months and not later than three (3) months prior to the expiry of the Term', with Term 'three years commencing on 1st April 2024' (expiry 2027-03-31, TERM-INCL), gives open_readings {OPEN-PLAIN 2026-09-30, OPEN-STRICT 2026-10-01}, close_readings {NOTICE-PLAIN 2026-12-31, NOTICE-CLEAR 2026-12-30}, window_open 2026-10-01 (latest) and window_close 2026-12-30 (earliest), with ambiguous=true.
- The same clause with bare 'three years from 1st April 2024' (expiry readings 2027-03-31 and 2027-04-01) gives window_open 2026-10-02, the latest over both expiries and both open rules, and window_close 2026-12-30, the earliest over all.
- 'within thirty (30) days after the fifth anniversary of the Commencement Date' with commencement 2024-04-01: the anniversary is 2029-04-01, window_open is 2029-04-02 (AFTER-S9 beats AFTER-INCL), window_close is 2029-04-30 (WITHIN-INCL beats WITHIN-S9 2029-05-01). Property test: for every generated anniversary date and N, window_open > anniversary.
- Empty window: 'not earlier than two (2) months and not later than three (3) months prior to expiry' gives open > close, so status is needs_lawyer, the reminder plan is empty for business owners, and legal is notified.
- A window narrower than the org minimum (e.g. open 30 Dec, close 30 Dec) is needs_lawyer.
- tests/test_obligation_reminders.py, plan_reminders over a frozen clock from 2026-08-01 to 2026-12-31 for the six-months/three-months window: no act_now message on any day before 2026-10-01; heads_up only on 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-30; the first act_now on 2026-10-01; close-based reminders only on or after 2026-10-01; exactly one message per (kind, offset, channel) over two consecutive runs.
- 'Handled' posted on 2026-09-20 for that window doesn't set done. It sets pending_legal_review, notifies legal and writes an audit row.
- Lawyer override moving window_open earlier to 2026-09-30 without a reason is refused; with a reason in a two-lawyer org it needs a second lawyer. Narrowing the window needs a reason only.
- DB test: confirming a row with window_open > window_close violates the CHECK constraint.
- Changing open_readings, close_readings, rule_table_version or the quote clears confirmed_by/confirmed_at (trigger test). A user in another org can't read the row (RLS).
- A confirmed obligation on a document whose P42 execution_status is partially_executed sends no business-owner reminder until a lawyer sets 'treat as binding' with a reason.
- Regression tests from round 2 still pass: 'commencing on' deadline 2026-12-30, 'with effect from' TERM-INCL only, 'commencing from' TERM-AMBIG, plain 'ninety (90) days prior to' schedules 2026-12-30, 'within thirty (30) days from the date of invoice dated 1 Jan 2026' closes 2026-01-30, 'eleven (11) months commencing 1st January 2025' expires 2025-11-30, '1/4/2024' parses as 1 April, '04/05/24' gives needs_lawyer, 'sixty (90) days' gives needs_lawyer, model 60 vs quote ninety gives needs_lawyer, an unverified quote is dropped and counted, month-end clamping is recorded.
- A quote containing a duration that code can't assign to either bound gives needs_lawyer with no dates.
- Amendment fixture 'Clause 15.1 shall be substituted with: ... not earlier than four (4) months ...' supersedes the old window only after confirmation; the new one is recomputed under the same rule table.
- The ICS feed has 'Window opens' and 'Last safe day' events, no clause text, and rejects an invalid token.
- evals/obligations: recall of hand-labelled date obligations >= 0.85. Hard failures: any scheduled window_close later than the lawyer's hand-computed latest safe day, and any window_open earlier than the lawyer's hand-computed earliest safe day.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- The label 'send by 30 Dec 2026' is wrong whenever the notices clause deems service on receipt or N days after dispatch, for example 'deemed served 5 days after posting by RPAD'. That clause is in the document, so code can read it. Either label the close bound 'must be served by' or subtract the longest deemed-service period from the notices clause to give a dispatch date. Do the same check at the opening bound: a notice posted before the window but deemed served inside it.
- For an act the other side owes us, the overdue day should be the latest reading, which the proposal already says. Make sure escalation timing uses that reading and not the reminder reading.
- Migration 015 assumes the P15 holiday_calendar exists. Make the build order explicit.
- For deadline-only notices, safe_open is the effective date. Some termination notices have their own premature-notice risk, for example 'notice not earlier than the lock-in end'. The parser already handles a two-sided quote, but add an eval case where the opening bound sits in a different clause from the closing one, so it isn't silently dropped.
- WhatsApp reminders to business staff carry clause quotes from confidential contracts. Keep email as the default, as stated, and drop the clause quote from WhatsApp bodies (title and dates only), as is done for ICS.
- Typo in answers_to_objections ('EARIEST').
- It depends on P15's holiday_calendar and P42's execution_status. Ship a stub execution_status ('unknown', with lawyer 'treat as binding') if P42 lands later, so obligations aren't silently blocked.
- Migration 015 numbering must be coordinated with the other proposals.
- Staff WhatsApp reminders must go through P33's outbound_policy reason (e) with an 'internal' audience template.

Where a CLM computes dates, it uses one unexplained convention. Harvey and CoCounsel answer questions about a document but don't keep live dated obligations with owners, and an LLM's date arithmetic is neither reproducible nor explained. Clio is organised around matters and time, not contract obligations. We model every obligation as a window and compute both bounds from the verified clause under a named, versioned rule. solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

At drafting and before execution, a deterministic lookup with sources tells the team the following. Which state's Stamp Act applies: place of execution, the property's state or the state of receipt, with any differential duty. The article, and the duty on the actual consideration, rent or deposit. The stamping methods the state offers. Whether registration is compulsory. Whether the instrument can be e-signed (IT Act First Schedule exclusions). It also produces an execution checklist in order. Rates come from a vendor-maintained shared table, verified by two vendor lawyers per row, with optional per-org overrides approved inside the firm. Every assessment records which source it used.

### What it can't fix

Buying stamps, collecting printed certificates, vendor stock shortages and impressed-paper-only states are physical or government constraints; we link the portal and say what to buy. Disputed classifications are for the Collector to adjudicate. Coverage starts with ten states and the high-volume instruments; anything else returns 'not covered: check the schedule' with no amount. Rates change by notification, so freshness depends on the vendor update process below. The shared table is information, checked by our legal-content team; it is not a legal opinion, and the firm remains responsible for the classification it confirms. NeSL digital stamping is open only to financial institutions.

### What the user sees

A 'Stamp & execution' panel on every draft in Studio and every uploaded contract. Example: 'Leave and licence, Maharashtra (property in Pune). Article 36A, Maharashtra Stamp Act. Inputs: licence fee Rs 40,000/month for 11 months, deposit Rs 2,00,000 (quoted from cl. 4 and cl. 5, verified). Duty: Rs X (formula shown step by step). Methods: e-SBTR / franking / e-stamp. Registration: compulsory, within the period stated. E-sign: allowed for this instrument. Source: shared table v2026.10.2, row MH-36A (Maharashtra Stamp Act Sch. I Art. 36A, notification ref, effective_from), verified 2 Oct 2026 by two Digi Lawyer legal-content advocates (enrolment nos. shown).' If the firm has its own override, the panel reads 'Source: your firm's override (approved by P. Shah, 14 Oct 2026; shared row differs: view)'. The user confirms instrument type and state from pre-selected dropdowns, never silently. A banner warns when the row is more than 180 days past verification. A changelog page lists shared-table versions and what changed.

### What the system does

1. Shared corpus, following the migration 008 pattern. Migration 016_stamp_duty.sql adds stamp_duty_rows: org_id NULL for the shared table; columns state, instrument_key, article, act_section, formula, min, max, methods, registration_rule, esign_rule, penalty, source_url, notification_ref, effective_from, last_verified_at, verifiers jsonb (two entries: name, enrolment no., date), table_version. RLS lets every signed-in user read shared rows and their own org's override rows. Only the service role writes shared rows. 2. Vendor verification is a documented process (docs/legal-content/stamp-verification.md). The source of truth is data/stamp_duty/<state>.json in the repo. A change needs a PR reviewed by two different members of the legal-content CODEOWNERS group (practising advocates). CI (scripts/validate_stamp_tables.py) rejects any row without two distinct verifiers, a source URL, a notification reference and effective_from, and recomputes the golden fixtures. On merge, scripts/load_stamp_tables.py upserts the rows with service role and bumps table_version. This is a deploy-time loader, not a user path, and it is documented in invariant 2. A weekly vendor job, scripts/check_stamp_freshness.py, lists rows past 180 days, and the legal-content team checks state gazettes on a written monthly cadence. 3. Per-org overrides live in stamp_duty_overrides (org_id NOT NULL, same columns plus base_row_id and reason). They are created only through approval_requests with new actions 'stamp_override_create' and 'stamp_override_retire': requesters are partner/associate, approvers owner/partner, and the approver must differ from the requester. They affect only that org. Lookups prefer an active override for (org, state, instrument_key), otherwise the shared row. When the shared row for an overridden key changes later, the org gets a 'shared row changed; review your override' item. 4. Formulas use a small safe expression language (+ - * / min max ceil, slabs, percentages of named inputs) evaluated by our own parser, never Python eval. 5. Classification: Claude, on PII-masked text, proposes the instrument key and the inputs, each with a verbatim quote checked by quote_found. Amounts are parsed by code from the quote, covering Indian digit grouping, lakh, crore and words; if the model and the code disagree the field is left blank. The user confirms the instrument key and state; until then no amount is final. 6. Place-of-execution and differential-duty rules and e-sign eligibility are fixed rule tables in the same shared corpus. 7. stamp_assessments stores document_id, row_source shared|override, row_id, table_version, inputs with quotes, result, confirmed_by and confirmed_at. P15, P43 and P45 reuse it.

### Where it is built

Migration 008's org_id-NULL shared-corpus pattern and RLS policy, approval_requests (migration 013, which gains the stamp_override actions in requester_roles/approver_roles), app/services/jurisdiction_service.py (Indian state profiles), app/services/drafting_engine.py ([●stamp duty●] placeholders and the panel), app/services/review_service.py, app/services/evidence_service.quote_found, app/services/citation_service.py registry (state Stamp Acts added). New files: data/stamp_duty/*.json, docs/legal-content/stamp-verification.md, .github/CODEOWNERS entry for data/stamp_duty/, scripts/validate_stamp_tables.py, scripts/load_stamp_tables.py, scripts/check_stamp_freshness.py, app/services/stamp_duty/registry.py, formula.py, assess.py, supabase/migrations/016_stamp_duty.sql, app/routers/stamp.py, a Studio panel component, tests/test_stamp_formula.py, tests/test_stamp_assess.py, tests/db/test_stamp_rls.py, fixtures/stamp_cases.json.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel, Lexis+ AI, Clio and Ironclad have no concept of Indian state stamp law. SpotDraft and Leegality sell e-stamp paper but don't give the article, the duty on the deal's own numbers, the registration requirement or the e-sign eligibility. An LLM asked about stamp duty produces confident wrong rates. Here the rate comes from a sourced table with a named two-advocate verification per row. It is maintained once for every customer, so it works from sign-up, and a firm with a different view can record an override approved inside its own firm without affecting anyone else. Every assessment says which source it used.

### Safeguards

Output is information on statutory charges with sources, marked 'check against the current schedule before payment', and the lawyer confirms classification. Shared rows change only through two-advocate review in CI and are loaded by a deploy-time service-role script, never from a user path. Overrides need maker-checker inside the firm and never leak across orgs. Every assessment records row source and version. Text is PII-masked before Claude. Citations to state Acts are checked by citation_service. The system makes no purchase or payment.

### How the panel's objections were answered

The objection was that the rate-table trust model was unclear: repo JSON was shared but approved through org-scoped approval_requests. Fixed with two separate layers. (1) A vendor-maintained shared corpus in stamp_duty_rows with org_id NULL, following migration 008: readable by all, written only by the deploy-time loader. Its verification process is documented in docs/legal-content/stamp-verification.md: two distinct legal-content advocates per row, recorded in verifiers with enrolment numbers, enforced by CODEOWNERS review and a CI validator. So the tables are active from sign-up (P43) and no firm verifies ten states by hand. (2) Optional per-org overrides in stamp_duty_overrides, created through approval_requests (new stamp_override actions, approver different from requester), affecting only that org. Every stamp_assessment records row_source shared|override, row_id and table_version. RLS tests prove that one firm can't change another's rates.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_stamp_formula.py: the parser rejects attribute access, imports and non-whitelisted names; slab formulas give the expected values at each boundary.
- Golden fixtures (fixtures/stamp_cases.json, 40 cases hand-computed from the official schedules with page references): each computed duty equals the expected value exactly and records table_version and row_source.
- scripts/validate_stamp_tables.py fails CI on a row with one verifier, two entries with the same verifier, or a missing source_url, notification_ref or effective_from.
- tests/db/test_stamp_rls.py: an authenticated user can read shared rows but can't insert, update or delete them. Org A's override is invisible to org B. Org B's assessment for the same key uses the shared row (row_source='shared').
- An override request by an associate stays pending. Approval by the same user is refused. A partner's approval activates it for that org only, and the next assessment records row_source='override' with the override id.
- When the shared row under an active override is reloaded with a new version, the org gets a review item.
- An unknown state or instrument returns 'not_covered' with no amount. A row past 180 days returns the amount with a stale flag, and the banner renders.
- Amount parsing: 'Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only)' gives 200000; digits and words that disagree leave the field blank.
- A mocked model classifies a lease as 'agreement not otherwise provided for': no final amount appears until the user confirms the key, and the confirmed key is recorded with the user id.
- E-sign rule: a general power of attorney and an agreement to sell immovable property are 'cannot be e-signed'; an NDA can.
- Executed in Karnataka, received in Maharashtra: the differential line equals Maharashtra duty minus Karnataka duty paid.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- The proposal says the 'Coverage starts with ten states' but doesn't list them. Publish the list and the instrument keys on the changelog page, so users know when 'not covered' is expected.
- The two-advocate verification by vendor staff should carry professional indemnity or a clear non-opinion disclaimer on the panel, not only in the docs.
- BCI Rule 49 bars a practising advocate from being a full-time salaried employee. If the 'legal-content advocates' are Digi Lawyer employees, they cannot be described as practising. Either retain them as independent consultants or describe them as 'legally qualified content reviewers'.
- Displaying verifiers' enrolment numbers to every customer reads like an endorsement. Keep the enrolment numbers in the audit record and show names and roles only.
- Migration 016 collides with P24, P35 and P38.
- The two-advocate legal-content team and the monthly gazette cadence are organisational dependencies. Coverage should launch only for states whose rows have passed CI validation.
- Competitors: Leegality/BharatStamp and state IGR calculators compute duty. The edge is quote-backed classification on the draft plus registration and e-sign eligibility; keep that framing.
