solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Proving, matter by matter and user by user, four things:
- (a) client identifiers never left the firm unmasked, except raw audio, which is disclosed and gated;
- (b) every call to an outside AI or speech processor (Anthropic, Tavily, Indian Kanoon, Deepgram STT and Aura TTS) was made by a named lawyer, or under their supervision, for a named matter or for a named user's general research, with a stated purpose;
- (c) where the firm requires client consent, it was recorded before any client data, audio included, reached a processor;
- (d) each processor is recorded with its region, its retention and what it receives.

This is the DPDP data-fiduciary evidence and the record of work done at counsel's direction (the Heppner gap).

General research stays usable for ordinary Indian research, which names governments, banks, insurers and reported cases. The party scan exists to attribute work to the right matter; it does not protect confidentiality, because names are deliberately not masked.

Changed this round: a private firm party is exempt only inside a citation that resolves by a citation key to a reported judgment, and only when that judgment is not the firm's own matter. An unresolved case title that names a private firm party is refused and moved to the matter, whatever sits on the other side of the 'v.'.

### What it can't fix

Untested law: whether an Indian court will treat AI-assisted work as protected under BSA ss.132-134 or BCI Rule 17. Software can produce evidence, not privilege.

Raw audio and images from the OCR vision fallback cannot be masked. We gate them behind a matter and consent, ledger them and disclose them; we cannot remove them.

What vendors do with the data rests on their contracts. We record those contracts; we cannot enforce them.

Names, places and dates are not masked, by design.

General-research attribution is best effort, and its limits are these:
- The party scan only knows parties already in the firm's index.
- An institutional litigant (government, PSU, bank, insurer, listed company) that is also a firm client is logged in general research, not refused, unless the firm marks it 'private for research'.
- A case title naming a private firm party is exempt only when it carries a reporter or neutral citation, or a stored Indian Kanoon document reference, that resolves to a reported judgment which is not the firm's own matter. This is stricter than before: a lawyer researching a High Court judgment cited only by name, where a party shares a name with a firm client, must add the citation or run the question in a matter. We accept that friction.
- A misspelling below the Strong band is not refused. It needs an attestation, which is recorded and reported (see step 4).
Choosing the right scope stays the lawyer's professional responsibility. Per-user reporting makes misuse visible, not impossible.

A database superuser can still tamper with rows. The hash chain makes that detectable, not impossible. We will not claim 'privileged by design'.

### What the user sees

Unchanged from round 4:
- the 'AI use' tab on every matter, with the downloadable PDF;
- mic and push-to-talk disabled until consent is recorded;
- the DTMF consent notice on the phone line;
- WhatsApp voice notes sent before consent are not processed;
- the 'Link to a matter' dialog;
- the /compliance page and its party-class page.

Research box and case-law search:
- Questions naming only institutional bodies ('State of Punjab', 'Union of India v. <non-firm party>', 'SBI', 'LIC') go through, with a grey note 'Mentions an institutional party on firm matters (logged)'.
- Changed: 'In State of Rajasthan v. Ramesh Kumar Sharma, can we argue default bail?', where Ramesh is a firm client and no citation key is given, shows 'This names a party in <matter title>. Run it in that matter?' with 'Move to matter'. The same refusal applies to 'Ramesh Kumar Sharma v. XYZ Traders'. A second line reads: 'Researching a reported judgment? Add its citation, e.g. (<year>) <vol> SCC <page> or <year> INSC <no>.'
- With a citation key that resolves to a reported judgment not in a firm matter, the question goes through, with the note 'Cites a reported judgment naming a firm party (logged)'.
- If the cited judgment is the firm's own matter, the user sees 'This judgment is in <matter title>. Run it in that matter?'.
- A Possible-band look-alike inside a case title asks for one confirmation: 'Does this concern a firm matter? No, this is not a firm matter / Move to matter'. 'No' is recorded and appears on the partner's research report.
- If the user cannot see the matter, the refusal names the responsible lawyer only, never the title.

### What the system does

Steps 1-3 and 5-8 from round 4 are unchanged: the guarded_call and open_stream choke points, the StreamPermit, the CI grep, the ai_route resolvers, the speech consent gate, firm_internal, segment tagging, the hash-chained ledger and ALLOWED_AI_HOSTS. The scope resolution of /caselaw/search?thread_id=T from round 5 is also unchanged.

4) General-research pre-checks, revised. They run in this order; any refusal makes 0 processor calls.
- (a) Limits: one typed prompt of at most 1,500 characters (200 for a case-law query). document_id, attachments and memory return 422.
- (b) assert_masked on the raw prompt. Any identifier refuses with 'unmasked_identifier'.
- (c) citation_spans(db, text), local only. It reuses citation_service._extract and case_lookups to find every 'X v. Y' / 'vs' / 'versus' / 'बनाम' span and every reporter or neutral citation. Each span gets a resolution:
  - key_resolved=true when a reporter or neutral citation inside or immediately after the span matches legal_authorities.citation_keys, AND that row's name_tokens contain the tokens of both sides of the span;
  - or when an Indian Kanoon document id or URL in the span is present in the persisted table ik_documents (doc_id, title_tokens, court, decision_date). Rows in that table are written only by earlier thread-scoped searches and citation checks, and the stored title must contain both sides;
  - name_resolved=true for a name-only match (the existing subset match).
  The live Indian Kanoon call in lookup_authorities is not used here: a new lookup_authorities_local() reads only the local tables, and a test patches the socket to prove it.
- (d) conflict_service.scan_text(org_id, text) gives each hit with its band (exact, strong or possible), party_class, matter ids and the span it falls in.
- (e) Decision table, in code (research_scope.decide, pure and table-tested):
  1. An Exact identifier hit anywhere refuses with names_party.
  2. An institutional hit allows, counted in institutional_hits, unless research_private is set.
  3. A Strong hit of class individual or private_company:
     - outside any span, refuses with names_party;
     - inside an unresolved or name_resolved span, refuses with names_party, whatever the class of the other side. This is the fix: name-only resolution is not enough, because common Indian names collide with unrelated reported cases;
     - inside a key_resolved span, allows, counted in citation_hits, unless the resolved judgment is the firm's own matter (rule 4).
  4. Own-matter test for a key_resolved span: the judgment is treated as firm matter M if (i) its CNR, or its case number and court, equals a court_cases row of M; or (ii) its party pair equals M's party pair (same normalisation as conflict matching) and its decision date is on or after M's opening date. Then it refuses with names_party, citing M (own_matter_judgment).
  5. A Possible-band private hit:
     - inside any span, requires attest_not_firm_matter=true on a re-submit. The ledger stores possible_attested=true and the hit's party_index id (never the text), and the partner's research report lists every attestation by user;
     - outside spans, allows, counted in possible_party_hits.
  The refusal names the matter title only if the caller can SELECT that thread; otherwise it names the responsible lawyer.
- (f) No consent check in general research, because refusal keeps firm matters out of it. The ledger row records matter_kind='general_research', user_id, institutional_hits, citation_hits, possible_party_hits, possible_attested and refusal_reason.

Refused rows are written with no prompt text. 'Move to matter' creates a new request under the thread scope, with T's RLS check and consent rule; it never re-labels the refused row.

Party classes, classify_party, data/institutional_parties.yaml, research_private and party_class_history are unchanged from round 5. Research answers are never written to thread memory.

### Where it is built

Unchanged from round 5: ai_ledger.py, matter_resolver.py, research.py, compliance.py, the migration 014 and 017 columns, caselaw.py with its thread_id scope, conflict_service.classify_party and scan_text, and data/institutional_parties.yaml.

Changed this round:
- app/services/citation_service.py:
  - new lookup_authorities_local(db, keys, names), with no Indian Kanoon network call;
  - new citation_spans(db, text), returning spans with key_resolved and name_resolved, side tokens and the matched authority id.
- app/services/indiankanoon_service.py: find_cases and the thread-scoped search persist hits to ik_documents. The existing lru_cache stays for speed but is never used for scope decisions.
- app/services/research_scope.py (new): the pure decide() table and the own-matter test against court_cases (cnr, case_number, court_name, petitioners/respondents) and the P46 party pairs.
- Migration 017 (with P46):
  - ik_documents;
  - ledger columns possible_attested and own_matter_judgment;
  - refusal_reason values names_party and own_matter_judgment.
- frontend: the refusal text with the citation hint, the attestation prompt, and the attestation column on the partner's research report.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI send raw client text under zero-retention contracts. Nothing ties a call to a lawyer, a matter and a consent, and they do no Indian identifier masking. Transcription tools record from the first second. Indian legal-GPT apps have no processor register, no consent gate and no per-user research record.

Ours puts every processor, speech included, behind one scope resolver, consent check and hash-chained ledger. The research lane follows how Indian research actually reads ('Union of India v. ...', 'State of ...', SBI, LIC, cited reported judgments) without opening a back door: a firm's own unreported case title, which is the commonest shape ('State of <S> v. <our client>'), is steered back to its matter, and so is a reported judgment that is the firm's own matter. The exemption is a deterministic citation-key match, not a name guess.

### Safeguards

Every processor call, text or speech, has a resolved scope, purpose and user, or it does not happen. Consent is checked before the first audio frame. Only the ledger can mint speech permits.

General research:
- per user, with no documents or memory;
- refused on identifiers;
- refused on any Strong private firm party unless it sits in a key-resolved reported judgment that is not the firm's own matter;
- look-alikes inside case titles need a recorded attestation;
- matter titles are never revealed to someone who cannot see the matter;
- the scope decision is a pure, table-tested function that uses only local data.

Party classes are rule-set, and every manual change is audited. The ledger is server-written, content-free and hash-chained, and is listed in invariant 2. The record says 'prepared at the direction of counsel', never 'privileged'.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection 1 and 2 (the unresolved-span exemption lets the firm's own matters into general research, and the out_of_scope text did not match the behaviour):
- The exemption for unresolved spans is removed. A Strong private firm party inside an unresolved span is refused with names_party and the move-to-matter offer, whatever the class of the other side. 'State of Rajasthan v. Ramesh Kumar Sharma' and 'Ramesh Kumar Sharma v. XYZ Traders' are both refused.
- Going further than asked: name-only resolution no longer counts either, because the existing subset match lets a common name hit an unrelated reported case. Only a key_resolved span counts: a reporter or neutral citation in legal_authorities, or a stored Indian Kanoon document, whose title contains both sides.
- Even a key_resolved span is refused when the judgment is the firm's own matter (a CNR or case-number match, or the same party pair on or after the matter's opening date).
- Possible-band look-alikes inside spans need a recorded attestation that appears on the partner report.
- The out_of_scope now states this rule exactly, and a test asserts the decision table matches it.
- Tests added: the unresolved State v. client title is refused with 0 model calls; the same text with a resolving citation key is allowed; the own-matter reported judgment is refused; the unresolved private-v-private title is refused; name-only resolution never exempts.

### Acceptance tests

- Unit (objection): Ramesh Kumar Sharma is the accused client on thread T against the State. '/research/ask: In State of Rajasthan v. Ramesh Kumar Sharma, can we argue default bail? <1,200 characters of facts>', with no citation key, is refused with names_party and T's title, makes 0 model calls, and writes a ledger row with no prompt text.
- Unit (objection): the same text plus '(2019) 4 SCC 123', where a legal_authorities fixture row has that key and name_tokens containing both sides, and with no CNR or party-pair match to T after T's opening date, is allowed with citation_hits=1 and one model call.
- Unit (objection): the same reported citation, where the fixture authority's CNR equals T's court_cases.cnr, is refused with own_matter_judgment and T's title.
- Unit (objection): 'Ramesh Kumar Sharma v. XYZ Traders', unresolved, is refused with names_party. 'SBI v. Ramesh Kumar Sharma' resolved by name only (no key) is refused. With a matching key it is allowed.
- Unit (objection): a name-only resolution never exempts a Strong private hit. A parametrised test over 30 Strong-hit spans with only name_resolved=true gives 30 refusals.
- Unit: 'Union of India v. Rajesh Traders' (Rajesh Traders not indexed; Union of India institutional on 3 firm matters) is allowed with institutional_hits>=1. GET /caselaw/search?q=State of Punjab with no thread_id is allowed, with one Indian Kanoon call.
- Unit: a Possible-band look-alike ('Ramesh Kumaar Sharmaa') inside 'State v. Ramesh Kumaar Sharmaa' returns 428 attestation_required with 0 model calls. Re-submitting with attest_not_firm_matter=true is allowed, the row has possible_attested=true, and the partner research report lists it under the associate.
- Unit: citation_spans and lookup_authorities_local make 0 network calls (socket patched to raise). An Indian Kanoon id not in ik_documents gives key_resolved=false. ik_documents rows are written only by thread-scoped calls: a test asserts that general_research case-law search never inserts.
- Unit: research_scope.decide is a pure function; a table test covers every (band, class, span resolution, own-matter) combination, and the out_of_scope text is asserted to match the table: only key_resolved, non-own-matter spans exempt private Strong hits.
- Round-5 tests retained: classify_party fixtures at 100%; research_private set by a partner (an associate gets 403); thread-scoped case-law search with consent_missing returning 409 and 0 calls; 'Move to matter' creates a new row and leaves the refused row unchanged (chain verifies); the speech consent gate, WebRTC, telephony DTMF, the WhatsApp voice note before YES, TTS blocked; PermitRequired, the StreamPermit sentinel and the CI grep; the identifier refusal, the length limits and the 422 cases; research-row visibility; and every round-3 resolver, masking, ledger-immutability and verify test.

### Still blocking

- The only way to exempt a Strong private firm-party hit inside a case title is key_resolved. In this repository, key resolution cannot succeed for the citations Indian lawyers actually use. legal_authorities holds only Supreme Court judgments, and scripts/ingest_sc_judgments.py writes citation_keys only from the dataset's S.C.R. report citation and INSC neutral citation (authority_row: keys from `citation` and `case_id`). Three consequences follow. (1) An SCC citation, the dominant way SC judgments are cited, never matches. The hint 'add its citation, e.g. (<year>) <vol> SCC <page>' and the acceptance-test fixture '(2019) 4 SCC 123' describe an exemption that does not exist in production. (2) INSC neutral citations exist only from 2023 onwards. (3) No High Court judgment can be key-resolved at all, whether cited as AIR, SCC OnLine or an HC reporter. The ik_documents path works only after a thread-scoped search has already stored that document. In practice, a lawyer researching an unrelated reported judgment whose party shares a common name with a firm client (Ramesh Kumar, Sunil Sharma) is left with one option: 'Move to matter'. Test (i), 'CNR, or case number and court, equals a court_cases row of M', has no data to run on. legal_authorities (migration 008) has no CNR or case-number column (only title, citation, neutral_citation, decision_date, citation_keys and name_tokens), and the proposed ik_documents stores only doc_id, title_tokens, court and decision_date. In practice the only own-matter test is (ii), the same party pair with a decision date on or after M's opening date. The commonest Indian engagement pattern is a client who arrives after losing below. The firm opens appeal matter M after the High Court or Sessions judgment 'State of Rajasthan v. Ramesh Kumar Sharma' was decided. That judgment is key_resolved (in legal_authorities, or in ik_documents because the associate had already searched it inside M), and its party pair equals M's. It predates M's opening, so it is treated as not the firm's matter. (b) Tag every ik_documents row with the thread that persisted it, and treat a doc first persisted from matter M as own-matter for M. (c) Either add cnr and case_number columns where the data exists, or delete test (i) and its acceptance test, which needs a CNR column on the fixture authority that the schema doesn't have.
- The own-matter test and the advertised citation remedy depend on data the index does not contain. legal_authorities (008) has no cnr, case_number or court-case columns, and scripts/ingest_sc_judgments.py writes citation_keys only from the S.C.R. citation and the INSC neutral id. Change the hint to the formats that actually resolve (S.C.R., INSC neutral citation, or an Indian Kanoon link already in ik_documents). Rewrite the fixtures to use keys in the form the ingest script produces.

proposal.out_of_scope:
Untested law: whether an Indian court will treat AI-assisted work as protected under BSA ss.132-134 or BCI Rule 17. Software can produce evidence, not privilege.

Raw audio and images from the OCR vision fallback cannot be masked. We gate them behind a matter and consent, ledger them and disclose them; we cannot remove them.

What vendors do with the data rests on their contracts. We record those contracts; we cannot enforce them.

Names, places and dates are not masked, by design.

General-research attribution is best effort, and its limits are these:
- The party scan only knows parties already in the firm's index.
- An institutional litigant (government, PSU, bank, insurer, listed company) that is also a firm client is logged in general research, not refused, unless the firm marks it 'private for research'.
- A case title naming a private firm party is exempt only when it carries a reporter or neutral citation, or a stored Indian Kanoon document reference, that resolves to a reported judgment which is not the firm's own matter. This is stricter than before: a lawyer researching a High Court judgment cited only by name, where a party shares a name with a firm client, must add the citation or run the question in a matter. We accept that friction.
- A misspelling below the Strong band is not refused. It needs an attestation, which is recorded and reported (see step 4).
Choosing the right scope stays the lawyer's professional responsibility. Per-user reporting makes misuse visible, not impossible.

A database superuser can still tamper with rows. The hash chain makes that detectable, not impossible. We will not claim 'privileged by design'.
proposal.what_the_system_does:
Steps 1-3 and 5-8 from round 4 are unchanged: the guarded_call and open_stream choke points, the StreamPermit, the CI grep, the ai_route resolvers, the speech consent gate, firm_internal, segment tagging, the hash-chained ledger and ALLOWED_AI_HOSTS. The scope resolution of /caselaw/search?thread_id=T from round 5 is also unchanged.

4) General-research pre-checks, revised. They run in this order; any refusal makes 0 processor calls.
- (a) Limits: one typed prompt of at most 1,500 characters (200 for a case-law query). document_id, attachments and memory return 422.
- (b) assert_masked on the raw prompt. Any identifier refuses with 'unmasked_identifier'.
- (c) citation_spans(db, text), local only. It reuses citation_service._extract and case_lookups to find every 'X v. Y' / 'vs' / 'versus' / 'बनाम' span and every reporter or neutral citation. Each span gets a resolution:
  - key_resolved=true when a reporter or neutral citation inside or immediately after the span matches legal_authorities.citation_keys, AND that row's name_tokens contain the tokens of both sides of the span;
  - or when an Indian Kanoon document id or URL in the span is present in the persisted table ik_documents (doc_id, title_tokens, court, decision_date). Rows in that table are written only by earlier thread-scoped searches and citation checks, and the stored title must contain both sides;
  - name_resolved=true for a name-only match (the existing subset match).
  The live Indian Kanoon call in lookup_authorities is not used here: a new lookup_authorities_local() reads only the local tables, and a test patches the socket to prove it.
- (d) conflict_service.scan_text(org_id, text) gives each hit with its band (exact, strong or possible), party_class, matter ids and the span it falls in.
- (e) Decision table, in code (research_scope.decide, pure and table-tested):
  1. An Exact identifier hit anywhere refuses with names_party.
  2. An institutional hit allows, counted in institutional_hits, unless research_private is set.
  3. A Strong hit of class individual or private_company:
     - outside any span, refuses with names_party;
     - inside an unresolved or name_resolved span, refuses with names_party, whatever the class of the other side. This is the fix: name-only resolution is not enough, because common Indian names collide with unrelated reported cases;
     - inside a key_resolved span, allows, counted in citation_hits, unless the resolved judgment is the firm's own matter (rule 4).
  4. Own-matter test for a key_resolved span: the judgment is treated as firm matter M if (i) its CNR, or its case number and court, equals a court_cases row of M; or (ii) its party pair equals M's party pair (same normalisation as conflict matching) and its decision date is on or after M's opening date. Then it refuses with names_party, citing M (own_matter_judgment).
  5. A Possible-band private hit:
     - inside any span, requires attest_not_firm_matter=true on a re-submit. The ledger stores possible_attested=true and the hit's party_index id (never the text), and the partner's research report lists every attestation by user;
     - outside spans, allows, counted in possible_party_hits.
  The refusal names the matter title only if the caller can SELECT that thread; otherwise it names the responsible lawyer.
- (f) No consent check in general research, because refusal keeps firm matters out of it. The ledger row records matter_kind='general_research', user_id, institutional_hits, citation_hits, possible_party_hits, possible_attested and refusal_reason.

Refused rows are written with no prompt text. 'Move to matter' creates a new request under the thread scope, with T's RLS check and consent rule; it never re-labels the refused row.

Party classes, classify_party, data/institutional_parties.yaml, research_private and party_class_history are unchanged from round 5. Research answers are never written to thread memory.

proposal.why_incumbents_fail_and_this_wont:
Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI send raw client text under zero-retention contracts. Nothing ties a call to a lawyer, a matter and a consent, and they do no Indian identifier masking. Transcription tools record from the first second. Indian legal-GPT apps have no processor register, no consent gate and no per-user research record.

Ours puts every processor, speech included, behind one scope resolver, consent check and hash-chained ledger. The research lane follows how Indian research actually reads ('Union of India v. ...', 'State of ...', SBI, LIC, cited reported judgments) without opening a back door: a firm's own unreported case title, which is the commonest shape ('State of <S> v. <our client>'), is steered back to its matter, and so is a reported judgment that is the firm's own matter. The exemption is a deterministic citation-key match, not a name guess.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Turning an AI policy into enforced settings inside the firm's tool. Producing a filing-ready Verification Record (each citation, its machine status, who confirmed it and when) that a partner signs and that can be annexed or shown to a court. Generating a client AI-use disclosure from real usage data rather than boilerplate. Making the sanctioned tool the convenient one without opening a new unchecked answer path.

### What it can't fix

We cannot stop a lawyer opening ChatGPT on a personal phone. Shadow AI is reduced only by making the sanctioned tool convenient and safe, and by attestation, not by surveilling personal devices (which would itself raise DPDP and employment problems). Whether a court accepts our record format is up to that court. We do not decide whether a citation supports a proposition. That is P12's verifier and the lawyer's judgment, so the record states what was machine-checked and what a human confirmed, and never certifies correctness. We make no latency promise for Quick ask, because the check runs before the answer is shown.

### What the user sees

Owners get a 'Firm AI Policy' page (in /safety) with switches, not a PDF:
- which features are allowed (live consultation, drafting, web research, WhatsApp intake, Quick ask);
- whether client consent is required before AI (shared with P20);
- whether drafts with any citation not grounded / known_case / statute can be exported;
- whether paralegal-generated drafts need partner approval;
- who may export to a court.
Each member accepts the policy text once, and again on each new version, and the acceptance is recorded.

Every draft has a 'Verification' panel. It lists each citation found by citation_service with its status (grounded / known_case / statute / repealed / invalid / unverified), and a per-citation 'I have read this authority' tick that records the lawyer and time. Export and court-bundle buttons stay disabled until the policy conditions are met, with the exact reason shown. 'Download Verification Record' produces a one-page PDF/DOCX annexure.

Per matter, 'Client AI disclosure' produces a letter in English or Hindi. It lists which AI functions were used, the processors involved and what was masked, and states that a named advocate reviewed the output. The firm edits the letter and sends it themselves.

A 'Quick ask' box on every page is labelled 'Internal research aid, not for clients or court'. The answer appears once checked, with authorities already marked (green known_case / statute / grounded, amber repealed with the new-code equivalent, red [unverified]). A disclaimer is appended when the answer reads as advice or a guarantee. 'Copy' copies the annotated text, markers included. 'Open in Studio' moves it into a draft, where the full Verification panel applies.

### What the system does

1) New table `org_ai_policy` holds versioned policy JSON plus a text body; past versions are append-only. `policy_acceptances` records user, version and accepted_at. Policy changes go through the existing approvals flow (safety_service maker-checker).

2) Enforcement is deterministic, in FastAPI dependencies. `require_policy(feature)` is added to the drafting, consultation, research, WhatsApp and quick-ask routers. A disabled feature returns 403 with the policy clause. A member who has not accepted the current version gets 428 'accept policy'.

3) Verification state lives in a new table `citation_confirmations` (draft_id, citation_key normalized by citation_service, machine_status, confirmed_by, confirmed_at, note) together with the draft text hash. Confirmations lapse when the draft text changes, as approved_by does in migration 013.

4) Export gate in the drafting_engine export:
- Every citation in the current text must have a machine_status in policy.allowed_statuses or a human confirmation.
- invalid citations can never be confirmed (a hard block, consistent with invariant 3).
- approved_by must be set by a role the policy permits.
- Otherwise export returns 409 with the list of blocking citations.

5) The Verification Record generator (pdf_service plus python-docx) is a pure template over citation_confirmations, citation_service statuses, approved_by and the P20 ledger rows for the draft. Its footer carries the P20 hash chain.

6) The disclosure letter is a fixed bilingual template filled from ai_use_ledger aggregates for the matter. No LLM writes it, so it cannot overstate or understate use.

7) Quick ask uses the same checked path as the drafter (fixes objection 1). A new shared function `services/reply_finalizer.finalize_reply(text, sources, lookup)`, extracted from node_drafter's post-processing so there is one implementation, runs in order:
- (a) citation_service.case_lookups + lookup_authorities;

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Enterprise tools log prompts for IT security, not for the supervising partner or the court. None produces a per-filing record of which citations were checked by whom, and none ties export to that record. Their quick-chat panes answer without any citation check, which is how fabricated authorities reach filings. Clio surveys show 53% of firms have no AI policy, because a policy is a document nobody can enforce.

Ours is settings that block actions, plus a record generated from the same checks that blocked or allowed them. Even the convenience box runs the same citation and UPL checks as the drafter, so the easiest path is also a checked one. Small Indian firms get this at chamber price, not as an enterprise governance add-on. - The 3-second promise is dropped. The answer is returned only after the check completes, so no unmarked text reaches the screen or clipboard, and latency is measured, not promised.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Indian coverage where checks and drafting actually happen. Index High Court judgments from open data and tribunal orders through Indian Kanoon. Recognise Indian HC and tax reporter formats. Replace the 22-row IPC/CrPC/IEA correspondence table and the max_section counts with the official correspondence tables and exact section lists from India Code. Add priority state acts and the 1961/2025 Income-tax Acts. Make code defaults date-aware the right way: substantive defaults from the offence date, procedural and evidence defaults from the date the proceeding was instituted.

### What it can't fix

Most district court judgments are not published in any open corpus, and there is no official eCourts API (we never bypass the captcha). Divergent High Court views on straddling IPC/BNSS proceedings are law to be argued, not a lookup: we surface them as notes from the knowledge base, not as a rule. State law is added act by act, not 'all of it' at once.

### What the user sees

Citations to HC judgments ('2024:DHC:1234', 'AIR 2019 Bom 12', '2023 SCC OnLine Del 456', 'ILR', '(2019) 414 ITR 1', '[2020] 117 taxmann.com 45') appear in the ledger instead of slipping through. 'Section 3 of the Maharashtra Rent Control Act' shows 'known act, section exists' instead of 'not checked'. A criminal matter has two dates: 'Date of offence' and 'Date the FIR, complaint or proceeding began'. Drafts then default to the offence code (BNS or IPC) from the first date and the procedure and evidence codes (BNSS/CrPC, BSA/IEA) from the second. When the second date is missing, or the dates straddle 1 July 2024, the draft shows the note 'Transition: check s.531 BNSS; High Courts differ on straddling cases' instead of silently picking a code. The bail workflow asks for both dates. /about states coverage: which courts and acts are indexed, and as of when.

### What the system does

1. scripts/ingest_hc_judgments.py indexes metadata from the AWS Open Data bucket indian-high-court-judgments (Dattam Labs, 25 HCs, CC BY 4.0, Parquet metadata, quarterly) into legal_authorities: court, neutral citation keys, name_tokens, and separate petitioner and respondent fields for P12. Full text for chosen courts and years goes into judgment_texts. The script is resumable via external_id. 2. Tribunals: an Indian Kanoon doctypes filter (ITAT, NCLAT, CESTAT, NCDRC and others) in authority_resolver, with the cache. 3. New citation_service patterns for HC neutral citations (court-specific regexes from a data table), state reporters, ILR and ITR/taxmann/GSTL, plus the P03 catch-all. 4. scripts/ingest_india_code.py pulls each registry act's section list from India Code (government text), including the priority state acts and ITA_1961/ITA_2025, into a shared statutes table: act key, section ids including lettered and omitted ones, and section text. max_section becomes a fallback only. 5. Correspondence: the official MHA/BPR&D BNS-IPC, BNSS-CrPC and BSA-IEA tables are loaded into checksummed data files that jurisdiction_service reads. CORRESPONDENCE_CAVEAT stays until a lawyer signs off on the files. 6. Dates: migration 014 adds offence_date, offence_end_date, proceeding_instituted_on and proceeding_kind (fir|complaint|chargesheet|trial|appeal|other) to case_threads and court_cases. A single pure function, criminal_codes(dates), shared with P03's transition_rules, returns {substantive, procedural, evidence, notes}. substantive = BNS if offence_date is on or after 1 July 2024, else IPC, with a note when the offence spans the date. procedural = BNSS and evidence = BSA if proceeding_instituted_on is on or after 1 July 2024. If it is earlier, procedural = CrPC and evidence = IEA, with the s.531(2) BNSS / s.170(2) BSA savings note. If it is missing, there is no procedural default: drafts use the placeholder [●procedure code: enter FIR/complaint date●] and show the 'check s.531' note. Where the offence is before and the proceeding after 1 July 2024, the default is BNSS with a note on divergent HC views. The exceptions table (s.479 BNSS for all undertrials, SC Aug 2024) overrides. 7. workflow_service bail is changed to use criminal_codes(): it asks for proceeding_instituted_on as well as offence_date, and the CrPC/BNSS choice of bail, default-bail and undertrial provisions follows the proceeding date, not the offence date. Today it keys the whole procedure on offence_date (CRIMINAL_CODES_START at line 21 and around line 245), which is the bug the objection describes.

### Where it is built

scripts/ingest_sc_judgments.py (pattern for the HC script), supabase/migrations/008_shared_legal_corpus.sql (legal_authorities, shared corpus), app/services/citation_service.py ACTS and patterns, app/services/jurisdiction_service.py IPC_TO_BNS and related tables, app/services/workflow_service.py bail (switch to criminal_codes(); add the proceeding_instituted_on Field). New: scripts/ingest_hc_judgments.py, scripts/ingest_india_code.py, app/data/correspondence/*.csv, app/services/criminal_codes.py (shared with P03), migration 014 statutes table (shared, read-only) and the date columns.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis have little Indian primary law, and their Indian users are top-tier firms doing SC/HC work. SCC Online and Manupatra cover SC/HC well, but their AI only searches: it doesn't do date-aware code selection or check a draft. Generic AI picks a single 'new code or old code' by one date and gets straddling matters wrong. We build on open government and CC BY data (India Code, SC and HC open buckets), which is cheap to keep current, and wire coverage straight into the citation checker. Code selection follows the statutory structure: substantive by offence date, procedure and evidence by proceeding date, with the savings provisions and SC exceptions as notes.

### Safeguards

The shared corpus and statutes table are written only by service-role ingest scripts (invariant 2) and are read-only to users. CC BY 4.0 attribution for the HC data is added to /about beside the SC credit. Government statute text is public; no proprietary reporter content is copied. The correspondence and transition data files stay labelled indicative until a named lawyer signs them off, with the sign-off recorded in the repo. When the procedural code is uncertain, drafts show a placeholder rather than guessing a code into a filing.

### How the panel's objections were answered

offence_date and proceeding_instituted_on (with proceeding_kind) are now stored separately. One shared function, criminal_codes(), picks substantive defaults (BNS/IPC) from offence_date only, and procedural and evidence defaults (BNSS/CrPC, BSA/IEA) from proceeding_instituted_on. With no proceeding date, it gives no procedural default: drafts get a [●…●] placeholder and a 'transition: check s.531' note. Straddling dates get the savings or divergent-HC notes, and s.479 BNSS is applied to all undertrials through an exceptions table. Tests cover both straddling cases (2023 offence with a 2024 FIR, and 2023 offence with a 2023 FIR) and the missing-date case. I also found that the existing workflow_service bail pack picks the whole procedure by offence date (CRIMINAL_CODES_START, around line 245), the bug the objection describes. This proposal switches it to criminal_codes() and adds the proceeding-date field, with bail tests for both straddling cases.

### Acceptance tests

- Extraction recall: a fixture of 80 Indian citation strings across SC, HC, tribunal and tax reporters is 100% extracted (each yields a ledger item, resolved or flagged)
- HC ingest: a fixture Parquet row gives a legal_authorities row with the correct neutral key and petitioner/respondent fields; re-running inserts no duplicates
- Statutes table: 'Section 124B IPC' is invalid even though 124 <= 511; 'Section 498A IPC' is valid; 'Section 3 Maharashtra Rent Control Act' is statute, not 'not checked'
- Correspondence checksum: jurisdiction_service refuses a modified file without an updated checksum; IPC 420 maps to BNS 318(4) from the file
- criminal_codes straddle 1: offence 2023-11-10, FIR 2024-08-14 gives substantive IPC, procedural BNSS, evidence BSA, with a divergent-HC note
- criminal_codes straddle 2: offence 2023-11-10, FIR 2023-11-12 gives IPC/CrPC/IEA with the s.531(2)/s.170(2) savings note
- Offence 2024-09-03 with no proceeding date gives substantive BNS, no procedural default, and the 'check s.531' note; a generated draft contains the [●procedure code…●] placeholder, not a CrPC or BNSS section
- Bail workflow: offence 2023-11-10 with FIR 2024-08-14 suggests s. 480/483/482 BNSS and s. 187(3) BNSS (not CrPC); offence 2023-11-10 with FIR 2023-11-12 suggests CrPC provisions with the savings note; s. 479 BNSS is offered for an undertrial in either case (exception table)
- A Kerala HC neutral citation resolves against the fixture HC index; an unknown one is flagged, not passed

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Both P14 and this proposal rewrite workflow_service._bail. Implement one shared criminal_codes() plus the P14 punishment-table fix once.
- The HC open-data bucket's coverage and licence per court should be recorded per row on /about, since coverage varies widely by High Court.
- Record the India Code terms of use and the date each act was pulled on /about, next to the CC BY credits.
- India Code has no API. The ingest script depends on scraping its HTML, so pin the parser to fixtures and alert when an act page changes shape.
- Unify proceeding_instituted_on with P14's fir_date/investigation_started_on before both change _bail.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Software can turn a vernacular record (FIR, deposition, order sheet, revenue record), scanned or typed, into an English draft translation aligned segment by segment. The segmentation splits real sentences, including Hindi and Marathi typed with '.' in place of '।', and doesn't break Indian legal abbreviations. Deterministic checks catch the silent, fluent errors: dropped or merged segments; changed numbers, dates, amounts, FIR/cheque/khasra references and section numbers; lost negation; operative legal terms rendered outside an approved glossary; OCR words below a confidence threshold. A named human reviewer must clear every segment before a true-translation export, with a certificate that the human signs. Cost drops because the translator becomes a reviewer of flagged segments, and approved segments are reused from translation memory.

### What it can't fix

AI translation has no legal status: certification attaches to a named person, and the tool certifies nothing. It can't decide which courts accept which translators, or replace official translator panels. It can't reliably read hard handwriting (Shikasta Urdu, faded carbon FIRs): those pages are flagged for a human to type or correct. It can't convert Vikram Samvat or Fasli dates; they are flagged as unconverted. It can't judge meaning beyond the invariants and glossary, so a human still reads every segment. No abbreviation lexicon or verb list is complete. A rare single-akshara abbreviation outside a dotted run, or a sentence ending in an unlisted single-akshara word placed right before another single akshara and '.', can still be split or merged wrongly. The reviewer fixes it with merge or split, and the fix is learnt for that org. Languages without a Tesseract pack, or not yet evaluated with the model, are out of scope.

### What the user sees

Studio has a new 'Translate record' tab. The advocate uploads the vernacular PDF or image and picks the source language (auto-detected from script) and the target (English). They get a two-column view: numbered source segments, with OCR words below 60% confidence underlined, beside the draft English. Segments carry flag chips: 'amount 2,50,000 missing in English', 'negation नहीं not reflected', 'operative term बहाली: expected reinstatement, got re-establishment', 'section 302 changed', 'low OCR confidence', 'segment not translated', 'long segment: check split'. Reviewers can merge two adjacent segments, or split one at a chosen point. A merge across an abbreviation offers 'remember भा.दं.सं. as an abbreviation for this firm'. A split after a word offers 'remember <word> as sentence-final'. Reviewers tick each segment as reviewed. A progress bar shows reviewed/total and the open blocking flags. Export (DOCX/PDF) unlocks at 100% reviewed with no open blocking flags. It ends with a translator's certificate naming the reviewer, the date, the source SHA-256, the glossary version, the segmenter version and a machine-assistance disclosure.

### What the system does

1. Text. ocr_service runs with OCR_LANGUAGES set per job and keeps per-word confidences. The Vision fallback is off by default for translation jobs and can be turned on per job. 2. Segmentation (app/services/segmenter.py, deterministic, no model). Tokens and aksharas are extended grapheme clusters from the `regex` module (\X), with an explicit virama-join rule so conjuncts such as श्री and क्ष count as one akshara whatever the Unicode version. (a) Protect spans with sentinels: lexicon abbreviations (data/segmentation/abbrev_{hi,mr,en}.json plus org_abbreviations); dotted-initial runs, i.e. regex (?:A\.\s?){2,} where A is a single akshara or Latin letter (भा.दं.सं., द.प्र.सं., रा. कु., I.P.C., P.S.); honorifics (Sh., Smt., Dr., Km., श्री., श्रीमती., कु.); legal shorthand (u/s, r/w, w/o, s/o, d/o, Vs., बनाम); numeric patterns (302/34, No. 123/2025, क्र. 45/2024, 12.03.2025, १२.०३.२०२५, Rs. 2,50,000.00, रु. 2,50,000/-, decimals). A lexicon honorific never joins a dotted run with the token before it, so 'है. श्री. रमेश' does not make है part of a run. (b) Hard terminators: split on ।, ॥, '?' and '!' followed by whitespace or end of text. (c) '.' followed by whitespace, in Indic scripts (Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam): split, unless the previous token is inside a protected span from (a). There is no blanket single-akshara exclusion. A lone single akshara + '.' blocks a split only when (i) it is in the lexicon, (ii) it belongs to a dotted run, or (iii) the next token is itself a single akshara + '.' that is not a lexicon honorific. (d) Sentence-final whitelist, data/segmentation/final_verbs_{hi,mr}.json: a closed list of finite verbs and auxiliaries. Hindi: है, हैं, था, थी, थे, हो, हूँ, गया, गई, गयी, गए, दिया, किया, लिया, रहा, रही, रहे, सका, सकी, चुका. Marathi: आहे, आहेत, होता, होती, होते, होतो, केले, केला, केली, गेला, गेली, गेले, आले, आला, आली. A token on the list followed by '.' and whitespace always splits and overrides (iii). Each entry has a source note. Orgs can add entries via reviewer splits. (e) Latin text keeps the English rules: '.' splits when the previous token is not protected, not a single letter or a number, and the next token starts with an uppercase letter, a digit or an opening quote. (f) Split at numbered paragraph markers at line start ('1.', '(i)', 'क.', '१.') and at OCR table row boundaries. (g) Never split inside a protected span. A segment over 600 characters is flagged 'long segment', not force-split. (h) Unmask the sentinels. Each segment gets a stable id and a source sha256. The segmenter is lossless: the concatenated segments equal the normalised source. SEGMENTER_VERSION is stored on the job. 3. Reviewer split/merge rewrites boundaries, re-hashes, clears reviewed_by on the affected segments, is audited, and can add an org_abbreviations or org_final_words row (RLS by org). 4. Translation memory: an exact normalised match with an approved segment is reused with no model call. 5. Translation: masked segments go to Sonnet in batches as JSON {id, text}, with the batch's glossary terms in a cached system block. The ids returned must match exactly. A parse failure gets one retry, after which the segment is flagged untranslated. 6. Deterministic checks (translation_check.py): id coverage; numbers (Unicode digits through unicodedata.digit, Hindi/Marathi number words, unparseable ones flagged); dates; references; sections (धारा/कलम N must survive as s. N, and IPC must not be 'updated' to BNS); negation; glossary (blocking for operative terms); the length-ratio band. 7. Review gate: any change to a target clears reviewed_by. Export returns 409 until every segment is reviewed and every blocking flag is resolved or overridden with a reason, which is audited. 8. Export through the drafting_engine DOCX/PDF with the certificate. Approved segments feed translation_memory.

### Where it is built

Extend app/services/ocr_service.py (per-word confidence spans, layout lines, per-job language), app/services/draft_check.py (shared extractors move to app/services/invariants.py for P24), app/services/citation_service.py (धारा/कलम extraction), app/services/evidence_service.py (Devanagari-aware normalisation), app/services/drafting_engine.py and pdf_service.py (Indic fonts, shaped PDF), app/services/queue_service.py and app/worker.py (task_translate_record), Dockerfile (tesseract-ocr-hin/mar/tam/ben/guj/pan/kan/mal/tel/ori/urd, fonts-noto-core), requirements (`regex` for \X). New: app/services/segmenter.py; data/segmentation/abbrev_{hi,mr,en}.json and final_verbs_{hi,mr}.json (each entry with a source note); tests/fixtures/segmentation/ (20 typed-'.' and '।' records with hand-segmented gold); app/services/translation_service.py; app/services/translation_check.py; app/routers/translations.py (with split/merge endpoints); data/glossary/legal_glossary_hi_en.json. Migration supabase/migrations/015_translations.sql: translation_jobs (segmenter_version), translation_segments, glossary_terms (org_id NULL shared, read-only), translation_memory, org_abbreviations, org_final_words, with RLS by org. Frontend: a Translate tab in frontend/src/app/studio/page.tsx.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

SUVAS and Anuvaad are court-internal reading aids for judgments, with no per-segment checks on an advocate's own FIR. Google, DeepL and ChatGPT produce fluent output with no record that every segment was translated or that the amounts, dates and operative terms survived. Generic splitters (spaCy, NLTK, ICU) either break on 'भा.दं.सं.' and 'P.S.' or, with naive abbreviation guards, never split typed-'.' Hindi at है/था. Either way, the alignment-based checks built on them fail. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI are English-first and don't OCR Hindi FIRs. Here, segmentation protects dotted runs and lexicon abbreviations, always splits after known sentence-final verbs, is lossless by property test, and is measured against hand-segmented gold. Trust comes from deterministic invariants, and nothing exports until a named human has reviewed every segment.

### Safeguards

Every AI translation stays a draft until a named human reviews each segment. Only that person signs the certificate, and the export discloses machine assistance. Segment boundary changes are audited and clear review, and the segmenter version is recorded so a later rule change can't silently re-cut an approved job. PII is masked before the model. Vision is off by default for translation jobs and logged when turned on. Records remain privileged work product: org-scoped RLS, and no translation memory, learnt abbreviations or learnt final words are shared across orgs. Only the read-only shared glossary, seed lexicons and verb lists are common. Blocking-flag overrides need a reason and are audited. Approval points: the reviewer approves segments; an owner/partner approves operative firm glossary entries.

### How the panel's objections were answered

The single-akshara rule (both objections). The blanket 'previous token is not a single akshara' condition is gone for Indic scripts. A '.' followed by whitespace now splits unless the previous token is protected. A lone single akshara blocks the split only if it is (i) in the abbreviation lexicon, (ii) part of a dotted-initial run ((?:akshara\.\s?){2,}, so रा. कु. and भा.दं.सं. are protected), or (iii) followed by another single akshara + '.' that is not an honorific. A closed whitelist of Hindi and Marathi sentence-final verbs and auxiliaries (है, हैं, था, थी, थे, हो, गया, गई, गए ... आहे, होता, होते, केले ...) always permits the split and overrides (iii). That also covers 'दर्ज है. श्री. रमेश', where the next token is an honorific. Aksharas are measured as grapheme clusters with a virama-join rule, so conjuncts such as श्री count correctly. Fixtures added: 'वह घर पर था. पुलिस आई.' -> 2, 'आरोपी फरार है. तलाश जारी है.' -> 2, 'श्री. रा. कु. शर्मा' -> 1, 'मामला दर्ज है. श्री. रमेश ने बताया.' -> 2, and two Marathi cases. A Hypothesis test asserts that N verb-final clauses joined with '. ' give N segments. A gold corpus of 10 typed-'.' and 10 '।' records must reach boundary F1 ≥ 0.97 with no spurious long segments, so typed-'.' FIRs can't collapse into blobs that hide dropped sentences from the coverage checks.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_segmenter.py, kept as one segment: 'धारा 302/34 भा.दं.सं. के अंतर्गत प्रकरण दर्ज किया गया।'; 'FIR No. 123/2025, P.S. Kotwali, u/s 420 IPC was registered on 12.03.2025.'; 'Smt. Sunita Devi w/o Sh. Ram Lal'; 'रु. 2,50,000/- दिनांक १२.०३.२०२५ को दिए गए।'; 'अपराध क्र. 45/2024 थाना कोतवाली द.प्र.सं. की धारा 154 के तहत'; 'श्री. रा. कु. शर्मा'
- Splits on typed '.' in Indic text: 'आरोपी फरार है. तलाश जारी है.' -> 2; 'वह घर पर था. पुलिस आई.' -> 2; 'मामला दर्ज है. श्री. रमेश ने बताया.' -> 2 (an honorific after a final verb does not block the split); Marathi 'तो घरी होता. पोलीस आले.' -> 2 and 'आरोपी फरार आहे. शोध सुरू आहे.' -> 2; 'धारा 302/34 भा.दं.सं. के तहत मामला दर्ज किया गया। आरोपी फरार है।' -> 2; 'The accused absconded. Search is on.' -> 2; numbered paragraphs '1. ... 2. ...' at line start are split
- Akshara handling: श्री, क्ष and त्र each count as one akshara under \X plus the virama rule (a unit test over 30 conjuncts); 'रा. कु.' is detected as a dotted run and 'था.' alone is not
- Property tests (Hypothesis): (a) joining N random Hindi/Marathi clauses, each ending in a whitelist verb, with '. ' gives exactly N segments; (b) inserting lexicon abbreviations and dotted runs at random positions never produces a split inside them; (c) the segmenter is lossless and deterministic (same ids and hashes on re-run)
- Gold corpus: over the 20 fixture records (10 typed with '.', 10 with '।'), boundary F1 against the hand-segmented gold is at least 0.97, and no segment over 600 characters appears where the gold has none
- Reviewer merge across an unknown abbreviation clears reviewed_by on both segments, writes audit_logs, and with 'remember' adds an org_abbreviations row; re-segmenting then keeps the span together for that org only. A reviewer split after an unlisted verb with 'remember' adds an org_final_words row that takes effect for that org only
- Checks: 'रु. 2,50,000' and '१२/०३/२०२५' translated as 25,000 raises an amount flag; the correct output raises none
- Coverage: a mock missing id 7 flags 'not translated'; a response that merges 3 and 4 flags both; an extra id is rejected
- Glossary: 'नौकरी पर बहाली' rendered as 're-establishment' raises a blocking operative-term flag; 'reinstatement' passes
- Negation: 'उसने पैसे नहीं दिए' rendered as 'he paid the money' raises a negation flag
- Sections: 'धारा 302' rendered as 's. 103 BNS' raises 'section changed'; 's. 302' passes
- Number words: 'पांच लाख रुपये' gives 500000; 'सवा पांच लाख' is flagged unparseable
- Review gate: export returns 409 with one unreviewed segment; an edit clears reviewed_by; an override without a reason is rejected, and one with a reason is audited
- The certificate names the reviewer, source SHA-256, glossary version and segmenter version, carries the disclosure, and never names the AI as translator
- Translation memory: a re-run on the same source makes zero model calls
- Masking: Aadhaar and phone numbers reach the mocked model only as placeholders; Vision is not called unless the job opted in
- Docker: 'tesseract --list-langs' includes hin, mar, tam, ben, urd
- PDF round trip: OCR of the bilingual PDF with tesseract hin reaches at least 95% character accuracy

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Many typists in Hindi-belt courts type the danda as ASCII '|' or 'l' (legacy-font habit), and some converted Kruti Dev text yields '|'. Treat a '|' surrounded by Devanagari as a hard terminator.
- The certificate should follow the target court's format: the Supreme Court and many High Courts expect the advocate's 'true translation' certification. Make the certificate text a per-court template instead of a single format.
- Urdu (Nastaliq) FIRs and revenue records are common in UP and J&K. State explicitly that urd OCR quality is not yet evaluated, even though the tesseract pack is installed.
- FIRs and depositions in sexual-offence, POCSO and juvenile matters name victims or children whose identity is protected (s.72 BNS, s.23 POCSO, s.74 JJ Act). PiiMasker keeps names, so these names would go to the model. Offer a per-job 'protected identity' option, on by default when the record's sections include those offences, that masks the victim's or child's names before translation and restores them only in the reviewed export.
- Courts differ on whose certification of a translation they accept: an official translator, an advocate-on-record, or a sworn translator. The export should take the target court's requirement from a court profile. It should not imply that the reviewer's certificate is acceptable everywhere.
- Masking runs before translation. Check that PiiMasker placeholders don't swallow tokens the invariant checks compare, such as long FIR or cheque numbers that look like account numbers. Otherwise the reference check passes vacuously on placeholders. Add a fixture where a 12-digit cheque number must survive as itself.
- Indian court tools such as Adalat AI, and Bhashini-based pipelines, already do vernacular-to-English drafts. The differentiator is the per-segment invariants, the review gate and the signed certificate, so marketing should lead with those, not with translation quality.
- Migration 015 is fine, but sequence it after the 014 collision is resolved.

The Vision fallback is off by default for translation jobs and can be turned on per job. 2. Segmentation (app/services/segmenter.py, deterministic, no model). Tokens and aksharas are extended grapheme clusters from the `regex` module (\X), with an explicit virama-join rule so conjuncts such as श्री and क्ष count as one akshara whatever the Unicode version. (a) Protect spans with sentinels: lexicon abbreviations (data/segmentation/abbrev_{hi,mr,en}.json plus org_abbreviations); dotted-initial runs, i.e. regex (?:A\.\s?){2,} where A is a single akshara or Latin letter (भा.दं.सं., द.प्र.सं., रा. कु., I.P.C., P.S.); honorifics (Sh., Smt., Dr., Km., श्री., श्रीमती., कु.); legal shorthand (u/s, r/w, w/o, s/o, d/o, Vs., बनाम); numeric patterns (302/34, No. 123/2025, क्र. 45/2024, 12.03.2025, १२.०३.२०२५, Rs. 2,50,000.00, रु. 2,50,000/-, decimals). A lexicon honorific never joins a dotted run with the token before it, so 'है. श्री. रमेश' does not make है part of a run. (b) Hard terminators: split on ।, ॥, '?' and '!' followed by whitespace or end of text. (c) '.' followed by whitespace, in Indic scripts (Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam): split, unless the previous token is inside a protected span from (a). There is no blanket single-akshara exclusion. A lone single akshara + '.' blocks a split only when (i) it is in the lexicon, (ii) it belongs to a dotted run, or (iii) the next token is itself a single akshara + '.' that is not a lexicon honorific. (d) Sentence-final whitelist, data/segmentation/final_verbs_{hi,mr}.json: a closed list of finite verbs and auxiliaries. Hindi: है, हैं, था, थी, थे, हो, हूँ, गया, गई, गयी, गए, दिया, किया, लिया, रहा, रही, रहे, सका, सकी, चुका. Marathi: आहे, आहेत, होता, होती, होते, होतो, केले, केला, केली, गेला, गेली, गेले, आले, आला, आली. A token on the list followed by '.' and whitespace always splits and overrides (iii). Each entry has a source note. Orgs can add entries via reviewer splits. (e) Latin text keeps the English rules: '.' splits when the previous token is not protected, not a single letter or a number, and the next token starts with an uppercase letter, a digit or an opening quote. (f) Split at numbered paragraph markers at line start ('1.', '(i)', 'क.', '१.') and at OCR table row boundaries. (g) Never split inside a protected span. A segment over 600 characters is flagged 'long segment', not force-split. (h) Unmask the sentinels. Each segment gets a stable id and a source sha256. The segmenter is lossless: the concatenated segments equal the normalised source. SEGMENTER_VERSION is stored on the job. 3. Reviewer split/merge rewrites boundaries, re-hashes, clears reviewed_by on the affected segments, is audited, and can add an org_abbreviations or org_final_words row (RLS by org). 4. Translation memory: an exact normalised match with an approved segment is reused with no model call. 5. Translation: masked segments go to Sonnet in batches as JSON {id, text}, with the batch's glossary terms in a cached system block. The ids returned must match exactly. A parse failure gets one retry, after which the segment is flagged untranslated. 6. Deterministic checks (translation_check.py): id coverage; numbers (Unicode digits through unicodedata.digit, Hindi/Marathi number words, unparseable ones flagged); dates; references; sections (धारा/कलम N must survive as s. N, and IPC must not be 'updated' to BNS); negation; glossary (blocking for operative terms); the length-ratio band. 7. Review gate: any change to a target clears reviewed_by. Export returns 409 until every segment is reviewed and every blocking flag is resolved or overridden with a reason, which is audited. 8. Export through the drafting_engine DOCX/PDF with the certificate. Approved segments feed translation_memory.
