proposal.why_incumbents_fail_and_this_wont: SUVAS and Anuvaad are court-internal reading aids for judgments, with no per-segment checks on an advocate's own FIR. Google, DeepL and ChatGPT produce fluent output with no record that every segment was translated or that the amounts, dates and operative terms survived. Generic splitters (spaCy, NLTK, ICU) either break on 'भा.दं.सं.' and 'P.S.' or, with naive abbreviation guards, never split typed-'.' Hindi at है/था. Either way, the alignment-based checks built on them fail. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI are English-first and don't OCR Hindi FIRs. Here, segmentation protects dotted runs and lexicon abbreviations, always splits after known sentence-final verbs, is lossless by property test, and is measured against hand-segmented gold. Trust comes from deterministic invariants, and nothing exports until a named human has reviewed every segment.
acceptance_tests: tests/test_segmenter.py, kept as one segment: 'धारा 302/34 भा.दं.सं. के अंतर्गत प्रकरण दर्ज किया गया।'; 'FIR No. 123/2025, P.S. Kotwali, u/s 420 IPC was registered on 12.03.2025.'; 'Smt. Sunita Devi w/o Sh. Ram Lal'; 'रु. 2,50,000/- दिनांक १२.०३.२०२५ को दिए गए।'; 'अपराध क्र. 45/2024 थाना कोतवाली द.प्र.सं. की धारा 154 के तहत'; 'श्री. रा. कु. शर्मा'

Splits on typed '.' in Indic text: 'आरोपी फरार है. तलाश जारी है.' -> 2; 'वह घर पर था. पुलिस आई.' -> 2; 'मामला दर्ज है. श्री. रमेश ने बताया.' -> 2 (an honorific after a final verb does not block the split); Marathi 'तो घरी होता. पोलीस आले.' -> 2 and 'आरोपी फरार आहे. शोध सुरू आहे.' -> 2; 'धारा 302/34 भा.दं.सं. के तहत मामला दर्ज किया गया। आरोपी फरार है।' -> 2; 'The accused absconded. Search is on.' -> 2; numbered paragraphs '1. ... 2. ...' at line start are split
Akshara handling: श्री, क्ष and त्र each count as one akshara under \X plus the virama rule (a unit test over 30 conjuncts); 'रा. कु.' is detected as a dotted run and 'था.' alone is not

Property tests (Hypothesis): (a) joining N random Hindi/Marathi clauses, each ending in a whitelist verb, with '. ' gives exactly N segments; (b) inserting lexicon abbreviations and dotted runs at random positions never produces a split inside them; (c) the segmenter is lossless and deterministic (same ids and hashes on re-run)

Gold corpus: over the 20 fixture records (10 typed with '.', 10 with '।'), boundary F1 against the hand-segmented gold is at least 0.97, and no segment over 600 characters appears where the gold has none

Reviewer merge across an unknown abbreviation clears reviewed_by on both segments, writes audit_logs, and with 'remember' adds an org_abbreviations row; re-segmenting then keeps the span together for that org only. A reviewer split after an unlisted verb with 'remember' adds an org_final_words row that takes effect for that org only
Checks: 'रु. 2,50,000' and '१२/०३/२०२५' translated as 25,000 raises an amount flag; the correct output raises none
Coverage: a mock missing id 7 flags 'not translated'; a response that merges 3 and 4 flags both; an extra id is rejected
Glossary: 'नौकरी पर बहाली' rendered as 're-establishment' raises a blocking operative-term flag; 'reinstatement' passes
Negation: 'उसने पैसे नहीं दिए' rendered as 'he paid the money' raises a negation flag
Sections: 'धारा 302' rendered as 's. 103 BNS' raises 'section changed'; 's. 302' passes
Number words: 'पांच लाख रुपये' gives 500000; 'सवा पांच लाख' is flagged unparseable
Review gate: export returns 409 with one unreviewed segment; an edit clears reviewed_by; an override without a reason is rejected, and one with a reason is audited
The certificate names the reviewer, source SHA-256, glossary version and segmenter version, carries the disclosure, and never names the AI as translator
Translation memory: a re-run on the same source makes zero model calls
Masking: Aadhaar and phone numbers reach the mocked model only as placeholders; Vision is not called unless the job opted in
Docker: 'tesseract --list-langs' includes hin, mar, tam, ben, urd
PDF round trip: OCR of the bilingual PDF with tesseract hin reaches at least 95% character accuracy
proposal.safeguards: Every AI translation stays a draft until a named human reviews each segment. Only that person signs the certificate, and the export discloses machine assistance. Segment boundary changes are audited and clear review, and the segmenter version is recorded so a later rule change can't silently re-cut an approved job. PII is masked before the model. Vision is off by default for translation jobs and logged when turned on. Records remain privileged work product: org-scoped RLS, and no translation memory, learnt abbreviations or learnt final words are shared across orgs. Only the read-only shared glossary, seed lexicons and verb lists are common. Blocking-flag overrides need a reason and are audited. Approval points: the reviewer approves segments; an owner/partner approves operative firm glossary entries.
proposal.answers_to_objections: The single-akshara rule (both objections). The blanket 'previous token is not a single akshara' condition is gone for Indic scripts. A '.' followed by whitespace now splits unless the previous token is protected. A lone single akshara blocks the split only if it is (i) in the abbreviation lexicon, (ii) part of a dotted-initial run ((?:akshara\.\s?){2,}, so रा. कु. and भा.दं.सं. are protected), or (iii) followed by another single akshara + '.' that is not an honorific. A closed whitelist of Hindi and Marathi sentence-final verbs and auxiliaries (है, हैं, था, थी, थे, हो, गया, गई, गए ... आहे, होता, होते, केले ...) always permits the split and overrides (iii). That also covers 'दर्ज है. श्री. रमेश', where the next token is an honorific. Aksharas are measured as grapheme clusters with a virama-join rule, so conjuncts such as श्री count correctly. Fixtures added: 'वह घर पर था. पुलिस आई.' -> 2, 'आरोपी फरार है. तलाश जारी है.' -> 2, 'श्री. रा. कु. शर्मा' -> 1, 'मामला दर्ज है. श्री. रमेश ने बताया.' -> 2, and two Marathi cases. A Hypothesis test asserts that N verb-final clauses joined with '. ' give N segments. A gold corpus of 10 typed-'.' and 10 '।' records must reach boundary F1 ≥ 0.97 with no spurious long segments, so typed-'.' FIRs can't collapse into blobs that hide dropped sentences from the coverage checks.

minor: Many typists in Hindi-belt courts type the danda as ASCII '|' or 'l' (legacy-font habit), and some converted Kruti Dev text yields '|'. Treat a '|' surrounded by Devanagari as a hard terminator.

The certificate should follow the target court's format: the Supreme Court and many High Courts expect the advocate's 'true translation' certification. Make the certificate text a per-court template instead of a single format.
Urdu (Nastaliq) FIRs and revenue records are common in UP and J&K. State explicitly that urd OCR quality is not yet evaluated, even though the tesseract pack is installed.

FIRs and depositions in sexual-offence, POCSO and juvenile matters name victims or children whose identity is protected (s.72 BNS, s.23 POCSO, s.74 JJ Act). PiiMasker keeps names, so these names would go to the model. Offer a per-job 'protected identity' option, on by default when the record's sections include those offences, that masks the victim's or child's names before translation and restores them only in the reviewed export.

Courts differ on whose certification of a translation they accept: an official translator, an advocate-on-record, or a sworn translator. The export should take the target court's requirement from a court profile. It should not imply that the reviewer's certificate is acceptable everywhere.

Masking runs before translation. Check that PiiMasker placeholders don't swallow tokens the invariant checks compare, such as long FIR or cheque numbers that look like account numbers. Otherwise the reference check passes vacuously on placeholders. Add a fixture where a 12-digit cheque number must survive as itself.

Indian court tools such as Adalat AI, and Bhashini-based pipelines, already do vernacular-to-English drafts. The differentiator is the per-segment invariants, the review gate and the signed certificate, so marketing should lead with those, not with translation quality.
Migration 015 is fine, but sequence it after the 014 collision is resolved.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Software can give the client a clause-by-clause or paragraph-by-paragraph rendering, in their own language, of the document they are about to sign or the order they received. Each part stays anchored to the English source, is checked by the P23 invariants engine, and is sent only after lawyer approval. It goes over a channel the client agreed to for that purpose, by a route WhatsApp accepts at that moment, and only through P33's outbound guard, under one template contract that P24 and P33 share as code. Before execution, the client can review each factual paragraph of an affidavit in their language and confirm or correct it, as an internal record for the lawyer, never the sworn interpreter endorsement. Software can also generate Hindi pleadings from fixed lawyer-written templates, and stop English/Hindi-only safety checks from silently passing AI replies in other Indian languages.

### What it can't fix

It can't make HCs or the SC accept vernacular pleadings. It can't guarantee the client understood: the log shows what was sent and what the client replied. It can't replace the read-over at execution or the interpreter's certificate. It can't help clients who can't read, beyond the in-person read-out and voice. It can't control Meta's template review, pricing or the 24-hour window. The linter enforces the documented and observed structural rules, but Meta can still reject, pause or recategorise a template, and then that route is unavailable. STT/TTS only work where Deepgram supports the language. Hindi templates come first, and Marathi, Tamil and others follow as lawyers write and approve them. P33 owns the outbound guard's policy (who may be messaged and why). The template contract module is co-owned, and P24 can't send if the guard refuses.

### What the user sees

Unchanged from round 5. Lawyer: 'Explain to client' in Studio, with the English clause on the left, an editable explanation in the client's language on the right, P23 flag chips and per-explanation approval. A character counter uses the per-language limit from the contract (for example '312 / 350'), and over-limit explanations are split at sentence boundaries into 4a/4b. The send panel shows consent status, the route ('will send as a chat message', 'will send as approved template client_explanation_v1 (Hindi)' or 'Can't send now: no approved template for Tamil'), and a read-only preview of the slots: office name, the document description built from the record ('विक्रय विलेख दिनांक 12 मार्च 2026') and the approved explanation. The Templates admin page lists the rows of template_registry with lint result, pinned-hash status, Meta status and the contract version 'wa-templates/1'. Pre-execution review sends one paragraph at a time and shows a confirmed / correction / no answer table. The export always shows the interpreter endorsement as [●…●], and the optional annexure is off by default. Client: the opt-in in their language, then the approved explanations as chat messages, template messages or a PDF.

### What the system does

1-4. Unchanged: core/language.py detection; the explanation pipeline (P23 segmenter, masking, cached instructions, translation_check, verify_output_safety); client_explanations with approvals that any edit clears; client_channel_consents with can_send(thread, purpose). 5. One shared contract, as code: app/contracts/wa_templates.py, CONTRACT_VERSION = 'wa-templates/1'. Both P24 and P33 import it, and neither restates it. It defines the following. (a) STORE: the only template store is the table public.template_registry (name, language, body, body_sha256 pinned, slots jsonb, category, lint_ok, lint_errors, meta_status, meta_synced_at), primary key (name, language). Rows are seeded only by SQL migration, in P24's 016_client_language.sql for the four P24 templates. There is no data/wa_templates.json and no wa_templates_status table. (b) CANONICAL_TEMPLATES: client_explanation_v1, affidavit_text_review_v1, client_explanation_doc_v1, channel_consent_optin_v1. explanation_ready_v1, explanation_doc_v1, consent_optin_v1, affidavit_para_review_v1 and P33's old client_explanation_v1 variant are retired, and the contract lists them in RETIRED_NAMES so the inventory test can forbid them. (c) SLOT_KINDS, each with a server-side resolver and an example generator: int_small (1-999, digits only); org_field(field in {'office_name'}), max 60; case_title_from_matter (P33's existing resolver), max 80; document_title_from_record(ref = client_explanations.id), max 80, rendered as '<doc_kind label in the template language> dated|दिनांक <document_date formatted per language>' from data/doc_kind_labels.json (closed enum: sale_deed, lease, leave_and_licence, affidavit, legal_notice, court_order, nda, employment_agreement, power_of_attorney, other_agreement), with the same-matter check; filename and title are never read, and a missing doc_kind falls back to case_title_from_matter; approved_record_text(source, ref); approved_record_media(source, ref) for document headers. P33's document_title(ref) and approved_document are replaced by document_title_from_record and approved_record_media. (d) APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES: client_explanation -> client_explanations(text_col=template_param_text, hash_col=template_param_sha256, approved_col=approved_at, matter_col=thread_id); client_explanation_session -> client_explanations(text_col=text, hash_col=text_sha256, approved_col=approved_at, matter_col=thread_id); affidavit_paragraph -> affidavit_readbacks(text_col=paragraph_param_text, hash_col=paragraph_param_sha256, approved_col=approved_at, matter_col=matter_id). APPROVED_MEDIA_SOURCES: client_explanation_pdf -> client_explanations(path_col=pdf_storage_path, hash_col=pdf_sha256, approved_col=approved_at, matter_col=thread_id). (e) MAX_LEN for the approved_record_text slot, by (template, language): client_explanation_v1 {{3}}: en 350, hi 350, mr 350, gu 350, bn 330, pa 330, ta 300, te 300, kn 300, ml 280. affidavit_text_review_v1 {{2}}: en 450, hi 450, mr 450, others 400, ta and ml 380. A language not listed has no row, so its route is 'unavailable'. (f) TEMPLATE_SLOTS: client_explanation_v1 = [org_field(office_name), document_title_from_record, approved_record_text(client_explanation)]; affidavit_text_review_v1 = [int_small, approved_record_text(affidavit_paragraph)]; client_explanation_doc_v1 = header approved_record_media(client_explanation_pdf), body [org_field(office_name), document_title_from_record]; channel_consent_optin_v1 = [org_field(office_name)] only. The consent notice is fixed body text, not a slot, and notice_version is the pinned body_sha256 of that (name, language) row. client_channel_consents records it, and a fuller notice in data/consent_notices/{lang}.json can be sent on request via the session route with body_ref=('consent_notice', version). (g) SEND API: whatsapp_service.send_text(phone_number_id, to, *, reason, ref, body_ref=(source, row_id)). On guarded paths there is no text parameter: the guard resolves the body via APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES, checks approval, matter and sha256, then posts. send_template(phone_number_id, to, *, name, language, reason, ref, slots={index: {'kind': ..., ...}}). A raw string in any slot raises 'bound_slot_requires_reference' before any HTTP call. Both return msg_ref on triage numbers (P08) or the wamid otherwise. (h) LINT: one linter, app/services/wa_template_lint.py, used by P33's CI and by the seed migration's verification step. Its rules: unknown slot kind -> unknown_slot_kind; slot list differs from TEMPLATE_SLOTS -> slot_mismatch; body hash differs from pin -> pin_mismatch; plus the structural rules from round 5 (at least 20 fixed letters at each end, no adjacent variables, sequential numbering, NFC fixed_len >= sum(MAX_LEN), total <= 1024, footer <= 60, examples generated at max_len). 6. Routing (wa_delivery.route): unchanged. Session when the last inbound was under 23 h 30 m ago. Otherwise template_text when lint_ok, APPROVED, and the text fits MAX_LEN[(name, language)]. Then template_document, else 'unavailable' (409, zero Meta calls). Only the first outstanding item goes by template. 7. Sending always goes through the guard with reason='client_of_matter' and ref=matter_id: the session route uses body_ref=('client_explanation_session', id) and the template route uses slot references. Meta error 131047 marks the message failed and re-routes it as if the window were closed, with no free-form retry. Everything is audited with the template name, pinned hash and CONTRACT_VERSION. 8. Pre-execution review: unchanged (affidavit_readbacks, one outstanding paragraph, reply matched by msg_ref(context.id), a correction reopens the draft). 9. The endorsement is always a [●…●] placeholder, and the annexure is optional and placed after the verification. 10. Vernacular templates, Noto Indic fonts, DOCX w:cs, uharfbuzz shaping or a refusal to export. 11. intake_guard.check_reply fails closed for languages without lexicons.

### Where it is built

New shared module app/contracts/wa_templates.py (the contract: STORE, CANONICAL_TEMPLATES, RETIRED_NAMES, SLOT_KINDS, APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES, APPROVED_MEDIA_SOURCES, MAX_LEN, TEMPLATE_SLOTS, CONTRACT_VERSION), imported by P33's guard (whatsapp_service.assert_may_initiate and the slot resolvers) and by P24's wa_delivery, explain_service and lint. New shared test tests/contracts/test_wa_template_contract.py, collected by both P24's and P33's suites (marked contract). Extend app/services/whatsapp_service.py (the send_text and send_template signatures as in the contract, Meta 131047 parsing, upload_media), app/services/whatsapp_intake.py (last_inbound_at on inbound only, STOP, reply matching by msg_ref), app/services/intake_guard.py, app/services/drafting_engine.py, app/services/pdf_service.py, app/services/draft_check.py, app/services/tts_service.py, app/services/audit_service.py and app/worker.py. New: app/services/wa_template_lint.py (the single linter), app/core/language.py, app/services/explain_service.py, app/services/channel_consent.py, app/services/wa_delivery.py, app/routers/explanations.py, data/doc_kind_labels.json, data/consent_notices/{hi,en,mr,ta}.json, scripts/sync_wa_templates.py (reads template_registry only). Migration supabase/migrations/016_client_language.sql: case_threads.client_language, whatsapp_conversations.last_inbound_at, documents.doc_kind and document_date, client_explanations, affidavit_readbacks, client_channel_consents, template_registry columns lint_ok/lint_errors/meta_status if absent, and INSERTs for the four templates in hi and en with pinned body_sha256, followed by a verification DO block that fails the migration if a body's sha256 differs from its pin. All with RLS by org. Frontend: the Studio Explain and review panels, the inbox route display and the Templates page.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI explain in English and don't anchor explanations to clauses. A ChatGPT explanation in Hindi can change an amount or turn 'may' into 'must' with nothing to catch it. WhatsApp-first practice tools send from a lawyer's personal phone with no consent record, or use the Business API with free-text template variables that staff can fill with anything, including solicitation, and they fail silently outside the 24-hour window. Ours ties each explanation to its source clause, checks it in code, requires lawyer approval and a purpose-specific opt-in, and sends only through one guard. Template names, slot kinds, limits and approved-text sources are defined once in a single contract module that the sender, the guard and the linter all import. So the definitions can't drift between teams, and no person can type into a client-facing template.

### Safeguards

BCI Rule 36: every outbound P24 message goes through P33's assert_may_initiate with reason client_of_matter and the matter ref, including the session route, which has no free-text parameter at all. Every slot kind is defined once in the shared contract and resolved by the server from a closed enum, an org field or approved same-matter record text. Filenames and titles are never used. Templates exist once, in template_registry, seeded by migration with pinned hashes, checked by one linter, and guarded against retired names and drift by a test that both teams run. Sworn documents: the interpreter endorsement is always a placeholder. DPDP s.5/6: a purpose- and channel-specific consent, with the notice version tied to the pinned opt-in body, STOP honoured immediately, and everything audited separately from AI-processing consent. Delivery sends bytes hash-equal to lawyer-approved text, fails closed without a route, and never retries free-form after a re-engagement error. Message IDs are matched through P08's msg_ref on triage numbers. Informational tone, with LEGAL_DISCLAIMER on directive phrasing. PII is masked before the model. RLS by org on all explanation, review and consent tables.

### How the panel's objections were answered

All three objections asked for one jointly stated contract. It now exists as code, not prose: app/contracts/wa_templates.py, version 'wa-templates/1'. P33's guard and P24's sender, router and linter all import it, and no other module may define slot kinds, approved-text sources or limits (an AST test checks this). Its contents follow your preferred choices. Store: template_registry in the database, seeded only by migration with per-(name, language) pinned hashes, with no JSON file and no status table. Names: the four P24 names, with explanation_ready_v1, explanation_doc_v1, consent_optin_v1 and affidavit_para_review_v1 listed as RETIRED_NAMES and forbidden in code and data. proposal.solvable_part: Software can give the client a clause-by-clause or paragraph-by-paragraph rendering, in their own language, of the document they are about to sign or the order they received. Each part stays anchored to the English source, is checked by the P23 invariants engine, and is sent only after lawyer approval. It goes over a channel the client agreed to for that purpose, by a route WhatsApp accepts at that moment, and only through P33's outbound guard, under one template contract that P24 and P33 share as code. Before execution, the client can review each factual paragraph of an affidavit in their language and confirm or correct it, as an internal record for the lawyer, never the sworn interpreter endorsement. Software can also generate Hindi pleadings from fixed lawyer-written templates, and stop English/Hindi-only safety checks from silently passing AI replies in other Indian languages.
proposal.out_of_scope: It can't make HCs or the SC accept vernacular pleadings. It can't guarantee the client understood: the log shows what was sent and what the client replied. It can't replace the read-over at execution or the interpreter's certificate. It can't help clients who can't read, beyond the in-person read-out and voice. It can't control Meta's template review, pricing or the 24-hour window. The linter enforces the documented and observed structural rules, but Meta can still reject, pause or recategorise a template, and then that route is unavailable. STT/TTS only work where Deepgram supports the language. Hindi templates come first, and Marathi, Tamil and others follow as lawyers write and approve them. P33 owns the outbound guard's policy (who may be messaged and why). The template contract module is co-owned, and P24 can't send if the guard refuses.

proposal.why_incumbents_fail_and_this_wont: Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI explain in English and don't anchor explanations to clauses. A ChatGPT explanation in Hindi can change an amount or turn 'may' into 'must' with nothing to catch it. WhatsApp-first practice tools send from a lawyer's personal phone with no consent record, or use the Business API with free-text template variables that staff can fill with anything, including solicitation, and they fail silently outside the 24-hour window. Ours ties each explanation to its source clause, checks it in code, requires lawyer approval and a purpose-specific opt-in, and sends only through one guard. Template names, slot kinds, limits and approved-text sources are defined once in a single contract module that the sender, the guard and the linter all import. So the definitions can't drift between teams, and no person can type into a client-facing template.

Make the dependency explicit in sequencing: P33 lands first, or the contract module and its test land as a standalone PR that both proposals depend on.

### What software can fix

Catching Registry defects before filing, in one pass, against the specific court's published checklist (pagination, index-to-page consistency, annexure references, true/certified copy markers, court fee, vakalatnama and affidavit presence and dates, legibility, untranslated vernacular pages, limitation and condonation application), and after filing, tracking defect rounds, cure deadlines and days since cure without listing.

### What it can't fix

The Registry's own pace, defects raised in instalments by scrutiny staff, out-of-turn listing decisions, and the judgment calls a scrutiny officer makes. Court fee is computed only for courts whose fee schedule we have encoded and verified. We don't submit to the e-filing portal.

### What the user sees

A Pre-scrutiny tab in the Studio: upload the filing bundle (PDF or DOCX parts) and pick the court and case type. A report lists each check as pass/fail/needs-human with page numbers: 'Index says Annexure P-4 at p.57; it starts at p.61', 'Annexure P-7 referred in para 12 is not in the bundle', 'pages 33-35 illegible (OCR confidence 41%)', 'page 80 appears to be in Marathi; no translation follows', 'impugned order dated 02.06.2026; 112 days have passed; no condonation application found', 'vakalatnama page not detected: confirm'. After filing, a Defects tracker per matter: round number, defects raised, date, cure deadline under the court's rule, and listing status, with a 'listing delayed' flag after a firm-set threshold.

### What the system does

1. Checklist rules as data per court (app/data/registry_checklists/<court>.json): check id, type (structural, presence, arithmetic, date), source (rule or practice direction URL), status draft/verified by two advocates.
2. Structural checks in code on the PDF: page count vs. stamped page numbers, index table parsed and compared with detected annexure headers, cross-references 'Annexure P-n' in the body vs. annexures present, OCR confidence per page via ocr_service, script/language detection per page, file size and page size.
3. Presence checks: keyword and layout detection for vakalatnama, affidavit, verification, court-fee page; uncertain detections become 'needs human', never 'pass'.
4. Limitation: impugned-order date and remedy go through limitation_service (P06); if delay exists and no application titled for condonation is present, fail.
5. Court fee: computed from the encoded state schedule where verified; otherwise 'not computed'.
6. Post-filing: defect rounds entered by the clerk (or imported from portal emails forwarded in); cure deadline computed from the court's rule as data; each becomes a P13 deadline.
No AI decides pass/fail; Claude may optionally suggest IA titles, shown as suggestions.

### Where it is built

app/services/ocr_service.py, document_service, limitation_service (P06), deadline_service (P13); new app/services/scrutiny_service.py and app/data/registry_checklists/; migration 017_filing_checks.sql (filing_checks, defect_rounds); Studio UI in frontend/src/app/studio/page.tsx.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

E-filing portals show defects only after filing, one round at a time; Harvey and CoCounsel don't know Indian Registry rules; nothing tracks cure deadlines across matters. Ours runs the whole checklist before filing in one pass and is deterministic, so the same bundle always gets the same report.

### Safeguards

Bundles are client documents: stored under RLS, processed on our server; no AI needed for checks (Tesseract only, OCR vision fallback disabled for this path). Checklist rules carry sources and two-advocate sign-off.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_scrutiny.py fixtures: synthetic SLP and writ bundles with planted defects (index mismatch, missing annexure, illegible page, Marathi page without translation, 112-day delay without condonation IA, no vakalatnama); every planted defect is reported with the right page, and a clean bundle reports zero fails.
- test_uncertain_is_not_pass: a vakalatnama page with low-confidence detection is 'needs human'.
- test_court_fee_unknown_court: a court without a verified schedule returns 'not computed', never a number.
- test_defect_round_deadline: a defect round raised 2026-10-01 under a court rule of 28 days total creates a deadline and reduces the remaining days on a second round.
- Determinism: running the same bundle twice yields byte-identical reports.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Too many 'needs human' results will drown the report. Track the share per check and tune it before calling the feature done.
- Limitation defects depend on choosing the right remedy. Show the remedy that was assumed in the report so a wrong pick is visible.
- Name the reviewer of each court's checklist in the report footer, so a 'pass' is not read as the vendor certifying compliance.
- Marathi and Hindi share the Devanagari script. Tesseract OSD detects the script, not the language, so the 'page appears to be in Marathi' test needs a language-ID step (or should flag 'vernacular page' without naming the language).
- Byte-identical reports require fixed timestamps and stable ordering. Exclude generated_at from the hashed body.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Turning a pleading into an e-filing bundle that is checked against the target court's own formatting rules. The bundle gets a searchable Unicode text layer, page numbers, an index, bookmarks, size splits, and page-size and resolution checks. Where a court prescribes them, it is also checked for font family, body size, line spacing and margins.

For courts that mandate a font (Supreme Court, Delhi HC, Bombay HC), the default input is the PDF the firm exports from Word on its own licensed machine. We check that PDF and assemble the bundle around it without re-rendering the body. Round 6 makes those checks match how Word actually lays out a page:
- Headers and footers that Word puts inside the margins are recognised and checked separately, not failed as margin breaches.
- Our own stamped page numbers are left out of the body checks.
- Neutral characters (spaces, punctuation, digits) inside Hindi or other non-Latin runs, and conjunct glyphs, are attributed to the script of their run.

Courts with no font mandate keep the DOCX path with metric-compatible free fonts. Also still covered: legacy Hindi DOCX conversion, replacing a single page, and a munshi preparing and queuing the bundle on a phone in Hindi or Tamil.

### What it can't fix

Things software can't fix:
- Court portals, terminals and internet access, and how many filing systems a court complex runs.
- OTP and credential steps, and clerks' livelihoods.
- We never log in to e-filing portals or upload to them.
- We can't ship Microsoft fonts, and we don't accept Windows or Office copies of them on our server.
- The Word export has to be done on a computer that has Word. A munshi on a phone uploads a PDF that a lawyer or an office computer exported.
- We can't decide whether a registry will accept a recorded deviation.
- We don't rewrite pleadings. We flag the problem and the fix is made in Word.
- Court rules change by notification. Profiles are data with a source and a review date, and overdue profiles are flagged, but we can't guarantee a profile is current on the day a court amends its rule.

Limits of the checks themselves (all reported, never hidden):
- With only a PDF, line spacing is measured within a tolerance.
- Header and footer detection on untagged PDFs is heuristic. Text in a margin that the detector can't classify is amber when it sits in only one place, and a failure, naming the page and text, when it is clearly body text. It is never silently passed.
- Quote-size findings are advisory.
- Some Indic glyphs carry no usable Unicode text in Word's output (the ToUnicode map is empty or points to the private-use area). Text copied from those glyphs may not be searchable, and we report that. We can't repair Word's ToUnicode map.
- Legacy-to-Unicode conversion flags unmapped glyphs and never guesses them.
- We don't check that a font Word embedded was licensed on the firm's machine.

### What the user sees

Steps 1 and 2 of /studio/bundle are as in round 5: choose the 'Filing in' court, then use the PDF-first card for courts that mandate a font. That card also accepts an optional .docx, shows Word export help, and offers the advanced licence-gated org-font route. Round 6 changes three things.

(a) Headers and footers. The formatting checklist has a separate item, 'Headers and footers (outside the margin rule)'. For example:
- Green, info: 'Pages 1-40: footer "Page N of 40" at 1.3 cm from the bottom edge, and running head "W.P.(C) No. __ of 2026" at 1.2 cm from the top edge. Recognised as Word headers and footers (tagged as pagination artifacts by Word).'
- On untagged PDFs the source reads '(repeats on 38 of 40 pages)' or '(page-number pattern)'.
- With the .docx supplied, it reads '(matches the document's footer)'.
The Margins item then reads 'Margins: body text starts 4.0 cm from the left edge and ends 2.6 cm above the bottom edge (rule: <value>): met'. If the profile has a header_footer_min_cm, the header/footer item also shows that value and passes or fails against it.
Genuine breaches still fail and name the text: 'Page 5: body text "...the respondent thereafter..." sits 1.4 cm from the bottom edge, inside the margin (rule: <value>).'
A single unclassifiable line in a margin is amber: 'Page 3: "Annexure P-2" in the top margin. Not recognised as a header. Check it.'

(b) Page numbering. If Word numbers are found on most pages, the 'Pages already numbered in Word' toggle is switched on automatically, with the line 'Word page numbers detected on 38 of 40 pages. We won't stamp numbers over them; we'll verify the sequence.' When we do stamp numbers, the preview shows where they go, and the post-assembly check states 'Our page numbers: checked for position and font only (not part of the body checks).'

(c) Bilingual pleadings. The font line reads, for example, 'Hindi runs on pages 3, 7 (including their spaces, punctuation and digits): Nirmala UI, allowed for Devanagari under this profile.'
- A real failure reads 'Page 9: English sentence "The petitioner states..." is set in Nirmala UI. The Supreme Court requires Times New Roman for English text.'
- A Western-digit-only line set in a Devanagari font, with no script around it, is amber.
- Glyphs that carry no Unicode text show as info: 'Page 7: 14 Hindi glyphs carry no copyable text in Word's export. Searching the PDF may miss them.'

Deviation acceptance and the final approval screen are unchanged.

### What the system does

1. Court profiles are as in round 5 (mandate_scope, overlay_fonts, script_fonts), with one new optional field. header_footer_min_cm is the minimum distance of header and footer text from the page edge, with its own source and reviewer, or null where the rule is silent. CI (scripts/check_court_profiles.py) validates it.

2. Region classification (new, in app/services/pdf_format_checks.py, deterministic). This runs before the margin and size checks. Every char from pdfplumber is labelled 'body', 'header_footer' or 'overlay'. The page has a top band and a bottom band, each running from the page edge to margin_cm + 0.3 cm. The first source that applies decides:

(i) Tagged PDF. A pikepdf.parse_content_stream walk records the marked-content property dict around every text-show operator, joined to pdfplumber chars in stream order. pdfplumber's char 'tag' is a cross-check. Chars inside /Artifact with /Type /Pagination (Subtype Header, Footer or absent) that lie within a band become header_footer. Pagination artifacts outside both bands stay body, so tagging can't hide body text from the checks. Other artifact types (Layout, Page, Background) also stay body.

(ii) DOCX supplied, and it passed the 0.98 token-overlap match. We read the text of word/header*.xml and footer*.xml, replacing PAGE, NUMPAGES and SECTIONPAGES fields with a digits pattern, along with sectPr w:pgMar header and footer distances. A line in a band whose normalised text matches a header or footer part becomes header_footer.

(iii) Untagged and no DOCX. A text line lying wholly within a band becomes header_footer if either:
- its text, normalised (whitespace collapsed, digit runs including Devanagari digits replaced by #), repeats at the same band position (within 0.5 cm) on at least 50% of pages and at least 2 pages; or
- it matches the page-number pattern set. That set covers 'N', '- N -', 'Page N', 'Page N of M', 'N/M', roman numerals, Devanagari and Tamil digits, and 'पृष्ठ N'.
Any other text in a band is unclassified.

(iv) Overlay. Chars inside bboxes recorded by our own assembly become overlay.

3. Margin and size checks use the labels:
- Margins: the per-page minimum and maximum of body chars only, compared with margins_cm. Body text inside a margin fails, naming the page and a text sample. Unclassified band text is amber when it is a single line under 12 words that doesn't repeat and isn't a sentence fragment that continues into the body. Otherwise it fails. Amber is never 'met' for the gate: it shows as advisory and doesn't block.
- Headers and footers: a separate checklist item. Where header_footer_min_cm is set, each header/footer line must be at least that far from the edge, or the item is unmet. Header/footer lines must also not overlap body bboxes.
- Font: header and footer chars are font-checked too. If mandate_scope is 'all_pages' they must use the mandated font M. If it is 'body', M or overlay_fonts is allowed.
- Body size and line spacing are computed from body chars only. Header and footer sizes are reported as info.

4. Script attribution (replaces round 5's per-char rule). We use fontTools.unicodedata.script_extension (UAX #24 Script_Extensions).
- A run is a maximal sequence of chars on one line with the same base fontname and x-gaps no larger than 1.5 x the space width.
- Each char's script set is its Script_Extensions. Chars whose set is only Zyyy (Common) or Zinh (Inherited) are neutral.
- For non-neutral chars, the allowed fonts are the union over scripts in its Script_Extensions: Latn maps to M's PostScript names, and any other script maps to its script_fonts list. So the danda (Deva, Beng, ...) passes in any of those scripts' fonts.
- A neutral char takes the strong script of its run: the nearest preceding strong char, else the nearest following one. If the run has none, it takes the strong script of the adjacent runs on the same line. Its font must then be allowed for that script. So spaces, commas, full stops, hyphens, brackets and Western digits inside a Hindi run may be in Nirmala UI or Mangal.
- A neutral-only line with no strong neighbour is accepted if its font is M. If its font is a script font, it is amber with the page named.
- Glyphs whose text is multi-codepoint (conjuncts) take the script of their first strong codepoint.
- Glyphs with empty, zero-width or private-use text from a font listed in some script_fonts entry belong to the run they sit in. They pass if that run's script allows the font. They are counted for the 'no copyable text' info line, and if they exceed 5% of a page's script glyphs, the text-layer item is amber.
- The same glyphs from any other font fail. The exception is the round 5 symbol-font bullet rule.
- A strong Latin char in a non-M font always fails. So an English sentence in Nirmala UI fails on its own page.

5. Assembly is as in round 5: the Word PDF's content streams are copied byte-identical, and pikepdf overlays add numbers, the index, bookmarks, splits and page replacement. Before stamping:
- If page-number-pattern header_footer lines exist on at least 80% of pages, 'already numbered' defaults on and the sequence is verified.
- Otherwise the stamp position is chosen in the bottom band so that it overlaps no body or header_footer bbox and respects header_footer_min_cm. If no such position exists, stamping is refused with the reason.
- mandate_scope 'all_pages' still refuses our stamping (number in Word) and sends the index out as a DOCX round-trip.

6. Post-assembly re-verification runs steps 2-4 on the whole bundle:
- Recorded overlay bboxes are excluded from the body margin, size and spacing checks.
- Overlay chars are checked separately: overlay_fonts only, inside a band, header_footer_min_cm respected, and no overlap with body or header_footer chars.
- A font outside the body allow-lists and the overlay list fails.
- Body pages must reproduce the same pre-assembly results.

7. The gate (409 court_format_unmet), deviations, the licence-gated org fonts, the no-mandate DOCX path, OCR, legacy Hindi conversion and profile pinning are all unchanged from round 5. There is no AI anywhere in this pipeline.

### Where it is built

Extend:
- app/services/pdf_format_checks.py: region classifier (tagged, DOCX, repetition/pattern, overlay), run-based script attribution, and header/footer and amber reporting.
- app/services/bundle_service.py: overlay placement and collision avoidance, auto 'already numbered', post-assembly scoped verification.
- app/services/format_checks.py: read the DOCX header/footer parts and the pgMar header/footer distances.
- app/data/court_profiles/*.json and schema.json: header_footer_min_cm with its source and reviewer.
- scripts/check_court_profiles.py.
- frontend/src/app/studio/bundle/page.tsx: the header/footer checklist item, amber rows, auto-toggle notice, and the bilingual font lines, with Hindi and Tamil strings.

New dependency: pdfplumber>=0.11, for marked-content tags on chars. fontTools is already used.

New fixtures:
- tests/fixtures/word_exports/: golden PDFs exported once by our team from Microsoft Word 365 on a licensed Windows machine. They are synthetic pleadings with no client data: tagged and untagged, with running head and footer page numbers, and Hindi+English. They are documents carrying font subsets under the fonts' own embedding permission, like any PDF a firm files, and no font file is extracted or committed. A README records the Word build and export settings.
- tests/fixtures/builders/: runtime generators for the synthetic cases (LibreOffice in the render image for shaped Devanagari; pikepdf for artifact tags and ToUnicode edits).

No migration change beyond round 5's 017.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Global AI tools stop at drafting and don't know Indian registry formatting directions. Indian e-filing vendors and DTP shops check by eye, so rejections come after upload. Generic PDF preflight tools either flag every header as a margin breach or skip margins altogether, and they treat any non-mandated font as a failure, so they break on bilingual pleadings. Our checks model how Word lays out a page:
- Word's own pagination artifacts, its header and footer parts, and repeating band text are recognised and checked under their own rule, so body margins are measured only on body text.
- Neutral characters and conjuncts inside Hindi runs are attributed by Unicode Script_Extensions and their run. An English sentence in a Hindi font is still caught.
- Our stamps are checked only against their own rules.

We prove this on real Word exports, not only on our own renderer's output. So a correctly formatted Supreme Court, Delhi HC or Bombay HC filing reaches 'met' with no deviation, and a real breach is still named by page and text.

### Safeguards

Everything runs on our server with no AI, under org RLS. No font file is uploaded on the default path, and the golden fixtures contain no extracted font files. Amber findings are advisory and are never reported as 'met'. Unclassified text in a margin is never silently passed. Pagination tags can exclude text only inside the header and footer bands, so marking body text as an artifact can't evade the checks. Only an associate, partner or owner can accept a deviation, with a reason; it is audit-logged and listed to the final approver. The body content of the Word PDF is never altered. We never handle portal credentials, and court rules are cited with a reviewer and pinned per bundle.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objections 1 and 2: Word's headers, footers and page numbers sit inside the margins and would fail the margin check, and our own stamps would too.
- Every char is now labelled body, header_footer or overlay before any margin or size check (step 2).
- header_footer comes from Word's tagged /Artifact /Pagination marked content, which the help panel's 'Document structure tags' setting produces. Failing that, it comes from the supplied DOCX's header/footer parts. Failing both, it comes from text in the top and bottom bands that repeats on at least half the pages or matches a page-number pattern.
- Body margins are measured only on body chars.
- Header and footer lines get their own checklist item, checked against a new sourced profile field, header_footer_min_cm. They are font-checked per mandate_scope.
- Our overlay bboxes are left out of the post-assembly body margin, size and spacing checks and verified against their own rules (step 6).
- Pagination tags outside the bands don't exempt text, so the fix can't hide breaches.
- On the fixture objection: tests cover tagged, untagged and DOCX-classified footers (test_word_footer_tagged_passes_margins, _untagged_repetition, _docx_parts), real breaches (test_margin_breach_still_fails), stamped bundles (test_assembled_bundle_with_stamps_passes), and real Word 365 exports (test_golden_word_exports).

Objection 3: neutral characters and conjuncts in bilingual pleadings.
- Script is resolved with UAX #24 Script_Extensions. Common and Inherited chars take the strong script of their run, then of adjacent runs (step 4), so neutrals inside a Hindi run may use that script's script_fonts.
- Multi-codepoint glyphs take their first strong codepoint. Empty or private-use glyphs from an allowed script font belong to their run, and they are counted and reported as a searchability info or amber.
- Strong Latin chars must always be in M.
- test_bilingual_neutrals_and_conjuncts uses shaped output with neutrals in the Devanagari font, conjuncts and edited ToUnicode entries, plus the golden Word bilingual export. test_bilingual_latin_in_script_font_fails proves that an English sentence in Nirmala UI fails.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_bundles.py::test_word_footer_tagged_passes_margins: a 14 pt, 1.5-spaced fixture with a 2.5 cm bottom margin. On every page a footer 'Page N of 40' sits at 1.25 cm from the edge inside /Artifact <</Type /Pagination /Subtype /Footer>>, with a running head inside /Subtype /Header. Margins are met, header_footer is met and lists both lines with source 'tagged', body size and spacing are met, and build returns 200 with no deviation.
- test_word_footer_untagged_repetition: the same fixture without tags. The cause-title running head, 'Advocate for the Petitioner' and the page numbers are classified by repetition and pattern, and margins are met. A 1-page variant with only 'Page 1' passes by pattern. A 1-page variant with 'Annexure P-2' in the band is amber, and the build is not blocked.
- test_word_footer_docx_parts: with the matching DOCX supplied, footer lines are classified from footer1.xml (the PAGE field becomes the digits pattern), with source 'docx'.
- test_margin_breach_still_fails: a body paragraph continuing into the bottom band on page 5 (a multi-line, non-repeating sentence) fails margins with page 5 and a text sample. A Pagination artifact placed mid-page is not excluded and is measured as body. A footer at 0.5 cm under a profile with header_footer_min_cm 1.0 makes the header_footer item unmet and build returns 409.
- test_golden_word_exports: every PDF in tests/fixtures/word_exports/ (real Word 365 exports, tagged and untagged, Supreme Court and Delhi HC layouts, numbered in Word, with running heads) gives margins met, mandated font met, body size met, and spacing met or amber within tolerance, under its profile, with no deviation.
- test_assembled_bundle_with_stamps_passes: a body numbered without Word gets our stamped numbers, and post-assembly verification passes. Overlay chars are excluded from body margin and size, and are checked for overlay font, band position and header_footer_min_cm. A stamp forced to overlap a Word footer is refused before stamping. A body already numbered in Word on 38 of 40 pages switches 'already numbered' on, and a gap at page 9 is flagged.
- test_bilingual_neutrals_and_conjuncts: a LibreOffice-shaped fixture has Hindi runs whose spaces, commas, full stops, hyphens, brackets, Western digits and danda are in a Noto Serif Devanagari stand-in renamed at run time to NirmalaUI. Its conjuncts map to multi-codepoint text, and 3 glyphs are edited by pikepdf to empty ToUnicode and 2 to private-use text. The 'Mandated font' gate is met and the no-copyable-text info lists 5 glyphs. The golden Word bilingual export passes too.
- test_bilingual_latin_in_script_font_fails: a full English sentence set in the NirmalaUI stand-in on page 9 fails 'Mandated font' with page 9 and the sentence sample. A line '12, 13' alone in the Devanagari font with no strong neighbour is amber. Empty-text glyphs from an unlisted font (Helvetica stand-in) fail.
- Carried over from round 5: test_word_export_pdf_meets_mandate (body streams byte-identical, no LibreOffice), test_word_export_wrong_font_pages, test_word_export_size_spacing_margins (now on body-labelled chars), test_unembedded_or_no_tounicode_fails, test_all_pages_scope_index_roundtrip (header and footer chars must use M under all_pages), test_replace_page_word_pdf, test_org_font_licence_refused, test_post_assembly_allowlist, test_profile_integrity (with header_footer_min_cm), and the round 3 and 4 suites including test_deviation_acceptance and the frontend build with Hindi and Tamil strings.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- The amber exemption for unclassified band text ('a single line under 12 words that doesn't repeat and isn't a sentence fragment that continues into the body') is not defined in code terms. The most common real filing error is a Word bottom margin set smaller than the court's rule. That puts each page's last body line inside the band, with different text on every page, so nothing repeats. Short paragraph-final lines would then come out amber page by page instead of failing. Define 'continues into the body' deterministically: the band line is in the body font and size and sits within 1.5x the body line pitch of the body line above it. Such a line is body and fails. Add a test where the bottom margin is 1.5 cm against a 2 cm rule and the last lines are short, and assert that margins fail.
- Joining the pikepdf marked-content walk to pdfplumber chars 'in stream order' is fragile when text sits inside Form XObjects or one TJ draws many glyphs. Assert that the walk and the char list agree on glyph counts per page. When they don't, fall back to the untagged path (iii) and note it in the report.
- The bands are only top and bottom. If a profile prescribes side margins and a stamp, line numbers or a marginal 'Annexure' label sits in a side margin, it gets measured as body and fails. Say so explicitly, or add left and right bands for unclassified text with the same amber/fail rule.
- The rule that a single unclassified margin line is amber (under 12 words, not repeating, not a 'sentence fragment that continues into the body') needs a precise definition and a test. One case must be covered: a short final line of a paragraph that Word pushed into the bottom margin is a real breach, and it must fail. It should not show as an advisory amber that lets the build through.
- Migration numbering clashes across proposals: P02 and P08 both claim 014, and this proposal relies on 017. Allocate migration numbers centrally before building so the Supabase versions don't collide.
- Golden fixtures: the README should record each embedded font's fsType embedding permission alongside the Word build. That backs up the statement that no extracted font file is committed.
- Joining pikepdf text-show operators to pdfplumber chars in stream order only works if you count glyphs per operator from each font's encoding (2-byte CIDs for Identity-H, 1-byte for simple fonts). Add a fixture with mixed simple and CID fonts on one page, and fall back to source (iii) for any page where the counts disagree. Never guess an alignment.
- Word puts watermarks ('DRAFT', 'CONFIDENTIAL') in the header part, usually in a non-mandated font, and draws them mid-page. Under the bands rule they become body text and fail the font check. That is probably the right outcome for a filing copy, but the message should say 'header-part watermark: remove it in Word', not 'English sentence in wrong font'.
- Word's 'Different first page' and 'Different odd and even' settings split a header into 2-3 variants, so each variant repeats on under 50% of pages. Group repetition by odd/even page and leave out page 1 before applying the 50% rule. Otherwise untagged exports go amber or red for no reason.
- A run currently breaks on any change of base fontname. A space Word sets in the Latin font between two Hindi words is then its own neutral-only run, and its script falls to the adjacent runs. Add a fixture for that case: Hindi word, Times New Roman space, Hindi word.
- Pin pdfplumber to a tested minor version (for example >=0.11,<0.12). Char 'tag' and 'mcid' are recent additions, and a later release could change their semantics.

proposal.solvable_part:
Turning a pleading into an e-filing bundle that is checked against the target court's own formatting rules. The bundle gets a searchable Unicode text layer, page numbers, an index, bookmarks, size splits, and page-size and resolution checks. Where a court prescribes them, it is also checked for font family, body size, line spacing and margins.

For courts that mandate a font (Supreme Court, Delhi HC, Bombay HC), the default input is the PDF the firm exports from Word on its own licensed machine. We check that PDF and assemble the bundle around it without re-rendering the body. Round 6 makes those checks match how Word actually lays out a page:
- Headers and footers that Word puts inside the margins are recognised and checked separately, not failed as margin breaches.
- Our own stamped page numbers are left out of the body checks.
- Neutral characters (spaces, punctuation, digits) inside Hindi or other non-Latin runs, and conjunct glyphs, are attributed to the script of their run.

Courts with no font mandate keep the DOCX path with metric-compatible free fonts. Also still covered: legacy Hindi DOCX conversion, replacing a single page, and a munshi preparing and queuing the bundle on a phone in Hindi or Tamil.
proposal.out_of_scope:
Things software can't fix:
- Court portals, terminals and internet access, and how many filing systems a court complex runs.
- OTP and credential steps, and clerks' livelihoods.
- We never log in to e-filing portals or upload to them.
- We can't ship Microsoft fonts, and we don't accept Windows or Office copies of them on our server.
- The Word export has to be done on a computer that has Word. A munshi on a phone uploads a PDF that a lawyer or an office computer exported.
- We can't decide whether a registry will accept a recorded deviation.
- We don't rewrite pleadings. We flag the problem and the fix is made in Word.
- Court rules change by notification. Profiles are data with a source and a review date, and overdue profiles are flagged, but we can't guarantee a profile is current on the day a court amends its rule.

Limits of the checks themselves (all reported, never hidden):
- With only a PDF, line spacing is measured within a tolerance.
- Header and footer detection on untagged PDFs is heuristic. Text in a margin that the detector can't classify is amber when it sits in only one place, and a failure, naming the page and text, when it is clearly body text. It is never silently passed.
- Quote-size findings are advisory.
- Some Indic glyphs carry no usable Unicode text in Word's output (the ToUnicode map is empty or points to the private-use area). Text copied from those glyphs may not be searchable, and we report that. We can't repair Word's ToUnicode map.
- Legacy-to-Unicode conversion flags unmapped glyphs and never guesses them.
- We don't check that a font Word embedded was licensed on the firm's machine.
proposal.what_the_user_sees:
Steps 1 and 2 of /studio/bundle are as in round 5: choose the 'Filing in' court, then use the PDF-first card for courts that mandate a font. That card also accepts an optional .docx, shows Word export help, and offers the advanced licence-gated org-font route. Round 6 changes three things.

(a) Headers and footers. The formatting checklist has a separate item, 'Headers and footers (outside the margin rule)'. For example:
- Green, info: 'Pages 1-40: footer "Page N of 40" at 1.3 cm from the bottom edge, and running head "W.P.(C) No. __ of 2026" at 1.2 cm from the top edge. Recognised as Word headers and footers (tagged as pagination artifacts by Word).'
- On untagged PDFs the source reads '(repeats on 38 of 40 pages)' or '(page-number pattern)'.
- With the .docx supplied, it reads '(matches the document's footer)'.
The Margins item then reads 'Margins: body text starts 4.0 cm from the left edge and ends 2.6 cm above the bottom edge (rule: <value>): met'. If the profile has a header_footer_min_cm, the header/footer item also shows that value and passes or fails against it.
Genuine breaches still fail and name the text: 'Page 5: body text "...the respondent thereafter..." sits 1.4 cm from the bottom edge, inside the margin (rule: <value>).'
A single unclassifiable line in a margin is amber: 'Page 3: "Annexure P-2" in the top margin. Not recognised as a header. Check it.'

(b) Page numbering. If Word numbers are found on most pages, the 'Pages already numbered in Word' toggle is switched on automatically, with the line 'Word page numbers detected on 38 of 40 pages. We won't stamp numbers over them; we'll verify the sequence.' When we do stamp numbers, the preview shows where they go, and the post-assembly check states 'Our page numbers: checked for position and font only (not part of the body checks).'

(c) Bilingual pleadings. The font line reads, for example, 'Hindi runs on pages 3, 7 (including their spaces, punctuation and digits): Nirmala UI, allowed for Devanagari under this profile.'
- A real failure reads 'Page 9: English sentence "The petitioner states..." is set in Nirmala UI. The Supreme Court requires Times New Roman for English text.'
- A Western-digit-only line set in a Devanagari font, with no script around it, is amber.
- Glyphs that carry no Unicode text show as info: 'Page 7: 14 Hindi glyphs carry no copyable text in Word's export. Searching the PDF may miss them.'

Deviation acceptance and the final approval screen are unchanged.
proposal.what_the_system_does:
1. Court profiles are as in round 5 (mandate_scope, overlay_fonts, script_fonts), with one new optional field. header_footer_min_cm is the minimum distance of header and footer text from the page edge, with its own source and reviewer, or null where the rule is silent. CI (scripts/check_court_profiles.py) validates it.

2. Region classification (new, in app/services/pdf_format_checks.py, deterministic). This runs before the margin and size checks. Every char from pdfplumber is labelled 'body', 'header_footer' or 'overlay'. The page has a top band and a bottom band, each running from the page edge to margin_cm + 0.3 cm. The first source that applies decides:

(i) Tagged PDF. A pikepdf.parse_content_stream walk records the marked-content property dict around every text-show operator, joined to pdfplumber chars in stream order. pdfplumber's char 'tag' is a cross-check. Chars inside /Artifact with /Type /Pagination (Subtype Header, Footer or absent) that lie within a band become header_footer. Pagination artifacts outside both bands stay body, so tagging can't hide body text from the checks. Other artifact types (Layout, Page, Background) also stay body.

(ii) DOCX supplied, and it passed the 0.98 token-overlap match. We read the text of word/header*.xml and footer*.xml, replacing PAGE, NUMPAGES and SECTIONPAGES fields with a digits pattern, along with sectPr w:pgMar header and footer distances. A line in a band whose normalised text matches a header or footer part becomes header_footer.

(iii) Untagged and no DOCX. A text line lying wholly within a band becomes header_footer if either:
- its text, normalised (whitespace collapsed, digit runs including Devanagari digits replaced by #), repeats at the same band position (within 0.5 cm) on at least 50% of pages and at least 2 pages; or
- it matches the page-number pattern set. That set covers 'N', '- N -', 'Page N', 'Page N of M', 'N/M', roman numerals, Devanagari and Tamil digits, and 'पृष्ठ N'.
Any other text in a band is unclassified.

(iv) Overlay. Chars inside bboxes recorded by our own assembly become overlay.

3. Margin and size checks use the labels:
- Margins: the per-page minimum and maximum of body chars only, compared with margins_cm. Body text inside a margin fails, naming the page and a text sample. Unclassified band text is amber when it is a single line under 12 words that doesn't repeat and isn't a sentence fragment that continues into the body. Otherwise it fails. Amber is never 'met' for the gate: it shows as advisory and doesn't block.
- Headers and footers: a separate checklist item. Where header_footer_min_cm is set, each header/footer line must be at least that far from the edge, or the item is unmet. Header/footer lines must also not overlap body bboxes.
- Font: header and footer chars are font-checked too. If mandate_scope is 'all_pages' they must use the mandated font M. If it is 'body', M or overlay_fonts is allowed.
- Body size and line spacing are computed from body chars only. Header and footer sizes are reported as info.

4. Script attribution (replaces round 5's per-char rule). We use fontTools.unicodedata.script_extension (UAX #24 Script_Extensions).
- A run is a maximal sequence of chars on one line with the same base fontname and x-gaps no larger than 1.5 x the space width.
- Each char's script set is its Script_Extensions. Chars whose set is only Zyyy (Common) or Zinh (Inherited) are neutral.
- For non-neutral chars, the allowed fonts are the union over scripts in its Script_Extensions: Latn maps to M's PostScript names, and any other script maps to its script_fonts list. So the danda (Deva, Beng, ...) passes in any of those scripts' fonts.
- A neutral char takes the strong script of its run: the nearest preceding strong char, else the nearest following one. If the run has none, it takes the strong script of the adjacent runs on the same line. Its font must then be allowed for that script. So spaces, commas, full stops, hyphens, brackets and Western digits inside a Hindi run may be in Nirmala UI or Mangal.
- A neutral-only line with no strong neighbour is accepted if its font is M. If its font is a script font, it is amber with the page named.
- Glyphs whose text is multi-codepoint (conjuncts) take the script of their first strong codepoint.
- Glyphs with empty, zero-width or private-use text from a font listed in some script_fonts entry belong to the run they sit in. They pass if that run's script allows the font. They are counted for the 'no copyable text' info line, and if they exceed 5% of a page's script glyphs, the text-layer item is amber.
- The same glyphs from any other font fail. The exception is the round 5 symbol-font bullet rule.
- A strong Latin char in a non-M font always fails. So an English sentence in Nirmala UI fails on its own page.

5. Assembly is as in round 5: the Word PDF's content streams are copied byte-identical, and pikepdf overlays add numbers, the index, bookmarks, splits and page replacement. Before stamping:
- If page-number-pattern header_footer lines exist on at least 80% of pages, 'already numbered' defaults on and the sequence is verified.
- Otherwise the stamp position is chosen in the bottom band so that it overlaps no body or header_footer bbox and respects header_footer_min_cm. If no such position exists, stamping is refused with the reason.
- mandate_scope 'all_pages' still refuses our stamping (number in Word) and sends the index out as a DOCX round-trip.

6. Post-assembly re-verification runs steps 2-4 on the whole bundle:
- Recorded overlay bboxes are excluded from the body margin, size and spacing checks.
- Overlay chars are checked separately: overlay_fonts only, inside a band, header_footer_min_cm respected, and no overlap with body or header_footer chars.
- A font outside the body allow-lists and the overlay list fails.
- Body pages must reproduce the same pre-assembly results.

7. The gate (409 court_format_unmet), deviations, the licence-gated org fonts, the no-mandate DOCX path, OCR, legacy Hindi conversion and profile pinning are all unchanged from round 5. There is no AI anywhere in this pipeline.

proposal.why_incumbents_fail_and_this_wont:
Global AI tools stop at drafting and don't know Indian registry formatting directions. Indian e-filing vendors and DTP shops check by eye, so rejections come after upload. Generic PDF preflight tools either flag every header as a margin breach or skip margins altogether, and they treat any non-mandated font as a failure, so they break on bilingual pleadings. Our checks model how Word lays out a page:
- Word's own pagination artifacts, its header and footer parts, and repeating band text are recognised and checked under their own rule, so body margins are measured only on body text.
- Neutral characters and conjuncts inside Hindi runs are attributed by Unicode Script_Extensions and their run. An English sentence in a Hindi font is still caught.
- Our stamps are checked only against their own rules.

We prove this on real Word exports, not only on our own renderer's output. So a correctly formatted Supreme Court, Delhi HC or Bombay HC filing reaches 'met' with no deviation, and a real breach is still named by page and text.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

An internal s.138 NI Act pack for law firms that handle cheque-bounce work, built on the P13 docket and P06 limitation engine rather than sold as a standalone collections platform. It gives per-cheque clocks from the return memo, a deemed-service computation that brackets an uncertain service date and shows only the safe filing window, and deterministic demand notices from the firm's template. Post-filing it tracks summons service, s.143A interim compensation, warrants and the s.148 deposit on appeal. Every date flows into the firm's verified docket with sampled partner approval.

### What it can't fix

Service of summons by the court, police executing warrants, the accused absconding, and court disposal rates. India Post delivery status is imported from bulk-customer reports or entered by hand; we don't scrape tracking pages behind captchas. Lender-side collection operations at portfolio scale (dialling, settlement, ODR, legal-notice dispatch as a service) are what CredGenics, Legodesk and similar platforms do, and we don't compete there. Whether a court accepts a particular presumed service date is for the court; where the evidence leaves no safe window we flag it for the lawyer, not decide it.

### What the user sees

A Cheque files page (/cheques) inside the firm's matters. The user imports a CSV from the client (one row per cheque: drawer, amount, cheque date, presented on, memo received, reason, branch), including exports from CredGenics/Legodesk-style platforms via a column mapper. Each file shows its stage and next date in columns: Notice due, Awaiting service, Pay window running, Safe filing window open, Filed, Summons, Evidence. For uncertain service, the file shows 'Service between 5 Mar (earliest) and 20 Mar (latest): safe filing window 5 Apr to 5 May', or a red 'no safe filing date: partner decision needed'. Other banners: 'premature if filed before 5 Apr', 'window closes in 3 days', 'cheque presented after validity'. Batch actions: generate notices for files in 'Notice due' from the template, approve in bulk after spot-checking, export a print/post manifest. After filing: summons service attempts, s.143A order date and its due date, s.148 deposit dates. Every date also appears on /deadlines with its owner and verification status.

### What the system does

1. `cheque_files` table (one row per cheque, grouped by transaction/drawer) with every date. The existing `_cheque_bounce` logic is the per-row engine. Each computed date is a P13 deadline (ladder from creation, earliest candidate governs).
2. Notice text is a fixed, partner-approved firm template filled from row fields in code (amount demanded equals the cheque amount, 15 days from receipt, s.138/142 language), never AI-generated. Template edits need partner approval.
3. Service date resolution, deterministic:
   a. Actual delivery date from the tracking report or acknowledgement card, if present, is the service date.
   b. For a 'refused' or 'unclaimed / intimation delivered' return, the endorsement date on the article or tracking report (date of refusal, or of intimation for unclaimed) is the service date. It is entered or imported with its source and flagged 'deemed service (C.C. Alavi Haji; s.27 General Clauses Act): check'.
   c. ### Why current tools fail and this won't

We re-scope rather than claim the market is empty. Lender-side platforms (CredGenics, Legodesk and similar) already generate bulk s.138 notices from NBFC CSVs, track dispatch and delivery, and track cases after filing. We have not verified their internal date logic, so we don't claim they lack a premature/time-barred guard. Our pack is for the law firm those lenders instruct (and for MSME and individual clients who have no such platform). Its dates live in the same docket as the firm's other matters, with owners, backups, reminder ladders and verification (P13). It computes a bracketed safe filing window when the service date is uncertain, refusing to show a date later than the safe one (P06). It applies s.4/COVID exclusions and tracks s.143A and s.148 clocks, and it requires sampled partner approval before notices go out. It imports those platforms' exports instead of replacing them. Harvey, CoCounsel, Manupatra and SCC AI don't do s.138 workflow; Clio doesn't know NI Act timelines.

### Safeguards

Notices go to the drawer only after a lawyer's (batch) approval; nothing is sent automatically. Files with no safe filing date need a recorded partner decision. Drawer data is personal data under DPDP and stays under RLS, and the ledger needs no AI processing. The notice template is the firm's own, approved by a partner. Deemed-service dates carry their source (tracking report, article endorsement, or computed bracket) in the audit log.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection 1 (pay window counted from the return date): the service date is now the actual delivery date or, for refused/unclaimed, the postal endorsement date from the tracking report or article, recorded with its source (C.C. Alavi Haji; s.27 General Clauses Act). If neither is available, the system brackets service between dispatch + minimum transit and the return date, and shows only the safe filing window. It starts the day after the 15 days end for the latest plausible service date and ends one month after the cause of action for the earliest plausible service date, so no displayed date is premature (Yogendra Pratap Singh) or time-barred. An empty intersection is flagged and blocked pending a partner's decision. Tests: test_endorsement_vs_return_date (return and endorsement dates differ), test_bracketed_window, test_empty_window_flag, and the property test test_never_later_than_safe. Objection 2 (wrong incumbent claim): we name CredGenics and Legodesk, accept that they already do bulk notices, dispatch tracking and post-filing tracking for lenders, and take option (b). **Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Producing a cross-examination sheet per witness: contradictions and material omissions between the FIR, s.161 CrPC / s.180 BNSS statements, s.164 / s.183 statements and the deposition, each with exact verified quotes and page/line references in the original language, ready to confront the witness, extending the existing contradiction analyzer.

### What it can't fix

Deciding whether an omission is 'material' in law (the lawyer decides), handwritten statements Tesseract can't read reliably, and translation accuracy for the lawyer's own reading (P23's area). Courtroom use of the sheet is the lawyer's.

### What the user sees

In /studio Evidence: create a witness, attach their statements by type and date (FIR, s.161/180, s.164/183, chief, cross), in any supported language. The result is a table by topic: what the witness said in court (quote, page/line), what they said before (quote, page/line, statement type), finding type (contradiction / omission candidate / improvement), and a confrontation note. Omission candidates are labelled 'not found in the earlier statement: confirm' with the search terms used. Quotes are in the original script with a translation alongside. Export to DOCX for the brief.

### What the system does

1. Statement types and dates added to EvidenceSource; the deposition is parsed into numbered lines (existing parse_statement_text).
2. OCR for scanned vernacular statements via Tesseract Indic packs (vision fallback per OCR_VISION_FALLBACK setting); per-page confidence shown.
3. Claude (PII-masked, cached system prompt) returns contradictions and omission candidates with quotes in the original language.
4. Verification, deterministic: both quotes of a contradiction must pass quote_match against their source (invariant 6); for an omission, the deposition quote must pass, and the earlier statement must NOT contain the claimed fact's key terms (normalized search including common transliterations and the model-supplied keywords, all shown); if any key term is found the candidate is downgraded to 'check'. Unverified findings discarded and counted.
5. Severity computed as today (SEVERITY_SCORE).
6. Export through drafting_engine.to_docx, marked unreviewed until a lawyer approves.

### Where it is built

app/services/evidence_service.py (quote_match, verify_findings, parse_statement_text), app/routers/evidence.py (new witness grouping), app/models/analysis.py (ContradictionFinding gains finding_type, statement_type, page_line, search_terms), ocr_service.py language packs, drafting_engine.to_docx; migration 017 adds witnesses and witness_statements; Studio UI.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

CoCounsel and Harvey do English US-style deposition prep and can paraphrase or invent a quote, which is fatal in cross-examination; Indian research tools have no evidence analysis. Ours already discards any finding whose quotes are not in the sources, and extends that to omissions with a negative check, in the original vernacular text.

### Safeguards

Statements are privileged and contain sensitive personal data: PII-masked before Claude (names kept per guardrails), OCR vision fallback honoured per firm setting, results internal, export marked unreviewed. Case memory under RLS.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_witness.py: a fixture witness (English FIR, Hindi s.161 statement, English deposition) with 5 planted contradictions and 3 planted omissions; a mocked model returning those plus 4 fabricated findings yields exactly the 8 real ones and discarded_unverified=4.
- test_omission_negative_check: an 'omission' whose key term appears in the earlier statement is downgraded to 'check'.
- test_devanagari_quote_match: a Hindi quote with matra and whitespace variations still matches via normalization; a quote with a changed word does not reach 85%.
- Existing evidence tests keep passing (invariant 6).
- Eval: scripts/run_evals.py gains 5 witness cases; with the real model, planted-finding recall at least 75% and zero unverified quotes in output.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Label the translation shown beside each original-script quote as an unverified AI translation. Only the original quote is checked, and the lawyer confronts the witness with the original.
- Note on the sheet that statements under s.180 BNSS / s.161 CrPC can be used only to contradict the witness (s.148 BSA / s.162 CrPC), so omission candidates are prompts for the lawyer, not findings.
- In sexual-offence, POCSO and JJ matters, mask the victim's and child's names before Claude (s.72 BNS / s.23 POCSO / s.74 JJ Act sensitivity), even though names are normally kept. Force the OCR vision fallback off for these matter types.
- The export should note the s.181 BNSS / s.162 CrPC limit (statements usable only to contradict under s.148 BSA), so juniors don't treat the sheet as substantive evidence.
- evidence_service._normalize won't merge different matras or nukta forms. Add NFC normalization and a small Devanagari canonicalization (nukta, chandrabindu/anusvara) and test it, or the Hindi matching test may fail.
- The 'changed word below 85%' test only holds if the changed word is near the middle of a short quote. Fix the fixture so it is deterministic.
