### What software can fix

The search-and-cite surface for P12/P22 authority tokens inside /studio and /verify. A lawyer finds or pastes an authority, from our open corpus, from Indian Kanoon, or as a citation found in SCC Online, CaseMine or Jhana. It enters the draft as a resolved, pre-verified token. Indian Kanoon spend is capped per org by a tamper-proof, server-recorded ledger. The cap covers every path that can call Indian Kanoon: user requests, WhatsApp and phone intake, and worker jobs. Public channels get their own small sub-cap.

### What it can't fix

We don't compete on corpus size or search quality with SCC Online, Manupatra, CaseMine, Jhana or Indian Kanoon itself. We can't replace headnotes or SCC/AIR page numbers. Pricing belongs to the P19 head. Whether Indian Kanoon's terms allow merging its results into our results is a contract question; until it is confirmed in writing, its results stay in a separate attributed list. When a public-channel budget is exhausted, citations in intake replies that only Indian Kanoon could have confirmed stay unverified and are removed or marked, per invariant 3. That is the safe outcome, but it means those replies get fewer confirmed authorities.

### What the user sees

In /studio, an 'Authorities' panel with three tabs:
- 'Search': results from the shared corpus, plus a separate 'Indian Kanoon results (powered by IKanoon)' list.
- 'Paste a citation': anything found in another tool. It is resolved, or shown red and not inserted.
- 'Section': India Code text with the BNS/IPC correspondence.
'Cite this' inserts a green token.

On /billing the owner sees the month's Indian Kanoon spend, split by channel (in-app, WhatsApp intake, phone intake, background jobs). There are two caps: an org cap, and a public-intake sub-cap that defaults to Rs 0 until the owner sets it, with a per-conversation daily limit. When a cap is reached, in-app users see 'Monthly Indian Kanoon budget reached; ask your owner to raise it', and cached results still work. In WhatsApp or phone intake the client sees nothing different. The lawyer's inbox view of the chat shows 'citation not checked against Indian Kanoon (intake budget reached)' beside any citation that was marked unverified.

### What the system does

1. GET /caselaw/search gains a shared-corpus mode (hybrid BM25 + bge over judgment_texts). Indian Kanoon results are returned separately.

2. POST /authorities/resolve runs the P12 resolver. 'Cite this' adds the authority id to the draft.

3. GET /statutes/{act}/{section} reads the P22 statutes table.

4. Spend ledger (migration 014): ik_tariff; ik_budget (org_id, monthly_cap_paise, public_intake_cap_paise default 0, per_conversation_daily_calls default 5); ik_spend (org_id, user_id nullable, channel in_app|whatsapp|telephony|worker, scope_key, call_kind, paise, cache_key, created_at). ik_spend is append-only by trigger, and anon and authenticated have no insert, update or delete grants.

5. One internal function, _ik_reserve(p_org, p_user, p_channel, p_scope_key, p_kind, p_cache_key), does all reservations. It is security definer, and execute is revoked from public, anon and authenticated. It:
- takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('ik:'||p_org));
- reads the price from ik_tariff;
- checks the org monthly cap;
- for whatsapp and telephony, also checks public_intake_cap_paise and the per-scope_key daily call limit;
- inserts the row and returns true, or returns false.

6. Two callable wrappers:
(a) reserve_ik_call(p_org, p_kind, p_cache_key) is granted to authenticated. It requires p_org = active_org_id() and membership, sets channel in_app and the user to auth.uid(), and is used in user-JWT paths.
(b) reserve_ik_call_for_org(p_org, p_channel, p_scope_key, p_kind, p_cache_key) is granted only to service_role, and p_channel must be whatsapp, telephony or worker. It is used only from the server jobs already listed in invariant 2, each scoped explicitly to one organisation: WhatsApp intake (the number's org_id, with the conversation id as scope_key), phone sessions (the number's org, with the call SID), and the ARQ worker (the job's org, after its existing role re-check, with the job id).

7. In code:
- citation_service.lookup_authorities(db, keys, names, *, ik_budget) and indiankanoon_service.find_cases(names, ik_budget) and search(..., ik_budget) take a required IkBudget protocol argument. Implementations are UserIkBudget(db, org_id), which calls the rpc through the user's JWT client, and OrgIkBudget(admin, org_id, channel, scope_key), which calls reserve_ik_call_for_org. NoIkBudget makes zero calls.
- There is no default, so a call site that forgets its budget fails at type-check and test time rather than spending without limit.
- The process lru_cache becomes an explicit cache (dict plus an optional ik_lookup_cache table of name-token tuples and existence booleans, with no client data). It is checked before reserving, so cache hits cost nothing.
- whatsapp_intake.py:245 passes OrgIkBudget(admin, number['org_id'], 'whatsapp', conversation_id). live_session and telephony_session pass the user's or the number's budget. drafting.py:283 and the caselaw router pass UserIkBudget.
- If a reservation returns false, the lookup stops. Unresolved names stay unverified and invariant 3 removes or marks them.

8. set_ik_budget(org, cap, public_cap, per_conversation) is owner-only and audit-logged.

9. Query rewriting uses mask_pii first.

10. The Indian Kanoon terms review is recorded in docs/compliance/indiankanoon-terms.md. Merge and retention stay behind feature flags that are off by default.

### Where it is built

- app/services/indiankanoon_service.py (required ik_budget parameter; explicit cache replacing lru_cache)
- app/services/citation_service.py lookup_authorities (required ik_budget)
- app/services/whatsapp_intake.py (line 245), app/services/telephony_session.py, app/services/live_session.py (_lookup_authorities), app/routers/drafting.py (line 283), app/worker.py (pass budgets)
- app/routers/caselaw.py
- app/services/rag_service.py
- the P12 resolver and drafting_engine tokens
- the P22 statutes table
- frontend/src/app/studio/page.tsx and the billing page (spend by channel, caps)

New:
- app/services/ik_budget.py (the IkBudget protocol, UserIkBudget, OrgIkBudget, NoIkBudget)
- migration 014: ik_tariff, ik_budget (with the public sub-cap), ik_spend (channel, scope_key), _ik_reserve, reserve_ik_call, reserve_ik_call_for_org, set_ik_budget, ik_lookup_cache
- docs/compliance/indiankanoon-terms.md
- tests/test_ik_budget_paths.py and tests/db/test_ik_spend.sql

### Why current tools fail and this won't

This is not a better research tool; CaseMine, Jhana and Indian Kanoon search more. What they don't do is take a citation found anywhere, check it inside the firm's own draft and filing record, and feed the P02 gate. Our version of that runs at a cost that is capped, visible and attributable across every channel, including unauthenticated public intake, which no per-seat research product has to deal with. The budget is enforced in the database under a lock, priced from a server-side tariff, and required by the type signature of every function that can make a paid call. Forgetting to apply it is a test failure, not a bill.

### Safeguards

Licensed or open sources only. Indian Kanoon attribution is shown wherever its results appear. Merge and retention follow the recorded terms review. Spend is append-only, priced from the server, locked per org, and capped for every channel. Public unauthenticated intake has its own sub-cap (default zero) and a per-conversation daily limit, so an anonymous WhatsApp user can't drain the firm's credit. The service-role wrapper is granted only to service_role and is used only in the server jobs listed in invariant 2, each scoped to one organisation, with no new service-role use in user paths. An exhausted budget fails safe: citations stay unverified and are marked or removed. Masking applies before any LLM or Tavily call. Owners set caps, and every change is audit-logged.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Fixed for non-user paths. One internal _ik_reserve (same tariff, same advisory lock) sits behind two wrappers. reserve_ik_call is for user-JWT paths. reserve_ik_call_for_org(p_org, p_channel, p_scope_key, ...) is executable only by service_role, and it is called from WhatsApp intake (the number's org, with the conversation id), phone sessions (the number's org, with the call SID) and the ARQ worker (the job's org, after its existing role re-check). Those are exactly the server jobs invariant 2 already lists.
In code, lookup_authorities, find_cases and search now take a required ik_budget argument with no default, and whatsapp_intake.py:245 passes OrgIkBudget(admin, org_id, 'whatsapp', conversation_id). An AST test fails the build if any call site omits it.
Public channels also get their own public_intake_cap_paise, default Rs 0, plus a per-conversation daily limit, so public intake can't spend without limit even inside the org cap.
The requested test is added: a WhatsApp-intake citation check at the cap makes zero Indian Kanoon calls (asserted on the mocked transport) and the citation is marked unverified. Further tests cover the zero default, the per-conversation limit, telephony and worker spend, and the grants on the service-only wrapper.

### Acceptance tests

- Search: a fixture query returns a corpus paragraph with its neutral citation; mocked Indian Kanoon results come back in a separate attributed list, not merged while the merge flag is off
- Paste-a-citation: '2024 INSC 735' resolves and renders green; '(2026) 99 SCC 9999' returns not_found and can't be inserted
- In-app cap: with a Rs 5 cap and a Rs 0.50 tariff, the 11th reserve_ik_call returns false; cached repeats call no rpc
- WhatsApp at cap: an org with public_intake_cap_paise reached receives an inbound WhatsApp message whose agent reply cites an HC case the SC index doesn't know. The mocked httpx transport for api.indiankanoon.org receives zero requests, the reply marks the citation [unverified] or drops it from authority, and no ik_spend row is added
- WhatsApp default: a new org (public cap Rs 0) makes zero Indian Kanoon calls from intake; after the owner sets Rs 10, the same message makes one reserved call recorded with channel 'whatsapp' and the conversation id as scope_key
- Per-conversation limit: one WhatsApp conversation is refused after 5 reservations in a day, even with the org budget remaining; a second conversation still succeeds
- Telephony and worker: a phone session and a batch job reserve through reserve_ik_call_for_org with channels telephony and worker, and both count against the org monthly cap
- Concurrency: two parallel reservations at cap minus one call: exactly one succeeds (advisory lock shared by both wrappers)
- DB security: authenticated users can't execute reserve_ik_call_for_org or _ik_reserve; service_role can execute reserve_ik_call_for_org; direct insert, update or delete on ik_spend is denied for members and owners; a non-member calling reserve_ik_call for another org is refused; no caller can pass an amount
- Static guard: an AST test asserts that every call to indiankanoon_service.search, find_cases or citation_service.lookup_authorities in app/ passes an ik_budget argument, and that no IkBudget is constructed with a service-role client outside whatsapp_intake.py, telephony_session.py and worker.py
- set_ik_budget by an associate is refused; by an owner it writes an audit_logs row
- Hinglish query: only the masked query reaches the mocked Anthropic client
- GET /statutes/BNS/103 returns the India Code text with the 'formerly s. 302 IPC' note

### Reviewers' minor notes

- ik_lookup_cache is shared across orgs. Party-name tuples drawn from intake conversations could reveal that some org searched for a client's name. Either scope the cache per org, or only cache names already present in a public citation string.
- Show the owner the expected monthly spend at the current tariff when they set the caps, not only the spend so far.
- Migration 014 collides with other proposals. Renumber it.
- Record in the docs/compliance note that the per-conversation scope_key for WhatsApp, the conversation id, is retained in ik_spend. Purge it, or replace it with a hash, on the same schedule as the intake conversation, so spend rows do not outlive the client's data.
- Python has no type-check step in CI, so 'fails at type-check' really means a runtime TypeError plus the AST guard. Rely on the AST test and say so.
- A reservation counts even when the Indian Kanoon call then fails. That is conservative and fine, but the billing view should show failed calls separately so owners don't think the spend is a leak.
- Choose the migration number together with the five other proposals claiming 014.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Taking the unbilled clerical day off juniors and solos and making the rest of their work visible and paid: an automated daily run-sheet (tomorrow's hearings, proxy briefs, certified-copy follow-ups, client updates queued for approval, fee reminders, first drafts), plus credit for juniors' work on matter ledgers and invoices, so seniors can see and bill the value juniors create.

### What it can't fix

Low junior incomes and stipends are set by seniors, Bar Councils and the market; BCI stipend guidelines are advisory and no software makes them binding. Court-logistics work that is physical (standing in filing queues, collecting certified copies at the copying section, terminal shortages) stays physical; we only track and schedule it. Product pricing in INR is a commercial decision (noted to the P19 owner).

### What the user sees

A 'My day' page (and a 7 pm WhatsApp summary to the junior): 'Tomorrow: 4 matters. Saket Court 2 items - proxy briefs ready (open). Certified copy applied 12 days ago in Sharma - follow up at copying section (limitation exclusion running). 3 client updates drafted - waiting for Adv. Rao's approval. 2 fee reminders scheduled. Draft vakalatnama for new matter Mehta - ready.' Each item has one action button. The senior sees a 'Junior contribution' tab: appearances, proxy appearances, drafts and hours each junior logged, how much of it was invoiced and collected.

### What the system does

1. services/run_sheet.py (deterministic) builds the next day's list per user from court_cases (next_hearing_date = tomorrow, court, item number when the cause-list provider returns it), copy_applications (new small table: matter, order date, applied_on, status, ready_on; feeds the limitation exclusion owned by P06), queued client updates (P01 owner's queue), P09 fee reminders due, and drafts with status draft assigned to the user.
2. Proxy brief: a one-page brief per hearing generated from the case thread: last order text (from eCourts provider_data or uploaded order), stage, what was sought last time, open tasks; facts and dates are copied from records by code; the 'what to ask for' paragraph is AI (sonnet) from masked thread memory with citations checked by citation_service; the brief is internal (lawyer-to-lawyer) and marked 'for the appearing advocate, verify against file'.
3. Assignment: court_cases and case_threads get assigned_to (user) and appearing_advocate; junior work is captured as work_events (P10) under the junior's user id, and invoice lines carry timekeeper so the 'Junior contribution' report sums invoiced and collected amounts per junior from the P09 ledger.
4. Worker task_run_sheet at the user's chosen evening hour sends the summary via an approved WhatsApp template to the member's own registered number (not to clients).
5. Time saved is shown only as counts of completed automated items, not invented minutes.

### Where it is built

Extend: supabase/migrations/011_court_cases.sql (assigned_to, appearing_advocate columns in a new migration), app/services/ecourts_service.py (agenda(), provider_data orders), app/services/memory_service.py and app/services/citation_service.py (proxy brief), app/services/drafting_engine.py (first drafts), app/worker.py (task_run_sheet), P09 ledger and P10 work_events. New: supabase/migrations/017_run_sheet.sql (copy_applications, assignment columns), app/services/run_sheet.py, app/services/proxy_brief.py, app/routers/run_sheet.py, frontend/src/app/today/page.tsx, frontend/src/components/JuniorContribution.tsx, tests/test_run_sheet.py.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Clio, CoCounsel and Harvey are priced in USD per seat for BigLaw research, drafting and US billing, not an Indian junior's cause-list, copying-section and proxy-appearance day. Indian tools are diaries and trackers that list dates but don't prepare the brief, queue the client update, chase the fee or credit the junior. We already hold the hearings, case memory, drafting and WhatsApp channel, so the run-sheet is assembled from existing data; only the brief's argument paragraph is AI, citation-checked and labelled.

### Safeguards

Client updates and fee reminders in the run-sheet still need the responsible lawyer's approval (no AI text to clients without a lawyer). Proxy briefs are internal and labelled as aids to verify against the file; citations checked (invariant 3). PII masked before the model. Junior contribution data visible to the junior and to owners/partners only. Run-sheet worker runs server-side per org (to be added to the invariant 2 list).

### Acceptance tests

**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Letting a firm give a prospect a written, stage-wise fee estimate within minutes of an enquiry. It is built in code from the firm's own fee card (drafting, per-appearance and stage fees), the out-of-pocket items the firm enters (court fee, typing, stamp, travel), and an expected range of appearances for that matter type in that court (from P32's statistics, or the firm's default). It checks that no line breaks BCI fee rules, needs a lawyer's approval before it goes out, and later shows quoted vs actual.

### What it can't fix

We don't set or recommend what lawyers charge, and we don't publish a public price list (that may be advertising under Rule 36, and it's the firm's call). State court-fee schedules are many and changing, so the firm enters them; we compute only the few we can encode safely and cite (e.g., consumer commission fee slabs, already in workflow_service). The opponent's conduct, adjournments and appeals make any estimate a range, not a promise. Affordability is a legal-aid problem software can't fix (a pointer is given on decline; see P08).

### What the user sees

Lawyer: on an intake brief or case thread, 'Prepare estimate'. The matter type and court are prefilled. The screen shows: 'Fixed: legal notice Rs 5,000; complaint drafting Rs 15,000. Per appearance Rs 3,000 x expected 8-14-22 appearances (based on 41 similar s.138 matters of this firm in Saket courts; median 14). Out of pocket: court fee Rs (firm entry); process fee. Estimate: Rs 44,000 / 62,000 / 86,000 (low/expected/high).' Assumptions are listed, lines can be edited, and Approve and send sends it. Prospect: a one-page PDF and a WhatsApp message in their language with the same stage-wise table, an 'estimate, not a final bill' line and 'fees per hearing apply only for hearings actually attended'. Later the lawyer sees 'Quoted 62,000; billed so far 38,000 after 9 appearances'.

### What the system does

1) Migration 014 adds `fee_cards` (org_id, matter_type enum shared with workflow packs and practice areas, court_level, items[] {code, label, kind fixed|per_appearance|per_stage|out_of_pocket, amount_paise, stage}). A validator in code rejects kind values or labels matching contingency or percentage patterns ('% of', 'percent', 'success fee', 'share of award', 'हिस्सा'), citing BCI Rules Part VI ch. II r.20 and B. Sunitha; amounts must be fixed rupee values. 2) `fee_quote.compute(card, appearances_range, out_of_pocket, overrides) -> Quote` is pure integer-paise arithmetic giving low/expected/high totals and per-stage subtotals. 3) appearances_range comes from duration_service.hearing_counts(org, matter_type, court) (P32): P25/P50/P75 of hearings per disposed matter, used only if n >= 10. Otherwise the firm's default range is used, labelled 'firm default'. 4) The quote is stored in `fee_quotes` (status draft|approved|sent|accepted|expired, approved_by/at stamped by trigger and cleared on any edit, valid_until), rendered by pdf_service (ReportLab) and a fixed message template per language. 5) Sending: as a pending whatsapp_message inside the client's own conversation, released only by settle_held_reply after approval (intake_guard would hold any amount anyway), or attached to the engagement letter (P09 owner). 6) Variance: actual appearances come from court_cases hearings history, and billed amounts from the P09/P10 billing data when it exists; the variance panel is lawyer-only. 7) Audit: GENERATE_QUOTE, APPROVE_QUOTE, SEND_QUOTE.

### Where it is built

app/services/workflow_service.py (matter types; consumer fee rule reused), app/services/pdf_service.py (quote PDF), app/services/whatsapp_intake.py settle_held_reply (sending through the held-message path), app/services/audit_service.py. New: app/services/fee_quote.py, app/services/fee_card_rules.py (BCI validator), app/routers/quotes.py (GET/PUT /api/v1/fee-cards, POST /api/v1/quotes, POST /quotes/{id}/approve, POST /quotes/{id}/send), migration 014 (fee_cards, fee_quotes with RLS: owners/partners edit fee cards, all members create quotes, approval by owner/partner or the matter's lawyer), frontend/src/app/quotes/page.tsx and a 'Prepare estimate' button on the /inbox brief card.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Clio bills flat fees after engagement but doesn't estimate an Indian per-appearance matter. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI price their own seats, not the client's case. LawRato and Vakilsearch list consultation prices only. Nobody knows how many appearances a s.138 complaint takes in a given court. We get that from the firm's own disposed matters (synced from eCourts hearing history), compute the money in code from the firm's own card, refuse contingency lines, and send nothing without a lawyer. So the quote is the firm's real price, defensible and compliant, and it reaches the client in the window where P07 says they choose a lawyer.

### Safeguards

BCI: a deterministic rule against contingency and percentage-of-award fees; quotes go only to someone who contacted the firm (no public price advertising unless the firm chooses it). UPL: a quote states fees, not legal outcomes; assumptions text is fixed. A lawyer approves every quote. DPDP: the quote is tied to the consented conversation and erased with it. No AI in the arithmetic: the only data inputs are the firm card and statistics, both visible on the quote.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_fee_quote.py::test_compute_golden: card {notice 5000, complaint 15000, per_appearance 3000}, appearances (8,14,22), out_of_pocket 1200 -> totals exactly 45,200 / 63,200 / 87,200 in paise, with per-stage subtotals matching the fixture.
- test_validator_rejects_contingency: items labelled '10% of recovered amount', 'success fee', 'award ka 20 percent' -> ValidationError citing the BCI rule; a fixed 'Rs 10,000 on filing' passes.
- test_small_sample_falls_back: duration stats with n=6 -> the quote uses the firm default range and the label 'firm default', not the statistics.
- test_approval_cleared_on_edit: an approved quote whose line is edited -> approved_at null and the send endpoint returns 409.
- test_send_only_after_approval: POST /send on a draft -> 409 and the mocked whatsapp_service is not called.
- test_quote_message_template: the rendered hi/en message contains the 'estimate, not a final bill' line and no percentage sign.
- test_pdf_renders: the quote PDF builds and its extracted text contains each line label and total.
- RLS test: an associate can't edit fee_cards; org B can't read org A quotes.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Show the GST treatment on the quote. Legal services to business entities are under reverse charge, so the client pays GST directly. Otherwise business clients receive wrong totals.
- Widen the contingency validator to outcome-linked triggers ('on success', 'if we win', 'on recovery', 'jeetne par', 'वसूली पर') on per_stage items. Keep partner approval of fee cards as the real control.
- The example in what_the_user_sees (44,000 / 62,000 / 86,000) disagrees with the golden test (45,200 / 63,200 / 87,200) for the same inputs. Align them.
- The quoted-vs-actual panel depends on P09/P10 billing, which doesn't exist yet. Show it as unavailable until then.

**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Giving a client an honest, data-based range for how long matters like theirs have taken, using the firm's own matters in that court and case type (eCourts filing, disposal and hearing history). The estimator corrects for two biases in this data. Right censoring: some matters are still pending. Left truncation (delayed entry): a firm onboards matters that are already pending, and the matters it disposed of before onboarding are missing. When the client's case is already some months old, the range is conditional on that age. Published NJDG pendency-age figures appear separately, with their label. The panel says 'not enough data' instead of guessing. It also adds a lawyer-reviewed list of things that can shorten a case type (Lok Adalat, mediation, compounding), framed as options to discuss.

### What it can't fix

Judge vacancies, adjournment culture and backlog are not ours to fix. NJDG publishes aggregates (pendency by age band and court), not per-case disposal times, and its dashboards sit behind captcha-protected search, which we will never bypass. So we can't compute a district-level 'time to disposal' from NJDG. We show it only as 'X% of pending cases of this type here are older than N years'. Delayed-entry correction removes the onboarding bias, but it needs enough matters observed early in their life. A firm that only ever takes on old matters can't estimate durations for new ones, and we say so instead of extrapolating. Matters added to the system after they were already disposed can't be used without biasing the result, so they are excluded and counted. No one can predict how long a specific case will take.

### What the user sees

Lawyer, on a court case or an intake brief, sees a 'How long?' panel. Example: 'Similar matters (s.138 complaints, Saket district courts) in this firm's records: 41 (29 disposed, 12 still pending; 6 excluded because they were added after disposal). Measured from filing date. Each matter counts only from the date this firm started tracking it (Kaplan-Meier with delayed entry). For a matter already 9 months old, like this one: half were disposed within a further 14 months; 1 in 4 took more than 26 more months. Reliable from 4 months after filing (at least 10 matters under observation).' A 'Method' line names the estimator and the 'measured from' basis. A second line shows public data: 'NJDG, as of 1 Oct 2026, source link: 38% of pending NI Act cases in South Delhi are older than 3 years.' If the data can't support an estimate, the panel names the reason, for example 'Not enough similar matters observed early enough after filing to estimate', and shows only the NJDG line. A checklist offers lawyer-reviewed 'Ways this can be shorter' for the case type, each to include or leave out. 'Approve and send' gives the client a short Hindi or English WhatsApp/PDF explainer. It contains the range, what it is based on (number of matters and that it counts from filing), the sentence 'every case is different and no duration is guaranteed', and the chosen options as 'to discuss with your lawyer'.

### What the system does

1) Migration 014 adds columns to court_cases: case_type, filing_date, registration_date, disposal_date, disposal_nature and hearings_count, mapped by ecourts_service.from_provider from the provider fields. It also adds tracking_started_at date not null default (created_at::date). A BEFORE UPDATE trigger makes tracking_started_at immutable, so nobody can backdate it to put old matters at risk from day 0. 2) duration_service.similar(org, case_type, court) selects the org's matters through RLS, matching on exact normalized case_type and court. A fallback widens to district, then state, and the panel names the level used. 3) For each matter the time scale is days since filing_date. entry = max(0, tracking_started_at - filing_date); exit = disposal_date (event) or today (censored). A matter with exit <= entry was added after it was disposed. It is excluded and counted in 'excluded_added_after_disposal'. 4) duration_service.km_delayed_entry(entries, exits, events) is a plain-Python product-limit estimator with left truncation and right censoring. At each event time t the risk set is {i : entry_i < t <= exit_i}, so a matter joins the risk set only from its entry time. It returns S(t), the risk-set size at each t, n, the number of events and the method string. 5) Reliability guard: t_min is the first time the risk set reaches 10. The curve is used only from t_min onward. For the client's case at age a, the estimate is conditional: S(t | T > a0) = S(t)/S(a0), with a0 = max(a, t_min). It returns the remaining-time P25, median and P75. The estimate is suppressed, with a reason code, when n < 10, events < 5, the client's case age is below t_min ('not observed early enough'), or the risk set falls below 5 before the requested quantile. A median the curve never reaches is shown as '>X months'. 6) The naive estimator (everyone at risk from filing) is computed only for internal comparison. It is never shown, but it is logged and used in tests. 7) Hearing statistics use only fully observed matters (filing_date >= tracking_started_at, disposed). The panel shows them with that label, or suppresses them below 10 matters. The median gap between consecutive hearings is taken from hearing history inside the tracked window. P31 uses these figures. 8) njdg_benchmarks is a shared read-only table (org_id null, migration 008 pattern) loaded by scripts/load_njdg_benchmarks.py. The loader reads only CSVs a person has downloaded by hand, requires source_url and as_of, and does no captcha automation. The UI shows the figures verbatim, with their date. 9) The 'shorten' options are a static file, app/data/duration_options.json, with en/hi text per case type. CI checks every statutory reference in it with citation_service: each must have status 'statute' and none may be 'repealed'. The lawyer ticks the options that apply. 10) The client message is a fixed template filled with numbers, with no AI. It includes n, the 'measured from filing' basis and the conditional age. It goes out through the P01 approval and send path (client_updates kind 'duration').

### Where it is built

Existing: app/services/ecourts_service.py (from_provider gains the new mapped fields), migration 011's court_cases (new columns and the immutable tracking_started_at trigger in migration 014), migration 008's shared-corpus pattern (njdg_benchmarks), app/services/citation_service.py (CI check of option references), app/routers/cases.py, and the P01 client_updates send path. New: app/services/duration_service.py (similar, km_delayed_entry, conditional_quantiles, hearing_stats), scripts/load_njdg_benchmarks.py, app/data/duration_options.json, tests/fixtures/channing_house.csv with a reference-output fixture, GET /api/v1/court-cases/{id}/duration and POST /api/v1/duration/estimate (for briefs), and the panel in frontend/src/app/cases/page.tsx and the /inbox brief card.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

NJDG shows aggregate dashboards, not an estimate for a client. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI have no Indian disposal data. Manupatra and SCC have judgments, not timings. An LLM asked 'how long' invents a number. Practice-management trackers that report 'average age of our cases' make exactly the onboarding mistake: inherited old matters inflate it. Ours uses a standard survival estimator that corrects for both censoring and delayed entry. It conditions on the client's case age, shows its sample size, basis and reliable range, refuses below fixed thresholds, and never lets a model produce the number. Firms that track their cases with us (P01) build the dataset as a by-product, and it grows more reliable as matters are tracked from filing.

### Safeguards

UPL: the ranges are historical statistics, phrased as 'matters like this have taken', with a 'no guarantee' line. The shortening options are 'to discuss' and are ticked by the lawyer. A lawyer approves every client message. Data honesty: the estimator corrects for delayed entry, the 'measured from' basis and method are always shown, the curve is used only where the risk set is at least 10, and estimates are suppressed with a stated reason below fixed thresholds. tracking_started_at is immutable, so the bias correction can't be gamed by backdating. There is no captcha bypass and no scraping of eCourts or NJDG. DPDP: the statistics are computed over the org's own matters through RLS and never leave the org. The shared benchmarks hold aggregates only.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Both blocking objections were about left truncation (delayed entry), which the old proposal ignored. Fixed as follows. (1) Each matter now joins the risk set only from entry = tracking_started_at - filing_date, which is a delayed-entry product-limit estimator (step 4). tracking_started_at defaults to when the matter was first added to the system and is immutable after insert, so it can't be backdated. Matters added after they were disposed are excluded and counted, not used. (2) Delayed-entry KM is unstable where few matters are under observation early on. So the curve is used only from t_min, the point where at least 10 matters are at risk. Estimates are conditional on the client's case age (S(t)/S(a0)), which is the honest question for an already-pending case. Below t_min the panel says 'not observed early enough' instead of extrapolating. (3) The method and basis are shown in the panel, the API payload and the client message: 'Kaplan-Meier with delayed entry; measured from filing; each matter counted from when the firm began tracking it'. (4) Tests: Channing House, the published left-truncated example in Klein & Moeschberger, is checked against stored survival::survfit output. A seeded synthetic fixture shows the naive and delayed-entry medians differ, with the naive one biased upward and the delayed-entry one close to the truth. There are also tests of risk-set construction, exclusion and conditioning. (5) Hearing-count statistics had the same selection bias, so they now use only fully observed matters (filed after tracking began) and are labelled that way.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_duration.py::test_km_right_censored_known_values: on the Freireich 6-MP treatment arm with no truncation (entry=0), survival values match the published Kaplan-Meier table to 3 decimals, and the median matches the published value.
- test_km_delayed_entry_channing_house: on the Channing House left-truncated data (Klein & Moeschberger, Survival Analysis, section 4.6), S(t) and the risk-set sizes equal the stored reference output from survival::survfit(Surv(entry, exit, event)) to 4 decimals at every event time. A dev-only cross-check against lifelines KaplanMeierFitter(entry=...) produces the same values.
- test_naive_vs_delayed_entry_differ: a seeded synthetic cohort has exponential durations with a true median of 18 months. Matters are filed over 10 years. The firm onboards in year 6, so matters disposed before then are missing, and matters still pending enter late. The naive KM median exceeds 22 months (biased up). The delayed-entry median is within 18 +/- 2.5 months. Matters disposed before onboarding are counted in excluded_added_after_disposal.
- test_risk_set_built_from_entry: a matter with entry=300 days and exit=500 days is not in the risk set at t=200 and is in it at t=400.
- test_added_after_disposal_excluded: a matter whose tracking_started_at is after its disposal_date is excluded and counted, and n drops by one.
- test_conditional_on_case_age: for a case already 9 months old, the reported median is the remaining-time median from S(t)/S(9 months) and matches a hand-computed fixture.
- test_suppressed_below_t_min: when the client's case age is below the first time the risk set reaches 10, the result is suppressed with reason 'not_observed_early_enough'.
- test_suppress_small_n_and_few_events: with n=9, or with 4 events, no estimate is returned and the reason codes are 'n<10' and 'events<5'.
- test_tracking_started_at_immutable: as an authenticated user, an UPDATE of court_cases.tracking_started_at raises 42501. Other columns stay editable.
- test_method_and_basis_in_panel_payload: the API response includes method='kaplan_meier_delayed_entry', measured_from='filing_date', t_min and the level used (court, district or state).
- test_fallback_level_labelled: 3 matches in the court establishment and 15 in the district give an estimate that uses the district, and the label says 'district'.
- test_hearing_stats_only_fully_observed: a matter filed before tracking started is not counted in hearing counts. P25/P50/P75 match numpy.percentile (linear method) computed without numpy in the product code.
- test_from_provider_maps_dates_and_hearings: a provider fixture fills filing_date, disposal_date and hearings_count correctly.
- test_options_citations_valid (CI): every reference in duration_options.json passes citation_service with status 'statute', and none is 'repealed' or 'invalid'.
- test_client_template: the rendered hi and en messages contain n, the 'measured from filing' basis, the source line and the 'no duration is guaranteed' sentence, and pass verify_output_safety without triggering the disclaimer.
- test_njdg_loader_requires_source: a CSV row without source_url or as_of is rejected.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Matters that leave the firm before disposal (client changes lawyer, transfer) are censored, and that censoring is plausibly informative. Exclude or flag them separately rather than treating them as ordinary censoring.
- Most firms will hit 'not enough data' for most (case type, court) pairs for a long time. Make the NJDG line and the fallback level the visible default, so the panel isn't usually empty.
- The client explainer should say the figures come from the firm's own past matters and are not an estimate for this case. It should also avoid figures from cells small enough (n near 10 in one court) that another client's matter could be inferred.
- Since estimates below t_min are suppressed, a0 = max(a, t_min) always equals a when an estimate is shown. Simplify the text.
- Delayed-entry KM assumes entry is independent of remaining duration. Firms that take matters at a particular stage (for example appeals after delay) can violate this. Note it in the Method line.

The estimator corrects for two biases in this data. Right censoring: some matters are still pending. Left truncation (delayed entry): a firm onboards matters that are already pending, and the matters it disposed of before onboarding are missing. When the client's case is already some months old, the range is conditional on that age. Published NJDG pendency-age figures appear separately, with their label. The panel says 'not enough data' instead of guessing. It also adds a lawyer-reviewed list of things that can shorten a case type (Lok Adalat, mediation, compounding), framed as options to discuss.

So we can't compute a district-level 'time to disposal' from NJDG. We show it only as 'X% of pending cases of this type here are older than N years'. solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Letting an advocate publish only what BCI Rule 36 permits, with a deterministic checker for bios, websites and posts.

The product's own outbound channels cannot open a conversation with a stranger, and cannot be turned into a marketing channel to past enquirers or clients.

Every legitimate send, template or in-window, goes through one registry and one guard, under one contract that P24 and P33 both cite. Each send carries a typed, recorded reason.

No client-facing slot carries staff-typed free text. Every value is a typed primitive, or is rendered by the server from closed enums, structured fields or a lawyer-approved, hash-pinned record of the same matter.

### What it can't fix

Whether a post or message is misconduct is decided by the State Bar Council under Advocates Act s.35, and the law is unsettled: Sulekha's SLP is pending. Our checker is conservative information, not clearance.

We will not build directories, ratings, badges, SEO, paid ads or review solicitation.

We cannot police what advocates post or send outside the product, or offline touting.

A lawyer can still approve a promotional explanation, either by phrasing it impersonally or by using the audited override. The approver stays responsible; we make it traceable, not impossible.

A lawyer typing a reply in the inbox, inside the 24-hour window to someone who wrote first, is a human message. It is checked and audited, but the lawyer stays responsible for it.

Template approval and categorisation by Meta, and its changing parameter rules, are outside our control. We re-sync and fail closed.

Generic labels ('your document dated 12 Oct') are less specific than a document's title. That is the price of closing the free-text channel.

### What the user sees

Unchanged: the 'Public profile' page, 'Check my text', the 'Who we can message' panel, the follow-up dialog and the Rule 36 override on approval.

Send dialog: it shows P24's template from template_registry in the client's language, every slot filled by the server and labelled with its source, for example:
- 'Document: Lease deed dated 12 Oct 2026 (from document type and date)';
- 'Case: Sharma v. Verma (from eCourts sync)', or 'Case: your case (hand-entered title not sent)';
- 'Explanation part 2 of 3: approved by A. Rao on 12 Oct';
- 'Consent notice v4 (Hindi)';
- 'Rs 25,000 received on 10 Oct: ledger entry #88'.

Slots cannot be typed into. A filename or title the staff typed is never shown as a slot value.

An in-window explanation (inside the 24-hour window) is sent as the approved record body itself, with the same labels.

A blocked send shows a specific reason:
- 'Changed since approval: re-approve';
- 'Record belongs to a different matter';
- 'Document type not set: choose one';
- 'Value looks like a contact or solicitation';
- 'Too long for this template in Hindi: send as document'.

### What the system does

1) One contract, app/services/template_contract.py, cited identically by P24 and P33.
- Store: template_registry is the only store. It is seeded and versioned by P24's migration. data/wa_templates.json and every P33-defined row are deleted.
- Ownership: P24 owns the content (names, bodies, languages, per-language max_len, param_schema, Meta categories). P33 owns enforcement (outbound_policy, slot resolvers, meta_param_check and the send functions).
- Canonical names are P24's: client_explanation_v1, client_explanation_doc_v1, affidavit_text_review_v1 and channel_consent_optin_v1. They sit alongside the P09, P35, reminder and enquiry templates under their round-4 names. CANONICAL_TEMPLATES in the contract module is the single list; explanation_ready_v1, explanation_doc_v1 and consent_optin_v1 exist nowhere.
- Slot kinds (SLOT_KINDS):
  - primitives: date, time, enum, int_small;
  - bound: org_field, document_title_from_record, case_title_from_matter, hearing_date_from_matter, approved_record_text, record_part_label, approved_record_media, consent_notice, and the ledger_* and invoice_* kinds.
- APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES maps kind to (table, param_text_col, param_sha_col, body_text_col, body_sha_col, approved_by_col, approved_at_col, matter_col, part_label_col, media_sha_col). P24 fills the entries for its tables and P09 the entry for fee_terms.
- P33 hardcodes no template's slots or limits. The guard reads param_schema and max_len (for example P24's 350 for client_explanation_v1 {{3}} in hi) from the row being sent.

2) document_title_from_record(ref) replaces document_title.
- The ref resolves to a same-org, same-matter document, draft or explanation-source record.
- It renders DOC_KIND_LABELS[lang][doc_kind] + DATED[lang] + format_date(lang, document_date). doc_kind is a closed enum (lease_deed, leave_and_licence, sale_deed, agreement, nda, employment_agreement, loan_agreement, guarantee_deed, sha, spa, will, poa, affidavit, legal_notice, bail_application, plaint, written_statement, order, other_document) and the labels are P24-authored per language.
- Filenames, titles and storage paths are never read by the resolver. It selects only doc_kind and document_date, and a test asserts the column list.
- If doc_kind is null, it falls back to case_title_from_matter; failing that, to GENERIC_DOC[lang] ('your document' / 'आपका दस्तावेज़').

3) case_title_from_matter is closed the same way.
- It renders '<petitioners[0]> v. <respondents[0]>' only from a court_cases row with source='ecourtsindia', whose arrays equal the provider_data snapshot, which is itself hash-checked.
- Hand-entered rows (source='manual'), court_cases.title and case_threads.title are never used. They render GENERIC_CASE[lang] ('your case').

4) Defence in depth on every rendered bound value (except org_field(office_phone) and the ledger and date kinds), via slot_value_guard:
- it refuses digit runs of 7 or more, URLs and e-mail addresses, and the record-profile solicitation patterns ('call', 'refer', 'contact us', 'best', 'no. 1' and their Hindi forms) with slot_value_flagged;
- org fields are checked by the publication profile when they are saved.

5) In-window sends: send_text(body_ref) replaces free-form text for anything not typed by a human.
- whatsapp_service.send_text is renamed _post_text. A CI grep fails on any call outside outbound_policy.
- outbound_policy offers exactly three in-window functions:
  - send_body_ref(kind, id, reason): resolves APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES body_text_col for the same org and matter, checks sha256(NFC(body)) equals body_sha_col (otherwise approval_stale), checks approved_by is not null, applies Meta's 4,096-character text limit, requires an open 24-hour window from an inbound message, and records body_sha256 and ref;
  - send_lawyer_reply(text): an authenticated lawyer's own typed text, in an open window only, checked by the publication profile (a flag blocks unless overridden with a reason) and audited with the actor;
  - send_intake_reply: the existing P07 intake path, unchanged, in-window only.
- AI-generated text can never reach send_lawyer_reply: the route takes only a request body typed in the inbox and rejects any draft_id.

6) Template sends.
- meta_param_check is unchanged: no newlines, tabs or runs of 4 or more spaces; per-slot max_len and a hydrated body of at most 1,024 characters, both from the row; body_sha256 pinned per language.
- assert_may_initiate is unchanged: reasons (a)-(f), the enquiry caps, MARKETING refused and no bulk.
- The Rule 36 record and publication profiles are unchanged from round 5.
- Sent rows store reason, ref, template, language, body_sha256, slot_refs and slot_values_sha256. Blocked attempts are audited (OUTBOUND_BLOCKED) with an HMAC of the number.

### Where it is built

Extend:
- app/services/whatsapp_service.py: send_text becomes the private _post_text; send_template takes a language and resolved parameters only;
- app/services/whatsapp_intake.py and app/routers/whatsapp.py: inbox replies go through send_lawyer_reply;
- app/worker.py: hearing reminders use hearing_reminder with case_title_from_matter and hearing_date_from_matter;
- app/services/twilio_service.py: as in round 4.

New (P33):
- app/services/outbound_policy.py;
- app/services/slot_resolvers.py (document_title_from_record, case_title_from_matter, approved_record_text, record_part_label, approved_record_media, consent_notice, org_field, ledger and invoice);
- app/services/slot_value_guard.py;
- app/services/rule36_service.py, app/rules/rule36.yaml, data/rule36_record_allowlist.yaml;
- app/routers/profile.py.

Shared and cited identically by both proposals:
- app/services/template_contract.py (CANONICAL_TEMPLATES, SLOT_KINDS, APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES, DOC_KINDS and the per-language labels, with P24 authoring the labels);
- tests/fixtures/template_refs.py;
- tests/test_template_contract.py.

Data and migrations:
- template_registry and its seed rows come from P24's migration;
- P33's migration adds the doc_kind enum column and document_date on documents and drafts (nullable, set in the upload and studio UI), the sent-message columns, approve_text() with the override columns, and the wa_templates_status view;
- P33's migration deletes nothing from P24's rows.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Clio Grow, Avvo, Justdial, Sulekha and SEO agencies assume advertising is legal. WhatsApp CRMs (Interakt, WATI, AiSensy) run broadcasts with free-text variables, so any 'reminder' can carry a pitch, and even their 'document name' variable is whatever staff typed.

Ours has no broadcast path and refuses MARKETING templates. It has one registry, owned for content by P24 and for enforcement by P33, under one contract module and one cross-proposal test. No slot ever carries a filename, a hand-typed title or other free text: labels come from closed enums, dates and court-synced party names, or from hash-pinned, lawyer-approved records of the same matter, with a contact and solicitation guard on top.

### Safeguards

Outbound sending is an allowlist in the send functions:
- no bulk endpoint and no MARKETING template;
- capped enquiry follow-ups;
- no free-text slot, and no filename or hand-typed title in any slot;
- one registry, one contract module and one cross-proposal CI test;
- every bound value is server-rendered from enums, structured or court-synced fields, or hash-pinned approved records of the same org and matter, then passes the contact and solicitation guard and Meta's checks before the call;
- in-window sends are either an approved, hash-checked body_ref, or a lawyer's own typed and checked reply. AI text never goes out free-form.

Overrides need a reason, are audited and stay labelled. The checker is information, not clearance.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objections on the registry contradicting P24 (two sources, names, slot kinds, max_len, opt-in slots, circular ownership, no send_text(body_ref)):
- We align with P24's design. template_registry, seeded by P24's migration, is the only store, and data/wa_templates.json is deleted. The names are P24's (client_explanation_v1, client_explanation_doc_v1, affidavit_text_review_v1, channel_consent_optin_v1), and explanation_ready_v1 and the other P33 names are gone. The slot kinds are P24's (document_title_from_record, approved_record_media).
- Ownership is stated once: P24 owns the content, P33 owns the enforcement. Both proposals cite app/services/template_contract.py for CANONICAL_TEMPLATES, SLOT_KINDS and the APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES columns.
- P33 hardcodes no slot lists or max_len values. It reads param_schema and max_len from the row, so P24's 350 and its opt-in slots govern.
- send_body_ref resolves approved bodies and checks their hashes for in-window sends, and raw send_text is made private and grep-gated.
- One shared test file checks the inventory and runs every seeded row through the guard.

Objections on document_title(ref) being a free-text hole:
- It is replaced by document_title_from_record, which renders a doc_kind enum label plus a date in the template language and never reads a filename or title. The fallback is case_title_from_matter, which itself now uses only eCourts-synced party names and never hand-entered titles, and then a generic label.
- slot_value_guard adds a contact and solicitation check on every rendered value.
- Tests added: the promotional filename is absent from the payload, the resolver's column list is asserted, and a hand-entered case title is not sent.

### Acceptance tests

With doc_kind null, it renders the case title fallback or 'आपका दस्तावेज़'.

- Unit: slot_value_guard refuses an eCourts party name containing a URL or a 10-digit number with slot_value_flagged, with 0 Meta calls.
- Cross-proposal CI (objection, registry): tests/test_template_contract.py applies every migration to embedded Postgres and loads template_registry. It asserts:

- 'explanation_ready_v1', 'explanation_doc_v1' and 'consent_optin_v1' appear in no row, no file under app/ or data/, and no test fixture;
- data/wa_templates.json does not exist;
- every param_schema slot kind is in SLOT_KINDS;
- every template has a reason mapping;
- no MARKETING row exists.

(2) Run send_intake_reply and send_reviewed_ai_reply through the Rule 36 publication profile plus slot_value_guard's contact and solicitation patterns, blocking or holding for a lawyer on a flag. (3) Correct the safeguard text. - case_title_from_matter trusts court_cases rows with source='ecourtsindia' whose petitioner and respondent arrays equal provider_data. All of those columns are writable by the staff member. Migration 011 grants authenticated a plain INSERT and UPDATE policy on court_cases with no column restriction. app/routers/cases.py sync_case runs ecourts_service.sync on ctx.db(), the user's own client. So anyone can POST to PostgREST a row with source='ecourtsindia', petitioners=['Pune's top property advocate Sharma'] and a matching provider_data. This reopens the free-text slot that this round claims is closed, in hearing reminders and in the fallback for document titles. proposal.solvable_part:
Letting an advocate publish only what BCI Rule 36 permits, with a deterministic checker for bios, websites and posts.

The product's own outbound channels cannot open a conversation with a stranger, and cannot be turned into a marketing channel to past enquirers or clients.

Every legitimate send, template or in-window, goes through one registry and one guard, under one contract that P24 and P33 both cite. Each send carries a typed, recorded reason.

No client-facing slot carries staff-typed free text. Every value is a typed primitive, or is rendered by the server from closed enums, structured fields or a lawyer-approved, hash-pinned record of the same matter.
proposal.out_of_scope:
Whether a post or message is misconduct is decided by the State Bar Council under Advocates Act s.35, and the law is unsettled: Sulekha's SLP is pending. Our checker is conservative information, not clearance.

We will not build directories, ratings, badges, SEO, paid ads or review solicitation.

We cannot police what advocates post or send outside the product, or offline touting.

A lawyer can still approve a promotional explanation, either by phrasing it impersonally or by using the audited override. The approver stays responsible; we make it traceable, not impossible.

A lawyer typing a reply in the inbox, inside the 24-hour window to someone who wrote first, is a human message. It is checked and audited, but the lawyer stays responsible for it.

Template approval and categorisation by Meta, and its changing parameter rules, are outside our control. We re-sync and fail closed.

Generic labels ('your document dated 12 Oct') are less specific than a document's title. That is the price of closing the free-text channel.
proposal.what_the_system_does:
1) One contract, app/services/template_contract.py, cited identically by P24 and P33.
- Store: template_registry is the only store. It is seeded and versioned by P24's migration. data/wa_templates.json and every P33-defined row are deleted.
- Ownership: P24 owns the content (names, bodies, languages, per-language max_len, param_schema, Meta categories). P33 owns enforcement (outbound_policy, slot resolvers, meta_param_check and the send functions).
- Canonical names are P24's: client_explanation_v1, client_explanation_doc_v1, affidavit_text_review_v1 and channel_consent_optin_v1. They sit alongside the P09, P35, reminder and enquiry templates under their round-4 names. CANONICAL_TEMPLATES in the contract module is the single list; explanation_ready_v1, explanation_doc_v1 and consent_optin_v1 exist nowhere.
- Slot kinds (SLOT_KINDS):
  - primitives: date, time, enum, int_small;
  - bound: org_field, document_title_from_record, case_title_from_matter, hearing_date_from_matter, approved_record_text, record_part_label, approved_record_media, consent_notice, and the ledger_* and invoice_* kinds.
- APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES maps kind to (table, param_text_col, param_sha_col, body_text_col, body_sha_col, approved_by_col, approved_at_col, matter_col, part_label_col, media_sha_col). P24 fills the entries for its tables and P09 the entry for fee_terms.
- P33 hardcodes no template's slots or limits. The guard reads param_schema and max_len (for example P24's 350 for client_explanation_v1 {{3}} in hi) from the row being sent.

2) document_title_from_record(ref) replaces document_title.
- The ref resolves to a same-org, same-matter document, draft or explanation-source record.
- It renders DOC_KIND_LABELS[lang][doc_kind] + DATED[lang] + format_date(lang, document_date). doc_kind is a closed enum (lease_deed, leave_and_licence, sale_deed, agreement, nda, employment_agreement, loan_agreement, guarantee_deed, sha, spa, will, poa, affidavit, legal_notice, bail_application, plaint, written_statement, order, other_document) and the labels are P24-authored per language.
- Filenames, titles and storage paths are never read by the resolver. It selects only doc_kind and document_date, and a test asserts the column list.
- If doc_kind is null, it falls back to case_title_from_matter; failing that, to GENERIC_DOC[lang] ('your document' / 'आपका दस्तावेज़').

3) case_title_from_matter is closed the same way.
- It renders '<petitioners[0]> v. <respondents[0]>' only from a court_cases row with source='ecourtsindia', whose arrays equal the provider_data snapshot, which is itself hash-checked.
- Hand-entered rows (source='manual'), court_cases.title and case_threads.title are never used. They render GENERIC_CASE[lang] ('your case').

4) Defence in depth on every rendered bound value (except org_field(office_phone) and the ledger and date kinds), via slot_value_guard:
- it refuses digit runs of 7 or more, URLs and e-mail addresses, and the record-profile solicitation patterns ('call', 'refer', 'contact us', 'best', 'no. 1' and their Hindi forms) with slot_value_flagged;
- org fields are checked by the publication profile when they are saved.

5) In-window sends: send_text(body_ref) replaces free-form text for anything not typed by a human.
- whatsapp_service.send_text is renamed _post_text. A CI grep fails on any call outside outbound_policy.
- outbound_policy offers exactly three in-window functions:
  - send_body_ref(kind, id, reason): resolves APPROVED_TEXT_SOURCES body_text_col for the same org and matter, checks sha256(NFC(body)) equals body_sha_col (otherwise approval_stale), checks approved_by is not null, applies Meta's 4,096-character text limit, requires an open 24-hour window from an inbound message, and records body_sha256 and ref;
  - send_lawyer_reply(text): an authenticated lawyer's own typed text, in an open window only, checked by the publication profile (a flag blocks unless overridden with a reason) and audited with the actor;
  - send_intake_reply: the existing P07 intake path, unchanged, in-window only.
- AI-generated text can never reach send_lawyer_reply: the route takes only a request body typed in the inbox and rejects any draft_id.

6) Template sends.
- meta_param_check is unchanged: no newlines, tabs or runs of 4 or more spaces; per-slot max_len and a hydrated body of at most 1,024 characters, both from the row; body_sha256 pinned per language.
- assert_may_initiate is unchanged: reasons (a)-(f), the enquiry caps, MARKETING refused and no bulk.
- The Rule 36 record and publication profiles are unchanged from round 5.
- Sent rows store reason, ref, template, language, body_sha256, slot_refs and slot_values_sha256. Blocked attempts are audited (OUTBOUND_BLOCKED) with an HMAC of the number.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Giving the firm a quick 'Claim check' for things clients bring from reels, YouTube or forwards. Code finds every section and case the claim mentions and labels each repealed (with the BNS/BNSS/BSA equivalent), non-existent, unverified or valid. Code also finds guaranteed-outcome phrases ('guaranteed bail', 'instant divorce', 'sure acquittal', Hindi and Hinglish forms). A grounded, plain-language explainer is drafted in the client's language and the lawyer approves it before it goes to their own client.

### What it can't fix

We can't take down influencer content, police non-enrolled advisers, or stop clients watching. We won't download or scrape Instagram/YouTube media. The input is text the client or lawyer pastes, a screenshot (OCR), or a voice note (transcribed). We don't publish counter-content publicly (Rule 36 limits lawyers' public posting, and it's the firm's decision). Whether a legal proposition is right for this client's facts needs the lawyer; the section registry checks that a section exists, not what it says.

### What the user sees

Lawyer: in /inbox or a case thread, 'Check a claim', with paste, screenshot or voice. Example result: 'Claim: "Section 498A IPC lagao, 24 ghante me guaranteed bail milegi". Found: s.498A IPC — REPEALED for offences from 1 Jul 2024; equivalent ss. 85-86 BNS. Phrase "guaranteed bail" — no outcome can be guaranteed (BCI circular 17 Jul 2026 prohibits such claims). Section 999 BNS — DOES NOT EXIST.' Below that is a draft explainer for the client in Hindi: what the video said, what the law currently says (only verified citations), what depends on their facts, and that no outcome is guaranteed. The lawyer edits it and sends it to the client through WhatsApp (held-message path) or as a PDF. Client: a calm, short explainer from their own lawyer that names no influencer.

### What the system does

1) Input: pasted text; a screenshot goes through ocr_service, then the text; a voice note through whatsapp_service.transcribe_voice_note. A client's forwarded WhatsApp message can be turned into a claim check by the lawyer from the inbox. 2) Deterministic checks first: citation_service.check(text, Sources(empty grounding)) returns per-citation status (repealed with equivalent, statute, invalid, known_case, unverified). `claim_check.guarantees(text)` is a regex list in en/hi/Hinglish ('guarantee', 'pakka', '100%', 'sure shot', 'instant divorce', 'zaroor milegi', 'गारंटी', 'पक्का') plus guardrails' guaranteed-outcome patterns. Limitation phrasing ('kabhi bhi case kar sakte ho', 'no time limit') is flagged 'check limitation'. 3) Grounding: RAG over the firm and shared corpus (rag_service) using the masked claim, and the jurisdiction notes. 4) AI step: claude-sonnet-5-5 with a fixed cached system prompt (prompt_engine.build_system) gets the masked claim, the deterministic findings as facts it must not contradict, and the retrieved passages. It returns the explainer in a fixed JSON {said, current_law[], depends_on[], no_guarantee}. 5) Post-checks in code: citation_service.verify_text on the explainer (invalid/unverified marked or removed per invariant 3); verify_output_safety (disclaimer appended); a check that every repealed citation in the claim is mentioned with its equivalent; and a check that the explainer itself contains no guarantee phrase. Failures hold the draft with reasons. 6) Stored in `claim_checks` (org_id, thread or conversation id, input_masked, findings jsonb, draft, status, approved_by/at trigger). Sent only after approval, through the P01/P07 approved-send path; audited (CLAIM_CHECK, SEND_CLAIM_EXPLAINER). 7) The repealed-code mapping and guarantee regexes are shared with intake_guard so public-facing replies benefit as well.
