solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Giving a small chamber a working DPDP kit inside the tool it already uses:
- client data moved off personal phones and Gmail into matter-scoped, encrypted, access-logged firm storage;
- itemised consent notices;
- a personal-data inventory per matter;
- a retention schedule that surfaces matters due for review but never erases unless the client has been offered their papers safely and an owner approves;
- a data-principal request and grievance register with timers;
- a breach register that drafts the Board and data-principal intimations.
The return of papers is designed so the kit itself cannot leak a file: the notice carries no link and no matter detail, and the export is released only after the lawyer re-verifies the client's identity. Most of the plumbing already exists: trash with erasure certificates, legal hold, maker-checker approvals, consent fields and WhatsApp Business intake (migrations 012-013).

### What it can't fix

We cannot delete what stays on an advocate's personal phone or Gmail. We can import it, give a checklist and record an attestation.

The firm remains the data fiduciary. These are legal judgments the firm makes, and our defaults are labelled as such:
- whether it is a Significant Data Fiduciary;
- how s.17(1)(a) and the retention rules apply to a file;
- when a closed file may safely be destroyed (limitation for negligence claims, connected matters, appeals).

We cannot know whether a mobile number has been recycled by the operator. We reduce the risk by sending a neutral, detail-free notice only after the lawyer reconfirms the contact, and by never releasing documents without identity re-verification. A stranger who receives the neutral message still learns that the firm wanted to reach someone at that number.

Identity re-verification is the lawyer's judgment. We record its method and time but cannot verify a physical ID check ourselves. Physical handover is recorded on the lawyer's word plus a receipt upload. Paper files are covered only through scanning.

Opposing parties' data is processed under the legal-claims exemption. We record that ground but cannot decide it.

### What the user sees

A 'Data & DPDP' section with five screens: Import, Inventory, Retention review, Requests & grievances, and Breach register. Import, Inventory, Requests and Breaches are as in round 2. Retention review now works like this:

(1) Due for review. Matters past closed_at plus the retention period, with eligibility or skip reasons.

(2) Reconfirm contact. Before any notice, the lawyer sees the client's contacts with their last confirmed date. A contact is current if the client messaged from it in the last 90 days. Otherwise the lawyer must record how they reconfirmed it (spoke to the client on it, the client confirmed it by email, other source plus a note) within 14 days before sending. Where no contact can be reconfirmed, the screen offers the printable neutral letter to the last known postal address instead.

(3) Send neutral notice. The message is fixed text, English or Hindi: 'Namaste. This is <firm name>. Please contact our office at <office phone> (<office hours>) regarding papers you entrusted to us.' It carries no link, no client name, no matter title, no case number and no party names. A preview shows exactly what will be sent.

(4) Client responds. The lawyer records an identity re-verification: in-person ID check, video call, or a phone call where the client answered details on file, with a note. Only the last 4 characters of an ID shown are recorded, never the full number.

(5) Release export. Only after step 4 is a 'Create secure download' button enabled. It produces a single-use link valid for 24 hours, delivered to a contact the client confirmed during verification. A separate 6-digit code is read out on the call or sent on a different channel from the link. The page shows 'Link used' or 'Expired' afterwards. Physical collection at the office is always offered as the alternative.

(6) Outcome. Recorded as exported, returned in person (date plus receipt), keep requested, destroy requested, or no response. 'No response' is set automatically when the notice is undeliverable or unanswered after the notice period, and it shows 'Physical collection was offered at the office'.

(7) Owner approval of the erasure batch. As before, with the 'client originals not returned' flag and a typed note where needed.

### What the system does

1) Importers, the access log, the inventory, the DSR register, the breach register, the consent notice and encryption are unchanged from round 2. Importers are deterministic parsers, the inventory holds counts and HMACs, and the DSR and breach timers are computed.

2) The retention queue is unchanged. queue_retention_candidates(p_org) is SECURITY DEFINER, granted to service_role only, and only queues and skips. It never trashes. Skip reasons cover legal hold, a pending linked court_case, unpaid fees, an open DSR, and a held connected matter.

3) Contact reconfirmation. This is new in this round and fixes the objection.
- New table contact_reconfirmations: queue_id, contact_kind (whatsapp | sms | email | postal), contact_hmac, method (recent_inbound | spoke_on_number | client_confirmed_email | other), note, confirmed_by, confirmed_at.
- retention_service.can_send_notice(queue_id) is true only if one of these holds:
  - (a) the contact sent an inbound message within 90 days, derived from whatsapp_messages and recorded automatically as method recent_inbound;
  - (b) a lawyer-recorded reconfirmation exists for that exact contact_hmac with confirmed_at no more than 14 days before the send.
  Otherwise the send returns 422 'reconfirm contact'.
- The postal letter is printable without a reconfirmation, but only to the address on file, with the same neutral text.

4) Neutral notice. RETURN_NOTICE_TEMPLATES (en, hi) are product-owned P33 template_registry rows with audience 'client_matter' and param_schema [office_name, office_phone, office_hours], all filled from organizations fields only.
- render_return_notice() takes no matter object at all, so matter data cannot reach it by construction.
- A post-render guard refuses the send if the body matches a URL pattern (https?://, www., wa.me, a domain followed by '/') or contains any of the matter's title, case_number, cnr, client_name or party_index display names.
- It is sent through outbound_policy reason client_of_matter to the reconfirmed contact. notice_sent_at and notice_delivery_status are recorded, and status is updated from Meta's status webhook (sent / delivered / read / failed).

5) Identity re-verification. New table identity_verifications: queue_id, method (in_person_id | video_call | phone_known_details | id_document_match), id_last4 (nullable), performed_by, performed_at, note (required), and confirmed_delivery_contact_hmac (the contact the client asked the link to go to).
- A check requires performed_at > notice_sent_at.
- Only lawyers on the matter or partners can record one.

6) Export release. POST /dpdp/retention/{queue_id}/export-link returns 403 unless an identity_verifications row exists with performed_at > notice_sent_at.
- It creates client_export_grants: token_sha256, code_sha256 (6-digit, random), expires_at = now() + 24h, max_uses = 1, used_at, attempts (max 5), link_channel, code_channel, and a CHECK constraint link_channel <> code_channel. 'read_on_call' counts as a channel.
- The link goes to confirmed_delivery_contact only.
- GET /export/{token} shows a code form. POST with the code streams the zip of client_supplied documents and correspondence, encrypted with a key derived from the code.
- On success used_at is set. Reuse returns 410, expiry returns 410, and after 5 wrong codes the grant is locked.
- Every attempt is audited (EXPORT_CLIENT_FILE, EXPORT_CODE_FAILED), and the download is logged as DOWNLOAD_DOCUMENT.

7) No response. If notice_delivery_status='failed', or no identity verification exists by notice_sent_at + return_notice_days (>= 30, default 60), the outcome may be set to no_response, with physical_return_offered=true (the neutral text invites the client to the office). If client_supplied documents exist, owner approval needs the typed note.

8) Erasure is unchanged: request_approval('retention_erase'), owner-only via approver_roles, the requester cannot decide, and trash_item runs under the owner's JWT, re-checking legal hold. Then the 30-day trash and the erasure certificate follow.

### Where it is built

Extend:
- supabase/migrations/013 functions, via migration 016: retention_erase in request_approval and approver_roles; trash_item accepts a retention_erase approval.
- app/services/safety_service.py.
- app/worker.py: task_retention_review, queue only.
- app/services/whatsapp_intake.py: the status webhook updates notice_delivery_status, and inbound messages feed recent_inbound reconfirmation.
- app/services/document_service.py and app/services/ocr_service.py: the client_supplied flag.
- app/core/guardrails.py: analyze-only counting.
- app/services/audit_service.py: IMPORT_CHAT, VIEW_DOCUMENT, DOWNLOAD_DOCUMENT, LOG_DSR, CLOSE_DSR, LOG_BREACH, SEND_RETURN_NOTICE, RECONFIRM_CONTACT, VERIFY_CLIENT_IDENTITY, CREATE_EXPORT_GRANT, EXPORT_CLIENT_FILE, EXPORT_CODE_FAILED, RECORD_RETURN, REQUEST_RETENTION_ERASE and ATTEST_DEVICE_CLEANUP.
- CLAUDE.md invariant 2: the retention queue builder.
New:
- app/services/import_service.py, app/services/dpdp_service.py and app/services/retention_service.py (render_return_notice, can_send_notice, export grants);
- app/routers/dpdp.py, plus the public app/routers/client_export.py (token plus code, no JWT, rate-limited by IP and token);
- supabase/migrations/016_dpdp_kit.sql: personal_data_inventory, retention_queue (notice_sent_at, notice_delivery_status, physical_return_offered), contact_reconfirmations, identity_verifications, client_export_grants (with the channel CHECK), data_principal_requests, breach_incidents and device_cleanup_attestations, plus the closed_at, retention_years, return_notice_days and client_supplied columns, all with RLS;
- frontend/src/app/data/ (retention flow steps 1-7) and frontend/src/app/export/[token]/page.tsx (code entry).
Uses P33's outbound_policy and template_registry, and P46's party_index for the leak guard.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI have no concept of a chamber's DPDP obligations. Clio isn't built for Indian law or WhatsApp. WhatsApp and Gmail keep no matter-level retention, consent or breach logs. Generic DPDP platforms treat retention as automatic deletion, which ignores the advocate's duty to return papers (no lien: R.D. Saxena v. Balram Prasad Sharma, 2000). Client portals that 'share files by link' send document links to whatever contact is on file, which in India may be a recycled number years later.

Ours offers the papers back without exposing them:
- a neutral, detail-free notice, guarded in code, sent only to a reconfirmed contact;
- documents released only after a recorded identity check;
- a single-use, 24-hour link bound to a code sent on a separate channel;
- physical collection always offered.
Every destruction still has a client-return record and an owner's approval behind it.

### Safeguards

The return notice is fixed, neutral text with no link and no matter detail, rendered without access to the matter and guarded in code against URLs and party names. It is sent only to a contact reconfirmed within 14 days, or one active in the last 90 days, and a postal letter is the fallback.

Documents are released only after a recorded identity re-verification made after the notice, through a single-use, 24-hour, code-bound, encrypted link where the code and the link travel on different channels. Physical collection is always offered. Every export attempt is audited.

Nothing is erased automatically. The cron only queues, through a service_role-only definer function. Erasure needs a recorded return outcome and an owner's approval under maker-checker, then trash_item under the owner's JWT with a legal-hold re-check, the 30-day trash and the certificate.

The inventory stores counts and HMACs. Imports never call the AI. Defaults are labelled as firm choices to be confirmed by counsel.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Blocking objection (the signed export link to the whole file goes to a possibly recycled number):
- (1) The notice now carries no document link and no matter detail. It is fixed neutral text: '<firm> asks you to contact the office about papers you entrusted to us', with the office phone and hours only. render_return_notice has no access to the matter, and a post-render guard refuses any URL or any matter title, CNR, case number, client name or party name.
- The notice is sent only after the contact is reconfirmed: an inbound message within 90 days, or a lawyer-recorded reconfirmation of that exact contact within 14 days. Otherwise 422, and a postal letter is the alternative.
- (2) The export is released only after the client responds and the lawyer records an identity re-verification (in-person ID, video call, a call with known details, or an ID match, with only the last 4 characters recorded) dated after notice_sent_at.
- The link is single-use and expires in 24h. It is bound to a 6-digit code delivered on a different channel (a database CHECK makes link_channel and code_channel differ), sent to a contact the client confirmed during verification, locked after 5 wrong codes, and every attempt is audited.
- (3) An undeliverable notice (Meta 'failed' status) or no answer within the notice period counts as no_response, with physical collection at the office offered in the notice itself.
- Tests added for each point: no URL or matter detail in the notice body; export-link 403 until a verification exists after notice_sent_at; the link works once and expires; the channel CHECK; the reconfirmation window.

### Acceptance tests

- Unit (objection): render_return_notice for a fixture matter (title 'Sharma v. Verma', CNR DLHC010012342024, client 'Ravi Sharma') in English and Hindi. The body matches no URL regex (https?://, www\., wa\.me, [a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z]{2,}/), and contains neither the title, the CNR, the case number, 'Ravi Sharma' nor any party_index name. Injecting a URL into organizations.office_name makes the guard refuse the send.
- Unit (objection): POST /dpdp/retention/{id}/export-link returns 403 with no identity_verifications row. It also returns 403 when the only verification has performed_at before notice_sent_at. It returns 201 once a verification exists after notice_sent_at.
- Unit (objection): an export grant works once (200, zip streamed). The second use returns 410. With frozen time at +24h01m an unused grant returns 410. After 5 wrong codes the grant is locked, and the correct code then returns 423.
- DB test: inserting a client_export_grants row with link_channel = code_channel = 'whatsapp' violates the CHECK constraint.
- Unit: sending the notice to a contact with no inbound message for 2 years and no reconfirmation returns 422 'reconfirm contact', with 0 Meta API calls. A reconfirmation dated 15 days before the send returns 422, and one dated 3 days before succeeds. A contact with an inbound message 10 days ago is accepted automatically.
- Unit: a reconfirmation recorded for contact A does not permit sending to contact B on the same matter.
- Unit: a Meta status webhook 'failed' on the notice sets notice_delivery_status='failed'. With frozen time past notice_sent_at + return_notice_days, the outcome no_response is accepted with physical_return_offered=true. Before that time, no_response is refused unless delivery failed.
- Unit: identity_verifications insert by a paralegal not on the matter returns 42501. A row with method in_person_id and a 12-digit id value in id_last4 is rejected (max 4 characters).
- Unit: WhatsApp fixture parsing, zip-slip rejection, and an inventory with no raw values, as in round 2.
- Unit, frozen time: retention_queue eligibility and skip reasons. After 400 simulated days trash_item has been called 0 times.
- DB test: queue_retention_candidates as authenticated gets 42501. As service_role it touches only the given org.
- DB test: request_approval('retention_erase') by an associate, decide_approval by the same user or a partner gets 42501, owner approval lets trash_item succeed for listed matters only, and a hold placed after approval blocks execution.
- Unit: a no_response outcome with client_supplied documents and no typed note means owner approval returns 422.
- Unit: the breach 72h deadline, the DSR legal-hold outcome rules and the bilingual consent notice, as in round 2.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- The export zip is 'encrypted with a key derived from the 6-digit code'. A 10^6 keyspace adds nothing once the file is downloaded, so don't present it as a safeguard. The real protections are the single use, the 24-hour expiry and the 5-attempt lock.
- The P33 template_registry slot types must include office_phone and office_hours (see the objection on P33).
- The method 'phone_known_details' on a possibly recycled number is weak. Require at least two details that aren't public (for example a fee paid or a date of first consultation), not just the case name.
- Migration 016 collides with P24.
- A zip encrypted with a key derived from a 6-digit code can be brute-forced offline if the file leaks. Use a random per-grant key that the server holds and delete it after use, and treat the code only as the online gate (already limited to 5 tries).
- The neutral notice still tells whoever holds a recycled number that this firm was trying to reach someone. This is disclosed. For sensitive practice areas (criminal, matrimonial), let firms default to the postal letter or the in-person route.
- Encrypting the zip 'with a key derived from the 6-digit code' adds nothing: 20 bits can be brute-forced offline. The real control is the server-side code check before streaming. Either drop the claim or use a random key delivered with the code.
- The export link and code sent over WhatsApp need a template or an open session window. Reuse P24's wa_delivery.route instead of a separate path.
- Migration 016 collides with P24.

proposal.out_of_scope:
We cannot delete what stays on an advocate's personal phone or Gmail. We can import it, give a checklist and record an attestation.

The firm remains the data fiduciary. These are legal judgments the firm makes, and our defaults are labelled as such:
- whether it is a Significant Data Fiduciary;
- how s.17(1)(a) and the retention rules apply to a file;
- when a closed file may safely be destroyed (limitation for negligence claims, connected matters, appeals).

We cannot know whether a mobile number has been recycled by the operator. We reduce the risk by sending a neutral, detail-free notice only after the lawyer reconfirms the contact, and by never releasing documents without identity re-verification. A stranger who receives the neutral message still learns that the firm wanted to reach someone at that number.

Identity re-verification is the lawyer's judgment. We record its method and time but cannot verify a physical ID check ourselves. Physical handover is recorded on the lawyer's word plus a receipt upload. Paper files are covered only through scanning.

Opposing parties' data is processed under the legal-claims exemption. We record that ground but cannot decide it.
proposal.what_the_user_sees:
A 'Data & DPDP' section with five screens: Import, Inventory, Retention review, Requests & grievances, and Breach register. Import, Inventory, Requests and Breaches are as in round 2. Retention review now works like this:

(1) Due for review. Matters past closed_at plus the retention period, with eligibility or skip reasons.

(2) Reconfirm contact. Before any notice, the lawyer sees the client's contacts with their last confirmed date. A contact is current if the client messaged from it in the last 90 days. Otherwise the lawyer must record how they reconfirmed it (spoke to the client on it, the client confirmed it by email, other source plus a note) within 14 days before sending. Where no contact can be reconfirmed, the screen offers the printable neutral letter to the last known postal address instead.

(3) Send neutral notice. The message is fixed text, English or Hindi: 'Namaste. This is <firm name>. Please contact our office at <office phone> (<office hours>) regarding papers you entrusted to us.' It carries no link, no client name, no matter title, no case number and no party names. A preview shows exactly what will be sent.

(4) Client responds. The lawyer records an identity re-verification: in-person ID check, video call, or a phone call where the client answered details on file, with a note. Only the last 4 characters of an ID shown are recorded, never the full number.

(5) Release export. Only after step 4 is a 'Create secure download' button enabled. It produces a single-use link valid for 24 hours, delivered to a contact the client confirmed during verification. A separate 6-digit code is read out on the call or sent on a different channel from the link. The page shows 'Link used' or 'Expired' afterwards. Physical collection at the office is always offered as the alternative.

(6) Outcome. Recorded as exported, returned in person (date plus receipt), keep requested, destroy requested, or no response. 'No response' is set automatically when the notice is undeliverable or unanswered after the notice period, and it shows 'Physical collection was offered at the office'.

(7) Owner approval of the erasure batch. As before, with the 'client originals not returned' flag and a typed note where needed.
proposal.what_the_system_does:
1) Importers, the access log, the inventory, the DSR register, the breach register, the consent notice and encryption are unchanged from round 2. Importers are deterministic parsers, the inventory holds counts and HMACs, and the DSR and breach timers are computed.

2) The retention queue is unchanged. queue_retention_candidates(p_org) is SECURITY DEFINER, granted to service_role only, and only queues and skips. It never trashes. Skip reasons cover legal hold, a pending linked court_case, unpaid fees, an open DSR, and a held connected matter.

3) Contact reconfirmation. This is new in this round and fixes the objection.
- New table contact_reconfirmations: queue_id, contact_kind (whatsapp | sms | email | postal), contact_hmac, method (recent_inbound | spoke_on_number | client_confirmed_email | other), note, confirmed_by, confirmed_at.
- retention_service.can_send_notice(queue_id) is true only if one of these holds:
  - (a) the contact sent an inbound message within 90 days, derived from whatsapp_messages and recorded automatically as method recent_inbound;
  - (b) a lawyer-recorded reconfirmation exists for that exact contact_hmac with confirmed_at no more than 14 days before the send.
  Otherwise the send returns 422 'reconfirm contact'.
- The postal letter is printable without a reconfirmation, but only to the address on file, with the same neutral text.

4) Neutral notice. RETURN_NOTICE_TEMPLATES (en, hi) are product-owned P33 template_registry rows with audience 'client_matter' and param_schema [office_name, office_phone, office_hours], all filled from organizations fields only.
- render_return_notice() takes no matter object at all, so matter data cannot reach it by construction.
- A post-render guard refuses the send if the body matches a URL pattern (https?://, www., wa.me, a domain followed by '/') or contains any of the matter's title, case_number, cnr, client_name or party_index display names.
- It is sent through outbound_policy reason client_of_matter to the reconfirmed contact. notice_sent_at and notice_delivery_status are recorded, and status is updated from Meta's status webhook (sent / delivered / read / failed).

5) Identity re-verification. New table identity_verifications: queue_id, method (in_person_id | video_call | phone_known_details | id_document_match), id_last4 (nullable), performed_by, performed_at, note (required), and confirmed_delivery_contact_hmac (the contact the client asked the link to go to).
- A check requires performed_at > notice_sent_at.
- Only lawyers on the matter or partners can record one.

6) Export release. POST /dpdp/retention/{queue_id}/export-link returns 403 unless an identity_verifications row exists with performed_at > notice_sent_at.
- It creates client_export_grants: token_sha256, code_sha256 (6-digit, random), expires_at = now() + 24h, max_uses = 1, used_at, attempts (max 5), link_channel, code_channel, and a CHECK constraint link_channel <> code_channel. 'read_on_call' counts as a channel.
- The link goes to confirmed_delivery_contact only.
- GET /export/{token} shows a code form. POST with the code streams the zip of client_supplied documents and correspondence, encrypted with a key derived from the code.
- On success used_at is set. Reuse returns 410, expiry returns 410, and after 5 wrong codes the grant is locked.
- Every attempt is audited (EXPORT_CLIENT_FILE, EXPORT_CODE_FAILED), and the download is logged as DOWNLOAD_DOCUMENT.

7) No response. If notice_delivery_status='failed', or no identity verification exists by notice_sent_at + return_notice_days (>= 30, default 60), the outcome may be set to no_response, with physical_return_offered=true (the neutral text invites the client to the office). If client_supplied documents exist, owner approval needs the typed note.

8) Erasure is unchanged: request_approval('retention_erase'), owner-only via approver_roles, the requester cannot decide, and trash_item runs under the owner's JWT, re-checking legal hold. Then the 30-day trash and the erasure certificate follow.

proposal.safeguards:
The return notice is fixed, neutral text with no link and no matter detail, rendered without access to the matter and guarded in code against URLs and party names. It is sent only to a contact reconfirmed within 14 days, or one active in the last 90 days, and a postal letter is the fallback.

Documents are released only after a recorded identity re-verification made after the notice, through a single-use, 24-hour, code-bound, encrypted link where the code and the link travel on different channels. Physical collection is always offered. Every export attempt is audited.

Nothing is erased automatically. The cron only queues, through a service_role-only definer function. Erasure needs a recorded return outcome and an owner's approval under maker-checker, then trash_item under the owner's JWT with a legal-hold re-check, the 30-day trash and the certificate.

The inventory stores counts and HMACs. Imports never call the AI. Defaults are labelled as firm choices to be confirmed by counsel.
proposal.answers_to_objections:
Blocking objection (the signed export link to the whole file goes to a possibly recycled number):
- (1) The notice now carries no document link and no matter detail. It is fixed neutral text: '<firm> asks you to contact the office about papers you entrusted to us', with the office phone and hours only. render_return_notice has no access to the matter, and a post-render guard refuses any URL or any matter title, CNR, case number, client name or party name.
- The notice is sent only after the contact is reconfirmed: an inbound message within 90 days, or a lawyer-recorded reconfirmation of that exact contact within 14 days. Otherwise 422, and a postal letter is the alternative.
- (2) The export is released only after the client responds and the lawyer records an identity re-verification (in-person ID, video call, a call with known details, or an ID match, with only the last 4 characters recorded) dated after notice_sent_at.
- The link is single-use and expires in 24h. It is bound to a 6-digit code delivered on a different channel (a database CHECK makes link_channel and code_channel differ), sent to a contact the client confirmed during verification, locked after 5 wrong codes, and every attempt is audited.
- (3) An undeliverable notice (Meta 'failed' status) or no answer within the notice period counts as no_response, with physical collection at the office offered in the notice itself.
- Tests added for each point: no URL or matter detail in the notice body; export-link 403 until a verification exists after notice_sent_at; the link works once and expires; the channel CHECK; the reconfirmation window.

minor: The export zip is 'encrypted with a key derived from the 6-digit code'. A 10^6 keyspace adds nothing once the file is downloaded, so don't present it as a safeguard. The real protections are the single use, the 24-hour expiry and the 5-attempt lock.
The P33 template_registry slot types must include office_phone and office_hours (see the objection on P33).

The method 'phone_known_details' on a possibly recycled number is weak. Require at least two details that aren't public (for example a fee paid or a date of first consultation), not just the case name.
Migration 016 collides with P24.

A zip encrypted with a key derived from a 6-digit code can be brute-forced offline if the file leaks. Use a random per-grant key that the server holds and delete it after use, and treat the code only as the online gate (already limited to 5 tries).

The neutral notice still tells whoever holds a recycled number that this firm was trying to reach someone. This is disclosed. For sensitive practice areas (criminal, matrimonial), let firms default to the postal letter or the in-person route.

Encrypting the zip 'with a key derived from the 6-digit code' adds nothing: 20 bits can be brute-forced offline. The real control is the server-side code check before streaming. Either drop the claim or use a random key delivered with the code.
The export link and code sent over WhatsApp need a template or an open session window. Reuse P24's wa_delivery.route instead of a separate path.
Migration 016 collides with P24.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Make matter knowledge and records belong to the firm, while respecting that in India the vakalatnama is personal to the advocate and clients may follow the lawyer out. Departure never destroys a firm record, including records sitting in the 30-day trash. Erasing a departed lawyer's account leaves no reference to their id anywhere: not in live tables, not in trash snapshots, and not one restored by a trigger. Removal ends with a verified sweep driven by a classified registry of every foreign key to users and every user reference inside trash snapshots. A client who leaves gets their file promptly, sent only to them or to an advocate they have named in writing. Know-how is captured at the moment of work, and approved drafts are reused only as code-anonymised templates.

### What it can't fix

Know-how that never entered the system can't be recovered. Filing the vakalatnama or NOC, the client's choice of advocate, and handing over original paper documents are human acts; we create and track the tasks. We can't verify that an uploaded client instruction is genuine; the lawyer confirms it and the record says so. Code anonymisation can miss an unusual identifying fact written in prose, which is why a partner confirms every template. Fee disputes are legal matters outside the app, and the app doesn't let them hold up a file. Snapshots already purged by the retention job are gone by design (only the tombstone remains), and departure doesn't change that. Historic data in personal channels belongs to P35/P37.

### What the user sees

Unchanged from round 4: 'Hand over first' on /team (records custodian, matter dispositions, number choices), followed by the 'Complete removal' summary.

The summary now also counts the trash, for example '412 records will move to Priya Shah, including 3 items in the trash (restorable until 14 Nov)'.

A restored record shows 'Restored, now owned by Priya Shah (records custodian for A. Mehta)'. An approved draft shows 'Approved by A. Mehta (former member)' even after Mehta's account is erased, and the approval date is kept.

The client-file release, Handover Pack, knowledge cards and template leak check are as in round 3.

### What the system does

1. Migration 014 changes owner foreign keys to RESTRICT and adds author_name snapshots, as before. NEW: drafts.approved_by_name. stamp_draft_approval fills it from public.users.full_name whenever it stamps approved_by, and clears it whenever approval lapses.

2. The registry public.member_owned_tables(table_name, column_name, org_column, class) is as before (owned_record | membership | identity | actor_set_null). NEW class snapshot_owner covers trash_items.owner_user_id. It is SET NULL in 013, but it is rewritten at offboarding (step d2), not left alone.

NEW registry public.member_snapshot_paths(kind, path, class) covers user references inside trash_items.snapshot:
- owned_record: ('transcript','row.user_id'), ('document','row.user_id'), ('draft','row.user_id'), ('review_grid','row.user_id'), ('court_case','row.user_id'), ('case_thread','row.user_id')
- actor_set_null: ('draft','row.approved_by'), ('case_thread','row.legal_hold_by'), ('case_thread','row.ai_consent_by'), ('court_case','row.legal_hold_by'), ('document','children[].reviewed_by'), ('review_grid','children[].reviewed_by'), ('knowledge_source','children[].created_by'), plus any further columns found by the test.

3. offboard_member(p_org, p_user, p_custodian, p_plan) keeps steps (a) to (f) from round 4. NEW step (d2), the trash: it locks this org's live trash_items (restored_at and purged_at null, snapshot not null) FOR UPDATE. For each item:
- if owner_user_id = p_user, set it to p_custodian;
- for each owned_record snapshot path of that kind whose value is p_user, jsonb_set it to p_custodian;
- then recompute snapshot_sha256 the same way trash_item computes it, and add {trash_id, kind, old_sha256, new_sha256, paths_changed} to the audit details.
It also inserts offboardings(org_id, departed_user_id, departed_name, custodian_id, at) for later lookups.
Step (g), the post-condition, now also asserts that no live trash item in p_org has owner_user_id = p_user or an owned_record snapshot path equal to p_user.

4. erase_account(user) is a security definer function, in one transaction:
(a) Preconditions as before: it deletes the sole-member personal workspace, and refuses, naming the firm, if the person is still in any firm.
(b) NEW: it sets set_config('app.erasing_user', uid, true) and set_config('app.legal_hold_change','on', true).
(c) NEW: for every actor_set_null registry row, it runs UPDATE <table> SET <col> = null WHERE <col> = uid, collecting {table, column, row ids} into the audit details with the person's name. For every actor_set_null snapshot path in live trash items, it nulls the value and recomputes the sha (also recorded).
(d) NEW trigger change: stamp_draft_approval's final else branch keeps old.approved_by unless all three hold: new.approved_by is null, current_setting('app.erasing_user', true) = old.approved_by::text, and current_user is not anon or authenticated. In that case approved_by stays null while approved_at and approved_by_name are kept. Ordinary user updates still can't blank an approver. stamp_ai_consent needs no change, because it only acts when ai_consent_at changes. guard_legal_hold passes because of the GUC and because it runs as definer.
(e) It deletes public.users and auth.users.
(f) NEW post-condition, over every registry row of every class: SELECT 1 FROM <table> WHERE <col> = uid returns nothing. No trash snapshot in any org contains uid at a registered path, and, as a backstop, snapshot::text doesn't contain the uid string. Otherwise it raises and rolls back everything.
(g) One audit_logs row, which keeps attribution (name, former roles and nulled stamps) after the identity is gone.

5. NEW: restore_trash_item gets a defensive mapping before the insert:
- For each owned_record snapshot path whose user isn't a current member of the org (or no longer exists), it maps the owner to the custodian from offboardings for that org and user. If there's no offboarding record, it raises 'choose a new owner' (P0001), and a partner can call restore_trash_item(p_id, p_new_owner), where p_new_owner must be a current member.
- For each actor_set_null path whose user no longer exists, it sets null.
- trash_items.owner_user_id is updated to match.
This covers a record trashed by the departing person concurrently with offboarding, and legacy departures from before migration 014.

6-8 (client-file release, knowledge cards, template leak check, retrieval walls and Handover Pack) are unchanged.

### Where it is built

Extend:
- supabase/migrations/013 functions, redefined in 014: stamp_draft_approval (the erasure branch and approved_by_name) and restore_trash_item (the owner and actor mapping, optional p_new_owner). trash_item is unchanged; its sha recipe is reused.
- app/services/org_service.py remove_member, which calls the offboard_member rpc with the user's JWT.
- app/routers/organizations.py
- app/services/safety_service.py: the trash restore route passes p_new_owner.
- app/services/handover_service.py
- the P13 deadline engine
- app/worker.py
- frontend/src/app/team/page.tsx (trash counts in the summary)
- the trash UI's restored-owner label

New in migration 014:
- the member_owned_tables class snapshot_owner
- member_snapshot_paths
- offboardings
- drafts.approved_by_name
- the updated offboard_member and erase_account

Tests: tests/db/test_member_registry.py, extended with snapshot-path completeness and trigger coverage, and tests/db/test_offboarding_trash.py.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

iManage, NetDocuments and Harvey Vault store documents but don't capture reasoning, rely on manual precedent scrubbing, and assume the firm owns the client relationship. Their deletion and retention features treat a departed user's items as orphans. Most Indian firms have no DMS at all.

We model Indian practice: a personal vakalatnama, an NOC, clients following the advocate, and the client's right to the file with no lien. Ownership transfer is one verified transaction. It covers live rows and trash snapshots, its registry classifies every user reference including those inside jsonb snapshots, and schema tests fail CI on any unclassified one. Erasure proves its own completeness with a post-condition, so a trigger or a snapshot can't leave a dangling reference.

### Safeguards

Records:
- No firm record is destroyed when someone leaves, live or trashed. RESTRICT foreign keys and a transactional sweep cover live rows and trash snapshots, with post-conditions, all audit-logged with before and after snapshot hashes.
- Memberships are deleted, never reassigned.
- The custodian must be an existing owner or partner.

Erasure:
- Erasure (DPDP) is complete and provable. Explicit nulling under a definer-only GUC, which no client path can set, is followed by a post-condition over every registered column and snapshot path.
- Attribution survives in author_name, approved_by_name and the audit row, not in a live foreign key.
- Ordinary users still can't blank an approver.

Access and clients:
- Restoring a departed person's record goes to the custodian or to a partner-named member, never to a non-member.
- Client files go only to the client or a client-named advocate, can't be held for fees (R.D. Saxena), and escalate when overdue.
- offboard_member runs with the caller's JWT, with no service role in the user path (invariant 2).

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection 1 (the SET NULL on drafts.approved_by was undone by stamp_draft_approval): erase_account no longer relies on foreign-key actions.
- Before deleting the user, it sets app.erasing_user (and app.legal_hold_change) with set_config(..., true), then explicitly nulls every actor_set_null column, and every actor path inside trash snapshots, recording each nulled stamp in the audit row.
- stamp_draft_approval's else branch lets approved_by become null only when the GUC equals old.approved_by and current_user is not anon or authenticated, so ordinary edits still can't blank an approver.
- The new drafts.approved_by_name, stamped by the same trigger, keeps the approval attributed as 'A. Mehta (former member)', and approved_at is kept.
- A post-condition over every registry row of every class, plus all trash snapshots, proves no reference to the erased uuid remains, or it rolls back.
Tests: an approved-draft erasure, a trigger-reverting test table that forces rollback, and a check that the trigger still blocks client-side blanking.

Objection 2 (the trash was never swept): offboard_member gains step d2. It locks the org's live trash_items, rewrites owner_user_id and every owned_record snapshot path from the departed user to the custodian, recomputes snapshot_sha256 with trash_item's recipe, and logs the old and new hashes. The post-condition now includes the trash.
As a second layer, restore_trash_item maps any owner who is no longer a member, or no longer exists, to the custodian recorded in the new offboardings table, or to a partner-chosen current member, and nulls actor paths whose user no longer exists. A record trashed in a race, or under a pre-014 departure, therefore still restores.
A snapshot-path registry, with a pg_constraint completeness test, keeps new tables from reopening the gap.
Tests: trash, offboard, erase, restore gives a record owned by Priya; restore after offboarding but before erasure gives the same; knowledge-source children restore with created_by null; and the race fallback works.

### Acceptance tests

- Approved draft survives erasure: Mehta approves a draft and is offboarded (custodian Priya), then erased with erase_account. drafts.approved_by is null, approved_at is unchanged, approved_by_name is 'A. Mehta', and the erase audit row lists the draft id under drafts.approved_by. No row anywhere references Mehta's uuid, checked over every registry row of all classes
- Trigger still protects approvals: an authenticated user's update that sets approved_by to null with approved_at unchanged keeps the old approver. The same update with app.erasing_user set through a client-callable path is impossible (current_user is authenticated), so the approver is kept
- Erasure post-condition: a test-only table with an actor_set_null column and a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that restores old values makes erase_account raise and roll back. public.users and auth.users still hold Mehta and nothing is nulled
- Trash before offboarding: Mehta trashes their own draft and Priya approves trashing their transcript. offboard_member, then erase_account, then Priya restores both: each comes back with user_id Priya, readable under RLS by Priya and by matter associates. The draft's approved_by is null and approved_by_name is kept. The audit rows record old and new snapshot_sha256
- Trash restored before erasure: after offboarding but before erasure, a restored transcript is owned by Priya, not Mehta, and the round-4 post-condition holds
- Knowledge-source children: a knowledge source created_by Mehta in the trash restores after erase_account with created_by null and no 23503
- Race fallback: a trash row inserted with owner Mehta after offboarding (simulated by direct insert) restores owned by the custodian found in offboardings. With no offboarding record, restore raises P0001 'choose a new owner', and restore_trash_item(p_id, Priya) succeeds while a non-member p_new_owner is refused
- Snapshot-path completeness: for each trash kind, the test reads the kind's table and child tables from pg_constraint. It fails if any FK column to public.users is missing from member_snapshot_paths, or if its class disagrees with the FK delete rule (cascade/restrict owner gives owned_record, set null gives actor_set_null)
- Classification completeness from round 4 still holds, now accepting class snapshot_owner only for trash_items.owner_user_id
- Round-4 tests still pass: custodian already a member, owned records move, actor stamps untouched at offboarding, other orgs untouched, active org reset, custodian preconditions 409, post-condition rollback, numbers, multi-org refusal naming firm B, associate caller refused, audit counts
- Round-3 client-file release, fee-reason rejection, overdue escalation, template leak, client_preference constraint and retrieval wall tests all still pass

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Step d2 (rewriting trash snapshot owners) and the owner remap in restore_trash_item change who owns a matter without an UPDATE of court_cases.user_id, so P41's custody trigger never fires on them. Emit the custody event from these paths, or call a shared function. This seam must be closed on one side.

proposal.solvable_part: Make matter knowledge and records belong to the firm, while respecting that in India the vakalatnama is personal to the advocate and clients may follow the lawyer out. Departure never destroys a firm record, including records sitting in the 30-day trash. Erasing a departed lawyer's account leaves no reference to their id anywhere: not in live tables, not in trash snapshots, and not one restored by a trigger. Removal ends with a verified sweep driven by a classified registry of every foreign key to users and every user reference inside trash snapshots. A client who leaves gets their file promptly, sent only to them or to an advocate they have named in writing. Know-how is captured at the moment of work, and approved drafts are reused only as code-anonymised templates.
proposal.out_of_scope: Know-how that never entered the system can't be recovered. Filing the vakalatnama or NOC, the client's choice of advocate, and handing over original paper documents are human acts; we create and track the tasks. We can't verify that an uploaded client instruction is genuine; the lawyer confirms it and the record says so. Code anonymisation can miss an unusual identifying fact written in prose, which is why a partner confirms every template. Fee disputes are legal matters outside the app, and the app doesn't let them hold up a file. Snapshots already purged by the retention job are gone by design (only the tombstone remains), and departure doesn't change that. Historic data in personal channels belongs to P35/P37.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

One matter file that fills itself. Documents arriving by WhatsApp (images, PDFs, voice notes), by email to an unguessable matter address, by upload, and from the court tracker (orders) land in the right matter: OCR'd, de-duplicated, versioned, on a timeline, and labelled with their provenance. 'Where is the latest X' is answered by search that returns the documents themselves, not an AI guess. Email is auto-filed only when it reaches us through one pinned receiving provider whose deliveries are cryptographically signed (Amazon SES receiving, notified via signed SNS), the provider's own DMARC/DKIM/SPF verdicts show the sender is authenticated and aligned, and the sender is on the allowlist. Everything else waits in quarantine for a human.

### What it can't fix

We won't scrape court portals behind captchas, read the lawyer's whole Gmail or personal WhatsApp, or sync every cloud drive in round 1 (a Google Drive import can follow). Documents a client never sends us stay scattered. Physical files need scanning by someone. Email authentication proves the sending domain, not that a member's mailbox wasn't compromised. Senders whose domains publish no DMARC record and fail our aligned-DKIM/SPF check will always need a manual release. A document calling itself a court order is not proof it exists: only the eCourts-sourced copy is marked verified. Round 1 supports exactly one inbound provider, Amazon SES. Mailgun (HMAC-signed routes) is a possible second adapter. Postmark and SendGrid Inbound Parse don't sign deliveries, so they are not supported for auto-filing. We depend on AWS's signing and verdicts being correct, and on the region the firm chooses for SES receiving (a DPDP cross-border question we disclose; we can't fix it in code).

### What the user sees

Each matter has a 'File' tab: a timeline of everything in it, including the client's WhatsApp photos of the FIR, the forwarded email with the notice, the order downloaded from eCourts, drafts and transcripts. Each item shows its source, date, type (order, notice, agreement, evidence, receipt), version group and a provenance badge: 'eCourts (verified source)', 'WhatsApp from client', 'Email - authenticated (DMARC pass via SES, partner@firm.in)', 'Uploaded by A. Rao'. Orders from anywhere but eCourts are labelled 'order - not verified against eCourts'.

The matter email address ('m-k7q2x9fh3w4tzr6bny5c8dj2ma@in.<firm receiving domain>') is shown with a copy button, plus 'Rotate address' and 'Revoke' buttons for owners and partners, and the date of the last rotation. Settings shows the receiving setup as 'Inbound email: Amazon SES (<region>), signed delivery verified', with the last verified delivery time, or a red 'Not configured - email filing off'.

An 'Unfiled' tray lists items the system couldn't match, with suggested matters filed in one click. A 'Quarantine' tray lists emails that failed authentication or came from unknown senders, with the reason ('DMARC fail (SES verdict); From claims partner@firm.in', 'Sender domain has no DMARC (GRAY) and no aligned DKIM'). Each shows a plain-text preview (no HTML, no live links) and 'Release to matter' or 'Discard'. Releasing needs a lawyer's click and is audit-logged.

The search box takes queries like 'latest order in Sharma', 'lease agreement' or 'e-filing receipt' and returns ranked documents with snippets and dates.

### What the system does

1. Migration 018_matter_file.sql adds:
   * columns on documents: thread_id, source (upload|whatsapp|email|ecourts|draft), source_ref, sha256 (unique per org), doc_class, doc_date, version_group, received_from, provenance jsonb, source_verified
   * inbound_items (Unfiled and Quarantine trays, with a reason)
   * matter_addresses (thread_id, token_hash bytea unique, token_prefix, created_at, rotated_from, revoked_at)
   * inbound_events (sns_message_id primary key, ses_message_id unique, received_at), for replay and duplicate protection like stripe_events
2. Pinned inbound channel: Amazon SES email receiving for the firm's receiving subdomain (MX to SES). A receipt rule (a) stores the raw MIME in a private S3 bucket (SSE-KMS, lifecycle delete after 1 day) and (b) publishes the SES notification to one SNS topic, configured with SignatureVersion 2. Our endpoint POST /api/v1/inbound/ses is subscribed to that topic over HTTPS. Config: SES_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN, SES_INBOUND_BUCKET, SES_INBOUND_PREFIX, SES_REGION. Without them, email filing is off and the endpoint returns 404.
3. services/inbound_auth.py (deterministic; shared with P42), verify_sns(request) -> SnsEnvelope or reject (401, nothing written):
   * The body must parse as an SNS JSON message. Type must be Notification or SubscriptionConfirmation, TopicArn must equal SES_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN exactly, and SignatureVersion must be '2' (SHA256withRSA; version 1/SHA1 is refused).
   * SigningCertURL must be https, with a host matching ^sns\.[a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com$ and a path ending .pem, and no userinfo, port or query. Any other URL is refused before anything is fetched. The certificate is fetched with redirects disabled and cached by URL. It must chain to the system trust store, be within its validity period, and have subject CN sns.amazonaws.com.
   * The canonical string is built per the SNS spec (for Notification: Message, MessageId, Subject if present, Timestamp, TopicArn, Type, each as 'key\nvalue\n'), and the RSA signature is verified with the certificate's key.
   * Timestamp must be within 1 hour of now (replay window). MessageId is inserted into inbound_events, and a conflict means a duplicate, answered 200 and ignored.
   * SubscriptionConfirmation is honoured only for the configured topic, and SubscribeURL must pass the same host check. As defence in depth, the endpoint path also carries a basic-auth secret, but that is never treated as authentication of the mail.
4. Email verdicts come only from the signed envelope, never from the message headers. services/inbound_auth.email_verdict(ses_notification, raw_mime):
   * The ses_notification is the 'Message' field of the verified SNS envelope.
   * receipt.virusVerdict FAIL means reject and discard. receipt.spamVerdict FAIL means quarantine.
   * AUTHENTICATED if receipt.dmarcVerdict.status == PASS. SES evaluates DMARC against the RFC5322.From domain, so PASS includes alignment.
   * Otherwise (dmarcVerdict GRAY, no DMARC record), it is AUTHENTICATED only if:
     - receipt.dkimVerdict == PASS and our own DKIM check of the raw MIME (dkimpy) finds a valid signature whose d= has the same organizational domain as From (vendored Public Suffix List); or
     - receipt.spfVerdict == PASS and mail.source (the envelope MAIL FROM recorded by SES) has the same organizational domain as From.
   * dmarcVerdict FAIL is always NOT_AUTHENTICATED, even if other checks pass.
   * Multiple From addresses, a missing From, or a From that doesn't match mail.commonHeaders.from also give NOT_AUTHENTICATED.
   * Any Authentication-Results, Received-SPF or X-* verdict headers inside the MIME are ignored for authentication.
5. Raw message retrieval: the notification's receipt.action must be S3, with bucketName == SES_INBOUND_BUCKET and an objectKey under SES_INBOUND_PREFIX; otherwise reject. The object is fetched with the server's IAM role (read-only on that prefix). Its message id must match mail.messageId, and it is deleted after ingestion. For messages under 150 KB, SES's Base64 SNS content may be used instead, but only from the verified envelope.
6. Filing decision for email:
   * The matter token is taken from the envelope recipients in receipt.recipients, not from To/Cc headers. It is hashed and looked up.
   * Auto-file only if AUTHENTICATED, the token is active, and From is an org member's verified email or a client email already on that matter.
   * Everything else goes to quarantine with a reason: not authenticated (with the SES verdicts), unknown sender, a rotated token in its 7-day grace period, a token whose matter the sender has no relation to, or a spam verdict.
   * Unknown or revoked tokens get the same 200 response as valid ones and are dropped. Attempts are counted per envelope sender and source IP (mail.source and receipt data) and rate-limited through core/rate_limiter.
   * Release from quarantine is a lawyer's click, recorded in audit_logs, and the provenance keeps the failure reason.
7. Matter tokens are secrets.token_bytes(16), base32 (26 characters). Only sha256(token) is stored; the full address is kept in an encrypted column readable only by RLS-scoped members. Rotation and revocation are unchanged from round 2.
8. WhatsApp media: whatsapp_intake is extended to download image and document messages (download_media), OCR them and attach them to the conversation's thread, behind the existing consent gate. The vision fallback is used only with OCR_VISION_FALLBACK on and the thread's ai_consent_at set.
9. eCourts orders: new order entries with a provider PDF link are filed as doc_class 'order' with source_verified=true. Orders from any other source are unverified and never change hearing dates.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

iManage and NetDocuments are enterprise-priced and heavy for small Indian firms. Harvey Vault and CoCounsel need manual uploads. Clio stores files but doesn't ingest WhatsApp media, OCR Indian-language scans or file court orders automatically. Spellbook lives in Word, SpotDraft in CLM. Mail-to-matter features elsewhere usually trust the From header, or an unsigned parse webhook whose fields anyone who learns the URL can forge. Our trust root is a delivery signed by AWS: SNS's RSA signature from a pinned certificate host, a fixed topic, and a replay window, with SES's own DMARC/DKIM/SPF verdicts inside the signed payload. Nothing an attacker can put in a POST body or a mail header changes the verdict. Documents are then filed by deterministic keys (a 128-bit matter token from the envelope recipient, CNR, client contact) into the same matter that holds the consultation, research, drafts, hearings and bills, each with its provenance, so a forged 'order' can never pose as a verified one.

### Safeguards

Authenticity:
* One pinned inbound provider (SES via SNS). Every delivery is verified by SNS RSA-SHA256 signature from a pinned certificate host, an exact topic ARN, a 1-hour replay window and MessageId de-duplication.
* Mail verdicts come only from SES's receipt inside the signed payload: DMARC PASS, or DKIM/SPF aligned to the From organizational domain when DMARC is absent. Message headers never count.
* Raw MIME is fetched only from the pinned bucket/prefix and deleted after ingestion.
* Unsigned providers (Postmark, SendGrid parse) are not supported for auto-filing.
* Auto-filing also needs an allowlisted sender. Everything else is quarantined, excluded from RAG and search, and released only by an audited lawyer click.
* Matter tokens are 128-bit, taken from envelope recipients, stored hashed, rotatable and revocable, with no existence oracle, and rate-limited.
* Only eCourts-sourced orders are marked verified.

DPDP and privilege:
* Nothing from a client channel is processed before consent.
* The SES receiving region is disclosed in Settings and on the About page as a cross-border transfer where it is outside India. The S3 copy is encrypted and deleted within a day.
* Documents are RLS-scoped. PII is masked before any model call.
* The vision fallback respects OCR_VISION_FALLBACK and per-matter consent.

Prompt injection: email and document text is data, wrapped with provenance. The quarantine preview is plain text with links disabled.

Service role: the SES endpoint is a server-side job, signature-verified and scoped to the token's org (to be listed under CLAUDE.md invariant 2).

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection (the trust root named providers that don't sign inbound webhooks): fixed as the reviewer proposed, by pinning one provider that signs deliveries and reports verdicts itself.

* Postmark and SendGrid are dropped. Round 1 supports only Amazon SES receiving with SNS notification. They are not offered even as a weak quarantine-only channel, so no unsigned path to the matter file exists. Mailgun (HMAC-SHA256 timestamp/token signature plus a replay window) is named as a possible later adapter behind the same interface.
* services/inbound_auth.verify_sns checks the SNS envelope:
  - SignatureVersion 2 RSA-SHA256 over the spec's canonical string;
  - SigningCertURL limited to https on ^sns\.[a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com$ with a .pem path, checked before any fetch, no redirects, and the certificate chaining to the system trust store with CN sns.amazonaws.com;
  - TopicArn equal to the configured topic;
  - Timestamp within 1 hour;
  - MessageId de-duplicated in inbound_events.
  An attacker who learns the URL can no longer POST a fabricated message: without AWS's signing key the request gets 401 and nothing is fetched or written.
* email_verdict uses only SES's receipt.dmarcVerdict, dkimVerdict, spfVerdict, spamVerdict and virusVerdict from inside the signed payload. DMARC PASS counts directly, since SES evaluates DMARC against the From domain. When DMARC is GRAY, we require organizational-domain alignment (our own dkimpy check of d=, or SES's mail.source for SPF). The authserv-id header parsing is removed: no header in the MIME can affect the verdict.
* The matter token is read from the signed receipt.recipients, not from the To header. The raw MIME is fetched only from the pinned S3 bucket/prefix.
* inbound_auth is one shared module with P42 (a note has been sent to P42's owner).
* Tests: test_unsigned_webhook_rejected (now buildable: an unsigned, mis-signed or attacker-signed SES-shaped body gives 401), test_sns_signature_valid, test_sns_cert_url_pinning, test_sns_topic_and_replay, test_subscription_confirmation, test_dmarc_fail_quarantined, test_dmarc_gray_alignment, test_forged_auth_header_ignored, test_virus_and_spam_verdicts, test_s3_location_pinned, test_token_from_envelope_recipient and test_not_configured.

The round-2 fixes (128-bit hashed tokens, quarantine, provenance) are unchanged.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Configuration is platform-level (one SES_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN, one bucket), yet the text says 'the region the firm chooses'. State that the platform operates SES receiving in one region, and disclose that region. Also check that SES email receiving is offered in the region you pick: it isn't available in every region, including possibly ap-south-1. If it isn't, the cross-border disclosure is mandatory, not conditional.
- SNS signing certificate CNs and hosts in some partitions differ (for example amazonaws.com.cn). Treat that as unsupported explicitly rather than silently refusing it.
- Opposing counsel's notices reach the firm from senders who aren't on the allowlist, so they will always go to quarantine unless a lawyer forwards them. That's correct, but tell users plainly that forwarding is the normal path.
- P42 still describes trusting Authentication-Results headers. Make sure P42 actually uses this module, because otherwise the forgeable path P37 closed still exists.
- SES email receiving is offered only in a few AWS regions. Today that likely excludes ap-south-1, so in practice every firm's mail will be stored outside India. Say so plainly in Settings and on the About page, not only 'if outside India'.
- A client email auto-filed to a matter runs OCR and classification. The haiku classification fallback should go through the P20 matter and consent gate, the same way the WhatsApp media path is gated on ai_consent_at.
- Migration 018 collides with P42's 018_contracts_repository.sql. Renumber.
- SES email receiving is available only in a subset of AWS regions. Confirm the regions the firms are likely to pick, since ap-south-1 may not be offered, and state the cross-border consequence in the setup docs.
- The SES notification carries mail.source (the envelope MAIL FROM) but no sending IP in a dependable field. Rate-limit by envelope sender and token-guess counts, not by 'source IP'.
- P42's proposal still trusts provider Authentication-Results headers. The shared inbound_auth module only helps if P42 actually adopts it (raised as a blocker on P42).

proposal.solvable_part: One matter file that fills itself. Documents arriving by WhatsApp (images, PDFs, voice notes), by email to an unguessable matter address, by upload, and from the court tracker (orders) land in the right matter: OCR'd, de-duplicated, versioned, on a timeline, and labelled with their provenance. 'Where is the latest X' is answered by search that returns the documents themselves, not an AI guess. Email is auto-filed only when it reaches us through one pinned receiving provider whose deliveries are cryptographically signed (Amazon SES receiving, notified via signed SNS), the provider's own DMARC/DKIM/SPF verdicts show the sender is authenticated and aligned, and the sender is on the allowlist. Everything else waits in quarantine for a human.
proposal.out_of_scope: We won't scrape court portals behind captchas, read the lawyer's whole Gmail or personal WhatsApp, or sync every cloud drive in round 1 (a Google Drive import can follow). Documents a client never sends us stay scattered. Physical files need scanning by someone. Email authentication proves the sending domain, not that a member's mailbox wasn't compromised. Senders whose domains publish no DMARC record and fail our aligned-DKIM/SPF check will always need a manual release. A document calling itself a court order is not proof it exists: only the eCourts-sourced copy is marked verified. Round 1 supports exactly one inbound provider, Amazon SES. Mailgun (HMAC-signed routes) is a possible second adapter. Postmark and SendGrid Inbound Parse don't sign deliveries, so they are not supported for auto-filing. We depend on AWS's signing and verdicts being correct, and on the region the firm chooses for SES receiving (a DPDP cross-border question we disclose; we can't fix it in code).
proposal.what_the_user_sees:
Each matter has a 'File' tab: a timeline of everything in it, including the client's WhatsApp photos of the FIR, the forwarded email with the notice, the order downloaded from eCourts, drafts and transcripts. Each item shows its source, date, type (order, notice, agreement, evidence, receipt), version group and a provenance badge: 'eCourts (verified source)', 'WhatsApp from client', 'Email - authenticated (DMARC pass via SES, partner@firm.in)', 'Uploaded by A. Rao'. Orders from anywhere but eCourts are labelled 'order - not verified against eCourts'.

The matter email address ('m-k7q2x9fh3w4tzr6bny5c8dj2ma@in.<firm receiving domain>') is shown with a copy button, plus 'Rotate address' and 'Revoke' buttons for owners and partners, and the date of the last rotation. Settings shows the receiving setup as 'Inbound email: Amazon SES (<region>), signed delivery verified', with the last verified delivery time, or a red 'Not configured - email filing off'.

An 'Unfiled' tray lists items the system couldn't match, with suggested matters filed in one click. A 'Quarantine' tray lists emails that failed authentication or came from unknown senders, with the reason ('DMARC fail (SES verdict); From claims partner@firm.in', 'Sender domain has no DMARC (GRAY) and no aligned DKIM'). Each shows a plain-text preview (no HTML, no live links) and 'Release to matter' or 'Discard'. Releasing needs a lawyer's click and is audit-logged.

The search box takes queries like 'latest order in Sharma', 'lease agreement' or 'e-filing receipt' and returns ranked documents with snippets and dates.
proposal.what_the_system_does:
1. Migration 018_matter_file.sql adds:
   * columns on documents: thread_id, source (upload|whatsapp|email|ecourts|draft), source_ref, sha256 (unique per org), doc_class, doc_date, version_group, received_from, provenance jsonb, source_verified
   * inbound_items (Unfiled and Quarantine trays, with a reason)
   * matter_addresses (thread_id, token_hash bytea unique, token_prefix, created_at, rotated_from, revoked_at)
   * inbound_events (sns_message_id primary key, ses_message_id unique, received_at), for replay and duplicate protection like stripe_events
2. Pinned inbound channel: Amazon SES email receiving for the firm's receiving subdomain (MX to SES). A receipt rule (a) stores the raw MIME in a private S3 bucket (SSE-KMS, lifecycle delete after 1 day) and (b) publishes the SES notification to one SNS topic, configured with SignatureVersion 2. Our endpoint POST /api/v1/inbound/ses is subscribed to that topic over HTTPS. Config: SES_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN, SES_INBOUND_BUCKET, SES_INBOUND_PREFIX, SES_REGION. Without them, email filing is off and the endpoint returns 404.
3. services/inbound_auth.py (deterministic; shared with P42), verify_sns(request) -> SnsEnvelope or reject (401, nothing written):
   * The body must parse as an SNS JSON message. Type must be Notification or SubscriptionConfirmation, TopicArn must equal SES_INBOUND_TOPIC_ARN exactly, and SignatureVersion must be '2' (SHA256withRSA; version 1/SHA1 is refused).
   * SigningCertURL must be https, with a host matching ^sns\.[a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com$ and a path ending .pem, and no userinfo, port or query. Any other URL is refused before anything is fetched. The certificate is fetched with redirects disabled and cached by URL. It must chain to the system trust store, be within its validity period, and have subject CN sns.amazonaws.com.
   * The canonical string is built per the SNS spec (for Notification: Message, MessageId, Subject if present, Timestamp, TopicArn, Type, each as 'key\nvalue\n'), and the RSA signature is verified with the certificate's key.
   * Timestamp must be within 1 hour of now (replay window). MessageId is inserted into inbound_events, and a conflict means a duplicate, answered 200 and ignored.
   * SubscriptionConfirmation is honoured only for the configured topic, and SubscribeURL must pass the same host check. As defence in depth, the endpoint path also carries a basic-auth secret, but that is never treated as authentication of the mail.
4. Email verdicts come only from the signed envelope, never from the message headers. services/inbound_auth.email_verdict(ses_notification, raw_mime):
   * The ses_notification is the 'Message' field of the verified SNS envelope.
   * receipt.virusVerdict FAIL means reject and discard. receipt.spamVerdict FAIL means quarantine.
   * AUTHENTICATED if receipt.dmarcVerdict.status == PASS. SES evaluates DMARC against the RFC5322.From domain, so PASS includes alignment.
   * Otherwise (dmarcVerdict GRAY, no DMARC record), it is AUTHENTICATED only if:
     - receipt.dkimVerdict == PASS and our own DKIM check of the raw MIME (dkimpy) finds a valid signature whose d= has the same organizational domain as From (vendored Public Suffix List); or
     - receipt.spfVerdict == PASS and mail.source (the envelope MAIL FROM recorded by SES) has the same organizational domain as From.
   * dmarcVerdict FAIL is always NOT_AUTHENTICATED, even if other checks pass.
   * Multiple From addresses, a missing From, or a From that doesn't match mail.commonHeaders.from also give NOT_AUTHENTICATED.
   * Any Authentication-Results, Received-SPF or X-* verdict headers inside the MIME are ignored for authentication.
5. Raw message retrieval: the notification's receipt.action must be S3, with bucketName == SES_INBOUND_BUCKET and an objectKey under SES_INBOUND_PREFIX; otherwise reject. The object is fetched with the server's IAM role (read-only on that prefix). Its message id must match mail.messageId, and it is deleted after ingestion. For messages under 150 KB, SES's Base64 SNS content may be used instead, but only from the verified envelope.
6. Filing decision for email:
   * The matter token is taken from the envelope recipients in receipt.recipients, not from To/Cc headers. It is hashed and looked up.
   * Auto-file only if AUTHENTICATED, the token is active, and From is an org member's verified email or a client email already on that matter.
   * Everything else goes to quarantine with a reason: not authenticated (with the SES verdicts), unknown sender, a rotated token in its 7-day grace period, a token whose matter the sender has no relation to, or a spam verdict.
   * Unknown or revoked tokens get the same 200 response as valid ones and are dropped. Attempts are counted per envelope sender and source IP (mail.source and receipt data) and rate-limited through core/rate_limiter.
   * Release from quarantine is a lawyer's click, recorded in audit_logs, and the provenance keeps the failure reason.
7. Matter tokens are secrets.token_bytes(16), base32 (26 characters). Only sha256(token) is stored; the full address is kept in an encrypted column readable only by RLS-scoped members. Rotation and revocation are unchanged from round 2.
8. WhatsApp media: whatsapp_intake is extended to download image and document messages (download_media), OCR them and attach them to the conversation's thread, behind the existing consent gate. The vision fallback is used only with OCR_VISION_FALLBACK on and the thread's ai_consent_at set.
9. eCourts orders: new order entries with a provider PDF link are filed as doc_class 'order' with source_verified=true. Orders from any other source are unverified and never change hearing dates.
10. Filing rules in code, in order: matter token (email); CNR regex; case number + court; sender equals the matter's client contact; otherwise Unfiled. The AI may suggest a matter from the masked first page, but only a human click files it.
11. De-duplication by sha256; versioning by normalised filename stem + doc_class within a thread. Classification is rule-based first, with a haiku fallback that returns a label only, from masked text.
12. Untrusted content: extracted text is stored with its provenance and wrapped as quoted source data when agents or RAG use it. Quarantined items are excluded from RAG and search.
13. Search: Postgres full-text plus the existing pgvector embeddings, filtered by thread and RLS. 'Latest' is parsed in code and sorts by doc_date descending. It returns documents, not generated prose.

proposal.safeguards:
Authenticity:
* One pinned inbound provider (SES via SNS). Every delivery is verified by SNS RSA-SHA256 signature from a pinned certificate host, an exact topic ARN, a 1-hour replay window and MessageId de-duplication.
* Mail verdicts come only from SES's receipt inside the signed payload: DMARC PASS, or DKIM/SPF aligned to the From organizational domain when DMARC is absent. Message headers never count.
* Raw MIME is fetched only from the pinned bucket/prefix and deleted after ingestion.
* Unsigned providers (Postmark, SendGrid parse) are not supported for auto-filing.
* Auto-filing also needs an allowlisted sender. Everything else is quarantined, excluded from RAG and search, and released only by an audited lawyer click.
* Matter tokens are 128-bit, taken from envelope recipients, stored hashed, rotatable and revocable, with no existence oracle, and rate-limited.
* Only eCourts-sourced orders are marked verified.

DPDP and privilege:
* Nothing from a client channel is processed before consent.
* The SES receiving region is disclosed in Settings and on the About page as a cross-border transfer where it is outside India. The S3 copy is encrypted and deleted within a day.
* Documents are RLS-scoped. PII is masked before any model call.
* The vision fallback respects OCR_VISION_FALLBACK and per-matter consent.

Prompt injection: email and document text is data, wrapped with provenance. The quarantine preview is plain text with links disabled.

Service role: the SES endpoint is a server-side job, signature-verified and scoped to the token's org (to be listed under CLAUDE.md invariant 2).
proposal.answers_to_objections:
Objection (the trust root named providers that don't sign inbound webhooks): fixed as the reviewer proposed, by pinning one provider that signs deliveries and reports verdicts itself.

* Postmark and SendGrid are dropped. Round 1 supports only Amazon SES receiving with SNS notification. They are not offered even as a weak quarantine-only channel, so no unsigned path to the matter file exists. Mailgun (HMAC-SHA256 timestamp/token signature plus a replay window) is named as a possible later adapter behind the same interface.
* services/inbound_auth.verify_sns checks the SNS envelope:
  - SignatureVersion 2 RSA-SHA256 over the spec's canonical string;
  - SigningCertURL limited to https on ^sns\.[a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com$ with a .pem path, checked before any fetch, no redirects, and the certificate chaining to the system trust store with CN sns.amazonaws.com;
  - TopicArn equal to the configured topic;
  - Timestamp within 1 hour;
  - MessageId de-duplicated in inbound_events.
  An attacker who learns the URL can no longer POST a fabricated message: without AWS's signing key the request gets 401 and nothing is fetched or written.
* email_verdict uses only SES's receipt.dmarcVerdict, dkimVerdict, spfVerdict, spamVerdict and virusVerdict from inside the signed payload. DMARC PASS counts directly, since SES evaluates DMARC against the From domain. The authserv-id header parsing is removed: no header in the MIME can affect the verdict.
