proposal.safeguards:
Invariant 2:
- Every user-initiated write goes through a SECURITY DEFINER function called with the user's JWT and org header (get_supabase_for_user). That covers upload registration, execution confirmation, field confirmation, amendment links, counterparty domains, tags and confirmer grants. Each function checks auth.uid(), active_org_id(), role, department visibility and evidence in SQL.
- Users write the bytes to Storage with their own JWT, under a policy bound to their org and user folder. There is no update or delete policy.
- authenticated holds no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on the contract tables.
- The service role is used only by the ARQ worker and the connector webhooks. These are server-side jobs scoped to one org, the worker re-checks the uploader's membership, and they write status only through record_classification.
- With no Redis there is a 503 and no inline fallback.
- An AST test bans get_supabase_admin from the user paths.

Integrity of status:
- Every row is created 'pending', enforced for all roles by the guard trigger.
- sha256 is computed by the worker from stored bytes, never taken from the uploader.
- Status columns change only inside record_classification or confirm_execution, via a transaction-local app.contract_write flag.
- Pending rows are excluded from Q&A, portfolio answers, dedup and confirmation.
- Paralegal promotion is bound to sha256 and recorded append-only.
- Trash restores come back pending.

Signatures:
- Only CCA-chained or allowlisted vendor-sealed identities count, and self-issued certificates never do.
- The legal character is labelled: s.3A signature versus s.10A electronic record.
- First Schedule documents are blocked from confirmed cards.
- Trust-store fingerprints are pinned and CI-gated.

Data protection and the no-advice rule (UPL):
- Email intake trusts only AWS-signed verdicts.
- Text is PII-masked before it reaches Claude.
- Connector scopes are minimal (drive.file, Sites.Selected), for DPDP minimisation.
- Employment and personal-data contracts are visible to legal only by default.
- Stored signer data is limited to name, email, organisation, issuer, serial, time and authentication method. Aadhaar numbers are never stored.
- Business users see only lawyer-confirmed clauses, phrased as 'cl. X provides', with the disclaimer and an Ask-legal path to a lawyer.
- Retention follows the 013 trash flow.

objections: Trash restore cannot work as specified. Migration 013's restore_trash_item (supabase/migrations/013_approvals_trash_and_intake.sql, lines 627-705) re-inserts the snapshot with `insert ... select * from jsonb_populate_record(null::<table>, v_row)`. For a contract document that row still carries execution_status='executed', execution_evidence, signature_types and sha256. The new contract_documents_guard rejects any non-pending INSERT with 42501. It raises; it does not coerce. restore_trash_item's exception block only catches unique_violation and foreign_key_violation, so the restore aborts. The proposal says rows 'come back pending with sha256 null and are re-queued', but nothing does that: restore never writes a contract_ingest_queue outbox row, so even a pending row would never be re-classified. The sweep only picks up outbox rows. trash_item is also unspecified for this kind. Deleting a contract_documents row either breaks the append-only execution_confirmations rows (cascade) or is blocked by them (restrict). contract_fields lawyer confirmations would also be lost unless they are snapshotted as children. Fix I would accept: (1) add an explicit 'contract_document' branch to trash_item that snapshots contract_fields as children, and leaves execution_confirmations in place with no FK (or with an FK to a stable document id that is never deleted). (2) Add a branch to restore_trash_item that inserts the row with the classification columns overwritten to their pending defaults (status 'pending', evidence null, signature_types '{}', required_parties null, first_schedule_flag false, sha256 null), keeps storage_path, uploaded_by and claimed_sha256, and inserts a contract_ingest_queue row in the same transaction. (3) Have the trash round-trip test assert the outbox row exists and that no 42501 is raised.

The trash round trip, which has its own acceptance test, cannot work as specified. restore_trash_item (013, lines 627-706) re-inserts the snapshot with `insert ... select * from jsonb_populate_record(null::<table>, v_row)`. For a classified contract document, that snapshot carries execution_status='executed', non-null execution_evidence, signature_types and sha256. The proposal's own contract_documents_guard raises 42501 'Contract documents are created pending' on any such INSERT; it does not coerce the row. So every restore of a classified or paralegal-confirmed document fails instead of 'coming back pending with sha256 null'. Two further gaps: (a) nothing in restore writes a new contract_ingest_queue row, so the row is never re-queued; and (b) the re-apply depends on execution_confirmations surviving trash_item's DELETE of the contract_documents row, but the FK behaviour is unspecified. With ON DELETE CASCADE the 'append-only' confirmations are destroyed. With RESTRICT, trash_item fails. Fix I would accept: add a 'contract_document' branch to restore_trash_item that overwrites v_row with execution_status='pending', execution_evidence=null, signature_types='{}', required_parties=null, first_schedule_flag=false and sha256=null before the insert, and that inserts a fresh outbox row. Declare execution_confirmations.document_id with no FK, or ON DELETE NO ACTION handled by keeping a tombstone, so confirmations survive trash. Then test that the restore succeeds as the definer and that the guard still rejects a non-pending insert.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Contract-management value without a CLM implementation project. A zero-configuration start: pick files or folders, or forward emails, and within a day get a repository, candidate obligations, and a count of contracts awaiting stamp classification. Exposure appears only for confirmed assessments. Indian defaults work out of the box (Indian playbook pack, review presets, and vendor-verified shared stamp tables). Adoption is measured in the product, and full export means the customer is never trapped.

### What it can't fix

Organisational change management, executive sponsorship and training culture: per Gartner, the main reasons CLMs fail are people and data problems that software can only nudge. Deep ERP/CRM integration and complex approval workflows are deliberately not built. We can't make sales stop emailing Word files; we can only make the email-in path catch them. We won't show stamp exposure figures before a person confirms the classification, so the first-day headline is a to-do count, not a rupee number.

### What the user sees

An onboarding screen with three steps. 1. Pick Drive files or folders in Google Picker, share a folder with the workspace's service account, or get your forwarding address (verify your domain in one DNS step). 2. Pick your contract types (presets). 3. Invite your team. Within hours a progress page shows, for example: 'Ingested 412 files (9 rejected: 6 legacy .doc, 3 password-protected); 371 contracts (298 executed, 41 drafts, 32 to confirm); 58 amendments linked, 11 to confirm; 1,204 candidate obligations, 0 confirmed. Start confirming: next 30 days first. 23 contracts need stamp classification: confirm each in two clicks. Confirmed stamp exposure: none yet.' As legal confirms, the line becomes 'Confirmed stamp exposure: Rs 1.8 lakh across 7 contracts (16 still need classification)'. There is no unconfirmed amount or range. The GC's Adoption page shows: share of contract requests that came through intake versus contracts found later without one, obligations confirmed versus pending, stamp classifications confirmed versus pending, reminders acknowledged, and median time to answer business questions. 'Export everything' downloads a ZIP containing original files, CSV and JSON of all fields with quotes and confirmation status, obligations as CSV and ICS, stamp assessments with row source and version, and playbooks as JSON.

### What the system does

1. Defaults: the repository preset (P42), obligations preset (P16), Indian playbook (P44) and the shared stamp corpus (P17, vendor-verified, org_id NULL) are active from sign-up, and nothing needs configuring. 2. A backfill background job runs over connected sources, with per-org progress counters (files, rejections by reason, execution_status counts, link items, candidate and confirmed obligations). 3. Stamp exposure on onboarding and adoption pages is a SQL view: the sum of deficit or duty only over stamp_assessments with confirmed_by not null and status computed. It is shown beside a count of contracts needing classification (stamp_assessments missing or unconfirmed on executed contracts). Unconfirmed assessments contribute no amount anywhere: not in UI, digest or export totals. 4. An onboarding work queue orders confirmations by urgency: obligations due soonest, then high-value stamp classifications, so the headline numbers fill in fast. 5. Adoption metrics are SQL views over contract_requests, contracts, contract_obligations, obligation_reminders and stamp_assessments. A 'bypass' is a contract whose earliest source date has no matching request (same counterparty and type within 30 days). 6. A weekly digest of aggregate counts goes to the GC via n8n. 7. Export is a worker job producing a ZIP in the reports Storage bucket, downloaded via a signed URL (the existing pattern), with a schema README. It is available on every plan, and for 30 days after cancellation. 8. Pricing is per contract volume, not seats (note to P19).

### Where it is built

app/worker.py and the reports bucket signed-URL pattern (task_generate_pdf_report), app/routers/jobs.py, app/services/n8n_service.py, the P42/P16/P17/P44 modules (stamp_assessments.confirmed_by, contract_documents.execution_status), the team page and invitations (migration 009), frontend/src/app/team. New files: app/services/adoption_service.py, app/services/export_service.py, app/services/onboarding_queue.py, task_export_org in app/worker.py, SQL views in supabase/migrations/019_adoption_views.sql, frontend/src/app/onboarding/page.tsx and frontend/src/app/adoption/page.tsx, tests/test_export.py, tests/test_adoption.py, tests/test_onboarding.py.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Ironclad, Icertis, Agiloft and DocuSign CLM deliver value only after workflow design, integrations and migration, which is where half of first implementations stall. We start from contracts where they already are, with Indian defaults and shared stamp tables already verified, so first value arrives before anyone designs a workflow. The first numbers are honest: candidates and to-confirm counts, with rupee figures only once a person confirms. The adoption page shows the GC under-use early instead of at renewal, and full export removes the lock-in fear that stops mid-size Indian companies from buying.

### Safeguards

Export is restricted to owners and audit-logged, and signed URLs expire. The digest contains aggregates only. No rupee figure for stamp duty is shown, sent or exported unless a person has confirmed the classification, consistent with P17/P45. Backfill uses the same PII masking, minimal-scope connectors and DMARC rules as P42. Deletion and retention follow the existing trash and legal-hold rules.

### How the panel's objections were answered

The objection was that the zero-configuration 'stamp exposure Rs 4.6 lakh' headline contradicted P17/P45's rule of no amount before confirmation. Fixed: onboarding now shows 'N contracts need stamp classification', with an urgency-ordered queue to confirm them. Confirmed exposure is a SQL view summing only stamp_assessments with confirmed_by set, and it starts at 'none yet'. No unconfirmed amount or range appears in UI, digest or export. The acceptance tests were changed to match: confirmed_exposure_inr = 0 with no amount fields before confirmation, then exactly the sum of the confirmed rows. The same honesty applies to obligations, shown as candidates versus confirmed, and to execution status counts from P42.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_onboarding.py: a local folder connector fixture of 20 sample contracts with a mocked Claude, and no configuration beyond choosing the folder, creates repository rows, candidate obligations and unconfirmed stamp assessments. The progress payload shows 'N need stamp classification' with N equal to the unconfirmed executed contracts and confirmed_exposure_inr = 0. No amount field for unconfirmed rows exists in the payload or the rendered page (snapshot test).
- After two stamp assessments are confirmed in the test, confirmed_exposure_inr equals exactly the sum of those two results, and the 'need classification' count drops by two.
- The weekly digest and the export totals exclude unconfirmed assessments (seeded case with one confirmed and three unconfirmed).
- tests/test_adoption.py: on seeded data, a contract ingested via Drive with no request for that counterparty and type within 30 days counts as a bypass; one with a request doesn't.
- tests/test_export.py: the ZIP contains every original file (hash-matched); contracts.csv has one row per contract with its execution_status; obligations.ics parses with the icalendar library; stamp_assessments.csv carries row_source and table_version; playbooks.json re-imports into a fresh org to the same positions.
- Export is refused for a non-owner, and is available for 30 days after cancellation (Stripe status fixture).
- The weekly digest payload contains only aggregate counts, with no clause text or party names.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- 'Within a day' and 'within hours' depend on OCR volume and Claude rate limits for large backfills. Show an ETA computed from the queue instead of promising a time.
- The bypass metric (no request within 30 days for the same counterparty and type) will over-count legacy contracts signed before the product was adopted. Exclude contracts whose execution date predates onboarding.
- The 'Export everything' ZIP contains counterparty and employee personal data. Encrypt it, or at least put a short expiry on the signed URL, and record the export in the P35 processing records.
- Depends entirely on P42, P16, P17 and P44 shipping first. 'Within a day' assumes the backfill throughput of OCR plus a per-document Claude call. Measure it on a 400-file fixture before promising it on the onboarding screen.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Making every redline follow the firm's or legal team's own written positions, the same way every time: (1) the playbook is data the partners write and approve: preferred clause text, ordered fallbacks and walk-away for each clause topic, plus machine-checkable rules; (2) the inserted wording is the playbook's approved text, copied character for character, never text the model writes; (3) every suggested change quotes the counterparty clause it touches, and that quote is checked; (4) proper Word tracked changes are produced and read; (5) each reviewer's accept/reject decision on each position is recorded, so inconsistent reviewers show up. Indian points ship as a default pack: s.27 Contract Act non-competes, s.74 liquidated damages, seat vs venue, foreign seat/law for two Indian parties (PASL), stamp-duty-sensitive clauses, and indemnity vs cap carve-outs.

### What it can't fix

Commercial judgment on which fallback to concede in a live negotiation, and the counterparty's leverage. The quality of a firm's own playbook: we ship a default Indian pack, but a weak playbook produces consistent weak redlines. Clauses on topics the playbook doesn't cover still need a lawyer; we flag them rather than invent a position. Complex formatting such as tables inside tracked changes, moved-text markup and comments threads gets a best-effort round trip; the plain-text clause diff stays authoritative.

### What the user sees

A Playbooks page (/playbooks): a list of clause topics (limitation of liability, indemnity, governing law, seat, non-compete, payment terms, termination, assignment, confidentiality term, IP, data protection, stamp duty and costs). For each topic: preferred text, Fallback 1, Fallback 2, walk-away, and rules in plain form ('cap must not exceed 1x annual fees', 'governing law must be India', 'seat must be one of Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru', 'payment within 45 days or less'). Partners edit; a second senior approves each version, and the version number and approver are shown. In Studio > Redline, after uploading the counterparty's paper (PDF, DOCX or a DOCX with their tracked changes), the lawyer sees each clause with a badge: Matches preferred / Within Fallback 1 / Within Fallback 2 / Breaches walk-away / Not in playbook. Each suggested change shows the counterparty quote (a green tick means it was found in the document), the playbook text that would replace it, and why (the rule that fired, for example 'cap = 3x fees > 1x'). Buttons: Accept, Use other fallback, Reject, Escalate to partner. 'Download tracked-changes DOCX' produces a Word file with real insertions and deletions authored by the reviewer's name. A Consistency report (owners/partners) shows, for each position, how often each reviewer conceded it, for example 'Liability cap Fallback 2 accepted 9/10 by A, 1/12 by B'.

### What the system does

1. New migration 014_playbooks.sql: playbooks(id, org_id, name, contract_type, version, status draft|approved, approved_by, approved_at), playbook_positions(playbook_id, topic, preferred_text, fallbacks jsonb [{rank, text, variables}], walk_away text, rules jsonb), redline_decisions(org_id, document_id, playbook_version, topic, position_suggested, decision accepted|other_fallback|rejected|escalated, reviewer_id, decided_at). RLS like review_grids; approval goes through the existing approval_requests maker-checker (new action 'approve_playbook'), and editing an approved version creates a new draft version (the same lapse-on-change pattern as stamp_draft_approval). 2. Ingest: DOCX with tracked changes is parsed in new services/docx_redline.py (python-docx plus raw OOXML: w:ins, w:del, w:moveFrom/w:moveTo) into an 'original' and a 'revised' text, so contract_diff_service.compare runs on the real before/after instead of on flattened text. 3. Clause-to-topic mapping: deterministic keyword and heading rules first (headings such as 'Limitation of Liability' or 'Governing Law'); Claude (PII-masked through PiiMasker, playbook in a cached system block via prompt_engine.build_system) maps only the clauses left over, returning topic plus a verbatim quote of the clause. The quote must pass evidence_service.quote_found or the mapping is dropped and the clause is marked 'Not in playbook - lawyer review'. 4. Rule evaluation is deterministic code (services/playbook_rules.py): the existing governing_law.detect for law, seat and courts; regexes for money and multiples ('three times the fees', 'INR 50,00,000', 'aggregate fees paid in the preceding 12 months'); day counts for payment and notice; non-compete after term (post-termination restraint, flagged under s.27); a liquidated damages or penalty clause, flagged under s.74 with a note that compensation must be reasonable; arbitration seat outside India with both parties Indian (PASL flag); indemnity outside the cap. If a rule can't parse its input, the result is 'cannot evaluate', never a pass. 5. Position selection: the highest-ranked playbook text whose rules the counterparty clause already meets is 'within'. Otherwise the suggestion is the preferred text, or the next fallback the reviewer picks. The replacement is the playbook text with only its declared variables filled (party names, amounts from the deal sheet); a test asserts the replacement equals the template after variable substitution, byte for byte. Free-form AI edits are allowed only as a separate 'AI suggestion (not playbook)' card that needs explicit lawyer acceptance and is tagged in the export. 6. Export: services/docx_redline.py writes w:del (original runs) and w:ins (replacement) produced from a word-level diff-match-patch of the original clause against the replacement, with w:author set to the reviewer and w:date set to now; risk_delta still comes from contract_diff_service's deterministic score. 7. Every decision writes redline_decisions and an audit_logs row; the consistency report is a SQL aggregate. 8. Citations in explanations (s.27, s.74, Interplay) go through citation_service as usual. 9. Nothing goes to the counterparty from the system: the lawyer downloads the DOCX and sends it.

### Where it is built

Extend app/services/contract_diff_service.py (alignment, inline diff, risk score), app/services/governing_law.py, app/services/evidence_service.quote_found, app/services/prompt_engine.build_system (cached playbook block), app/services/anthropic_service.REDLINE_PROMPT (add playbook-mapping prompt), app/routers/documents.py /compare (add playbook_id), approval_requests in supabase/migrations/013. New: supabase/migrations/014_playbooks.sql, app/services/playbook_service.py, app/services/playbook_rules.py, app/services/docx_redline.py, app/routers/playbooks.py, data/playbooks/india_default.json, frontend/src/app/playbooks/page.tsx, a Redline tab update in frontend/src/app/studio, tests/test_playbooks.py, tests/test_docx_redline.py, evals/redlines/ (20 Indian MSAs/NDAs with expected badges).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

On the VLAIR redlining task, Harvey and Vincent scored below lawyers because the model writes standard text and loses formatted redlines. Here the model never writes the inserted text: it only maps clauses to topics, the replacement is the firm's approved wording, rule checks are code, and tracked changes are parsed and written as real OOXML. Spellbook and LegalOn apply US/UK-tuned playbooks; ours ships Indian defaults (s.27, s.74, seat vs venue, PASL, stamp) and lets the firm override them. None of them records which reviewer conceded which position; we do, and that is what fixes inconsistency between associates.

### Safeguards

Text goes through PiiMasker before Claude; the playbook is firm work product, kept in the org's RLS scope and never in the shared corpus. Playbook versions need two seniors (maker-checker, existing approval_requests). Nothing is sent to the counterparty by the system; the lawyer downloads and sends. Inserted text is human-approved playbook language, and AI-written alternatives are labelled. Citations go through citation_service, and verify_output_safety applies to explanations. Every decision is audit-logged. The document text is treated as data (prompt-injection line already in the prompts).

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_playbook_rules.py: a fixture clause 'aggregate liability shall not exceed three (3) times the Fees paid in the preceding twelve months' against a rule cap<=1x gives a breach with parsed multiple 3; 'shall not exceed the Fees paid' gives within preferred; an unparseable cap gives 'cannot evaluate' and never 'within'.
- Governing law 'laws of England and Wales' with seat London, both parties with Indian addresses: the walk-away rule fires even when a mocked Claude mapping labels the clause acceptable (deterministic rule wins).
- A non-compete clause 'for 24 months after termination' fires the s.27 flag; the same clause limited to the term does not.
- The replacement text for an accepted Fallback 1 equals playbook fallback text with variables substituted (byte equality); a mocked model response that alters one word of the fallback is rejected.
- A mocked Claude topic mapping whose quote isn't in the document is dropped and the clause shows 'Not in playbook'; the count of dropped mappings is returned.
- tests/test_docx_redline.py: export a redline, re-open it with python-docx, count w:ins and w:del elements equal to the changed clauses, w:author equals the reviewer's name, and accepting all changes (programmatically removing w:del and unwrapping w:ins) yields text identical to the expected revised contract.
- Parse fixtures/counterparty_tracked.docx (made in Word with insertions, deletions and a move): the reconstructed original and revised texts match hand-made expected files.
- DB test: an associate cannot set playbooks.status='approved'; approval needs a second senior via approval_requests; editing an approved version's text produces a new draft version and leaves the old one approved.

**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Auditing a client's or company's existing contracts for stamping and registration exposure before a dispute: for each document, what stamp evidence the copy shows (e-stamp certificate number, denomination, franking, impressed paper text), what duty the P17 table says was due, the deficit, the penalty as of today under that state's penalty provision, the route to cure (adjudication or voluntary payment of deficit and penalty), and the procedural consequence in plain terms with the authority checked (inadmissible in evidence until duty and penalty are paid; for arbitration agreements, after In Re Interplay (2023), a curable defect for the tribunal, not a bar to appointment). It also prioritises: contracts with arbitration clauses, high value, near-expiry or in dispute come first.

### What it can't fix

Whether the original physical document was stamped when the copy we have is a scan without the stamp page; we say 'no stamp evidence in this copy', never 'unstamped'. The Collector's adjudication and discretion on penalty. Whether paying now is commercially wise (it may also alert the authorities) is the client's and lawyer's decision. Privilege: in India, communications with in-house counsel may not get the protection s.132 BSA gives to an advocate's professional communications, so a company wanting the audit privileged should commission it through external counsel. The product can label the report and route it, but it can't create privilege.

### What the user sees

'Stamp exposure audit' on the repository (P42) or a selected folder. A table, one row per contract: name, state, instrument (as confirmed), stamp evidence found ('e-Stamp IN-KA12345678901234A, Rs 500' with the page image crop), duty due, deficit, penalty today (with the formula and the penalty section), registration status (compulsory and not evidenced / evidenced / not required), arbitration clause yes/no, priority. Filters: under-stamped, no evidence, needs classification. 'Cost to cure now' total at the top. A draft memo to the client (DOCX/PDF) is generated from the table: which documents, which Act, cost to cure, consequences with Interplay explained, and recommended steps. It's marked 'Draft: requires advocate review' and can't be sent or exported as final until a lawyer approves it (the existing drafts.approved_by mechanism).

### What the system does

1. Stamp evidence detection is deterministic: OCR text of the first and last pages (ocr_service; Tesseract with eng plus regional languages for stamp paper) is scanned with regexes for SHCIL certificate numbers (IN-<state code><digits><letter>), 'Certificate Issued Date', 'Stamp Duty Amount(Rs.)', 'Account Reference', franking imprints ('Franking', 'Stamp Duty Paid', denomination), impressed paper text ('INDIA NON JUDICIAL', denomination in words), and registration endorsements ('Sub-Registrar', 'Document No.', 'Book I'). The amount is parsed by code. 2. Duty due comes from the P17 assessment (confirmed instrument key and inputs); without a confirmed classification the row is 'needs classification' and no deficit is shown. 3. Penalty: the state row's penalty formula (for example a percentage per month on the deficit up to a cap, or a multiple of the deficit) evaluated with the execution date from a verified quote and today's date; the result is labelled 'maximum exposure' where the statute leaves the amount to the authority's discretion. 4. Consequence text is fixed, lawyer-written template text keyed by context (suit evidence, arbitration agreement, registration), not generated; it cites In Re Interplay and the relevant Stamp Act sections, and citation_service confirms each (Interplay must be a known_case in legal_authorities, and the sections must exist in the registry). 5. Priority score is code: arbitration clause, value band, dispute flag from the case tracker (court_cases linked), expiry soon. 6. The memo is assembled from the table plus template paragraphs; Claude may only write the cover summary, which passes verify_output_safety and citation_service and is labelled. 7. Runs as an ARQ job (task_stamp_audit) re-checking the user's role, results stored in stamp_assessments with audit_id.

### Where it is built

P17 stamp_duty registry and stamp_assessments; app/services/ocr_service.py; app/services/citation_service.py; app/services/drafting_engine.py and drafts approval (migration 013); app/worker.py job pattern; app/services/queue_service.py; court_cases (migration 011) for dispute flags; app/services/pdf_service.py. New: app/services/stamp_duty/evidence.py, app/services/stamp_duty/audit.py, task_stamp_audit in app/worker.py, frontend/src/app/obligations or a new /contracts/audit page, tests/test_stamp_evidence.py, tests/test_stamp_audit.py, fixtures with synthetic e-stamp certificate images (made by us, no real certificate numbers).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Manupatra and SCC Online find Interplay but don't apply it to a client's documents; Harvey and CoCounsel don't know Indian stamp law; CLMs don't look at the stamp page. This audit is mostly code: evidence detection by pattern, duty from the sourced table, penalty by formula, consequences from lawyer-written templates with checked citations. The only AI step is the cover summary, which a lawyer approves.

### Safeguards

Lawyer approval before any memo leaves the system (invariant on AI output reaching a client). Fixed consequence text with citation checks (invariant 3). PII-masked AI summary. The privilege caveat for in-house audits is shown on the audit screen. No contact with stamp authorities. Audit logged. RLS per org; the job runs with the user's role re-checked, as the existing worker does.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_stamp_evidence.py: a synthetic e-stamp certificate OCR text gives certificate number, state code KA and amount 500; franking text gives the franked amount; a copy with no stamp page gives 'no_evidence_in_copy' (never 'unstamped').
- A Karnataka agreement with Rs 500 paid and Rs 1,000 due (golden fixture) gives deficit Rs 500 and a penalty equal to the hand-computed value for the fixture's execution date and a frozen today.
- An unconfirmed instrument key gives 'needs_classification' with no deficit or penalty.
- A memo draft can't be exported as final while approved_by is null (API returns 409); after a partner approves, editing any paragraph clears the approval (existing trigger).
- The consequence paragraph for an arbitration agreement contains the Interplay citation and citation_service returns known_case for it; with legal_authorities empty the citation is marked [unverified] and the memo is blocked from approval until fixed.
- Priority ordering on a seeded set: an arbitration-clause contract with a linked court case ranks above a low-value NDA.
- The worker job re-checks that the requesting user is still a member with associate or higher; a removed user's job does nothing.
- Penalty with discretion is labelled 'maximum exposure'.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Add a link to the SHCIL 'verify e-stamp certificate' page per detected certificate. Fake e-stamps are common, and a matching regex isn't authenticity.
- Penalty rows for states where the authority has discretion (for example a 'up to 10 times' deficit) should show the range and the minimum as well as the maximum exposure.
- In Re Interplay's consequence text is correct. Also note that s.35 inadmissibility applies in suits and that the impounding route sits under ss.33/38 of the Indian Stamp Act or the state equivalent.
- A Drive or ZIP backfill audit run by in-house teams creates a discoverable record of known deficits. Make the privilege caveat a required acknowledgement before the run, not just a banner.
- When the stamp page is detected only from OCR, attach the page crop with the detected amount so the lawyer verifies it. Tesseract misreads denominations.
- Inherits P17's table-ownership issue. Fix that first.
- With no stamp page, 'no_evidence_in_copy' is the right wording. Keep any total exposure figure limited to rows that have a confirmed classification.
- The test for a removed user's job fits the existing worker re-check pattern.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Building a firm-wide party index automatically from data the firm already has, and running a deterministic match (transliteration- and relation-aware) on identity fields before any facts are received.

The decisions a lawyer can record are constrained by BCI Rule 33, computed in code and enforced by a database trigger:
- a hard link to an existing matter, adverse to our client, allows only Decline;
- only 'undetermined' connections can be cleared, by a countersignature;
- wrong links are cured only by audited data correction;
- 'not the same person' applies only to Strong name hits.

New this round: the side a prospective client says they are on is never trusted. On a hard link, a role taken from intake answers is 'claimed' and counts as adverse. A same-side role must come from a case type the firm set or eCourts synced, or from corroboration that a lawyer recorded against a document and a different partner countersigned.

### What it can't fix

Relationships that exist nowhere in the firm's data, other firms' clients, and undisclosed corporate groups are out of reach.

Whether a matter 'arises from' another cannot be fully decided by code; the residual judgment stays with a lawyer and a countersigning partner.

Police-station coverage is limited to the states we have seeded.

A corroborating document can itself be forged, or misread by the lawyer. We bind the confirmation to the document's hash and two lawyers' names; we cannot authenticate an FIR copy.

Genuine co-accused or same-side enquirers at pre-filing stage will see Decline-only until a lawyer corroborates their role. That is deliberate friction.

What eCourtsIndia returns and what lawyers enter limit the linkage. Name matching is imperfect, and we report precision and recall.

### What the user sees

Conflict check card: as in round 5, with four bands and matter-link labels, plus a role line on every hard link:
- 'Role: claimed by enquirer: complainant (not verified). Treated as adverse.' The buttons are Decline only, plus 'Record role corroboration'.
- 'Role: from case type (bail application, set by A. Rao)' or 'from eCourts record'.
- 'Role: corroborated by A. Rao from FIR copy p.2, countersigned by S. Iyer'.

'Record role corroboration' opens a form:
- pick a document on the check: an FIR copy, chargesheet, court order or eCourts party list;
- give a page or paragraph reference;
- pick the role it shows, from the closed enum;
- give a reason of at least 30 characters;
- submit, which creates a conflict_role_confirmation approval that a different owner or partner must execute.
Until it is executed, the card stays Decline-only.

The intake questions are unchanged, but the enquirer's role answer is labelled 'claimed' everywhere it appears.

### What the system does

1)-3) party_index, normalisation, matching, police stations, fir_compare and same_matter v4 are unchanged from round 5.

4) Role side, revised. role_new is (value, source), with source in {case_type_firm, case_type_ecourts, corroborated, claimed, unknown}.
- case_type_ecourts: the case type comes from a court_cases row with source='ecourtsindia', mapped through ROLE_BY_CASE_TYPE (a bail, anticipatory bail or quashing applicant is on the accused side; an execution petitioner is the decree-holder; and so on).
- case_type_firm: the case type was set by an authenticated member with role associate or above, through the matter form. The case-type column has case_type_source and case_type_set_by, and a value written by whatsapp_intake, telephony_session or any service-role intake path is stored with case_type_source='intake' and maps to claimed.
- corroborated: an executed conflict_role_confirmation approval exists for this check_id and link_hash.
- claimed: the role comes from intake answers (WhatsApp, phone, web form) or from an intake-set case type.
- unknown: there is no information.

Adverse for a hard link: effective_adverse = (role_new.source in {claimed, unknown}) OR (role value opposite to our client's role on the linked matter). Only the case_type_firm, case_type_ecourts and corroborated sources can make a hard link same-side.

5) allowed_decisions is unchanged in shape:
- hard and effective_adverse gives {declined};
- hard, same-side and trusted source gives {cleared, declined};
- undetermined, Strong or Possible, and different are as in round 5.

6) DB enforcement, extended.
- record_conflict_check() (SECURITY DEFINER) writes, for each hit, the role value, role_source and link_hash. link_hash covers the hard link bases, the party identities and the linked matter's client role, but not role_new, so a role confirmation does not void itself.
- The BEFORE INSERT trigger on conflict_decisions now recomputes effective_adverse itself from the stored hit. For each hard hit it treats role_source in ('claimed','unknown') as adverse, and accepts 'corroborated' only if an executed conflict_role_confirmation approval exists that:
  - matches check_id and link_hash;
  - names a document_id on the same org and matter-intake, whose stored sha256 equals the approval's doc_sha256;
  - has a requester of role associate or above, and an approver who is a different owner or partner.
  It raises on any decision other than 'declined' while any hard hit is effectively adverse. The trigger does not trust the adverse flag written by the API.
- Any change to the hits (a new link, a linkage correction) changes link_hash, and that voids the confirmation.

7) Linkage correction, the intake hold, purge on decline and re-check on linkage change are unchanged.

8) Corroboration flow. POST /conflicts/{check_id}/role-confirmation {hit_id, document_id, page_ref, role, reason} creates the approval (migration 013's machinery, new kind conflict_role_confirmation). Executing it re-runs the check: role_source becomes corroborated and allowed_decisions is recomputed. Each step is audited (CONFLICT_ROLE_CONFIRMATION_REQUESTED and EXECUTED).

### Where it is built

Extend:
- app/services/conflict_service.py: role_side v5 with sources, effective_adverse and link_hash;
- app/routers/conflicts.py: the role-confirmation endpoint;
- app/services/whatsapp_intake.py and telephony_session.py: intake answers are written with role_source='claimed', and any case type they infer gets case_type_source='intake';
- app/routers/cases.py: the case-type write sets case_type_source='firm' and case_type_set_by from the caller's JWT;
- the migration 013 approvals, which gain the kind conflict_role_confirmation with doc_sha256, page_ref and role;
- the frontend ConflictCard: the role line and the corroboration form.

Migration 017_conflict_index.sql adds:
- the hit fields role_value, role_source and link_hash;
- case_type_source and case_type_set_by on court_cases and on intake records;
- the v5 trigger, which recomputes effective_adverse.

Fixtures: role_claims.csv, with intake-claimed roles against the true FIR roles.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Intapp and Aderant follow US and UK rules, where consent cures most conflicts, and trust the intake form's role field. Clio and PracticePanther do exact-name search with free-text resolution. Harvey and CoCounsel do no conflicts. Indian small firms rely on a register and memory.

Ours links proceedings deterministically, makes a hard same-matter link Decline-only in code and in the trigger, and never lets the enquirer's own account of which side they are on unlock it. Only firm-set or court-synced case types, or a document-bound corroboration countersigned by a different partner, can show a same-side role, and the trigger checks this itself.

### Safeguards

Rule 33 is enforced in code and in a database trigger that recomputes adverseness itself.

On a hard link, an enquirer's self-reported role and an unknown role both count as adverse. Same-side status needs:
- a firm-set case type, with the setter recorded;
- an eCourts-synced case type;
- or a document-hash-bound corroboration by a lawyer, countersigned by a different owner or partner and voided by any change in the links.

Only 'undetermined' connections can be cleared. Wrong links are cured by audited correction. Identity comes before facts, nothing substantive is processed on hold, and identifiers are HMACs.

### How the panel's objections were answered

Objection (the Decline-only rule depends on a role the untrusted prospective client supplies):
- role_new now carries a source.
- Intake answers, and any case type inferred or written by an intake path, are 'claimed'. On a hard link, a claimed or unknown role is adverse, both in conflict_service and, independently, in the trigger, which recomputes from the stored role_source and does not trust the API's adverse flag.
- A same-side role on a hard link comes only from a firm-set case type (setter recorded from the JWT), an eCourts-synced case type, or an executed conflict_role_confirmation. That approval is bound to the check_id, the link_hash and the corroborating document's sha256, with page reference and reason, and is countersigned by a different owner or partner.
- Test added: a same-FIR intake claiming the complainant role, with no corroboration, gives {declined} only, and a direct INSERT of 'cleared' raises.

### Acceptance tests

- DB test (objection): our client is the complainant on FIR 123/2025, PS Saket. A WhatsApp intake gives the same FIR, and the enquirer answers 'I am the complainant / victim'. There is no case type and no corroboration. role_source='claimed', allowed_decisions={declined}, and the API offers nothing else. A direct INSERT of 'cleared' into conflict_decisions raises, as service_role or as a partner, even when record_conflict_check's stored adverse flag is forced to false in the fixture.
- DB test: in the same case, an associate files conflict_role_confirmation with an FIR copy that shows the enquirer as complainant. Until a different partner executes it, the card is Decline-only. After execution, role_source='corroborated' and {cleared, declined} is offered. If the requester executes their own request, it raises. If the document's sha256 no longer matches the approval's doc_sha256, the trigger raises on 'cleared'.
- DB test: after the confirmation, a linkage correction that adds a connected CNR changes link_hash. The confirmation is void and the card returns to Decline-only.
- Unit: a case type 'Bail Application' written by whatsapp_intake has case_type_source='intake' and maps to claimed. The same case type set by an associate in the matter form maps to case_type_firm (accused side); against our complainant client that is adverse, so Decline-only.
- Unit: a co-accused, our client being the accused on the same FIR, with the case type synced from eCourts as a bail application, gets the same-side options. The same co-accused with only an intake claim gets Decline-only.
- Fixture: role_claims.csv (60 rows of claimed roles, including false ones) gives 0 hard-link checks where a claimed role unlocks anything other than Decline (a hard CI gate).
- Round-5 tests retained: the same-FIR adverse hit raises on consent or cleared even with executed approvals; not_same_person does not remove a hard matter-link finding; the linkage_correction flow and hash voiding; an Exact identifier hit never offers not_same_person; Mehroli against Mehrauli unseeded gives undetermined; Kotwali in different districts gives differ; the sessions case with committal details skipped gives undetermined, and with them gives same; an unknown case type gives undetermined; linked_proceedings.csv has 0 linked pairs classified 'different'; recall at least 0.95 and precision at least 0.90; the intake hold with 0 AI calls; purge on decline; party_hits_view isolation.

### Still blocking

- case_type_firm is accepted as a trusted source that can make a hard link same-side, but for a new enquiry it is only the enquirer's claim re-typed by one associate. Before filing, the case type on the prospective matter (for example 'Bail Application') reflects what the enquirer told the firm. A single associate entering it in the matter form turns role_source from 'claimed' into 'case_type_firm', and that unlocks {cleared, declined} with no document, no hash binding and no different-partner countersignature. The corroborated path requires all three, so case_type_firm is a one-person bypass of the control this round adds. Under Rule 33, a complainant who poses as a co-accused (to conflict the firm out, or to learn the defence) gets cleared by an associate's data entry. Fix I would accept: for role_new on a hard link, a firm-set case type counts as trusted only when it is tied to a filed proceeding, meaning the new matter's court_cases row has a CNR/case number confirmed by eCourts sync (case_type_ecourts), or when it goes through the same conflict_role_confirmation approval (document sha256, page_ref, a different owner or partner). Otherwise map it to 'claimed'. Add a DB test: an associate sets 'Bail Application' on an intake that hard-links to our complainant client's FIR, and the result is still {declined}, with a direct 'cleared' insert raising.
- The 'case_type_firm' path re-launders the enquirer's claim, and the trigger does not verify it. (1) For a pre-engagement enquiry, the only source of a case type for the new matter is what the enquirer said. A single associate who types 'Bail Application' into the matter form after hearing the enquirer's account produces role_source='case_type_firm'. That unlocks {cleared, declined} on a hard same-FIR link with no document and no second lawyer, while the 'corroborated' path for the same fact needs a document hash and a different partner's countersignature. (2) The trigger accepts 'corroborated' only after checking the approval, but it takes 'case_type_firm' and 'case_type_ecourts' as stored by record_conflict_check. It does not re-derive them from court_cases.case_type_source and case_type_set_by, or apply ROLE_BY_CASE_TYPE in SQL. A buggy or forged hit payload with role_source='case_type_firm' therefore clears a hard adverse link, the same class of trust the round claims to remove. Fix I would accept: (a) on a hard link, a firm-set case type on a matter not yet engaged, or on one whose case type was set after the conflict check began, counts as claimed unless it is eCourts-synced or corroborated with countersignature. Equivalently, require the same different-partner countersignature for case_type_firm. (b) The trigger re-reads the linked court_cases or intake record, checks case_type_source and the setter's role, and maps the role in SQL, ignoring role_source from the hit payload except for 'corroborated', which it verifies. (c) Add a test: a hit with role_source forced to 'case_type_firm' and no matching firm-set court_cases row raises on 'cleared'. A second test: an associate setting the case type on the enquiry's own matter does not unlock clearing without a countersignature.
- The trusted sources that unlock a same-side hard link can be forged by staff or are hearsay. (1) case_type_source, case_type_set_by and source='ecourtsindia' are set only in app/routers/cases.py. But authenticated users have direct INSERT and UPDATE on court_cases (011), and the eCourts sync itself writes through the user's client. Any member, including a paralegal, can PATCH case_type_source='firm', case_type_set_by=<a partner's uuid>, or source='ecourtsindia' with any case type through PostgREST. The trigger that 'checks this itself' then reads forged sources. (2) Even an honest case_type_firm is only the enquirer's story relayed by a single associate. In the round's own example, the associate sets a case type mapping the enquirer to the complainant side, and the hard link becomes clearable with no countersignature. The countersigned, document-bound corroboration path exists precisely to stop that, so this source is a bypass of it. Fix I would accept: add a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on court_cases and intake records. It derives case_type_source and case_type_set_by from auth.uid(), role and session role ('intake' for service_role intake paths), ignores client-supplied values, and refuses authenticated writes of source='ecourtsindia' or of the provider fields. Alternatively, verify a server HMAC over the provider payload. Then, for hard links, accept only case_type_ecourts (server-verified) or an executed corroboration as same-side, and let case_type_firm narrow only 'undetermined' findings. Add db tests for a direct forged PATCH and for a single-associate case type on a hard link (Decline-only).

proposal.out_of_scope:
Relationships that exist nowhere in the firm's data, other firms' clients, and undisclosed corporate groups are out of reach.

Whether a matter 'arises from' another cannot be fully decided by code; the residual judgment stays with a lawyer and a countersigning partner.

Police-station coverage is limited to the states we have seeded.

A corroborating document can itself be forged, or misread by the lawyer. We bind the confirmation to the document's hash and two lawyers' names; we cannot authenticate an FIR copy.

Genuine co-accused or same-side enquirers at pre-filing stage will see Decline-only until a lawyer corroborates their role. That is deliberate friction.

What eCourtsIndia returns and what lawyers enter limit the linkage. Name matching is imperfect, and we report precision and recall.

solutions.solution_markdown:
**Effort:** M

### What software can fix

Building the hearing-ready one-pager automatically the moment a matter is listed: last order and its directions, compliance due, open IAs, the bench, adjournment history, limitation points and open tasks, from the order sheets and files the firm already holds.

### What it can't fix

Reading the full brief and preparing arguments, which stays the lawyer's job; orders the court has not uploaded; documents that never reached the matter file.

### What the user sees

At 19:00 for every matter on tomorrow's board (or when a short-notice listing is detected), a Hearing brief appears on the matter and in the advocate's board strip: listing details (court, item, bench, list type); last order date with its operative paragraph quoted; directions and whether each was complied with; pending IAs; deadlines from the docket; adjournment count; prior bench; key documents with links. Each AI-written line has a 'source' link highlighting the quote in the order PDF. One click exports to PDF for the phone.

### What the system does

1. Trigger: P05 match or next_hearing_date within 2 days.
2. Deterministic sections from data: listing, deadlines (P13), adjournments (P04), IAs and documents linked to the matter, order list from provider_data/uploads.
3. AI section: the latest order text (PII-masked) is sent to Claude with a cached system prompt (prompt_engine.build_system) asking for directions and compliance items, each with a verbatim quote; quote_match verifies each against the order; failures are discarded and counted. Dates in directions are computed in code from the order date.
4. Citation check on any authority mentioned (citation_service).
5. Brief stored per hearing date; regenerated if a new order arrives.

### Where it is built

P05 board, P13 deadline_service, P04 hearing_outcomes; app/services/evidence_service.quote_match; prompt_engine.build_system; anthropic_service; pdf_service for export; new app/services/brief_service.py and app/routers/briefs.py; frontend matter panel in frontend/src/app/cases/page.tsx.

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Harvey and CoCounsel summarise what is uploaded but don't pull Indian order sheets and cause-list entries or know a matter is listed tomorrow; Indian trackers show dates, not a summary. Ours is triggered by the listing itself and every AI line is quote-verified against the order.

### Safeguards

Internal work product, not client-facing; PII masked before Claude; prompt caching per invariant 5; citations checked per invariant 3.

### Acceptance tests

- tests/test_briefs.py::test_trigger: a P05 exact match for tomorrow creates one brief; a second ingest of the same list does not duplicate it.
- test_quote_verification: mocked Claude output with one verified and one fabricated direction keeps one and reports discarded_unverified=1.
- test_direction_date: 'file reply within four weeks' in an order dated 2026-10-01 yields 2026-10-29 computed in code.
- test_no_order_available: with no order text the brief still renders deterministic sections and says 'last order not available'.
- Eval: evals/cases.json gains 10 Indian order sheets (English and Hindi) with expected directions; scripts/run_evals.py checks recall at least 80% and zero unverified quotes.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Directions often run from receipt or service, not from the order date. Capture the trigger event and fall back to the safe date.
- Many district order sheets are handwritten or typed in Hindi on scanned pages. Show the OCR confidence on the 'last order' section and say 'order text unreliable' rather than extracting from a low-confidence scan.
- Briefs should honour ethical walls when shown in the board strip of an advocate not on the matter team.
- Order texts from provider_data may be links rather than text. Say how the order PDF is fetched and OCR'd (Tesseract; vision fallback per setting) before the AI step.

**Effort:** L

### What software can fix

Giving every client an automatic, tamper-evident record of what their firm actually did and when, without the lawyer having to write it up. The record has three kinds of entry: court events (fetched by our server from the provider), system events (the product's own actions: drafted, approved, exported, filed with a proof hash, update sent, quote sent, message answered) and lawyer-recorded milestones, each labelled with its source. Clients and third parties can check the record independently. Every client-facing message carries the current chain head. A daily root is timestamped by an outside timestamp authority. The exported work log can be recomputed offline, including across internal entries, whose contents are hidden behind salted commitments.

### What it can't fix

Software can't change how fast the Bar Council handles complaints (s.35/36B), or the D.K. Gandhi ruling taking advocates out of consumer law. A firm that doesn't use the system, or never records its filings, produces no log, and we can't prove that work done outside the system happened. The log shows what was done, not whether it was done well. A lawyer-recorded milestone is the lawyer's assertion and is labelled that way. Only court and system events are attested by our server. Tamper-evidence is not tamper-proofing. Someone with database-owner access (our own operators, or the operator of a self-hosted install) could still rewrite events and recompute hashes. What they can't do is make the rewritten chain match the heads already sent to clients and the timestamped daily roots, so the rewrite is detectable, not impossible. On a self-hosted install the attestation key belongs to the operator, so court and system labels there are only as trustworthy as that operator.

### What the user sees

Client: after the lawyer turns on 'Share timeline', the client receives the P01 updates and a monthly WhatsApp digest. Every one of these messages ends with a line such as 'Record check: entry 23, code 7f3a91c2e04b5d18'. A private link (no login, no app) opens a read-only page listing, for example: '3 Oct: Legal notice sent (firm system, proof: postal receipt hash). 4 Nov: Complaint filed, CC 212/2025 (court record). 24 Oct: Hearing; next date 14 Nov (court record). 25 Oct: Update sent to you (firm system).' Internal entries appear only as 'internal entry (contents not shared)', so the client can see there is no gap. 'Download work log' gives a PDF plus a JSON file. On a public /verify page anyone can drop the JSON file and paste any record-check code from their WhatsApp messages. The page recomputes the chain in the browser, checks that the codes occur in it, checks the latest daily timestamp proof, and reports 'consistent' or exactly where it breaks. Lawyer: a 'Timeline' tab on each court case or case thread lists everything, internal and client-visible, each with its source label. 'Record a milestone' takes a type, a date and an optional proof file. A 'Show to client' / 'Hide from client' toggle appears per entry, and each change is itself logged.

### What the system does

1) Migration 014 adds the following. matter_events: id identity; event_uuid unique; org_id; matter_kind in ('court_case', 'case_thread'); matter_id uuid with NO foreign key, so trash_item() deleting the case never cascades into this table; seq; occurred_at; recorded_at; source in (court, system, lawyer); kind (hearing, next_date, order, status_change, notice_sent, filed, document_approved, document_exported, update_sent, quote_sent, message_answered, milestone, correction, visibility_changed); summary rendered from fixed templates; proof_sha256; ref_seq; actor_user_id; default_visible, a pure function of (source, kind); salt (16 random bytes); commitment; prev_hash; hash. Uniqueness on (matter_kind, matter_id, seq) and on (matter_kind, matter_id, prev_hash). matter_chain_heads: (matter_kind, matter_id) primary key, org_id, seq, head_hash. timeline_shares: matter, token_sha256, contact_id, expires_at, revoked_at. chain_anchors: day, merkle_root, tsa_token, tsa_url. trash_items gains timeline_head_sha256, timeline_seq, and the new kind 'matter_timeline' for tombstones. 2) Hashing, identical in SQL and in Python and JS verifiers. canonical = a fixed field order joined by U+001F, with timestamps in UTC as microsecond ISO strings. commitment = sha256(canonical || salt). hash = sha256(prev_hash || ':' || commitment). The genesis prev_hash is sha256('dl-timeline-v1:' || matter_kind || ':' || matter_id). Because hidden events are exported as (seq, commitment, prev_hash, hash) only, a third party can recompute every link, and the salt stops anyone from guessing a hidden entry's templated contents. 3) Writing and serialisation: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on matter_events and matter_chain_heads are revoked from anon and authenticated. A BEFORE INSERT trigger also refuses any row unless the transaction-local GUC app.matter_emit='on' is set, and that refusal applies to service_role too. The only writer is the private SECURITY DEFINER function _append_event(). It sets the GUC, inserts the matter's head row with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, takes it with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (so per-matter appends are serialised), assigns seq = head.seq + 1 and prev_hash = head.head_hash, inserts the event, and updates the head. Concurrent emits for one matter queue on the row lock, and the unique constraints are a backstop. 4) Entry points: record_milestone(matter, kind, occurred_at, summary_params, proof_sha256) is callable by authenticated users. It checks membership and matter visibility with the court_cases/case_threads RLS rules, forces source='lawyer' and actor=auth.uid(), and renders the template server-side. emit_attested_event(fields..., p_attest) is how court and system events are written. The API process's hooks build them in-process: the ecourts_service.sync diff computed from the provider response the server itself just fetched (never from user-writable provider_data); the draft approve and export endpoints; the client_updates and fee_quotes sends; and reply_as_lawyer. The function recomputes HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical fields with a secret kept in a private schema table (or Supabase Vault) that anon and authenticated can't read, and the API knows the same secret as TIMELINE_ATTEST_KEY. It rejects a mismatch, and event_uuid uniqueness blocks replay. So a direct PostgREST call can't produce source='court' or 'system', and the hooks still run under the user's JWT, adding no service-role path in user-facing code (invariant 2). 5) Visibility: an entry's visibility is never updated in place. 'Show to client' / 'Hide from client' calls set_event_visibility(), which appends a 'visibility_changed' event (internal, ref_seq pointing to the target) to the same chain. Effective visibility is the latest visibility_changed for that event, falling back to default_visible. Court events, update_sent and quote_sent default to visible. Everything else defaults to internal (privilege). 6) Client access is through client_timeline(p_token), a SECURITY DEFINER RPC callable by anon and rate limited. It hashes the token, checks the share isn't revoked or expired and that the matter still exists (not in trash), and returns visible events in full and hidden ones as commitments, plus the head. 7) Anchoring outside the firm's control, in three ways. (a) Every client-facing message (each P01 update, the monthly digest, the PDF footer, the share page) carries the current seq and the first 16 hex characters of head_hash. The client therefore holds a growing set of commitments in their own WhatsApp that a rewritten chain can't reproduce. (b) A daily server job computes a Merkle root over all matter heads (leaf = sha256(matter_kind:matter_id:seq:head)). It obtains an RFC 3161 timestamp from a configured external timestamp authority (TIMELINE_TSA_URL; only the hash leaves our servers) and writes the root and token to chain_anchors and to a write-once object store bucket (S3 Object Lock, compliance mode). (c) The exported JSON includes the Merkle inclusion proof and TSA token for the latest anchor covering the matter. 8) Verification is offline-first. scripts/verify_timeline.py and the /verify page (WebCrypto) recompute the whole chain from the JSON, check that each pasted record-check code matches the hash at its seq, and verify the Merkle proof and TSA token. The verify_timeline_head(p_matter_ref, p_seq, p_head_prefix) RPC additionally confirms that the code occurs in the server's chain history at that seq. That is a convenience, not the root of trust. 9) Trash and erasure (migration 013 integration): trash_item() on a court_case or case_thread works unchanged, because there is no FK. trash_item() now also copies the matter's head (seq and head_hash) into the trash snapshot and revokes active shares. Events stay in the table, invisible while the matter is in trash. restore_trash_item() checks that the head still equals the snapshot's. purge_trash_item() and purge_expired_trash(), replaced in migration 014, call a private purge_matter_timeline(kind, id). That function sets the transaction-local GUC app.matter_events_purge='on' (the same pattern as set_legal_hold and app.legal_hold_change), writes timeline_head_sha256 and timeline_seq to the trash_items tombstone, deletes the matter's events, head row and shares, and clears the GUC. A BEFORE DELETE trigger on matter_events raises 42501 unless that GUC is on, so ordinary DELETEs fail for every role, service_role included. Legal hold still blocks trashing, and purge_expired_trash keeps its thread_on_hold check. Erasure is complete (DPDP s.8(7)): what survives is a hash, which reveals nothing about the events because they were salted.

### Where it is built

Existing: migration 004's audit_logs append-only trigger pattern. Migration 013's set_legal_hold GUC pattern, trash_item(), restore_trash_item(), purge_trash_item() and purge_expired_trash(), extended in migration 014. app/services/ecourts_service.py (the sync diff from P01, emitted from the in-process provider response). app/routers/drafting.py and documents.py (approve and export hooks). app/services/whatsapp_intake.py reply_as_lawyer. The P01 client_updates sender (appends the record-check line). app/services/pdf_service.py (work-log PDF). app/services/whatsapp_service.py (the timeline_digest template). app/worker.py (monthly digest and daily anchor crons). New: app/services/matter_timeline.py (canonical(), attest(), emit(), verify_chain(), merkle_root()), app/services/anchor_service.py (RFC 3161 client and object-lock upload), app/routers/timeline.py, migration 014 (tables, triggers, _append_event, record_milestone, emit_attested_event, set_event_visibility, client_timeline, verify_timeline_head, purge_matter_timeline, the updated trash functions), scripts/verify_timeline.py, frontend/src/app/cases/page.tsx (Timeline tab), frontend/src/app/t/[token]/page.tsx (read-only client view, noindex) and frontend/src/app/verify/page.tsx (offline verifier).

### Why current tools fail and this won't

Clio's activity feed is internal, editable by the firm and US-oriented. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI have no client layer. LawRato rates lawyers by reviews, not verified work. Indian case trackers show court dates, not the firm's own work. Ours fills itself from events the product already produces, so it costs the lawyer nothing. Its source labels can't be faked through the API, because court and system events need a server attestation and lawyer entries are forced to 'lawyer'. Its integrity doesn't depend on trusting our database: the client holds head commitments in their own WhatsApp, daily roots are timestamped by an outside authority and kept in write-once storage, and anyone can recompute the exported chain offline, internal entries included, without seeing privileged content.

### Safeguards

Privilege: client visibility is opt-in for anything that isn't a court record or a message already sent to the client. Hidden entries are exported only as salted commitments. Every visibility change is itself logged. Integrity: no role can write directly; court and system labels need a server attestation; appends are serialised per matter; heads go out in client messages and to an outside timestamp authority with write-once storage; verification works offline. DPDP: shares are purpose-limited and revocable. Erasure goes only through the 013 trash and purge flow, using a transaction-local GUC like set_legal_hold, and leaves a hash-only tombstone. Tokens carry no PII. Only hashes reach the timestamp authority. Invariant 2: hooks run under the user's JWT through SECURITY DEFINER functions. The client view is a narrow anon RPC, and the digest and anchor crons are per-org and global server jobs. These need CTO sign-off as additions to the invariant 2 list. BCI: the timeline is factual, not promotional, and goes only to the firm's own clients. Lawyer approval: no AI writes any entry, because summaries come from fixed templates.

### How the panel's objections were answered

(1) 'The client holds nothing that commits to the head', 'rewrite and recompute passes verify', and 'third parties can't check continuity through hidden events'. Every client-facing message (P01 updates, digest, PDF footer, share page) now carries seq and a 16-hex head prefix. A daily Merkle root of all heads is RFC 3161-timestamped by an outside timestamp authority and stored in object-lock storage. The verifier checks pasted codes against the chain history at that seq, plus the Merkle proof and TSA token, and runs offline, so it doesn't trust our database. Hidden events are exported as salted commitments (hash = sha256(prev || commitment)), so anyone can recompute the whole chain without seeing privileged content. Tests: test_tamper_detected, test_offline_verify_across_hidden_events, test_anchor_merkle_and_tsa, test_record_check_line_in_client_messages. (2) Append-only vs trash and purge, both objections. matter_events has no FK to court_cases or case_threads, so trash_item() deletes the case without cascading or aborting. The head goes into the trash snapshot, shares are revoked, and restore checks the head. Deletion happens only inside purge_matter_timeline(), called from the replaced purge_trash_item() and purge_expired_trash(). It sets the transaction-local GUC app.matter_events_purge, the same pattern as set_legal_hold and app.legal_hold_change, and writes a tombstone with the head hash and seq. Any other DELETE raises 42501 for every role. The tests now agree: test_direct_writes_refused covers an ordinary DELETE (refused), test_purge_erases_and_tombstones covers the purge path, and test_trash_court_case_with_timeline covers today's trash flow. (3) Concurrency forks, three objections. Appends go only through _append_event(), which locks the matter_chain_heads row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, assigns seq and prev_hash from it, and updates it in the same transaction. Unique constraints on (matter, seq) and (matter, prev_hash) are a backstop. test_concurrent_emits_linear runs 20 parallel emits. (4) Forgeable source labels. INSERT is revoked from authenticated and anon, and a trigger refuses rows not written through the function, even for service_role. record_milestone() forces source='lawyer' and checks membership. Court and system events need an HMAC attestation from the API process, whose key authenticated users can't read, and event_uuid blocks replay. Court events are built from the provider response the server fetched, not from user-writable provider_data. Tests: test_forged_court_source_rejected, test_sync_emits_events. (5) The client_visible toggle vs append-only. Visibility is no longer a mutable column. default_visible is fixed by (source, kind) and hashed. Changes are appended as visibility_changed events and read latest-wins. test_visibility_toggle_is_event shows the chain still verifies after toggles. Effort raised to L to cover the anchoring and verifier work.

### Acceptance tests

- Local Postgres test_direct_writes_refused: INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on matter_events through PostgREST as authenticated raises 42501. A direct INSERT or DELETE as service_role without the function GUCs also raises 42501.
- test_forged_court_source_rejected: calling emit_attested_event as authenticated with source='court' and a wrong or missing attestation is refused. Calling record_milestone with source='court' in the payload stores source='lawyer'. Replaying a valid attested event_uuid gives 23505.
- test_concurrent_emits_linear: 20 parallel emits for one matter (asyncpg, 20 connections) give seq 1..20 with no gaps, every prev_hash equal to the previous hash, and a passing verify_chain. 20 parallel emits spread across 4 matters give 4 independent unbroken chains.
- test_hash_chain_python_sql_agree: the hash, commitment and canonical string computed in SQL equal matter_timeline.canonical(), commitment() and hash() in Python, and the JS verifier, on a 5-event fixture including unicode summaries.
- test_tamper_detected: with triggers disabled in a raw-SQL fixture, editing event 2's summary makes verify_chain report a break at seq 2. Recomputing every later hash makes a pasted record-check code from seq 3 fail to match, and the stored Merkle anchor no longer includes the new head.
- test_offline_verify_across_hidden_events: from the exported JSON (visible events in full, hidden ones as commitments only), scripts/verify_timeline.py recomputes the head. Changing any visible field or any hidden commitment breaks it.
- test_hidden_content_not_inferable: the export for a hidden milestone contains no summary, kind or date, and the commitment differs between two events with identical content because the salts differ.
- test_visibility_toggle_is_event: hiding and re-showing an event appends two visibility_changed events. The chain still verifies, and client_timeline reflects the latest change.
- test_record_check_line_in_client_messages: every rendered P01 update, digest and PDF footer contains 'entry <seq>' and the 16-hex head prefix of the chain at send time.
- test_anchor_merkle_and_tsa: the daily job builds a root over the heads. The inclusion proof for each matter verifies. A fixture RFC 3161 response from a local test TSA verifies with the fixture CA, and one with a tampered root fails.
- test_trash_court_case_with_timeline: trash_item('court_case') on a case with 5 events succeeds (no cascade, no trigger abort). client_timeline returns nothing while the case is in trash, and restore_trash_item brings the timeline back with an unchanged head.
- test_purge_erases_and_tombstones: purge_trash_item deletes the matter's events, head row and shares, and the tombstone keeps timeline_head_sha256 and timeline_seq. A DELETE outside purge_matter_timeline still raises 42501.
- test_legal_hold_blocks: a case under legal hold can't be trashed, so its events can't be purged.
- test_sync_emits_events: the P01 diff fixture (a new next date and a new order) produces exactly 2 court events, attested, with default_visible true. Editing provider_data by hand through PostgREST produces no court event.
- test_draft_export_emits_system_event: exporting an approved draft creates a document_exported system event that is internal by default.
- test_client_timeline_rpc_filters: an internal milestone comes back only as a commitment. A revoked or expired token returns nothing. Another matter's token can't read this matter.
- test_token_not_pii: the share URL contains only the opaque token, with no phone number, name or CNR.
- RLS test: org B can't select org A's matter_events or matter_chain_heads through the REST API.

### Reviewers' minor notes

- Putting the record-check code on every WhatsApp message will look odd to most clients. Consider putting it only in the monthly digest and the PDF, with a short explanation of what the code means, while keeping the anchoring.
- Effort L for a feature whose demand is unproven: build the automatic timeline and share page first, and add the RFC 3161 and object-lock anchoring later.
- A no-login bearer link to a criminal or matrimonial matter's timeline is risky if forwarded or if the client's phone is seen by the other side. Offer an OTP to the client's recorded number as an org default for criminal and family matters, and use a short default expiry.
- Confirm that the digest and record-check codes go only to contacts with an outbound-update opt-in (see the P04 note).
- Lawyer milestones take any occurred_at. Show recorded_at beside occurred_at in the client view, so a late-recorded milestone isn't read as contemporaneous.
- Court events from the worker's daily sync run without a user JWT. List that emit path explicitly among the invariant 2 additions.
- Hidden-entry commitments reveal the count and timing of internal work. Consider batching hidden entries per day if firms object.
