'Show to client' / 'Hide from client' calls set_event_visibility(), which appends a 'visibility_changed' event (internal, ref_seq pointing to the target) to the same chain. Effective visibility is the latest visibility_changed for that event, falling back to default_visible. Court events, update_sent and quote_sent default to visible. Everything else defaults to internal (privilege). 6) Client access is through client_timeline(p_token), a SECURITY DEFINER RPC callable by anon and rate limited. It hashes the token, checks the share isn't revoked or expired and that the matter still exists (not in trash), and returns visible events in full and hidden ones as commitments, plus the head. 7) Anchoring outside the firm's control, in three ways. (a) Every client-facing message (each P01 update, the monthly digest, the PDF footer, the share page) carries the current seq and the first 16 hex characters of head_hash. The client therefore holds a growing set of commitments in their own WhatsApp that a rewritten chain can't reproduce. (b) A daily server job computes a Merkle root over all matter heads (leaf = sha256(matter_kind:matter_id:seq:head)). It obtains an RFC 3161 timestamp from a configured external timestamp authority (TIMELINE_TSA_URL; only the hash leaves our servers) and writes the root and token to chain_anchors and to a write-once object store bucket (S3 Object Lock, compliance mode). (c) The exported JSON includes the Merkle inclusion proof and TSA token for the latest anchor covering the matter. 8) Verification is offline-first. scripts/verify_timeline.py and the /verify page (WebCrypto) recompute the whole chain from the JSON, check that each pasted record-check code matches the hash at its seq, and verify the Merkle proof and TSA token. The verify_timeline_head(p_matter_ref, p_seq, p_head_prefix) RPC additionally confirms that the code occurs in the server's chain history at that seq. That is a convenience, not the root of trust. 9) Trash and erasure (migration 013 integration): trash_item() on a court_case or case_thread works unchanged, because there is no FK. trash_item() now also copies the matter's head (seq and head_hash) into the trash snapshot and revokes active shares. Events stay in the table, invisible while the matter is in trash. restore_trash_item() checks that the head still equals the snapshot's. purge_trash_item() and purge_expired_trash(), replaced in migration 014, call a private purge_matter_timeline(kind, id). That function sets the transaction-local GUC app.matter_events_purge='on' (the same pattern as set_legal_hold and app.legal_hold_change), writes timeline_head_sha256 and timeline_seq to the trash_items tombstone, deletes the matter's events, head row and shares, and clears the GUC. A BEFORE DELETE trigger on matter_events raises 42501 unless that GUC is on, so ordinary DELETEs fail for every role, service_role included. Legal hold still blocks trashing, and purge_expired_trash keeps its thread_on_hold check. Erasure is complete (DPDP s.8(7)): what survives is a hash, which reveals nothing about the events because they were salted.
proposal.build_on: Existing: migration 004's audit_logs append-only trigger pattern. Migration 013's set_legal_hold GUC pattern, trash_item(), restore_trash_item(), purge_trash_item() and purge_expired_trash(), extended in migration 014. app/services/ecourts_service.py (the sync diff from P01, emitted from the in-process provider response). app/routers/drafting.py and documents.py (approve and export hooks). app/services/whatsapp_intake.py reply_as_lawyer. The P01 client_updates sender (appends the record-check line). app/services/pdf_service.py (work-log PDF). app/services/whatsapp_service.py (the timeline_digest template). app/worker.py (monthly digest and daily anchor crons). New: app/services/matter_timeline.py (canonical(), attest(), emit(), verify_chain(), merkle_root()), app/services/anchor_service.py (RFC 3161 client and object-lock upload), app/routers/timeline.py, migration 014 (tables, triggers, _append_event, record_milestone, emit_attested_event, set_event_visibility, client_timeline, verify_timeline_head, purge_matter_timeline, the updated trash functions), scripts/verify_timeline.py, frontend/src/app/cases/page.tsx (Timeline tab), frontend/src/app/t/[token]/page.tsx (read-only client view, noindex) and frontend/src/app/verify/page.tsx (offline verifier).
proposal.why_incumbents_fail_and_this_wont: Clio's activity feed is internal, editable by the firm and US-oriented. Harvey, CoCounsel and Lexis+ AI have no client layer. LawRato rates lawyers by reviews, not verified work. Indian case trackers show court dates, not the firm's own work. Ours fills itself from events the product already produces, so it costs the lawyer nothing. Its source labels can't be faked through the API, because court and system events need a server attestation and lawyer entries are forced to 'lawyer'. Its integrity doesn't depend on trusting our database: the client holds head commitments in their own WhatsApp, daily roots are timestamped by an outside authority and kept in write-once storage, and anyone can recompute the exported chain offline, internal entries included, without seeing privileged content.
acceptance_tests: Local Postgres test_direct_writes_refused: INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on matter_events through PostgREST as authenticated raises 42501. A direct INSERT or DELETE as service_role without the function GUCs also raises 42501.

test_forged_court_source_rejected: calling emit_attested_event as authenticated with source='court' and a wrong or missing attestation is refused. Calling record_milestone with source='court' in the payload stores source='lawyer'. Replaying a valid attested event_uuid gives 23505.

test_concurrent_emits_linear: 20 parallel emits for one matter (asyncpg, 20 connections) give seq 1..20 with no gaps, every prev_hash equal to the previous hash, and a passing verify_chain. 20 parallel emits spread across 4 matters give 4 independent unbroken chains.

test_hash_chain_python_sql_agree: the hash, commitment and canonical string computed in SQL equal matter_timeline.canonical(), commitment() and hash() in Python, and the JS verifier, on a 5-event fixture including unicode summaries.

test_tamper_detected: with triggers disabled in a raw-SQL fixture, editing event 2's summary makes verify_chain report a break at seq 2. Recomputing every later hash makes a pasted record-check code from seq 3 fail to match, and the stored Merkle anchor no longer includes the new head.

test_offline_verify_across_hidden_events: from the exported JSON (visible events in full, hidden ones as commitments only), scripts/verify_timeline.py recomputes the head. Changing any visible field or any hidden commitment breaks it.
test_hidden_content_not_inferable: the export for a hidden milestone contains no summary, kind or date, and the commitment differs between two events with identical content because the salts differ.
test_visibility_toggle_is_event: hiding and re-showing an event appends two visibility_changed events. The chain still verifies, and client_timeline reflects the latest change.
test_record_check_line_in_client_messages: every rendered P01 update, digest and PDF footer contains 'entry <seq>' and the 16-hex head prefix of the chain at send time.

test_anchor_merkle_and_tsa: the daily job builds a root over the heads. The inclusion proof for each matter verifies. A fixture RFC 3161 response from a local test TSA verifies with the fixture CA, and one with a tampered root fails.

test_trash_court_case_with_timeline: trash_item('court_case') on a case with 5 events succeeds (no cascade, no trigger abort). client_timeline returns nothing while the case is in trash, and restore_trash_item brings the timeline back with an unchanged head.

test_purge_erases_and_tombstones: purge_trash_item deletes the matter's events, head row and shares, and the tombstone keeps timeline_head_sha256 and timeline_seq. A DELETE outside purge_matter_timeline still raises 42501.
test_legal_hold_blocks: a case under legal hold can't be trashed, so its events can't be purged.

test_sync_emits_events: the P01 diff fixture (a new next date and a new order) produces exactly 2 court events, attested, with default_visible true. Editing provider_data by hand through PostgREST produces no court event.
test_draft_export_emits_system_event: exporting an approved draft creates a document_exported system event that is internal by default.
test_client_timeline_rpc_filters: an internal milestone comes back only as a commitment. A revoked or expired token returns nothing. Another matter's token can't read this matter.
test_token_not_pii: the share URL contains only the opaque token, with no phone number, name or CNR.
RLS test: org B can't select org A's matter_events or matter_chain_heads through the REST API.
proposal.safeguards: Privilege: client visibility is opt-in for anything that isn't a court record or a message already sent to the client. Hidden entries are exported only as salted commitments. Every visibility change is itself logged. Integrity: no role can write directly; court and system labels need a server attestation; appends are serialised per matter; heads go out in client messages and to an outside timestamp authority with write-once storage; verification works offline. DPDP: shares are purpose-limited and revocable. Erasure goes only through the 013 trash and purge flow, using a transaction-local GUC like set_legal_hold, and leaves a hash-only tombstone. Tokens carry no PII. Only hashes reach the timestamp authority. Invariant 2: hooks run under the user's JWT through SECURITY DEFINER functions. The client view is a narrow anon RPC, and the digest and anchor crons are per-org and global server jobs. These need CTO sign-off as additions to the invariant 2 list. BCI: the timeline is factual, not promotional, and goes only to the firm's own clients. Lawyer approval: no AI writes any entry, because summaries come from fixed templates.
proposal.answers_to_objections: (1) 'The client holds nothing that commits to the head', 'rewrite and recompute passes verify', and 'third parties can't check continuity through hidden events'. Every client-facing message (P01 updates, digest, PDF footer, share page) now carries seq and a 16-hex head prefix. A daily Merkle root of all heads is RFC 3161-timestamped by an outside timestamp authority and stored in object-lock storage. The verifier checks pasted codes against the chain history at that seq, plus the Merkle proof and TSA token, and runs offline, so it doesn't trust our database. Hidden events are exported as salted commitments (hash = sha256(prev || commitment)), so anyone can recompute the whole chain without seeing privileged content. Tests: test_tamper_detected, test_offline_verify_across_hidden_events, test_anchor_merkle_and_tsa, test_record_check_line_in_client_messages. (2) Append-only vs trash and purge, both objections. matter_events has no FK to court_cases or case_threads, so trash_item() deletes the case without cascading or aborting. The head goes into the trash snapshot, shares are revoked, and restore checks the head. Deletion happens only inside purge_matter_timeline(), called from the replaced purge_trash_item() and purge_expired_trash(). It sets the transaction-local GUC app.matter_events_purge, the same pattern as set_legal_hold and app.legal_hold_change, and writes a tombstone with the head hash and seq. Any other DELETE raises 42501 for every role. The tests now agree: test_direct_writes_refused covers an ordinary DELETE (refused), test_purge_erases_and_tombstones covers the purge path, and test_trash_court_case_with_timeline covers today's trash flow. (3) Concurrency forks, three objections. Appends go only through _append_event(), which locks the matter_chain_heads row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, assigns seq and prev_hash from it, and updates it in the same transaction. Unique constraints on (matter, seq) and (matter, prev_hash) are a backstop. test_concurrent_emits_linear runs 20 parallel emits. (4) Forgeable source labels. INSERT is revoked from authenticated and anon, and a trigger refuses rows not written through the function, even for service_role. record_milestone() forces source='lawyer' and checks membership. Court and system events need an HMAC attestation from the API process, whose key authenticated users can't read, and event_uuid blocks replay. Court events are built from the provider response the server fetched, not from user-writable provider_data. Tests: test_forged_court_source_rejected, test_sync_emits_events. (5) The client_visible toggle vs append-only. Visibility is no longer a mutable column. default_visible is fixed by (source, kind) and hashed. Changes are appended as visibility_changed events and read latest-wins. test_visibility_toggle_is_event shows the chain still verifies after toggles. Effort raised to L to cover the anchoring and verifier work.

minor: Putting the record-check code on every WhatsApp message will look odd to most clients. Consider putting it only in the monthly digest and the PDF, with a short explanation of what the code means, while keeping the anchoring.
Effort L for a feature whose demand is unproven: build the automatic timeline and share page first, and add the RFC 3161 and object-lock anchoring later.

A no-login bearer link to a criminal or matrimonial matter's timeline is risky if forwarded or if the client's phone is seen by the other side. Offer an OTP to the client's recorded number as an org default for criminal and family matters, and use a short default expiry.
Confirm that the digest and record-check codes go only to contacts with an outbound-update opt-in (see the P04 note).
Lawyer milestones take any occurred_at. Show recorded_at beside occurred_at in the client view, so a late-recorded milestone isn't read as contemporaneous.
Court events from the worker's daily sync run without a user JWT. List that emit path explicitly among the invariant 2 additions.
Hidden-entry commitments reveal the count and timing of internal work. Consider batching hidden entries per day if firms object.
